name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Salvation Army is an organization that does a lot of good. That is the only reason giving 4 stars. I like that they do not collect sales tax when purchasing their donations. Store is large and spacious but not the best location on Nebraska near Bearss. The parking lot is well marked and large but typically busy.  Sadly they have followed the trend of thrift stores to raise prices near retail levels without the same return rights. This store is one of the best for new looking furniture as believe get direct furniture store donations. Books and exercise equipment are priced as used.  Electronics were organized and power outlets available for testing, pricing varied.  I saw shoes at 12.99 and clothing 7-8 dollars but many low end store brands that you can buy new for a couple dollars more and would avoid. The clothing was organized by type and color so need to go through a lot to find your size. They do have fitting rooms which is a plus. Housewares were organized by color and priced on the upper end and some had stickers from stores like Marshalls with the SA price being nearly the same. Not worth a special trip in my opinion but if you are in the area may want to check out as at least three other thrift stores nearby.

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center is an absolute treasure hunt in the best way possible! They have an incredible selection of furniture, with pieces that are clean, well-priced, and often in surprisingly great condition. I found some amazing items on my first visit, and the value you get here is unbeatable. You can tell they take the time to organize the floor so everything is easy to browse, and there’s always something new to discover.

The staff is friendly and helpful, and the store is spacious and well-maintained. It’s clear they care about both the customers and the donation process. I was really impressed by how smooth and welcoming the whole experience was.

I’m already planning to go back for more, because this location has quickly become one of my favorite spots for unique finds and great deals. If you’re looking for affordable, quality furniture or just love thrifting in a clean, organized store, this Salvation Army is a must-visit. Five stars all the way!

top_reviews.text:
St. Helena Island is a hidden gem if you’re looking for a quiet and relaxing coastal experience. The natural beauty is absolutely stunning — marsh views, Spanish moss hanging from the trees, and breathtaking sunsets over the water. It feels untouched and authentic compared to more commercial beach destinations.
The island has a rich Gullah history and culture, which makes the experience even more meaningful. It’s a great place to slow down, reflect, and enjoy nature. Hunting Island nearby offers beautiful beaches and scenic lighthouse views.
The only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is that dining and shopping options are somewhat limited, and some areas feel very rural — which can be a positive or negative depending on what you’re looking for.
Overall, I highly recommend St. Helena Island for anyone who wants peace, nature, and true Lowcountry atmosphere.

top_reviews.text:
I’ve stayed at a lot of high-end resorts, but Sea Island really does stand out. From the moment you cross the causeway onto the island, there’s an unmistakable sense of arrival. The landscaping is immaculate, the marsh views stretch forever, and every building has that signature coastal-Southern style that feels both elegant and inviting.

Setting & Atmosphere

Sea Island combines the charm of a historic Southern resort with the polish of a modern five-star property. It’s spread out over several distinct areas—The Cloister, The Beach Club, The Lodge at Sea Island Golf Club—yet everything feels cohesive. There’s a gentle pace to life here, and even when it’s busy, you never feel crowded.

Accommodations

I stayed at The Cloister, and the room was generous in size with high ceilings, plush bedding, and a private balcony that looked out on the river. Attention to detail was everywhere: fresh flowers, turndown service with local chocolates, and a bathroom that felt like a private spa. Friends who stayed at The Lodge raved about its boutique feel and direct access to the golf courses.

Dining

Food at Sea Island deserves its own chapter. You can do an elegant dinner at the Georgian Room (fine dining with impeccable service), grab fresh seafood at Tavola, or wander over to the Beach Club for casual bites. Breakfast on the terrace overlooking the marsh is a must. Service was consistently gracious without being stiff, and every meal had a strong sense of place—lots of local seafood, regional produce, and thoughtful wine pairings.

Activities

This is where Sea Island really shines. Golfers will be in heaven with three championship courses (Seaside, Plantation, and Retreat) plus a world-class Golf Performance Center. Tennis and pickleball courts are top notch. The spa is one of the best I’ve experienced—quiet relaxation areas, skilled therapists, and a full menu of treatments. For families, there’s a robust kids’ program, nature excursions, horseback riding on the beach, fishing charters, and even falconry demos. You can be as active or as relaxed as you want.

Service & Hospitality

Every interaction with staff—from the front desk to the beach attendants—felt genuine. They seem to anticipate what you need before you ask. Towels and chairs magically appear by the pool; water bottles are offered on the golf course; staff remember your name and preferences after one day. It’s old-school hospitality with modern polish.

Overall Impression

Sea Island Resort is one of those rare places that delivers on every promise. It has the pedigree and luxury of a classic destination but also the warmth and flexibility that make you feel at home. Whether you’re coming for a golf getaway, a family vacation, a spa retreat, or a special celebration, it’s hard to imagine leaving disappointed. It’s not inexpensive, but the level of service, amenities, and atmosphere justify the splurge. I left feeling refreshed, spoiled, and already plotting my return trip.

Visited Mesa Verde and hiked the Petroglyph Point Trail and drove the loop to view all the houses.

First, the hike was about 3 miles and started at the museum. The first half is rocky but a lot of fun, with the furthest away point being the wall of petroglyphs which is the largest display in the park. They were neat and I took many pictures of them. The last half of the hike was relatively flat and gravel proving to be quite easy.

The loop road stops at many overlooks and pithouses. There were great views of the stone cliff houses at many of them, with the best viewpoints of at "square tower house overlook" and "sun point view". The loop road is a must when visiting the park!

One more house worth viewing is the Spruce Tree House which is located behind the museum. Simply park and walk behind the museum for the best views of it, its the 3rd largest cliff dwelling in the park.
top_reviews.author: Explorer Man

top_reviews.text: Make sure you have at-least an hour added to the time what your car gps states to be on time for your tour. They have restrooms at various locations with is good. Glad we carried food as cafes were far. The roads are on a cliff, so many cars were driving cautiously. Signs were well places to plan for scenic location stops. Two hikes are literally next to a cliff, so sturdy shoes recommended. Would highly recommend Longhouse tour if you had to pick just one. Ranger Ray was very knowledgeable and shared a lot with us during our tour. These tours gets sold fast, so do book your tour in advance.

top_reviews.text: I went here to try and be of service. I was warmly welcomed, and the staff and residents showed genuine appreciation for my help. I retired in 2016 after a 30 year career as an R.N, and my retirement " hobbies " weren't cutting it for me anymore. I still have a gut-level need to contribute to the world instead of just thinking about what I can I do for myself and everyone else can deal with their difficult life situations on their own. I can't physically do the things I did most of my life, and I don't have a lot of anything, but I have more than I need and I don't feel like I can keep it without sharing what I do have. What I do have is more time most days, and sometimes just being present and listening to folks share what they are struggling with can hopefully help them see they have value and become willing to change. The Salvation army DOES change lives for the better. Maybe not everyone that are battling serious problems, but they give everyone help that they desperately need without shame or judgment.

top_reviews.text: My complaint is not geared toward the Salvation Army but the security company it employs to run its shelters. I'm not alone in my experience with them. I thought emergency shelters were for emergencies yet they expect you to plan tour emergency and call ahead and if you don't you are turned away regardless if there was no answer or if they have empty beds or not. The current guards have me waiting outside knowing I'm scheduled to have major surgery in the morning telling me that I did not register yet I spoke with the director here earlier this afternoon and register. Things like this happen often here they even turned a blind man away with spare beds. I'm currently gathering eye witness accounts of other episodes and sworn affidavits to present to the concerned party. I've talked with at least a dozen such people and hope to get more. I feel that a charitable organization as yourselves should be more understanding to the often I'll and mentally I'll. I look forward to speaking with someone from your organization concerning these matters. Yours Truly Kenneth Hale

top_reviews.text:
I just need to express that I am totally appalled over the total lack of compassion I recently experienced while showing up at Apache Junction location for a food box.  My friend and I are both homeless, and we were in need of food.  We were denied any help at all because we were HOMELESS. WE could not provide proof of residence or a lease agreement because we are homeless....without 4 walls and a roof to protect us, to keep us warm, but do have a place to prepare food if we had some to prepare.  We were actually told "This is the Salvation Army," as if to mean that they don't help the homeless. You must have a home in order to receive a food box from us.  I then asked if you all helped with housing or shelter, and was again told no,  you don't help with those services and was handed a piece of paper with some numbers on it.

Where and what are our donations being used for exactly?  I am just completely confused and baffled by the total lack of compassion and how we left there without a morsel of food and not a bit of service offered to us at all...because they are "The Salvation Army.

UPDATE:  after the let down above, I found a room to rent, but to my dismay, the person I am renting from has an obsession with smelting Lead, and does it inside the home, putting everyone at risk of lead poisoning from inhaling the toxic fumes and by further contamination due to the tiny particles that it puts into the air, only to leave a blanket of toxic dust all over the home. Turns out we start feeling sickly. He takes off to hospital. Leaving me behind in the toxic environment. He ended up inches from kidney failure and had to be put on dialysis 3 times a week for an indefinite time. I saw my doctor and my blood work showed exposure and I have tested the house with lead test kit, and only 2 swabs were negative out of 15 areas and surfaces in the home. All the rest were positive, including the hair on my head.  This place is not fit for humans. It has become toxic and a danger to be in.  I reached out to guess who? Salvation Army.  Once again, I was treated as if I was unimportant, and was even asked in a condescending tone "Well, what were you wanting from us?" I explained the danger and said I was hoping you might be able to help. And as if THE ANSWER IS NOT OVERLY OBVIOUS.  She said that they could not help, and I WAS GIVEN SOME LADIES NUMBER, IN WHICH I DID CALL, LEFT A MESSAGE EXPLAINING THE DANGER I WAS IN, AND MY DESPERATION.  I NEVER SO MUCH AS HEARD 1 WORD BACK.

I AM SORRY MAYBE I AM THE IGNORANT ONE HERE, BUT WHEN  I LOOK UP THE DEFINITION OF SALVATION, I READ THIS: SALVATION: The preservation or deliverance from harm, ruin, or loss.
???
top_reviews.author: Melissa Shepherd

The organization quickly expanded, first across England and then overseas to the United States in 1880, and now operates in over 120 countries."

top_reviews.text:
So. This place is BOTH the Salvation Army Thrift Outlet AND a regular Salvation Army Family Store.

If you go immediately to your right after you walk in, you will see the Thrift Outlet area. It's fenced off from the rest of the store. There are several (maybe 6, maybe 8) of those big table/bins on wheels. One held glass and housewares type item. One held shoes. The rest held clothing.

Unlike at the Goodwill bins store, there were only a few other shoppers in the area. There was not a bunch of loud noise to experience. There was no rush to dig through the bins. It didn't look like any workers were coming along to take them away any time soon.

My friend and I poked through the clothing. There was good stuff in there, but my friend didn't find anything she wanted/needed/that fit her. I found a pair of Bobby Brooks pants in my size and a style I like. Score! (The original Salvation Army store tag on the pants was marked $8.99.)

Clothes in the Thrift Outlet area sell for $1.89 a pound. There are signs saying there is a minimum purchase of one pound/$1.89 required. No problem. I thought $1.89 was a good price for the pants when I didn't find anything else I wanted.

You have to pay for Thrift Outlet area items before you leave the Thrift Outlet area. It took several minutes for a worker to come to the register to take payment. When she arrived, she seemed surprised that I only wanted the one pair of pants. She told me there was a minimum purchase required. I told her I had read the signs, and I understood the policy. She said, "So you don't mind if I charge you $1.89 for just this?" while gesturing to the pants I had chosen. I assured her I did not mind.

After buying my pants, my friend and I went into the Family Store part of the building. Well. While the store was neat, clean, and organized, the pricing was outrageous!

We didn't spend long looking at clothes, but a couple of items I stopped to look at as I passed by were on par with Goodwill prices. A purse I liked was priced $5.99, which seemed a little much for what it was. But when we got to housewares...that's when the sticker shock really set in.

Single items were mostly $3.99. There was a sign that said customers could get a free lid with the purchase of a pot. Then I picked up a large (but not giant) wide mouth canning jar with a lid. At Goodwill, such an item would usually be priced $2.49 or $3.49. Not here. Nope. Not at this Salvation Army Family Store. I gasped when I saw the price. The canning jar was priced at $5.99!!! You can buy a pack of 12 jars like that in Phoenix for under $20!!!

We looked around a little more, but neither of us purchased any of the regular priced items. We left pretty quickly.

If I were in the neighborhood, I might stop in again to check out the Thrift Outlet, but I'm not interested in overpaying at the Family Store.

name: Primavera Foundation - Project Action for Veterans

top_reviews.text:
I am writing to formally express grave concerns regarding the services and professional conduct experienced at Primavera Foundation Project Action for Veterans (PAV) in Tucson, Arizona. As a veteran seeking essential support, I encountered significant challenges that warrant immediate attention and investigation.

Despite my direct engagement with PAV, including mobile outreach during a period of extreme vulnerability due to homelessness and illness, I regrettably did not receive the expected comprehensive homelessness intervention, prevention, or rapid rehousing services. Furthermore, critical support such as community development, financial assistance, or financial education, which are vital for addressing the root causes of poverty and housing instability, were not provided. These gaps prevented PAV from partnering effectively to overcome barriers to stable housing.

I filed a formal grievance concerning harassment and discriminatory treatment by a PAV resource specialist, Mr. Jesus Manuel (Manny) Lopez. My discomfort and safety concerns stemming from Mr. Lopez's alleged differential behavior when I was alone versus when accompanied by family members in his office were central to this complaint. Following the grievance, Mr. Lopez allegedly attempted to reschedule appointments, despite my explicit request for new case management, and subsequently exited me from the program for non-compliance. This action appears retaliatory and unjust.

Moreover, I reported that responses from leadership, specifically Director Josefina Torres and Chief Operating Officer Margarita Bauza, regarding my grievance were inadequate, failing to ensure my safety or resolve the issues. I was informed that due to staffing shortages, I would remain with the case manager against whom I had reported harassment and discrimination.

The alleged harassment included unwelcome, hostile, and intimidating behavior, both verbal and visual, which I believe was rooted in discrimination based on my race, gender, and veteran status. This conduct has severely disrupted my access to critical veteran care, emergency financial rental assistance, and eviction relief. It has created a hostile and unsupportive environment, negatively impacting my well-being, diminishing my standing as a veteran and individual, and inducing severe anxiety, depression, and suicidal ideation, necessitating contact with the VA Crisis Line.

While I am now grateful to be in transitional housing facilitated by the VA Southern Arizona VA Healthcare System HOMELESS CLINIC, the experiences with PAV have been profoundly distressing. The lack of respect, compassion, and professional courtesy, coupled with alleged discriminatory practices, raises serious questions about the ethical standards and accountability within the organization.

I urge a thorough and impartial investigation into these matters to ensure accountability, prevent future occurrences, and safeguard other veterans from similar experiences. My aim in sharing this is to advocate for necessary reforms and improved oversight within veteran support services.

Sincerely,
Macklin — Salmon Family

name: Salvation Army Tucson South Corps & Youth Center

top_reviews.text:
This is an awesome facility & newly opened as per contractual agreement with the city of Tucson for at least the 2021 calendar year, from what I understand. Don't be cold out there, come on down by 4:30 PM nightly & you're good to go! Don't be any later than 6:00 PM or you WILL miss out! The cots are comfy with a sheet & blanket (bring a lint brush,they're disaster blankets!) & the food & service are all STELLAR! If you're familiar with the staff over at the Hospitality House on 1001 N Main Avenue at Speedway, then your favorites will be over here working as well! So far I've counted Margie, Cynthia, Steve, Jill, Captain O, & Jason here as well in my three nights here so far.

Bringing in your own cell phones & food is okay to do here, just make certain you check in any knives and/or weapons & you'll get them back when you ask for them in the morning. There's a fairly nice 48" TV in the large main sleeping room with 24 men's cots at present. Then there's probably 12-16 men's cots in the main men's hall, four in the back room, & one good-sized women's dorm off the men's main hall that sleeps around 8-12 women only. Dinner is served promptly at 6:00 PM with lots of leftover's, & breakfast is served at 6:00 AM, & again, the leftover's abound with plenty of fresh coffee served at both meals.

If you want to shower, the van will take you to the Hospitality House at 1001 N Main Ave at 5:00 PM then it leaves there at 5:30 PM to come back here again in plenty of time for dinner. Tell them when you check in before 4:30 PM that you want to go if you do - they only van shuttle six clients per trip. At 8:00 AM the van will shuttle you back to Hospitality House from here again for a shower or to do laundry if you request either or both, but do speak up and ask staff by 7:00 PM the night before if you want to go. There's room to store your stuff too - just ask Captain O or other staff the night before & you don't have to lug it around all day IF YOU ARE RETURNING the same night.

So the hours here are 4:30 PM - 8:00 AM, then with a ride back to The Ronstadt if you need it! Pretty cool & just a fantastically relaxed situation with staff very chill too! You'll like the faces of Salvation Army here that you're not familiar with! Wonderful! Everyone is very well-behaved here & that's about all you need to be able to fit in here. Good food & plenty of it! Cigarette breaks every hour on the hour & the last one's at 10:00 PM & then it's lights out. DON'T be COLD! Warm your bones here! We're waitin' on ya!

top_reviews.text:
Considering I’m in need of a place to sleep, i called this place a few times and didn’t get an answer. I drove two hours out of my way  to check if there were open beds and found the doors locked around 5:30pm, confused, I rang the bell(twice) until a lady came to open the doors up and seemed a bit frustrated I was even there. I asked if it was possible to register for a bed, she said she “didn’t have any beds open right now, just a warm shelter and to check in Fayetteville” which is 20-30min away from here, clearly not ideal. A warm shelter I could assume is an area for those who need to stay out of the cold, but can’t sleep there if needed. Helpful? Not really. If I didn’t have my car, how would I get there and back? If I had no phone, how would I check to see if their spots were open? I asked if she had any other resources in the area, anything at all, considering I work in bentonville and would need to stay in the area if possible. She shrugged, said “nope we don’t have other resources here I can’t help you.” and that was that.
How can you, a worker, in a homeless shelter, NOT have other resources for those in need? This isn’t my first rodeo, majority of shelters would atleast have another on speed dial incase spots are full, but not even a list of recommendations for someone is ridiculous. And judging from the other reviews, I’d be better off sleeping in my car/on the side of the road!
Please do better for those in need, a little effort goes a LONG way. We’re still human beings and shouldn’t be treated like stray animals!

name: The Salvation Army Anaheim Adult Rehabilitation Center

top_reviews.text:
This place and its program changed my life and gave me a purpose. I was at a very low point in my life. I was in and out of jail. I was addicted to drugs of all types. My behavior was poor and I just couldn’t stop using.
The year was 1994, and once again my probation officer was at my house to arrest me again for a probation violation. All I wanted was to stop using and still be able to enjoy life and have fun staying clean. I asked to be sentenced to a program in hopes that it could change my life and save my marriage.
I was picked up from jail and taken to The Salvation Army - Anaheim ARC.
(Adult Rehabilitation Center) This was the start of my new life without drugs and alcohol.
That place loved on me till I was able to see that I was capable and worthy of being a productive member of society.
Anyway long story short. I finished the program and begged for a job. I knew I needed to stay connected in order to stay clean and sober. They gave me a job driving a truck and picking up donations. I was only planning on staying for a year to get my feet back on ground.
However God had a different plan for me. I ended up working for the Salvation Army for 28 years. I worked my way up from truck driver to the top position of running the warehouse. God had a plan for me to stay and work with His children that also had the disease addiction.
My life today is one of worth, and a love for God. The wife that was at her wits end with me back then, well we will be celebrating 50 years of marriage next year.
From the bottom of my heart, thank you to
The Salvation Army for changing my life.

God is so Good  😊
top_reviews.author: Mike Beaudreau

top_reviews.text:
I’ve been lucky enough to see Captain Tim and Tanya Pemberton in action through the Salvation Army, and the impact they’ve had is incredible. They’re two of the most genuine, caring, and selfless people I’ve ever met.

What makes them stand out is how real they are. They don’t just talk about the mission—they live it. I’ve watched them change the lives of hundreds of clients, help people get back on their feet, and even rebuild families that had almost fallen apart.

Tim and Tanya show up every single day for the community with compassion and integrity. They meet people where they’re at, without judgment, and give them the kind of support and encouragement that can truly change a life.

The work they’re doing isn’t about them—it’s about the people they serve. And because of that, they’ve left a lasting impact on so many lives, mine included.

top_reviews.text:
TOTALLY DISHONEST WORKERS.

I found a cabinet piece that I wanted for my dining room. It was marked $25.99

I was surprised that it was that price. I figured about $40 would be fair. So, obviously I pounced on it. It needed a lot of care. That's probably why they had it marked down .

The inside shelving was missing its supports and needed to be replaced, there were Nick's and dings along the edging than needed to be sanded out and evened, the surface would fascia was peeling and needed to be sanded and repainted. But, the piece was sturdy and with some TLC would look great.

I grabbed a worker to have him help me move the piece and double check the price. I noted my concerns about the piece. He confirmed that it was $25.99.

As I started talking about restoring it, his tune changed. He said that it was mismarked. Even though there was no apparent movement of the sticker. There was no other pieces of furniture around it missing a sticker. He said that he would sell to me for $50.

Needless to say I was shocked. I understand that there are recovering addicts working for the salvation army. Being one myself, I think it's a great experience for people to be able to start their lives again.

That is no excuse to rip somebody off however. And that's exactly what this guy tried to do. Let this be a warning for anybody that tries to shop there.

You are always bound to find something!!

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Donating used clothing to the Salvation Army Covina branch is a rewarding and simple process. The staff is welcoming and appreciative, making the experience feel meaningful. They offer a convenient drop-off area, ensuring a smooth donation. The branch is well-maintained, and the staff's commitment to serving the community is evident. Knowing that your clothing helps those in need adds a sense of purpose to the donation. It's a great way to give back while also decluttering your space. Overall, the Covina branch makes donating a hassle-free and fulfilling experience, supporting a worthy cause.
top_reviews.author: Cowboy J

top_reviews.text: My friend was one of the orphans  Salvation Army cared for decades ago. She asked me to frequent their resale stores. This location is on Citrus at Arrow Highway next door to Starbucks and across from Superior Grocery. It's well maintained. They always have sales. You can get interesting new/used items. There is adequate parking. The service is friendly and the prices are affordable. They might have anything pertaining to your home. They have clothes for the entire family. You never know what you may find.
top_reviews.author: Daphne

top_reviews.text:
I enjoy coming to the Salvation Army thrift store on Citrus in Azusa. Ricky is always so helpful on the floor, and Antonio is very friendly and informative at the register. It’s always good vibes with them at every visit.

I love the discounted deals and pricing is clear when I’m shopping. Antonio made it very clear which color tags are discounted for the day meaning I don’t have to second guess the price.

Looking forward to the next thrift haul.

top_reviews.text: Some thrift stores have gotten WAY out of hand. Goodwill, for one is not even worth going to anymore. What do they pay for the merchandise they sell? NOTHING! But that hasn't stopped those greedy jerks from jacking up the prices they charge. And don't try to BS me with "oh, but they do so much 'good' for the community". So what? That doesn't justify getting donations and then charging so much for stuff!! As for the Salvation Army, well, they're somewhat better as far as prices go. Sometimes you can find good selection of things, depending on the particular store. It's nice when you come across something unexpected, something you want but maybe hadn't thought about. That's one of the thrills of shopping at thrift stores. But, the best thrift stores to shop at, for price and selection, go to a more local place.

top_reviews.text: Terrible experience. Considering this was my first time shopping at this location. I didn’t expect much. The store had a weird smell as soon as me and my friends entered but that’s reasonable for a thrift store. The selection was terrible. I only found one photo frame I considered and bought for $2.99. My friends bought nothing.  On our way out, we got stopped by a lady. I don’t know if she was the manager or a simple member of the staff, but she accused me and my friends of stealing. She had an accusatory tone and told us not to steal again, giving us “advice for next time”. Me and my friends DID NOT steal anything so we mentioned how she could check our bags, but she refused. She justified her accusations by saying that “the cameras told her” we were stealing, and even threatened to call security on us. I don’t know what the cameras might have detected, if there’s a built in AI system within them to detect these types of situations, or if theres a person in charge of the store’s cameras who told her so, but accusing us right of the bat was incredibly disrespectful. She then accused me of giving her a bad look because I was obviously upset upon hearing such accusations. She didn’t even bother to think of us as anything else but thiefs despite us trying to prove her otherwise. She then hurried back into the store, not allowing us to clear our name. Safe to say me and my friends will never be going back. This experience left a more than bitter taste in our mouths.

name: The Salvation Army Fresno Adult Rehabilitation Center

top_reviews.text: The day I walked into SA (11/25/16), I was lost & broken mentally, physically, emotionally and spiritually and finally hit rock bottom. I had lost everything including myself and was ready for a new way of life.... I just didn’t know how. The choices that I had made to get me to where I was were bad, but that didn’t make me a bad person. What SA taught me is priceless and the relationship I have with God today  is forever. The program opened my eyes to a whole new world without alcohol or drugs. It taught me the basics for every day life like responsibility,  accountability, self love, living life on life’s terms and expanding my relationship with my higher power who I call God and Jesus Christ. By doing life one day at a time, following Gods Will and taking action, I have 4 years clean and sober (All God, His Grace and Mercy) Today I have a life full of many blessings which include my family, my son and most importantly ME!! I may have graduated the program, but this new lifestyle is a continuous process full of changes and growth for life. I continue this beautiful journey of recovery by doing the next indicated thing ... thanking God all the time, prayer/meditation, weekly meeting with my sponsor, attending meetings, step work, fellowshipping and being of service. God is good all the time and all the time God is good!!! I will be forever grateful to God for His unconditional love and the Fresno ARC program for having a place where people like me can find their true authentic selves to be who God intended us to be. 🙏🏼❤️🙌🏼
top_reviews.author: Meche Rosales

top_reviews.text: I graduated on Sep 28 2016 I was with some of you brothers that have left comments on here and I am doing BLESSED up to this day. don't lose hope brothers my name is Misael Lopez and here for whoever needs me.God has restored my life my family my material things and even blessed me with my first home just by praying to him humbly and going every week to church just like we make time to do other things we need to make 1 hour at least for church a week.No matter what PRAY about everything EVERYDAY god hears and keeps ALL his promises I don't care if people talk and I left all my negative friends and focus 100% on my family I'm not perfect but god sees all my effort and PATIENCE.I am a SALVATION ARMY SOLDIER.If you need help go back to program and actually listen with a humble heart and give it your 100% and actually want to change so god can restore you with all the new fruits of the holy spirit and take away that old lifestyle stay all the time YOU need and god will bless you just like Art said now I see my past and it seems like just a bump in the road all my years of meth use and the stay at the program so stay up it can be done!
top_reviews.author: Misael Lopez

top_reviews.text: Absolutely best thing I’ve done in my life, FOR my life! Those that have left negative reviews are not ready to surrender. Including the family ;-) We joked in the program that ARC didn’t stand for Adult Rehabilitation Center - it stands for “always ready for change”. And it’s TRUE!! I learned surrender there. Surrender to things I didn’t agree with. Guess what, I’m not in charge!! Salvation Army’s not in charge either, GOD IS. But He works through Salvation Army to teach VALUABLE life lessons. Those that get kicked out or family members that are upset - aren’t ready to learn. To submit. The ego is still large & in charge. And that’s ok. Everyone’s timing is different! I’m SO glad God used Salvation Army to get my attention before it was too late. I don’t take one day for granted. Grateful to be alive!!

top_reviews.text:
Unprofessional Management & Poor Customer Handling

I visited this store with my 3-month-old baby to source vintage items for my resale business. While shopping, I found two very vintage wicker chairs that would have been perfect for an upcoming pop-up. A store associate saw me struggling to carry them while holding my baby and kindly offered to take both chairs to the back for pickup after I finished shopping. He even helped remove the tags so I could bring them to the front when I was ready to purchase.
I went to look at dresses for no more than 10 minutes. When I returned to the front to check out, I was informed that the chairs had been sold. Another associate had already been kind enough to keep my other items at the register due to me having a baby.

When I politely asked about the chairs, the store manager began raising her voice at me, saying that items cannot be held and that the associate “wasn’t supposed to do that.” How was I supposed to know that, when it was offered by an employee? I also mentioned that I still had the tags to purchase the chairs, to which the manager responded rudely, “I sold them.”

The issue wasn’t just the chairs it was the lack of accountability, poor communication among staff, and the manager’s disrespectful and aggressive attitude toward a customer, especially one shopping with an infant. This could have been handled calmly and professionally, but it wasn’t.

top_reviews.text:
I am deeply disappointed by my experience at this location. This morning, I brought a neighbor in need to their food pantry during the advertised hours, which began at 9:30 AM. We arrived on time, but by 9:40 AM, they were still closed. I called to confirm whether they were opening. The gentleman who answered said they were running behind and would open shortly. The doors finally opened at 9:48 AM.

Upon opening, the gentleman I spoke to on the phone directed us to the area by a metal gate, saying that’s where the food giveaway takes place. When I approached the door, it had a "closed" sign taped to it, so I stood back and waited. Once the sign was removed, I followed the initial directions and tried to go inside. At this point, another man (a white man) immediately began yelling at me, saying, "YOU DON'T COME IN HERE, GET OUT! YOU WAIT OUTSIDE." His tone and behavior were completely unnecessary and demeaning.

As someone involved in community outreach through my job, I was shocked by his blatant lack of respect and abuse of authority. I told him that he had no right to treat anyone that way and to not speak to me like that. Instead of correcting his behavior, he continued yelling at me, repeating, "GET OUT OF MY WAY!" At one point, after I complied with his instructions to stand back, he came to set a table near me and yelled again, "GET OUT OF MY WAY AGAIN!" It was all so unnecessary and extremely mean.

This experience left me deeply saddened and disturbed, especially when I think about how vulnerable people might feel being treated with such cruelty in such a difficult moment. When I tried to address the issue with another staff member, she seemed more focused on making excuses for his behavior than addressing it. My neighbor and I were so taken aback by this treatment that we ended up leaving without her being able to get the food assistance she needed.

If you have the option to seek help elsewhere, I strongly recommend doing so. The staff at this location lack the respect and empathy necessary to assist those in need. Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity, especially during vulnerable moments, and this location fell far short of that standard.

top_reviews.text:
I’m disappointed by my recent experience at the Salvation Army in Huntington Beach. As someone who values supporting charitable organizations I attempted to donate nine items including small kitchen appliances (a rice cooker, cast-iron pan, food warmer, crockpot, etc.) and a pair of boots. These items were neatly organized in a clear plastic bin for easy transport. My intention was to donate the items while keeping the bin, as it was my personal property and still useful to me.

Upon placing the bin on the donation table, I explained that I wished to donate only the contents. To my surprise, the staff member insisted that I must donate the entire bin or they would not accept the items. I reiterated that the items were clearly visible through the transparent bin and could be easily inspected, they were well-maintained and required no extensive sorting. However the worker dismissed my request stating he "didn't have time" to sort the items individually.

This response left me baffled and frustrated. The Salvation Army’s core mission relies on accepting donations to fund their charitable work yet they turned away perfectly viable items over a minor procedural preference. If I had arrived without a bin and placed the same items on the table individually, would they have been refused as well? The logic escapes me and the interaction felt dismissive, unprofessional and outright laziness of the associate.

To add context, I drove to the American Cancer Society donation center nearby, (I didn’t even know they existed until I googled another place that accepted donations). The staff gratefully accepted the same items without hesitation. Their kindness stood in stark contrast to my salvation Army experience.

It’s disheartening to encounter unnecessary resistance when trying to contribute to a cause. I hope this feedback prompts a review of their donation process as turning away quality donations undermines their purpose. I cannot recommend this location for charitable donations.

top_reviews.text:
I come here a lot. It is expensive and I dislike that permanent marker is used to write the price directly on the items. A few years ago I bought a nice vintage Kitchenaid mixer from here for $50 - they let me test it and it needed new grease based on the sound. I bought some grease and fixed it up for about $75 in total.

However, when I went in a few months ago, I wanted to buy this small fan and asked if I could test it to make sure it worked. They said no and that their manager tests all items. I asked if I could bring it back if it was broken - they said it isn't broken and that there's no refunds. Lo and behold I get it back home and it's actually a heater (my bad). But it's making an awful, horrible sound that no heater should ever make and seemed like a fire hazard to me. I threw it in the trash.

Even a few years ago, items I've been looking at actually have large issues (hole in the armpit) - the person I was with wanted to purchase this jacket regardless because they are able to sew, and asked if they would lower it from $15 due to the fact it needed a significant repair. They said no.

Overall it's well sorted and has a good collection of items - it's just really expensive considering you might not even get something that works, or that there might be a hole in it that you don't notice until after purchase. Of course, no refunds.

I visited the Hollywood Salvation Army on Sunset to inquire about Homeless services. There are two buildings so I didn’t know which one to go into. Thankfully somebody from the kitchen immediately greeted me and asked if I needed help, and directed me where to go.

After checking in with their staff at the Access Point, I waited in a short line for a case worker. I went around 1pm on a Tuesday and there was only one person in front of me. While I was waiting, a gentleman in line informed me, first, that he wasn’t gay. More importantly, he let me know that they were handing out sack lunches, so I went to grab on.

The same gentleman in the kitchen from before (tall, tattoos, unfortunately I didn’t get his name) gave me a tomato & cheese sandwich because they were out of the packed lunches. The sandwich was honestly pretty good, definitely stop here if you are in emergency need of food.

After a few minutes, the case worker named Catherine came out to help me. They ran through the protocol of the steps I’d need to take to get housing through them. Ultimately they didn’t have the services I needed, which to me seems like false advertising so that’s why I gave them the 4 stars.

name: The Salvation Army Tri-Cities Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
I have been familiar with the Salvation Army's good work for many years. Though some of their beliefs can be controversial to some people, what has to be remembered is their overall goodness and continued efforts to help people who are poor, disenfranchised, down on their luck, and those having problems with substance abuse.

I first became acquainted with this location in 2008, where I received assistance with food and paying my electric bill. In addition, I was hired as a bell ringer back then, where the shift schedule was very challenging, and involved standing for many hours. But, I really enjoyed the role of "Spreader of Christmas Cheer" That job was a real life saver for me. I moved to another area for a few years, but now I'm finding myself returning to this location for continued assistance.

Lts. David and Sharron are full of energy and compassion. They love kids and have offered an amazing children's program there full of many opportunities. The social worker Lily is truly amazing! She flies around doing a million things, but takes the time out to really listen and try to help. The other staff are very friendly and helpful too!

I love the new building! It offers so many opportunities to the community: a preschool program, an exercise group, church services, music program for the kids, and many others.

You can get food as often as you need it too. They offer other resources to people in need as well.
top_reviews.author: Katherine Rubie

top_reviews.text:

They were happy to help us and take the. Items. I think they made special arrangement for us. John and Mai ( hope I spelled your name correctly forgive me if I didn’t. charge it to my head and not my heart) were awesome!

Thanks

top_reviews.text: This place does not carry junk. There are many items which are closeout merchandise from major stores that have moved on to new products. top_reviews.text: Let me first say, The food distribution is a great help! There's a few things you should know before going: Bring your ID, Bring your own bags and/or carts! You'll need about 5 bags. Sometimes you'll have to pull a number and wait to be called. They start giving numbers @830am. Walk in and pick the food items you want. They'll explain how it works. Make sure to get one of their calendars (by the door) so you know the days to come. Just be patient as things can get a bit hectic. The adults in the household can get their own seperate food items. I want to note: The staff can be rude at times which is really sad. There's a lot of elderly people that come and need assistance. If you notice someone struggling please guide them. Just because one may know the process, another may not! No need to be rude! I truly hope this helps. 🙏🏽

For the merchandise being donations the staff does a nice job of sorting out the good items for sale.

Donation area: Fast, convenient, personable, and friendly are the words to describe the nice people I dealt with in donating.  Easy experience and I am grateful that my unused items could possibly benefit someone else.

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army's Adult Rehabilitation Center (ARC) serves as a beacon of hope for individuals seeking to reclaim their lives and embark on a journey of renewal. Recognizing the multifaceted challenges faced by those struggling with addiction, homelessness, or other life-altering circumstances, the ARC offers a holistic approach to rehabilitation. Its comprehensive programs are designed not only to address the immediate needs of participants but also to foster long-term personal growth and stability.

At the heart of the ARC's mission is a commitment to restoring hope. Through a combination of counseling, life skills training, and spiritual guidance, individuals are empowered to confront their pasts and envision a brighter future. The supportive environment encourages participants to engage in self-reflection and personal development, allowing them to build resilience and confidence. Additionally, the ARC provides essential resources such as job training and educational opportunities, equipping individuals with the tools necessary to reintegrate into society successfully.

Moreover, the sense of community fostered within the ARC plays a crucial role in the rehabilitation process. Participants often form meaningful connections with peers and staff, creating a network of support that extends beyond the program. This camaraderie not only helps individuals feel less isolated in their struggles but also reinforces the idea that transformation is possible. By nurturing a sense of belonging and purpose, the ARC instills a renewed sense of self-worth in its participants, paving the way for lasting change and a hopeful outlook on life. top_reviews.text: Although, the program didn’t work out for me due to my need for dual diagnosis, I still think it’s a great program. The staff are caring and patient. There are a lot of rules with strict consequences but it’ll help provide the structure and discipline you need. The work program can be a bit overwhelming but it’ll take time to get used to. You wake up at 5am weekdays and 6am on weekends. There is 8 hour shifts/5days a week in which you receive a small gratuity. The food is wonderful and the home is beautiful, well kept and clean. You are required to sign over your EBT benefits to them but they provide plenty of good food and you’ll easily gain healthy weight in no time. Shoutout to Courtney for being so patient and kind and Sabrina as well. The Filipino woman that answers the phone is extremely judgmental and rude. She questioned whether I was “real woman” because my chest is very small. Horrible feeling and it definitely didn’t give me a great start to things at all. They provide transportation to and from work and well as lunches you pack yourself at the house. You’re not allowed to smoke at work but get plenty of free time to smoke at the house. The showers/bathrooms are awesome. Bed are comfy and blankets nice and warm. It’s two people to a room but it’s spacious with plenty of storage. Curfew is 9 and lights out at 10pm. You get coffee in the morning and at work. There are plenty of books and movies to pass the time. Most clients or “beneficiaries” are court ordered. My only hang up is that it isn’t dual diagnosis so there is no mental health services at all and that religion is forced on you from the beginning. You must dress, act, sit and follow all of the captains commands to a T or there will be consequences. If you don’t mind the religious aspect then overall it’s a wonderful program. They have aftercare resources once you graduate as well. Thank you for my time there! I was difficult without the mental health resources but still think very highly of them. They made sure I was taken care of and even provided a jacket when I left. You’ll get plenty of good clothes while you are there that you return if you don’t graduate. Tons of snacks! Only other thing is that they could possible cut down the shifts to 5 hours in order to allow for meetings and classes from more trained professionals without taking away from the limited free time after work. You will be closely monitored but lead well by your peer  mentor for the first 30 days. Captain is a bit intense kind of with expectations but is still kind and caring

top_reviews.text: Large space for a thrift shop! Just not too many interesting pieces 🙂
top_reviews.author: Grace Lin

name: Salvation Army - Sand City - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text:
This organization is such a blessing! I moved across the country, on disability and that ate me alive, financially. I have lots of health issues and have tried to work but get sick every time.

Will, Lena, Larry, John, Rick and so many others have been amazing! They helped me with food when I needed it most. They gave me other ideas of how to help myself.

I have food allergies and they are so good about making sure I get foods that won’t make me sick. They are so friendly and welcoming! Will remembered my name the second time after only meeting me once.

It’s hard to swallow your pride and ask for help, but this organization makes it as easy and welcoming as possible!
top_reviews.author: Solenne Orchid

top_reviews.text: It was the closest place to home for me while being homeless. The people there are amazing,loving kind humans that treat us with compassion and empathy. I sometimes go just to see the workers. They have laundry available for us to wash clothes, mail service and hot showers. No one ever leaves hungry. What a blessing
top_reviews.author: Gina Starling

top_reviews.text: I am so grateful to this place.  I walked in totally uncomfortable...Rick the GEM helped me..made me feel welcomed and safe.  He also gave me resources...that actually are coming through.  We need more people in this world like him.  Thank you Rick. Live long and prosper my friend.
top_reviews.author: Janet Mohr

top_reviews.text: They accept men only, call ahead but I'm mainly posting how grateful my husband and I were to receive help from them while experiencing homelessness. The thing I dislike is that you must leave the facility by 7:00AM and cannot return before 5:00PM

name: The Salvation Army Santa Cruz Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text: I recently purchased a flashlight at the store ion union in Santa Cruz, and upon return and putting in new batteries, I found that it did not work and was defective. With receipt in hand I returned it to the store and they refused to refund my money for this defective item. So beware of being cheated, as the manager, who was ( pleasant enough, unlike a fellow named Chaz, who seemed gleeful in telling me they had my money and  I would not get my money back,) confirmed it was their policy to sell defective merchandise and they did not check to see in anything was functioning. So, seniors in particular be careful about doing business here, and undoubtedly the donners would be reluctant to donate goods if they were aware they were enabling this kind of unscrupulous conduct.  It seems a shame that at retail they tarnish the name and reputation an otherwise good name of a company that apparently does attempt to do good work in hiring people in need of work.  I will  pass along this information to my political action committee so may send out a  membership alert notice of this conduct and , as well so others may avoid being taken advantage of by this firm.  A former customer.

top_reviews.text: I don't know how many other people leaving reviews are actually homeless as a homeless person I have found them to be less than helpful they have more religious propaganda than they actually have food for the homeless small bag of an semi edible food and apparel socks don't get me wrong it's better than nothing but it's not really help it's crazy how much in cash donations they get and how little they give back if you look at their website they have so many programs for feeding people in foreign countries if you're willing to deal with the religious propaganda and don't mind waiting a year or two you can get help too
top_reviews.author: Michael Littrell

top_reviews.text: So they have nothing for homeless youth I tried to get into a shelter with me and my girlfriend through them and they said because I'm not from Santa Cruz I can't stay in the shelter. I'm homeless in the Bay area including santa Cruz but they dont care instead they made me wait months for a actual reply then sent me useless information and told me to have a good day. I rate this place one star seems like they don't have real resources.
top_reviews.author: Riko Olaguer

name: The Salvation Army Santa Maria Corps

top_reviews.text:
I want to say good things, I really do that's my aim. But I have been let down so many times on this particular place. I've gone through the Salvation Army in cities like Tucson Arizona, they were so caring and it's like they will do a little extra, but here not so much.
I wanted to sign up for Thanksgiving dinner as I am out of town here in Santa Maria living in a vehicle. they could not accept me because of my emotional support dog. Just to sign up I had to be in the same line that everybody goes through for pantry assistance or utilities assistance,  But that line was so long and it wasn't moving.  2+ hours....you can't be putting people in a line when there's no bathrooms, especially if you're a senior. I had to leave I wonder how many other people had issues with that. But they do have a set up for showers and a hot meal and whatever you think you may need set up outside the facility 3 days out of the week, I did use that service not to shower but for the hot meal and a warm hat/scarf. I can't get in the shelter, for a place to lay myself and my dog down.  I can't get anybody to talk to on the phone I leave messages, many and they do not return my calls. I want to say good things but I can only be honest. I feel for those in the same boat as me, there are many coming up behind us. Many seniors are going to be displaced from their homes and not finding something they can afford because the rent is so high. so I am here to test the situation. I hope things get better here and Across the Nation for everyone in need especially the elderly. Election year is coming up I doubt much will change especially if you're not on the right political side, but I'll pray. Peace.
top_reviews.author: Diana Garza

top_reviews.text: I love to go there. I went there a lot while I was homeless, and living on the street. I felt comfortable, and safe there. The people are very friendly, and the food is so good. You eat very well there, and you can take your leftovers with you.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Treasures galore, but buyer beware!  I used to love shopping here over the years, but not anymore. You can find treasures and bargains here but many of the good things are listed online. Prices have gone up a lot, so you really have to look and be patient to find a good deal.

The staff here are nice. Clothes are organized well. I enjoy browsing through the houseware section. I have only found a few items of clothing that I really like too, but I usually don't have the patience. The Boutique side has nice clothes, purses, shoes, housewares etc, but the prices are really not thrift store prices, but rather consignment store prices.

This is why I am giving just 3 stars. I want to give more stars, but since I am comparing the store to how it was before a few years ago, today, this store has lost its charm and joy for thrifting.

Free street parking as well as a small lot on site. There is metered street parking on Olympic Blvd.

Drop off your donations in the alley, behind the store. Enter on Olympic.
top_reviews.author: eriko p

top_reviews.text: The Sally Ann on 11th has good stuff in my opinion. Five stars because I found two fabulous items. A nearly new silk oscar de la Renta oblong scarf and a wintery black and grey winter scarf (marked $5 each and what a surprise when I got to the counter and it was an additional 50% off. $5 for both pieces!). I was visiting Santa Monica for a few days over thanksgiving and strolled around to various thrift stores to "treasure hunt".  The key to finding a good treasure is to look at everything. Their stuff and store was clean and did not have that musty smell some thrift stores have.

My review is solely based on the S.O.S (rental assistance program)
I applied at the end of July 2024, I was told every month untl the month of December it should be taken care of by the following month. He even emailed my landlord it would be taken care of by the end of October. By December they just stopped returning any form of communication.
If you need help, try all other programs. This one is not properly ran and will give you the false promises of it being taken care that will result in an eviction.
The guy is nice but I think it's just too overwhelming for one person to handle and you just fall through the cracks.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Did you know that the Salvation Army is rated one of the Top charities in America? Last time I looked, they spend about $.87 per dollar on helping people, not administration.
That’s one reason I donate to and buy from the Salvation Army.
Their store on Cuyamaca in Santee is well organized, CLEAN, with a huge variety of items. The staff is friendly and helpful.
Last time I shopped there, a sale was on. It was 50% off clothes and shoes!  That made it extra fun looking at what was on sale. It was pretty crowded that day, but the staff worked hard to get everyone checked out quickly.
I found a pair of brand name tan ankle boots that looked new!  I feel good about reusing a pair of perfectly good shoes, and knowing that I’m contributing to a good cause.

top_reviews.text: This is my go to place when I need to ffind something to wear for a great price! Also who doesn’t love a good sale on top of the already low prices! Also the staff is amazing always and greet me every time!  This store is the most organized that I’ve been too!

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
In a time of economic struggles SSF Salvation Army has decided starting this week to price individual items. Some items are absolutely insane, expect $17 jeans and $50 dresses. I witnessed multiple fast fashion brands Cider, Shein, Fashionova...  items costing no more than $4 new being sold for $7+ used.

Pricing items individually puts more work on their staff who now have to price everything. After standing in a very long check out I overheard the cashier telling a customer their scanner is down so they have to type everything in individually. So management decides to implement this harsh price tactic and then ensures their employees do not have the proper equipment to keep up with the new tags??? It's disgusting behavior from South San Francisco's management team to charge their community more and not have full support of their employees.

We can see from Goodwill bins that it does not matter how expensive they want to charge. These clothes will still end up in a landfill if overpriced and SSF Salvation Army does not care. As an almost weekly regular I will only be going on their $2 clothing days moving forward. That's really the only reason to step foot in the building otherwise thanks to their crappy management team.
top_reviews.author: Rose K

top_reviews.text: The experience was overall pretty good. I could find nice clothes, it was cheaper than Goodwill, and the cashier was very sweet and patient with me. I also like how the place is very spacious, which makes it easier to maneuver and find other people if you’re shopping with others. Although my experience was good, I cannot give all 5 stars due to a few minor things. The place seemed to have no air conditioning, which made it very sweaty and it didn’t smell the greatest in a few sections. Some of the items seemed to be a bit too dirty. I know it’s a thrift store so it’s second hand, but it seemed like they didn’t wash it before selling it, which is a bit gross. There was also a few little kids running around unsupervised. Around the age of a toddler. I think the store should be just a bit stricter about leaving your kids around alone, because in general it’s just not a good thing to be doing when they’re that young. Overall, I liked my experience there, but if you could fix up just a few things it would be better.

name: The Salvation Army Ray & Joan Kroc Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
Several of family and I made good use of  the Kroc Center facilities from 2012 through 2015 when we resided in Solano county. The Kroc center opened in 2012. So we were excited to have another recreation and fitness center available other than YMCA. The center offered a Performing Arts Center, Family pool, gym, climbing wall, competition lap pool, worship center, weight room, group exercise classes and more.

I paid for the fitness shuffle classes to include the Zumba classes which was so much fun. My two nephews would be placed in the child watch section while their parents (My cousin) worked out. My daughter also worked at the child watch section. My brother also worked as a personal fitness trainer. We were members of the Kroc prior to my daughter and brother’s employment.

All the employees were always friendly, nice and helpful. We surely enjoyed our time here. We have a lot of great memories.
top_reviews.author: Aileen M Cruz

top_reviews.text: I attended a Fairfield Suisun Rotary Lunch at this location. Was impressed at how big and nice this space is. I came in today to return them since it was an employee error however they wouldn’t take them back. I would’ve even accepted store credit but the manager refused and told me it was my responsibility to check my items and make sure everything is correct. While I understand somewhat I know what I gave the cashier to buy, and therefore didn’t think I needed to double check everything just in case she charged me for men’s jeans. It was clearly her mistake. The manager I spoke to wasn’t very kind about it and took no responsibility on their part. I shop at thrift stores for a reason and don’t appreciate being charged for items I don’t want and will never use. top_reviews.text:
I debated posting this but it's been weighing on me. I was recently homeless in watsonville. So I would like to think I have a fair opinion. I have been to multiple salvation armies but this Watsonville one is the worst because of the front desk lady. I don't remember her name but I have added  a picture. She usually has red lipstick on. She has made being hungry/in need  the worst experience of my life. She is unnecessary rude to almost everyone but especially to homeless people. Now in the day of technology people want proof for something to be true and I thought many to secretly record my interactions with her however I never did for fear of retaliation. But trust me when I say she is one of the meanest.
First of all salvation army offers dinner every week day at 5pm and take home dinner at 5pm every weekend that being said people need to eat more than once a day. They have food they "offer" in the day. It's right through the front door on a little side table. Managing to persuade her to let you in is another thing. I and many other have tried to utilize this but are met with judgement and hostility. I would knock multiple times and finally she would stick her head of our the crack of the door and say things along the lines of "what do you want!????" "What do you NEED?" The answer is food. If you manage to plead your case with her she'll let you in and your allowed to choose 2 things of the table while she watches closely with her hawk eyes. Mostly everything is expired, perishable iteams, and things that need to be heated like take and bake bread, frozen Mac and cheese. I do not have a microwave so many time I ate frozen Mac and cheese. They don't put these items in there weekly food bank distribution days so I don't know why this lady is so protective over this table. It just gets thrown away at the end of the day/week.
I would like to think that the people would decide to work here, work here because theyre nice and generous people who like to help but this lady must hate her job. Her attitude, actions and words make you feel like you're the worst person in the world. How does she work here?!
This is a story I witnessed and have the permission to speak about but someone I regularly ate with at dinner there went to the salvation army during food bank distribution day( which is intended for families not homeless people) she was wanting milk but there was none of the little table when you walk in. To avoid having to deal with the front desk lady she decide to go through the side(where people are leaving with their groceries) she decided to ask one of the nice worker if they had milk to spare and he told her sorry no and she left. Simple. When she walked out the lady at the front was visibly freaking out that she couldn't leave her post and have no control of the situation to yell at the lady. Instead of saying "please don't do that " instead this lady was being passive aggressive. She was pointing at the lady (like an upset child) telling her staff to get a good look at the lady that had just done this. She would t stop staring and pointing and making rude comments like we were in elementary school. I couldn't believe it! Later that day that lady didn't show up for dinner.She thought she would get rejected dinner and didn't want the humiliation. I know I and so many other have wanted and needed the help but haven't gotten it because of this lady. Recently my daughter was needing groceries but didn't go, remembering all the accounts people have had with this lady. When hungry people and women with children don't want to get help you know it's a problem.
If you have made it this far thank you for listening There is so much more to tell. And I hope my review is taken seriously and this lady is fired!

I donated for years to Salvation Army but now I don't see a reason why. Too bad it's really going to hurt the public losing a concerned person for someone with a large family, who needs help,
I'll try other places other religious institutions but never them. I even still put money in their kettles but I'll never physically go there again. I saw they reallly did not care.

top_reviews.author: Brian Williams

top_reviews.text:
Pretty excellent selection at this thrift store. Every time my wife and I go in, we find something (or multiple somethings) stylish. It feels good buy used and cast off clothing. But honestly, the stuff we buy might as well be new..

One critique about the store would be the lack of dressing room. I find myself switching into my boxers in the middle of an aisle to try on pants. Or (as a guy) taking off my shirt surreptitiously in the corner. I understand that there may be higher intentances of crime at thrift stores? I guess just expect to see my bear chest occasionally.
top_reviews.author: Jeffrey Klassen

top_reviews.text:
It can be great for treasure hunting. Yesterday, picked up like-new Hunter boots ($17) and tee (half off, $1.50).

But they have spent their last year becoming less customer-friendly. They redid their pricing; which was previously by type and now by item. The tags talk about returns, but the store is final sale. And yesterday in the middle of the afternoon they decided to close their fitting rooms forever. Their restroom is also closed.

Arc Thrift continues to reign supreme in CO.
top_reviews.author: A. Jinnie McManus

top_reviews.text: If y'all don't like it go somewhere else. Quit crying about the prices. And quit giving them your trash. The donations lady, Michelle and Mike. Are good people. The manager named Sam was also good people. I give y'all one star, because of the boy named Shane.

top_reviews.text: I go to the Food Bank on Tuesdays when I can, but I was recently given resources for assistance and I am truly blessed to have been helped by this organization. Thank you many times over to Danise and the rest of the staff at The Salvation Army!

top_reviews.text: I love this church and I love this organization! They have so much heart and do so much for the community! Down to earth people with authentic Bible preaching and teaching. They also have a food bank and a lot of outreach services to help people in the community. I love it here!!

Academy were rude, never interacted with anyone, didn't ring the bell..they just continuously had their faces buried in their phones. 5 stars for what the Salvation Army does in general but

0 stars for the bell ringers who don't do what they are supposed to do

top_reviews.text: Great thrift store. Occasionally some items will be a bit overpriced, but most of the time there are great finds. Staff are amazing, overall one of the best thrift stores in the springs.

name: The Salvation Army Family Hope Center

top_reviews.text: I was in a very bad situation with my 1year old we were homeless and these people helped me out very much, yes they have certain rules just like every place you can get help at. All the staff were so great with me and my baby I didn't even feel like we were in a shelter we felt like we were home here. I think they are a great place to be in a bad situation, they are not there to babysit you or your children they are there for you to have a warm safe place to lay your head while YOU get your life back on track. That's it not to do your responsibility for you. This is a great place to start.
top_reviews.author: Sharon Ceme

top_reviews.text:
Lisa is sadly very disappointing as someone who works at a family hope center . Very rude & not resourceful at all. My family and I called hoping for some answers and this lady hung up on us in the middle of a question, getting irritated because we aren’t familiar with the shelter.
some fields of work aren’t for everybody.
God bless all the families trying to get out of any situations they may be in & keep pushing! There will be people who don’t understand and don’t care but that doesn’t stop the grit & heart.

top_reviews.text:
From the moment I walked in Infelt relief. I was greeted and shown back where I met Jessica who was more than kind. I felt awful about having to come in and ask for help with our power being shut off, but she made that go away within seconds.
I filled out the paperwork and was given a very reasonable timeframe to hear back. After I was done there, she shiwed me back to the pantry where I got more groceries than we can afford at the store! We had to run some errands and bu the time we were home our power was back on!

Thank you from the bottom of our Hearts! It's an amazing service you guys provide there.

Blessings to you all!

top_reviews.text: Great place to volunteer and give to your community! We have a potluck on the second Sunday of the month after Service which is at 11am. The Fort Carson Kid's Closet and Operation Deploy Your Dress are also located in the building, and conference room and fellowship hall reservations are available too.
top_reviews.author: Gema Rivera

top_reviews.text: I love the volunteers here. I love the staff here and I love their mission. I never feel judged. I never feel as if I'm putting them out. They are always so kind and so helpful. And so funny, a lot of my favorite conversations come from some of the older gentlemen there. My family and I appreciate you guys more than you'll know!!
top_reviews.author: Taylor Rollins

top_reviews.text: I love this thrift shop. Best one in town. I almost always find clothes in my size and plenty of books for me and my kids. I always find things for everyone in my family. name: The Salvation Army Denver Red Shield

top_reviews.text:
I want to take a moment to recognize Doretta Tootle, the Social Service Coordinator at the Salvation Army Denver Red Shield Community Center. She has gone above and beyond for me in more ways than one. From the very first time we spoke, she made me feel heard, respected, and supported.

Doretta is not only professional but also compassionate, patient, and dedicated to truly helping people. She doesn’t just point you in the right direction—she walks alongside you to make sure you have the tools, resources, and encouragement you need to move forward. Her kindness, knowledge, and genuine care make a huge difference in the community and in the lives of everyone she serves.

I am deeply grateful for everything Doretta has done for me. The Red Shield Center is blessed to have her, and I can honestly say she has been a light in my life when I needed it most
top_reviews.author: TONYA TYLER

top_reviews.text: My son absolutely loved summer Camp. Ms. Ashley who runs the program was communicating very well, made accommodations for my son for his tutor to come in and work with him, and was very understanding. She helps the younger kids to express themselves to her when something happens. Ms. Ashley is very wonderful, and I love how she supports the families in any kind of way possible. She’s very positive and adores  kids very much and to make sure no kid is left behind in anything do inside of camp such as activities, prizes, and field trips they go on, and etc. She’s super passionate about the children and goes above and beyond for her families.
top_reviews.author: Marie Taylor

top_reviews.text: The Salvation Army camp was incredible. They got to know my daughter over the weeks she was with them, and they were so attentive to her needs. She was happy to go to camp every day, and when I picked her up, she didn’t want to leave. They have friendly staff and engaging activities for the kids. I loved that at the end of camp, each kid received a certificate for being an outstanding camper in some form or fashion, highlighting that each kid had something to bring to the table. I was very blessed as a mother to know my daughter was in such good hands.
top_reviews.author: Kelsey Staudacher

top_reviews.text:
Got a bed upstairs once.

Priority entry for people that get paid beds when the place opens. Then after all the paid customers go in, all the “do-nothing”losers get to enter afterwords.

If you pay a little extra, you get a paid room upstairs. The perks of having this room instead of a bed in the main area, is that you get to come and go when you ever you please, Instead of having to wait until shelter hours. Great place if you have money and a job and you actually do something with your time. If you don’t work, you are pretty much out on your rear.
top_reviews.author: Arminius of Germania

top_reviews.text: I live there. The staff tries to do the most, but I don't feel they care that much. I feel that this is due to the fact that most of my fellow residents show an incredible disrespect for everything that is provided for us free of charge.

top_reviews.text: Amazing place to work, the case managers and program manager are wonderful to work with. I connect very well with the guys because they remind me of a homeless brother I have and how I would want someone to treat him..

My family is greatful to be surrounded by such wonderful people and everyone is so welcoming. name: The Salvation Army Intermountain Divisional Headquarters

top_reviews.text:
The rude manager of the Boulder Salvation Army store closed the store 15 minutes early -- and then she ordered me out of the store because she said always closes the store early.  I rushed over there after work to buy a dog bowl.  Before I went there, I checked the store's website which says the store is open until 6:00 pm.  The sign on the front door also states that the store is open until 6:00 pm.  When I was in the store, the time on the clock in the store was 5:50, which I pointed out to her.  As I was leaving, I said to her that if she's going to close early, the website and the sign should indicate the true closing time so people don't find themselves turned away.

When I suggested this to her, she started yelling at me to get out of the store. When I tried to interject a few words, she began screaming at me to get out of the store. I stood there dumbfounded. She yelled about 20 times for me to GET OUT OF THE STORE, as I was already headed toward the door. The store's clock read exactly 5:50 pm (10 minutes before the stated closing time) when I left.  I'm reluctant to go in there again.

This lady shouldn't be managing anything. She doesn't know how to listen or how to treat customers. A very rude person who should be replaced. 🤨
top_reviews.author: FrankCoffman “Frank”

top_reviews.text:
Extremely poor signage in their parking lot, one small sign saying visitor parking & 2 hour limit. Apparently the rest of it implies it is restricted and only for the Salvation Army located here, which is not shown anywhere.
$300 to get your car back after they have called their towing company on you.
I am already struggling and they did not need that space as it was after hours. It's great that  they are so kind to others & went out of their way to call and have us towed.

10-22-24
