top_reviews.text: It’s very clear why this place has 1 star reviews and they don’t even deserve that. It is 12/12/2024 and I just had a 10min conversation with the grinch or the social services director crystal who was extremely snarky, cruel and judgmental. I called asking for help for hotel voucher after being almost killed by my husband, physically attacked by a customer on my job and dealing with the very recent death of my father. crystal made it clear that she was not going to help although they had the funds to do so. crystal heard me say that I was from a different state and quickly interrupted me to offer money to go back. I never asked her to go home. My dog and I are in a hotel  and they have hotel funding but not one emotion of empathy. I felt more compassion from her receptionist than her. Then she accused me of receiving help when I am an identical twin and names could’ve easily been incorrectly input because humans do error and especially with identical twins who have rhyming names. This was the most cruel conversation especially being in a compromised situation. People are donating hard earned money to help those less fortunate and they pick and choose who deserves help and who doesn’t.

top_reviews.text: If I could give it less than one star I would, since it is sad that according to organizations that are there to help those who need it in critical moments, not only can they not do so, but also the treatment over the phone is awful, apparently the only lady who speaks Spanish is super pedantic, not at all empathetic and rude with a hostile and annoying tone of voice in customer service, apart from the fact that now there is xenophobia among those who they can help, depending on your nationality. In short, simply sad for the sponsors and people who donate their money thinking that projects like this are really dedicated to helping people in need in society, I hope that no one else goes through the bad experience that I went through with this lady on the phone.

top_reviews.text: Who is pricing these items at this thrift store? Why are there items behind the register that aren’t for sale? I realize some items are collectible and some items resellers will sell but isn’t the point of Salvation Army to take “ donated “ items to sell to make money for their causes? How do they keep a high turnover rate  when they keep pricing things higher than retail? It sounds more like greed now than actually helping those in need. They are getting on the bandwagon with the other thrift stores and pricing things higher. Do they realize that some people shop at thrift stores because they can’t afford retail? I think they are keeping some of the more expensive items and not putting donations on the floor for sale.

top_reviews.text: This business has this ILLEGAL sign up. Service animals are protected under the ADA, and there’s NO SUCH THING AS A SERVICE ANIMAL CARD. You are violating FEDERAL AND COLORADO LAW.

top_reviews.text: Illegally asking for a “registered service animal card”, which does not exist and is a direct violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act. top_reviews.text: Do not bother to donate to this store.  I brought a dining room table to them and they would not accept it because it was not assembled. top_reviews.text:
The workers there are kind and helpful but please be cautious if you are calling to get any info on donations as it just directs you to a call center. I had called ahead to see if this specific location takes mattress donations (as some specific locations do take them) since we just bought a brand new one that didn't work out for us. Someone from the call center answered and I stressed to them we have to be certain they take them at this location as we had to rent a truck to bring the mattress. The lady from the call center reassured me multiple times the Dayville location took them, so we went through with renting a truck and bringing the mattress. When we got to the store however the manager let us know they did NOT take mattresses and apologized for our time and money being wasted and tried to help us out however they could. They also explained their in-store phone isn't connected or working so they cannot take the calls themselves. You are much better off going to the store first and asking the employees directly as it seems the people from the call center don't care to give you the right information per location.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
See the first few pictures? Almost all of that is beautiful, barely used real wood an/or upholstered furniture. I have donated such things 15 to 20 times over the last decade, without issue.

The guy rejected almost everything, citing that they "didn't have enough room."

Total BS. Your employee *didn't want to do his job.* See the pics of the store's floor space - PLENTY of room, and I would have  gladly done all the labor to get it into the store.  I literally move people's stuff for a living.

"Try Savers down the street," he said at one point, which is the monent I truly knew he was lying and didn't want to do his job. Savers is a FOR PROFIT thrift store that hardly even takes furniture anymore and requires a call ahead to even donate.

The pics don't lie. Given the amount of business I do, rest assured The Salvation Army will lose thousands of dollars in (often valuable) furniture donations. From now on I'm going to the ReStore in Cromwell. What a joke.

POST-RESPONSE EDIT 6/14/25:

😂😂😂.

Now I genuinely hope the Salvation Army goes bankrupt.

I literally provided photographic evidence of how gorgeous, pristine, and well constructed the furniture was, and that the store clearly had the floorspace for it.

And in response you insinuate that these donations could be... costly to the organization?

Hello?! YOU'RE A NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION WITH ZERO COST OF GOODS SOLD! What an absolutely ridiculous gaslight of a response.🤦

Thank you Salvation Army for, shall we say, "righteously affirming" my decision to take my beautiful furniture donations elsewhere going forward. Thoughts and prayers! 🙏🙄

top_reviews.text: My Salvation Army - At-Home Donation Pickup was, unfortunately, an absolute joke and I'm absolutely livid with the experience that I had yesterday, Tuesday, June 30, 2020 the entirety of all that transpired was undeniably a nightmare! I scheduled a donation pick up 3 weeks ago and was all set to go for the donation pickup, but my plans didn't go as I had presumed they would. I had an inkling, however, that something was off when I called customer service in the morning to inquire about the timeframe for my pickup - collectively I was given 2 different timeframes (8 am-11 am then that turned into 1 pm-4 pm) all-in-all the driver came past the timeframe given which was, 4:30 pm - this is not only very unprofessional but, very disappointing in seeing that no one at the establishment including the driver had regard for both, my mother and I with our schedule, etc. and thought that it would be okay for myself and/or anyone else for that matter to sit around and wait all day for them at their convenience to decide to come as if he the driver and/or the donation center are doing you/me a favor SMH when in reality I'm doing them all a favor by donating and donating quality, name brand, perfect condition, clean items! I spoke with customer service, dispatch and the manager, Robert multiple times throughout the day to enable a smooth process and AGAIN collectively I got the run around; I waited in my high-rise lobby for over an hour after Robert informed me that the driver was on his way and should be arriving shortly (shortly meant 1+ hr. I guess) and then to top it off when the driver did show up he not only flew by my building for which I had to leave my items behind and run down the block to catch up with the driver to stop him, he then proceeded to catch an attitude because 'he wasn't paying attention to me flagging him down' and would have to turn around to drive around the block to get back down the block to the front entrance of my building to retrieve the items - he even had the audacity to ask/think that I was going to carry 4 bags and a mirrored cabinet to him down the block where he was parked, especially after waiting hours throughout the day on him...Pure ridiculousness!! The driver never once took into account that I myself, alone had to lug all the items from my apt. down the hallway to the main front elevators and then load the items into the lobby and then outside near the entrance. The driver had no paperwork in-hand for my donation and refused to provide me with a receipt for items which made no sense to me at all; when inquiring what will be done to navigate me getting a receipt the driver stated, "I don't have the paperwork so, that's that", I then proceeded to ask that he call his manager, Robert because I was over it at this point after waiting all day, the inconvenience(s) caused, the runaround I got on the phone, the head games played throughout the day, and now not getting the necessary papers I needed - I wasn't at all in the position to not only argue with this man, but I too was NOT going to provide anything...A receipt was needed and the paperwork for tax purposes for the donation, he again refused my request rudely. I immediately called customer service and Robert directly and got no answer, how convenient. The whole experience was a complete waste of my time; I was honestly better off throwing the items away in the dumpster - you would think you're doing a good thing and doing your part to help aid those in need, etc. and yet, ignorant, unprofessional people like the employees at Salvation Army spoil it by NOT DOING THEIR DUE DILIGENCE AND/OR THEIR JOB FOR WHICH THEY'RE GETTING PAID TO DO?! I truly believe that I will NEVER again reach out to Salvation Army, this establishment that handles the donations is horrible, very unprofessional and it's clear that they could care less about quality customer service and/or people in actual need!!!! I am very inclined to call the Better Business Bureau because this is unacceptable!!!

top_reviews.text: This is one of the worst shelters in the state of Delaware.  Their supposed counselors are allowed to holler at, and belittle the homeless population that stays there in front of their children.  My daughter's and I resided at the Salvation Army for a very short time.  When my daughter's and I arrived at the Salvation Army, the counselor that was assigned to our case was out for a few days.  The Salvation Army by law is required to complete all intake paperwork within the first few days that the resident arrives at the shelter.  That wasn't done. (The counselor I'm speaking of is black with dreads).  When the counselor arrived she wanted me to falsify paperwork, and sign the paperwork with a date other than the date that my family and I arrived there.  She also left a note for me at the front desk stating that she needed to speak with me the following day, so that I could sign the falsified paperwork, and complete my families intake.  She left her phone number on the note, I called her back and left her a very respectful voicemail stating that I could not meet with her at the time she requested (with absolutely no notice) because my daughters transportation was not set up yet, and I needed to take my daughter to school on the bus.  When she arrived to work on that day, she knocked on the room door and I opened it.  She was one of the most nasty, rude, ghetto, unprofessional people I had ever met in my life.  She felt like her meeting was more important than my daughter's education.  I told her that she gave me the meeting time with absolutely no notice, and my daughter's education came first.  I told her that I did not like how she was speaking to me in front of my children (who barely got any sleep that night because it was freezing inside of the room, we all had to sleep with our coats on under the blankets).  She then stated that, "nobody asked me to come there, and if I didn't like it I could leave".  I reported her conduct immediately to the supposed director (who was of African descent, which was evident from her pronunciation of certain words).  The director did absolutely nothing!  As I was in the office the maintenance man came into the directors office and said that the people in the office were complaining that it was too hot in the building, so he turned the heat down.  In the office!  They went home every night!  So because they complained we froze every night! By this time both of my daughter's and I had developed bad colds from how cold the room was every night.  The Salvation Army has a policy that all residents have to leave between 12-4.  I called downstairs, I told them that were all sick, I didn't have the strength to be outside from 10 to 4 with two sick children.  They said I still had to leave, they told me to take my children to the hospital. This was the first time in life that I was so sick that I needed a prescribed cough medicine.  All because of this shelter!  That was the last day we stayed there.  I took my children back to the motel, I had to struggle to pay for it daily, but at least my daughters had heat.  My daughter's both were sick for an entire week!   I reported the Salvation Army to license and inspection for the heat, and I also reported them to the Carvel State building housing discrimination office for Discrimination because of how they allowed their counselor to speak to me in front of my children.  She should be fired!  She should not be working in that environment!  If there are any other people who stayed there, and were treated the same way by this counselor or any counselor there, please report them to the housing discrimination office at the Carvel State service building.  There is strength in numbers, if more people report the way the Salvation Army is allowing their counselors to abuse people, they will be held accountable for their actions, and to the people that work in the office at the Salvation Army, remember that every time you complain, your causing a child to freeze at night until the point where their sick!  How absolutely selfish!

top_reviews.text:
Cultish, egotistical, and shortsighted. I spent a little time here. When I showed up I was broken to say the least. Addicted to drugs, homeless and hopeless. Within an hour I was doing "work therapy" processing donations. Throughout my brief stay none of my core issues were addressed. Mostly what I heard was that if I just believed in Jesus all would be well. Most brought into this. But for a hardened addict like myself this" cure" was way too simplistic. Especially, after noticing that the warehouse manager who was supposedly clean for seven years behaved like he was smoking crack in his office, the counselor smelled like alcohol, and the intake supervisor who was very sweet and Christian like in the beginning, started behaving like an egotistical wench. I picked up on these things rather quickly. So when a plan was hatched for me to be unceremoniously discharged I was prepared. Brand new building with room for eighty men only eight were present. Guess why? Because God doesn't like ugly. And you can dress up a trash can, but it still is a trash can. Some have transformed their lives here. Sure. But the bottom line is making money. You no make no money you no stay.
Very Christian like you ask me.
What would Jesus do?
Only the most empty are wanted here. They like to fill your cup for you.
Do yourself a favor and find a real rehab whose agenda is recovery and not a lot of theological mumbo jumbo. I wish I could given them a half a star. Ijs.

THE TRUTH In the comments, I've noticed a lot of incorrect information.  First management does not make the policy or poceedures. The .99 sales were not decided by management.  As well as turning anyone away for clothes, the gentleman was told to go to 4th and orange, which is a 10-15 min walk away where he would receive a voucher for clothes and his needs. Now the special needs employee DOES NOT HAVE SPECIAL NEEDS NOR DOES HE LIKE BEING REFERRED TO IN THAT WAY. Never was he ever treated badly, and any comment to say otherwise is plain out made up. Not to mention, the same person who was accused in a comment was a contact with his family and counselor. Also, she bought him shirts and comics, etc. Also, employees have set break times and do not have to ask permission. The same goes for using the bathroom or break time. The only people who have to announce leaving  the floor are cashiers ( for obvious reasons).  Prices have went up but thats everywhere, cloths are donated but unfortunately electric, water, toilet paper, building space, employees, hangers  fixtures, cleaning supplies, trash bags and trash pick up, receipt paper, credit card services, internet to run it so credit cards can be used, etc
ARE NOT.  The comment that said the manager isn't too bright was not very bright bc it's not the managers decision, neither of them. TO BE FAIR, NOT EVERYONE IS GOING FEEL OR AGREE WITH EVERYTHING THATS CHANGED OR DECIDED WHEN IT COMES POLICY OR POCEEDURES HOWEVER, WHAT MOST WILL AGREE ON IS TO MAINTAIN A JOB AND TAKE CARE OF OUR FAMILIES AS EMPLOYEES WE MUST FOLLOW POCILIES AND PROCEDURES  NO MATTER WHAT. This place is hot mess. Yellow signs everywhere like it's a going out of business sale. Prices inflated just to see a permanent white sign saying half off sale for any white priced item over $1. Worst part was today coming into the store there is a yellow sign stating in bold black that all clothing inside and out are half priced. When I checked out with a child's dress I was told that it was a white sign item and the door sign stated all sales marked final were not included (the children's clothing are marked with a white final sign). It's $1.50 difference, it's not a deal, BUT the door sign doesn't state "women's clothes" for clarification AND when I brought it up as constructive feedback I was pushed back on.

Peach of a gal, Myra, insisted "that's what the sign says" but also verbally chastised another lady and told her "you all need to be reading the signs." How are we supposed to read what's not there? And why would you have a sign on the front door for women's clothing and not at the women's clothing racks like you did for men's, and children's clothing racks? It's a confusing set up and frankly a horrible staff experience.

I told Myra I was letting her know that the sign needs clarification since she's clearly annoyed by it, and annoyed at several customers about it (one before I walked up, myself, and other customer when I returned after purchase), and she just got more annoyed I was pointing out she gave false information and anything needed to be different.

top_reviews.text:
I came to this location after being referred here for assistance. Instead of being treated with compassion, I was approached by the director, Paul, who immediately profiled me, told me to leave, and even threatened to call the police on me. I was simply standing outside on the phone after speaking with staff, and there was no reason for this type of treatment.

For an organization that claims to serve the community, this behavior was unprofessional, discriminatory, and completely unacceptable. As a Black woman seeking support in a vulnerable situation, being treated like a problem instead of a person was both hurtful and unsafe.

If Salvation Army truly cares about helping families in crisis, their staff should be trained in respect, cultural sensitivity, and trauma-informed care. Turning people away and escalating with threats does the opposite of what this organization says it stands for.

top_reviews.text: Most of these good reviews are written by people who work there. Went there for help after I lost my job. Needed help with feeding my kids at that time. Right off the back , I was turned away. This was back when they did help people who needed food. I guess not all people.  I went to RCS and they were more grateful to help a mother who had just lost her job who needed food for her children. i signed up with RCS with no problems , and nobody turned me away. They also recommended that I could get help from christ the king or it's our christ the king. Which is BETTER than SALVATION ARMY SOCIAL SERVICE. there's also another place people can go for help for food if they ever need it.It's called St. Joseph's. It's somewhere on Belcher it's a church don't need nothing. All you need to bring is one small handbag to put the food inside, like the ones you get at Publix, not the plastic bag that you get when you check out. Medium bags that you buy. They don't accept huge big bags anymore, ok but they will help with just fruit, vegetables, bread and snacks. No meat. But It's still something. I got fresh carrots from the ground there. I got fresh potatoes, salary, onions. and cabbage so I made my family cabbage soup yesterday. And they are open Mondays from 5:30pm to 6:30pm and Friday's from 11:00am to 12:00pm . Just get there early. It will be a line and they're only open for an hour. If you want some meat , go to Our Christ the King its Somewhere close to indian rocks , but it says largo fl. Just make sure you have gas in your car. And they open Saterday from 1:00pm to 3:30pm. I would say that Because they close right on the dot at 4:00pm. And they Don't accept people after that. And there is a long line. You get a ticket and then you go inside , sit down and wait. All you need is your I.d that's it. You can go Monday's from 12:00pm to 3:00 pm just get there before 3pm. Salvation Army will turn you down. But the church , if you could get out there will accept you. I hope this will help somebody who needs help feeding their kids or just themself. Also I forgot to say you can get there early at our Christ.The king. Because there is a lot of people that go there and a lot of people wait from 7am to open at 1pm. If you go early and wait in line you get the good stuff right off the back it's first come first pick. If you go later like  after 1:00 pm you get what you get and you don't throw a fit. I recommend that you clear your schedule on Saturday. It's that if you choose to go to Our christ the King. Get there really , really , really Early and wait. I would bring a chair to sit down and have a lot of patience ok.

top_reviews.text:
Buyer Beware!!
When it comes to area thrift stores, overall I'm usually pretty pleased with the quality and items  available whenever I've shopped at The Salvation Army in Clearwater, Florida. Because of their strict "No refund" policy, I make sure I look over the items well prior to purchasing. My last couple trips I found some items but it wasn't until after bringing them home when I found large holes caused by the associates who are attaching the price tags. The first shirt someone used a stapler and the second tag was attached with a plastic tab. The issue is they were not attached to a tag or in a seam, the tags were attached right on the front of the shirts. Both the tag placements caused damage and noticeable holes. When I tried to return for maybe an exchange, I was told no, and placing the blame on the St. Petersburg location, saying they are who attaches all the price tags.
Granted, these items aren't overly expensive, but my time is, and taking time to find and select items only to come home to find damaging holes where one of your associates place a price tag is really infuriating! Please be mindful when attaching the price tags, chose the seams or maybe the back tags to avoid damaging the clothing. Disappointed!

Back in early 2024 I had nowhere to go and sleep except the front seat of my car... so TASK FORCE was given to me by Barbara V. - a horrible experience I had. I was still living with miss Nawal A. at the time ... she & her family chose to EVICT ME WITH NO MONIES OWED after 26 months living there with an 86% rent increase over 14 months tying me to HER RESIDENCE. Not an experience I ever would wish upon another. So ... I went and stood inline for several hours with people also having nowhere to sleep under a roof out in the hot sun. Finally I was given a "Golden Ticket" to arrive by 8:30pm at the side door to sleep on Army Cots with men & women. We all had to leave by 5 am. It was a Patio with plastic windows built long ago with Gov't Funds that was very cold with 38 army cots. Does not appear the monies were appropriated properly. DISCRIMINATION is what actualy happened. I have NO ADDICTIONS or Medical issues that they are aware of except my documented DIABETES TYPE II - I Simply wish to share how this REALLY works - and the Travesty of reaching out to Mayor Nan Rich on several occasions with NO REPLY!!!
And they encourage & welcome you losing all your belongings you have in storage that make you a HUMAN BEING because "that happens to everyone" - the food is not compatible for a VEGETARIAN OR A VEGAN or the individuals staying there that have CANCER and other Chronic Illnesses - released from the hospital... just the cold facts. top_reviews.text:
Honestly, I didn’t want to give this location a one-star review, but my experience—both over the phone and in person—was very disappointing. My family and I scheduled a furniture pickup to donate several pieces that had been in our home for less than a year. These were items my parents had carefully remodeled and painted by hand, but we no longer needed them.

The scheduling process was difficult from the start. They offered only one or two pickup date options, each with a broad 9 AM–5 PM time frame, which made it nearly impossible to coordinate around our full-time work schedules. There was no effort to accommodate our availability, which was frustrating.

About a week before the scheduled pickup, I received a call to reschedule—even though we had booked the appointment over two weeks earlier. That was disappointing, but we tried to be understanding and chose another date.

When the helpers finally arrived, the experience was even more discouraging. They looked over the furniture with little communication and ultimately rejected the items, claiming they had scratches and didn’t meet Salvation Army standards. This was disheartening, especially after waiting so long and preparing pieces that were in excellent condition and made with care.

Additionally, the customer service was poor. The team called only five minutes before arriving, leaving me little time to prepare, even though I had arranged my morning around their visit before heading to work. When I explained that I needed to leave soon, they were unkind and unaccommodating, expressing frustration instead of understanding.

Overall, the experience was frustrating—from scheduling to communication to the pickup itself. It’s unfortunate because I truly support the Salvation Army’s mission, but due to the lack of professionalism and empathy from this location, I won’t be donating here again. I hope this feedback helps them improve their customer service and better support donors in the future.

I’m very disappointed with my experience today. The prices have already gone up significantly, but what truly upset me was how I was treated by an employee.

Without any greeting — no “hello” or acknowledgment — she walked up to me and said, “The wheels need to be put up and they need to be with you.” Talking about my children and my son’s Heely shoes. I was simply browsing the book section while my children were within my eyesight looking at the toys. I am always attentive I make sure they return items where they found them, I purchase what they want, and I keep them close by.

A simple, polite approach such as, “Hi! Just a reminder of our store policy — thanks for understanding,” would have been completely fine. I would have gladly complied and continued shopping. Instead, I felt spoken to like I was a problem.

Because of this interaction, I chose to leave. I have donated thousands of dollars worth of items to this store over time, and after today, I will no longer be donating or shopping here. Kindness and basic customer service go a long way, especially in a retail environment where customers spend their hard-earned money — particularly when much of the inventory has been donated for free.

I hope management considers additional customer service training. This experience was highly disappointing, and I will be reaching out to someone higher up to share my concerns.

name: The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center - Jacksonville

top_reviews.text:
It's a great place to get yourself together and work on recovery. It is not for everyone; you *will* have to volunteer for the Salvation Army, which is very good for a person and also is a good way of saying thanks for the help and for not having to pay rent. It is not for people with extreme mental illness, as they do not have medical staff on hand. It is a Christian program and you will have to attend chapel, though you do not have to be a Christian. There are many rules you will have to follow, that you probably won't like.

The ARC staff deal with many colorful characters every day and can not always stop to give 5-star, personalized "customer service." Some people on here and elsewhere seem to be complaining due to simply not understanding the purpose of a rehabilitation facility. I graduate the program in 2 weeks, and highly recommended it to anyone who is looking for sobriety and a fresh start. I can only express gratitude that there is an organization wanting to help people that our society has largely cast out.
top_reviews.author: Juan Lopez

top_reviews.text: I graduated from the Salvation Army Jax ARC in August of 2022. The only way that a person could not be set on a path to recovery, after this group gives you the tools and resources to recover, is you don't want to recover. I mean my God, they give you room and food, the clothes on your back, recreation, free to roam after 30 days and entertainment. The main thing they give you is a Jesus centered Church, Celebrate Recovery, AA and other Jesus centered resources, and they pay you a little stipend for that! ARC will find you a job and a place to live if you need it. And they have great counselors and they provide health care! You can even have your stay extended if you follow the rules. But if you use after admission you are asked to leave. If you want to get clean this is where a man ought to be.
top_reviews.author: Tim Bennett

top_reviews.text: Salvation army in Jacksonville is awesome! As recovering addicts we have a many complaints ,but no solution.Mr.Stewart is a very Godly and helpful individual.Im going back now ,and gonna shut up ,and get my blessings .I'm grateful for Salvation army
top_reviews.author: Jeffrey Calhoun

top_reviews.text:
People keep telling us to use the Salvation Army as an address to have our mail sent, since we are unable to afford to live in an apartment or a home.   I wondered how this works, I tried to use the website but its not working.

They told us they would keep our dogs for us, while we are displaced from our homes.

They were so kind to host a come as you are church services for our extended family members.

They housed our pitbull dogs out back in the fenced off area, while we slept on internment camp style bunk beds, similar to that of USA military bootcamp.

They had a fema coffin at our disposal, one of our sisters and her baby, slept in the coffin, as a bed to sleep in.   We were trying to see if cameras were hidden in the fire detectors, and bulbs, if they were recording us.

I did notice a very young woman, doing work, the manager of the facility said she was married to the pastor of the salvation army.  They told us to call her first lady, so we did call her first lady.

We were so so so  greatful, to have a place to stay, during our displacement.  There were 26 of us, and 8 children, 3 expecting mothers, and we had a place to stay.  They are still helping us with our after needs and letting us get mail here.
top_reviews.author: Star Dream List

I am writing to express my deepest gratitude to Ellie’s Army for their incredible support during a time of desperate need. When every other door was closed and every other organization said no, Ellie’s Army said yes. Their unwavering support saved my family from the brink of homelessness.

We are a family of 5, including four small children, one of whom has cystic fibrosis. The stress and fear of not knowing where we would live were overwhelming. We were just days away from losing our home when Ellie’s Army stepped in. Their compassion and generosity provided us with the assistance we needed to stay together and secure a safe place to live.

Ellie’s Army didn’t just provide financial support; they gave us hope and a renewed sense of security. Their help has made an immeasurable difference in our lives, and we are forever grateful. Thank you, Ellie’s Army, for being our beacon of hope when we needed it most.

Sincerely,
Parker Family
top_reviews.author: Tanesha Parker (Harleen)

top_reviews.text:
When our son was diagnosed with X-ALD this past July, an incredible army of prayer warriors and supporters surrounded our family. At the same time, we were hit with additional personal hardships that left us feeling overwhelmed and unsure of how we’d get through it all.

In October, a new prayer warrior stepped forward... Ellie’s Army. Through their generosity and compassion, they provided financial assistance that made a meaningful impact on our son’s recovery following his bone marrow transplant. Their support came at a time when we needed it most, and it truly helped carry us through.

Ellie’s Army is now officially part of our son’s prayer warrior circle, and we will forever be grateful for their kindness, their strength, and the light they brought into our lives during such a difficult time.
top_reviews.author: Stephen Basl

top_reviews.text: I need to write a review how my experience was excellent with the Salvation Army. The process of trying to donate a couch was so simple and easy it was unbelievable. I was contacted by Michael the day before the pick up to give me the window for the delivery. It was amazing. It was right on the dot. Two nice gentlemen, Benjamin and Benjamin arrived very pleasant very professional very clean, they proceeded with maneuvering the couch and taking it out. The whole process took less than five minutes. It was like a movie. We were so delighted, but by the service not only you feel good about donating to the Salvation Army, but they are really doing it for a good cause and making it good for us people to do donations. I’m just hoping people have the goodness to do it to the Salvation Army. They’re a very great company. They help everyone in every aspect and they are hiring the best people ever. top_reviews.text: This is a great place to find a variety of goods for any common household. You can purchase everything from clothes, furniture, books, shoes, dvd's, etc. with quality and the comfort of knowing you are contributing to a worthwhile cause. Most of the proceeds from sales help individuals that are residing in the Salvation Army's treatment & rehabilitation program. As long as you take your time searching, you can discover some absolute bargains on some high end clothing articles. Here's a tidbit from me : go shopping on Thursday & Saturday and the clothing items are 50% off! The staff is great and is willing to go the extra distance to make sure you are satisfied. Whenever you are in Wynwood, make sure to stop by. Tell them Jay sent you. Great deals! JE.

I like to shop here! Great place to find deals the staff are nice and friendly except for the rude one Yelling at customers, snatching buggies from their hands. Threatening to call the cops on multiple customers and actually calling them on customers for being a disturbance and lying to the authorities saying the lady was yelling at her when the employee pictured was the one yelling and being rude to multiple shoppers. As soon as she opened the door she yelled everyone in line like she was talking to her kids. No good morning no "Welcome to Where Ya Bin". She has no customers service etiquette. top_reviews.text: Seriously AWESOME PLACE!!! TOTALLY WORTH IT! Pay attention to what days each item costs. Since that's going to reflect on the quality of item you receive. Ex. $10 day will be the best items. Just prepare to spend at least an hour or 2, looking at all the different things, or taking boxed items to designated areas to open them. 9.5 out of  10 stars from me only because they only accept cards, NO CASH!!

I get it's a light and lean business model, but just a SMIDGE of showmanship would go miles for the overall experience.

top_reviews.text: Pablo is our instructor. He's very efficient, prompt and compassionate. He has taught my child skills that will last a lifetime. Also Ms. Debbie the coordinator is always nice and responds promptly to emails.

top_reviews.text: I played pickleball here. Very welcoming. Indoor and air conditioned with 3 courts for 3 different skill levels. It can be very busy.
top_reviews.author: Jim W

top_reviews.text: I have donated here upward of 10 times. I occasionally pop in to browse. Twice now I've been charged over ticketed price. So say something was ticketed 5 something, it shows as 6 something on the receipt. It appears like they add tax onto ticketed price and again after the total. NONE of my items matched their ticketed price, this was not a mistake. I will not waste my time rectifying this, I just want others aware so they can pay attention. I will donate else where moving forward as I will not support dishonest or non transparent business.
top_reviews.author: Rebecca Pittman

top_reviews.text: I have seen others complain about this as well, but I went my first time and the price on the ticket was 1$ less than they charged me at the register and I'm not talking about the cash price thing, cuz I was paying cash. And when asked to sell it to me at the price listed they said it was marked wrong so I said well let's just refund it then since you can't take care of the 1$ difference. And the wait time for someone to even come to the register after ringing a bell was ridiculous. I will never be back.
top_reviews.author: Greg

top_reviews.text: I had tried 10 other stores trying to find a christmas tree stand.   Not only did I find one but I found some other great things.... and the clothes were 50% off.  Also, the lady at the register was very helpful!!!!  Will definitely be back on my next trip from Tennessee🥰
top_reviews.author: Kimberly Hunter

top_reviews.text: Very small. Large variety with good organization, and reasonable price. There isn't anywhere to park with the parking lot being so small and the volunteers taking up half of the parking lot. Had to park across the road on the side of the road. Plenty of customers coming and going with most leaving with something and not empty-handed.
top_reviews.author: Heidi

top_reviews.text: This is a great place to shop for good quality new and used items. Lots of books, CDs, DVDs, Bluerays, etc. Volunteers work like they are getting paid. All helpful/friendly people. New choices to choose from daily. One of the best organized cleanest thrift stores anywhere. sl26
top_reviews.author: Steve Love

top_reviews.text: On the smaller side compared to other local thrift stores, but the prices are very reasonable!! It’s very well organized, clean and employees are very helpful- someone offered to help carry out my purchase to my car. Glad I stopped by!
top_reviews.author: Madeline Miller

top_reviews.text:
Got really lucky and found this BEAUTIFUL black 1997 Naval Officer’s Greatcoat with rare and discontinued big shining gold (brass) buttons from Waterbury Button Co. I say they’re rare because I tried to find some more on Ebay to buy as spares, but I could only find smaller ones. I bought and returned like three orders and have yet to find the right size. Anyway, I LOVE THIS THING. 100% melton wool, SUPER heavy, SUPER warm, and the lapels and collar have full functionality. I was SUPER lucky to have found this because I’ve a small build, and the few other greatcoats were too big on me or were unideal in some other way, and one was not only very big on me, but was in dire need of being fixed up. On top of that, I visited two other military surplus shops and none of them had greatcoats, so this is a really rare and excellent find. $100 was an excellent price for the quality.
But this coat I bought not only fits me perfectly, but not one thing about it needed repairs. Later on, one of the buttons fell off, but we just sewed that back on and reinforced the others that didn’t fall off. I will get this coat modified due to personal preference, but it more than works in its current state and I have no real complaints.
top_reviews.author: Justanother Guy

top_reviews.text: The owner Andy is extremely friendly and knowledgeable about military history. His prices are fair and he is always interested in either seeing what you have to offer, or sharing insight to what you might be interested in. Highly recommend this place!
top_reviews.author: Keaton Rottero

top_reviews.text: Took my 12yr old son here, he loves everything military!! 🫡 He was so excited and we had a great time looking around at everything. The staff was also very friendly and offered to help us! Thanks again.

name: SuperThrift Pensacola- West Nine Mile Road

top_reviews.text:
I do like this store as a thrift store and appreciate the weekly or monthly sales. (50% off a certain color)

But this camera that looks into the dressing rooms is UNACCEPTABLE. This needs to be remedied immediately. Fix these doors with a curtain or remove the camera. It may be worth asking the police to check their security footage to see if they have images of people undressing. This is very sketchy. If I can see this camera in full view then it can see me inside the dressing room. Not cool.

top_reviews.text: Great furniture at excellent prices! Ken helped us our last visit - he was wonderful and so helpful. Will definitely be back

top_reviews.text: Very nice staff and awesome prices, shout out to Malcolm and Joey for their help!

This is a HUGE thrift store separated into three rooms: large furniture, small decor/accessories and clothing. Prices are such great deals!

Each week they have a color tag discount, which items are 50% off. Also, lots of large items that don’t get sold immediately (dressers, tables, etc) get additional discounts you can see on the tags. There is a restroom inside and lots of parking available. 100% recommend visiting!
top_reviews.author: Madeline Miller

top_reviews.text: I do agree with s lot of people about SOME of the prices, but I did still find some good bargains !! I also thought all the people I encountered that worked there were very friendly and helpful!! This includes the lady on the floor putting out the Christmas decor, and the kind and friendly cashier that was so sweet and helpful! She was a pretty black lady with short hair. Great people person!
top_reviews.author: Cynthia A

top_reviews.text: I visited for the first time in years. They have a large selection of furniture and clothes. We went in to get a small table to put a tv on. The cheapest night stand was $40, and it looked like it sat on someone’s back patio for a couple of months. A Christmas tree was $69. There was a knick knack the size of my hand for $4.75. A woman’s dress was $6.99. We just walked out after that.
top_reviews.author: Brittany May

top_reviews.text: When you schedule an appt for pick up for a couch, stay true to your word. You don’t bail on them last minute. So unprofessional. Just kept giving me excuses why she couldn’t deliver. I never would have bought the couch if I thought I wouldn’t be able to have it delivered. Spent the entire day getting my living room clean and ready and you left me hanging. I had to call a buddy with a truck to come help me. Thanks a lot. They also broke the couch as they were loading it on the truck. This is a piece of furniture. Maybe be a little gentle instead of sliding it really hard in there. This is someone’s couch. Very rude in my opinion even though I’m getting a huge discount on the couch. It was a pain in the butt to figure it out. All they had to do was show up and take my money. I won’t be buying anymore furniture from them unless I can load it myself.

top_reviews.text:
The clothes are not organized by size, rather they are organized by color.  For example, womens shirts were sorted by colors and to find a shirt in your size you had to go through each shirt to see what size it was. With racks of clothes in the store that would take hours to go through. We left without looking further.  It would be helpful if for example womens long sleeve shirts were displayed by small, medium, large, extra large etc.  Or women's jeans were displayed by size 2, 4, 6, 8 etc.

The store did have some furniture and a few other items however a majority of the store is clothes.
top_reviews.author: Partyof5

top_reviews.text: I had an absolutely amazing experience at Teen Thrift Challenge Store in Pensacola. The staff was incredibly friendly, welcoming, and genuinely kind from the moment I walked in. You can truly feel their Christian-based mission in everything they do, from the way they serve customers to the purpose behind the store itself. It is more than just a thrift store. It is a place that supports teens, gives back to the community, and operates with heart and integrity. The atmosphere was positive, uplifting, and inspiring. I highly recommend supporting this store if you are in the area.
top_reviews.author: BIANCA BROWN

top_reviews.text:
Hello! If you haven’t stopped by this great business you need to! They have just about everything you may need! We spent a couple of hours in the store today looking at just about everything! So be sure to check out this business! You’ll be surprised with the amount of money you can save!
Cheers

I don’t even know where to begin. The staff here was unbelievably rude. From the moment we walked in, no one explained that every customer needed a buggy. The lady working there kept insisting we were ‘making a mess’ because we weren’t fixing the hangers — which was NOT true. When we told her it wasn’t us, she became even nastier and ended up kicking us out of the store for no reason.
We left feeling completely humiliated.

We went there to spend our money, but with that kind of miserable attitude, they’re only going to lose customers and opportunities. This was one of the worst experiences I’ve had in a store.”

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
I've been a loyal customer for years, visiting weekly and supporting Salvation Army's mission. Last Thursday's experience at Pompano Beach was shocking.

As a disabled person, I entered with my  scooter (ADA-protected right). The manager demanded I remove it, calling it a "safety hazard." I complied and carried it without complaint.

After purchasing, I returned the cart I was using with hangers that were previously in it. She refused to take them, dismissively pointing where to hang them, she was confrontational and I refused to engage. She then told the cashier to refuse service next time I didn't place hangers "properly".

I regularly help in your stores—picking up clothes, rehanging items, assisting customers. I'm always respectful.

When I returned for her name to file a complaint, she refused. I took her photo for documentation. She threatened to call police, then FOLLOWED ME OUTSIDE while recording me and accusing me of harassment as I tried to leave peacefully.

This is completely unprofessional. In all my years shopping here, I've never experienced such treatment.

Management must address this conduct and provide ADA compliance training. No customer should face this treatment.

I'll continue supporting the Broward Blvd location but won't return to Pompano Beach until this is resolved.
top_reviews.author: Val Mendes

top_reviews.text: Anyone who gives this place a bad rep may not be nice to staff! I’ve been going here for years and every staff member has been kind me since day one. The older lady introduced herself the day she met me and talked to me like she’s known me her whole life. I always find THE best stuff at this thrift store. It’s my little hidden gem. I actually just purchased a dream couch of mine from 1975 and Lamont was such a great help. He was even able to recommend someone to help me move the piece of furniture to my house. All the staff at this location works very hard and they have always been so kind to me. I cant wait to continue shopping there in the future!
top_reviews.author: Brittany Patnaude

top_reviews.text: I always get all my furniture from this place on Copans and Dixie. Every Wednesday items are 50% off.  I purchased 3 beautiful drawers.  I am so happy !

name: The Salvation Army Corps & Community Center

top_reviews.text:
1st week of camp...GREAT!
2nd week and already true colors are showing regarding the staff... especially the staff member Melissa, whom consistently yells at all of the children & tells them all to SHUT UP, glares at them, my children have witnessed staff grabbing other younger children's arms and dragging them across the gym floor to place their body where they see fit...
I have spoken with the director Mr.Scott whom seems oblivious to what's going on in Summer Camp. I've spoken to him out of concern for others children as well my concerns for my own, as a concerned parent would do.
Honestly, out of all the staff there in Summer Camp,  Mrs. Kathy is the only person that treats parents and children with respect.
Understand that follow up will be filed to ensure safety of not just my children but others as well. I'm very disappointed.

top_reviews.text: The Salvation Army does such wonderful work in the Pasco County community. We were happy to volunteer to ring the bell, and it warmed our heart to see how many people were in the spirit of giving this year. I will definitely sign up for a shift in the future. It was fun seeing everyone give, and some stopping to have a short conversation with us. If you have a few hours to spare think about reaching out to the Salvation Army to volunteer your time.
top_reviews.author: L Reg

top_reviews.text:
Always a friendly and helpful atmosphere.
My mother use to shop here and I always feel her presence here. Great prices plus the 50% Off Sale. Love shopping here.
top_reviews.author: Kathy Wolfe

top_reviews.text: Fantastic place to buy quality, pre-loved items. I particularly enjoy the men's clothing selection. At 6'6 and 220lbs, finding clothes that fit has always been difficult for me. Not here! 4 tall sized shirts, and 4 pants that actually fit for $25! That would have been over $300 at a "big and tall" store. Talk about a savings! It seems the recent 1 star ratings are from people trying to air their "dirty laundry," as I didn't experience anything like what was mentioned. The staff was all friendly and helpful. As for costs, of course they're going to charge for donated items, it's called running a business. As for the "$600 used furniture" comment, show me where I can buy brand new sofa for under $400. You can't. Period. Great little thrift store, glad they reopened, and I'll definitely be back. Shopped here most of my 49 years of living in Punta Gorda.
top_reviews.author: Jason Coleman

top_reviews.text:
Okay, we went here around Christmas '23, not too long ago. I stumbled upon some videos I took in this store. Look at them! Someone has been putting so much love into organizing the aisles. I love that's it's stuffed to the brim with goodies. I love the organization by color.
A lot of reviews complain about the prices, we found lots of clothes for 5-6 bucks, and left with big shopping bags full. They were running some sales that we didn't know about until checkout, so we only ended up spending around $40.
Would love to visit again one day.
top_reviews.author: Maria Fletcher

top_reviews.text:
Save your money and just go to tj maxx and homegoods cuz what the heck is up with these prices
the prices are outrageous. It’s actually ridiculous the prices they are asking for some of their furniture. They are asking 300-400$ for some furniture. It’s crazy.
Really disappointed. There was an under armor shirt for 35$. A USED UNDER ARMOR SHIRT FOR 35$!! Like what the heck!?

top_reviews.text: I love the Salvation because when I go to service I feel the present of the lord there. In addition I enjoy the band everyone there is caring and very concern about each other. I have been to many denominations and the only church I feel the presence of the Holy Spirit is there at the Salvation Army. They also help in disasters, help the communities, they help to shelter homeless people, they run a ARC program for people with addictions. I truly see the good they do for this country as well as other poor countries that need help. Going there has changed my life and made be a better person.

name: The Salvation Army of Seminole County

top_reviews.text: My experience with Salvation Army so far has been that of a volunteer using their facility and hearing stories of those using them and attending their programs.  I hear nothing but good things.  One homeless and self-admittedly addicted man spoke of the care he received in their rehab and said they were very kind and really wanted to see their clients succeed. That they offered help when no one else cared.  The Salvation Army is a spiritually based organization, and as such touches many people’s lives through the word of God, but ALL appear to be welcomed with open arms and race, creed and religion is not a requirement to receive their gracious and unconditional services.

I thought the Salvation Army where I live was bad! Selling WELL USED clothes for far too high of prices (considering you get them for free) and thinking because they mark them "half off" that makes up for them having HOLES!

Picked up an awesome pair of pants that were absolutely almost worn out, but they were my favorite style of pants, so I wanted them, despite the HOLE I was going to have to sew to fix them.

Stopped an employee and asked if they could do better on the price. She assured me they could at the register.

I waited in line and asked the tall young man at the register, with a beard, if he could do better because of the rip.

His words... "No, because they're already half off."

So the other employee lied to me. Nice way to do business.

Even half off those pants were NOT worth the money.

Don't go here unless you like worn out, torn clothing and employees who expect you to accept them.

I'll NEVER be back!

top_reviews.text:
I want to give a huge shout-out to Mr. Blair, a resident monitor at The Salvation Army in St. Petersburg. He truly embodies what the Salvation Army claims to stand for: service, compassion, respect, and integrity. He is sweet, consistently respectful to residents, and always willing to go the extra mile. I’ve often seen him working alone, handling responsibilities without complaint, yet he still operates as a team player who treats everyone with dignity. His work ethic, patience, and professionalism are evident every time he’s on shift. Quite frankly, some of the other monitors could learn a lot from him. Mr. Blair sets the bar for how residents and coworkers should be treated. Unfortunately, not all staff reflect that same level of professionalism, and there have been instances where rude or dismissive behavior from others has painted the organization in a negative light. Mr. Blair, however, consistently represents the Salvation Army in a positive, respectful, and honorable way, regardless of what’s happening around him.

The Salvation Army is fortunate to have someone like Mr. Blair. He is an asset to this organization, a role model for his peers, and truly deserving of recognition for the exemplary work he does.

Soon as I can; ooh 9:25 clipboard is out and I've signed in. Ok, so now I've met with the rude lady. She said no food until after 1:00pm, bit there is very little, and gave me as much static as she could of why my 5 year old needed clothing. Its Christmas time lady. top_reviews.text:
This is place is just money-hungry.
The tall vanity didn't have a price, I asked the cashier. It costs $195.

The earth is dying because of how many waste is set to burn and rot away. IKEA, Walmart, and many places are over manufacturing furniture that dies easily because it is not strong enough, but "donation" places like this keep their goods to showcase and maybe keep the rental place for tax writeoff (I can't think of another reason since the whole store is empty all the time due to the high prices)

Their automated responses regarding this high-price issue is to communicate with the managers at the store. Us as clients shouldn't be having to even write this kind of review from a donation store. They know what they are doing, just go to look, not shop.

Even fabrics that were hanging in racks were $20. Not dresses nor pants. Fabrics which you can find cheaper at Walmart.

When did donation sites make large corporations win?

Now I’m stuck with a sofa in my dining room while my new furniture is being delivered. I understand not accepting destroyed or poorly maintained furniture but this was extremely frustrating. Outside of that, the 2 gentleman that did arrive were polite and friendly and apologized before they left as their supervisor was the one to make the call over the phone. 3/27/24 3:15 p.m.:

Until today. This man was so rude. Did not speak, did not get out of his chair, did not assist. After I unloaded my 5 large boxes & loaded them onto the truck, I had to ask for the receipt book. He said he didn't have one. I asked what was the receipt book next to him. He picked it up, tossed it at me & said he wasn't lieing.
I reloaded my boxes back into my car to which he had something derogatory to say but I couldn't understand him.
He needs to be spoken to about his attitude & demeanor if he's going to be dealing with the public who has taken time out of their day & gone out of their way to give. I pass 3 Goodwill on my way to SA. He is a terrible representative of the SA. Makes me not want to donate there anymore.

name: The Salvation Army USA | Southern Territory Headquarters

top_reviews.text:
One of the worst experiences donating. These guys took two months to come out. They canceled the initial pick up the day of the appointment.

We were trying to donate a perfectly fine sectional sofa. The sofa specifically did not have any stains or tears like the website had asked for. When they finally rescheduled and arrived two weeks after the initial month long wait I was told that they would not be able to take the sofa due to the fact that it had a layer of dust on it having have sat in the garage for two months while waiting for them to pick it up. Specifically there were no stains or tears on the sofa and after discussing that we have been waiting for them to pick up for so long that a layer of dust was reasonable I was told that they would not be able to sell the sofa being dusty and that if we had it cleaned then they would come back.

I was then told by the truck driver that they had a warehouse full of donated furniture and that they did not need anymore.

Very unprofessional. We have donated to the Salvation Army many times in the past and will no longer be donating in the future. The same sofa has now been sold without any issues.
top_reviews.author: Thomas “Tom” Xu

top_reviews.text: Third time in about 6 years I've requested help. All times I've been treated like a beggar. The last two times have been because I'm on the verge of homelessness. The first of last two I got lucky. As of Sunday, I'll be living in my car and literally have no where to turn. Not one time have they helped. Never a single time. I'll be in my car in the freezing cold and no way to have heat. I work everyday. I do my part. But I'm only one person. I can't afford the rent where I am. I tried to make other arrangements, but needed a little help. These people, in my eyes, are evil to the core. I'm curious as to what constitutes receiving help?? Do I give off the wrong vibes? Why am I being judged so harshly? Cartersville Georgia and Rolla Missouri both acting like I'm scum of the earth. What kind of people are getting help?? It isn't me. I'll never donate to you bunch. I'll never suggest you people. I'll always tell people never go there. The woman didn't even come back from lunch. EVIL ORGANIZATION!
top_reviews.author: Jennifer Roach

top_reviews.text: The corporate office needs to hold The Salvation Army of Wake County accountable for its poor leadership. They obviously condone retaliation against victims of sexual harassment. top_reviews.text: My son has been going there for years. It’s a fun loving safe place for a kid to be a kid. The staff are friendly and loving just like family. I’m proud to send my youngest son there who finally turned 6 so he to can experience the boys and girls club.

top_reviews.text: I'm grateful for the assistance. They are giving me a place to sleep and take a shower and they provide 2 maintenance meals a day breakfast at 7 am and dinner at 4 pm. The portions are very small for adults and it's sized like they feed inmates. There is a chore requirement and if you have to leave every day by 8 am and cannot come back into the building until 4 pm. The only way/day you won't have to leave is Sunday but you have to attend a church service for 1hr. I don't mind if I don't have to find somewhere to go. I don't like that rule because it forces you out into the streets of a city you're unfamiliar with. I keep getting lost with the weird driving directions and streets that all of a sudden become one way and the GPS with Google maps doesn't have it in the system yet. Driving in ATL is chaotic at best. I hope that Salvation Army will rethink this you must leave all day policy and provide things for people to do within the facility.
top_reviews.author: Lanise Franklin

top_reviews.text: I’ve been to this location 3x this week to volunteer for community service - always told to come back or I’ve arrived to late , staff isn’t helpful. Also told I need to bring paper work from court to complete community service and I will need to undergo background check. SMH. I totally see why the rating for this location is low they have no real passion for helping l people in need or allowing others to participate in helping them.

top_reviews.text:
As a long-time community member who regularly donates to the Salvation Army, helps maintain the neighborhood by picking up trash, and always cleans up after my pets, I was very disappointed by my experience at this particular location today.

My husband and I stopped by the open field near our home to let our dogs get a few minutes of fresh air before sunset. Shortly after arriving, we were approached by an older bald man who informed us that the field was for Salvation Army use only. I was surprised to hear this, as there are no posted signs indicating restricted access, and the gate remains open at all hours. In the years I’ve lived here, the field is rarely used for organized activities — when it is occupied, it’s often after hours and not supervised. It is the usual group of teenagers shooting off guns, smoking, and trashing the field.

As someone who values respect and cleanliness in our shared spaces, I take pride in maintaining the community and expected the same level of courtesy in return. Unfortunately, this experience has changed my perception of this location and its leadership. I will no longer be donating to the Salvation Army and will be sharing my experience with others in the community.
top_reviews.author: Lauren Selland

The parking lot here is trash. It's so bad, it's too tight and there are holes lumps and bumps. But overall great salvation please come support and visit.

top_reviews.text: I had an amazing experience at TAMC. Through the entirety of my family and my care which was roughly 3 months. I was medevac’d from Japan due to a hidden pregnancy complication and was coming to TAMC about twice a week until my daughter was born and then every day for a month while she was in the NICU. The staff at TAMC that I encountered were all wonderful, I truly don’t have one negative thing to say about the people they have working here. To highlight a few Mele in the liaison office, Leah in the ADC, Mila in Labor and Delivery, Dr. Tebak, Dr. Marenco and the pediatric surgeon residents, Kerri and Trina with social work and lastly Cassie and the rest of the NICU team. Our family had a hectic story but the staff from all different sections of the hospital did the best they could to advocate for us and get us the resources we needed. I had a wonderful induction experience with labor and delivery, Mila was an amazing nurse and highly contributed to my positive experience. I truly felt cared about as not just a patient but as a person. I can’t say enough praises to my experience here at Tripler. Especially Cassie and the NICU team who all felt like family while our daughter was under their care for her first month of life. I’ve always been someone a bit hesitant of the medical field from past experiences but Tripler really changed my mind. Don’t let negative reviews scare you about this hospital, they have a great staff and they have plenty of resources as well as support you can count on if you need it.

Every employee was very friendly. The color of the week was pink but I didn’t snag any crazy deals. Because it’s December I think everything holiday related is priced high for maximum profit, and there were lots of brand new things in the front with kind of a Dollar Tree vibe. If I had more time I would’ve looked at the clothing more, but all in all it was a decent thrift store. They have a bathroom!

I get to help my community and spend time looking at cool stuff

This is my favorite IYR store, but I have to leave a bad review because the ALL of the shopping carts are atrocious!! They are bulky and MOST IMPORTANTLY THEY DO NOT ROLL. So you have to hold all your items and hope you can still use one hand to browse around since they don't even have baskets.

I was there last week and checked all the carts none of them rolled. top_reviews.text: I just wanted to give a special thank you to Captain Amy for going above and beyond to help me yesterday. Her kindness and help made a significant impact on me and the new season in life I'm beginning. Thank you so very very much.

top_reviews.text: I volunteer there. I love it! The staff is wonderful and I love helping those that come and get the food boxes as they are so happy.  I wish they could get more than 1 box a month.  Generally we have a good supply of food as we get donations from schools restaurants and a lot of grocery stores as well as just average people who come and give what they can. Worldwide we are going through a crisis so we are having a difficult time as we are not getting a lot of donations from schools restaurant and grocery stores. If you can please bring in any food that you can especially bread any type of meat milk juice cheese fresh vegetables eggs or canned goods.  Any food items you can spare! You can also go to the website and donate even a small amount of money that can be used to buy items in need. We would appreciate anything.  Normally we also have church services on Sunday but we are closed now. My mother and I got started being volunteers after there was an article in the Press Tribune of Nampa saying food was needed so my dad went shopping and went and donated and my mom asked how to  help. So we go once a week and fill boxes and give them out!
top_reviews.author: Andrea Woodyard

top_reviews.text:
I really appreciate that places like this exist, and the people are very nice, very accommodating. I hate to say anything negative, and to be a beggar AND a chooser, but, I'm a bit tired of receiving rotten produce, dented soup cans (potential for botulism) and curdled milk products from this place. And it's not just this food bank, either. Is the health department not inspecting for this sort of thing, or...? It's very dangerous, we've gotten expired bean sprouts, from here TWICE, and if someone less knowledgeable about this stuff were to eat those, they could get VERY sick!

Just because we're poor and need help putting food on the table, doesn't mean we don't deserve better than rotten food. Most of it is just fine, and it really does help fill the gaps, when we can't afford another trip to the store, but, some of it, the dog won't even eat! I think that's wrong, and I really wish these folks would be a bit more careful about some of the things they're giving to the public.
top_reviews.author: amy pace

top_reviews.text: I went there for help with my water bill. They have an additional program for help. After going back and forth between Heidi and the water company I was advised that I don't quality because I'm a home owner. Really? So this program is only for renters that need help huh?I gotta say that pretty messed up. Other than they have been great!
top_reviews.author: Kristin Schneider

top_reviews.text: I have no idea why some people are complaining about service or prices. I think it's refreshing that they don't just sell random junk that someone wants to get rid of. In my experience, they have typically good quality items at very reasonable prices (not to mention they do sales routinely). Often times the men's section is very limited at most thrift stores but it's a good quarter here. If anyone is saying the staff is rude here they are either out of their mind or have unreasonably high expectations for what customer service should be. I've always found the staff to be delightful, friendly, and helpful. These women volunteer their time for a charity they believe in --- I think that alone speaks of their character. My only complaint is I wish they were open more days but that's a big ask considering the majority of its staff are volunteers.

I was in awe the amount of planning, organizing and people spending their spare time helping to pull this together...it was truly incredible. We really do have wonderful people in our community and this is a wonderful place. I sat in my car and cried for a bit because I am truly so greatful and blessed. Thank you to all of you! The store is clean, well‑organized, and the staff is friendly and very helpful. I absolutely love this place.

name: St. Vincent de Paul Society Thrift Store

top_reviews.text: There are days that I would give this thrift store a five-star rating and there are days such as yesterday. If possible I would have given them no Stars. I spend over $100 at this thrift store on a regular basis. As a regular customer that spends plenty of money there and plan to do so in the future, the manager Janelle, was extremely rude to me when all I was doing was checking clothing for stains and damage. I set these aside to give to them so they were not sold to others that didn't notice the damage because nothing is returnable. Most visits I am welcomed with smiles, pleasant communications and a feeling of appreciation and satisfaction after leaving. I was given attitude today by the manager janelle even after telling her I had separated the damaged materials and she told me to do it in the aisles and if I don't want  to purchase it , to place damaged goods back on the rack for someone else 2 weeks to waste their money on. When I decided not to purchase some items I was going to put the items on the dressing room return rack so I did not put them back in the incorrect place. For this I was pretty much yelled at. For a religious thrift store I was not treated with the actions of a religious person. I was so offended that I left my cart and any other items that I was going to purchase or put back right I was and walked out. This is not the person I am but I refuse to be disrespected by anyone let alone from the place that I donate to and spend plenty of money at. I understand people have bad days but even on my bad days I would prefer being kind and making others happy because that improves my life and emotional well-being. I am a firm believer in recycling, selling or giving away used items that are in good condition. Before visiting this thrift store ever again, I feel the need to call and check if Janelle is working because I want nothing to do with that place while she is in it. I cannot believe how much I was disrespected by the manager after trying to be very respectful. top_reviews.text:
I love this store, I almost always find great items! I also exclusively donate to your store as well! Today though, as I walked in the store, I saw a little stand with baskets. I immediately put it in my cart after seeing the price and shopped. When I went to the register, the cashier embarrassed me by saying “no, not the price” and proceeded to tell me it was just put out yesterday. Like I switched the tags. I would never do that! Salvation Army is truly a great charity and I would never switch tags. If it’s too high for my liking, I pass. Maybe retrain your cashiers to not embarrass honest customers. I’m aware it happens, but there must be a better way to handle that situation. It was marked 6.99 (purple tag) and she told me 10.99 and I said that was fine. Just embarrassing.

Thank you for such a fast response! I appreciate it, I was just so embarrassed because I would never do such a thing. I know it happens with dishonest people, so I understand her concern but really, there could be a better way to handle it. The store itself is great and I think pricing is really fair! top_reviews.text:

The store is packed with all kids of overpriced “Donated” junk. Any and ALL QUALITY items are sorted out and pulled to be sold through SA affiliated EBay accounts.

Current Management has no clue how price USED & DONATED items, unless you wanna pay $12.99 for an 8 year old OldNavy Sweater or $7.99 for a used adidas tshirt with stains to support local highschool’s girls JV soccer team, or an LL bean sweatshirt with stains and a hole for $14.99. If you’re into buying overpriced trash then this is your spot.

I love how they ask you’ “If you’d like to round up for rehab?”. The first thing that pops up in my head after that question, “where is my money going in the first place, if not for rehab and other support services?”

It’s getting ridiculous. This store and Salvation Army as a whole have become far too greedy to be considered a charitable organization. I will never again donate to this or any Corporate Thrift Stores.

top_reviews.text:
We had our first visit at the SA thrift store today located on N Illinois in Belleville. To say we were sticker shocked is disturbing. We understand prices at all retailers, thrifts, etc have increased. But when the majority of almost all the clothing is priced higher than purchasing brand new at a retailer, there's something majorly wrong. We commenting to employees, the majority stated "oh, we all know". The only thing they are able to do is give you the phone number to talk with corporate and leave bad reviews. So we're starting here.
If you're looking for lower cost clothing for anyone, please steer clear of these stores. They are priced at corporate, then sent to the stores where they have no power over pricing. Stick to smaller thrifts who are non-profit. You will even find high prices at Goodwill & Savers, but the SA thrift is even higher than those mentioned.

The employees were kind, helpful & understanding. It is also my understanding that the very high price increase is something that was just done recently.

top_reviews.text: This store employs differently abled people, so the service may be off or different from what you expect, but get over it. You cannot have a large bag with you since they don’t have security trackers on clothes, so you have to check it at the door. I didn’t love their cubby situation at the front, so just plan ahead and bring a small bag to hold your wallet and you’ll be fine. If you want the piece of furniture, you have to take part of the tag off of it to claim it. They sell fast, so check with the store management and buy it fast then keep shopping. The clothes are great quality, organized by category and color, the books are affordable and bestsellers, their junk aisle has weird adorable gems in it, and their Saturday sales are great. I’ve been going here for over 5 years, and they always have something. So donate here, shop here, be gracious humans, and move on if you can’t handle the thrift!

top_reviews.text:
Literal animals work here!

I’ve loved donating to this store throughout the years. I was just planning to do a huge drop off before moving cross country, but I will be going elsewhere after the atrocious story I just heard.

My sister unfortunately is homeless. She stopped in this store because she needed shoes. She took a pair of $4 sandals and didn’t pay for them because she had no money. I understand she stole an item, however, that does not give the team members, most of whom were men, the right to assault her.

She said all of the employees left the store and jumped her. Yanked her purse and threw it behind the glass counter. They dragged her back in the store and 2 large, male employees proceeded to beat on her her while 3 employees stayed outside and whooped her boyfriend’s butt outside.

All the while customers were watching and recording and no one stepped in to help her. She says it was about 2 months ago so it’s recent. So those employees are probably still there.

I worked in retail for over 15 years and we were told it was illegal for us to put our hands on anyone—even if they were stealing. I think they did this to my sister because they could tell she was vulnerable and they knew she would not report them.

top_reviews.text: A wide array of products, but the prices are crazy. Furniture and art work seems to go for $200-$500. Many items are sold at the same price as brand new items. I’m sure they’ll post a response about how sorting and selling items aren’t free and donations go to a good cause, like they copy and paste on every review, but I’ve never seen a Salvation Army or Goodwill with these prices. name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Salvation Army is one of those places where you never really know what you’re going to find, and that sense of surprise is a big part of the appeal. Every visit feels like a small treasure hunt. For me, the book section is easily the highlight. It’s easy to spend a lot of time flipping through shelves, discovering forgotten novels, oddball nonfiction, or the occasional hidden gem you’d never expect to see.

That said, the experience isn’t always perfect. There are clearly some customers who act as full-time resellers and seem to camp out the store. While that’s part of thrift-store culture, it can be frustrating when it appears that certain employees may be setting items aside or giving those shoppers early access. When that happens, it takes away from the fairness and spontaneity that make thrifting enjoyable in the first place.

Thrift stores work best when everyone has an equal chance at finding something special. When favoritism—real or perceived—enters the picture, it can make regular shoppers feel discouraged.

Even with that downside, Salvation Army still delivers moments of discovery, especially in the book section. With a little patience and the right timing, you can still walk away with something unexpected, which is ultimately why people keep coming back.
