name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
I’ve visited many Salvation Army stores throughout Chicagoland, but this location has been by far the most unwelcoming and problematic. Beyond the disorganization and extremely high prices, the most troubling issue is how customers are treated, especially those who are African American, Hispanic, or simply appear as if they don’t belong in the eyes of the staff.

There is a repeated pattern of racial profiling and false accusations. I’ve personally witnessed several incidents where African American customers were followed around the store, accused of switching price tags without cause, and treated with clear suspicion. In one incident, a young woman held clothes up to herself over her outfit to see if they would fit, since there is no dressing room. A staff member immediately accused her of trying to steal. That level of hostility is completely inappropriate. This is a thrift store, not a high-security facility.

Ironically, most of the staff are minorities themselves, primarily Hispanic women who have worked there for many, many years. Yet they continue to target their own community, along with African American customers, creating an environment of constant judgment and control. One particular woman, who has been there the longest, insists on always being at the register and refuses to let anyone else take that position. That kind of control is concerning, especially when it seems to be tied to who gets followed, accused, or mistreated.

On a personal note, I experienced this behavior when visiting with my boyfriend, who is African American and a practicing attorney. He was followed through the store and accused of altering a price tag, with absolutely no evidence. When we raised our concerns to staff, we were completely brushed off.

In addition to the unacceptable treatment of customers, I believe the Salvation Army should conduct a full audit of this location. The prices are far beyond what is reasonable for a secondhand store, and there are real concerns about whether items are being priced and tracked appropriately. The way some employees behave, it is as if they are personally losing money. There is no other explanation for the level of aggression and defensiveness we have seen from them.

This store does not reflect the values the Salvation Army promotes. The staff operate in a culture of suspicion and blame, treating people  especially minority shoppers as if they are criminals rather than individuals simply looking for affordable clothing and household items.

I sincerely urge Salvation Army leadership to investigate this location thoroughly. What is happening here is not only unacceptable, it is harmful to the very communities the organization is meant to serve.
top_reviews.author: Jen Starks

top_reviews.text: If I can give 0 stars I would My family and I have lived in many states & shopped at many Salvation Army locations. We also donate items frequently & donated in other ways to other salvation army organizations throughout the years & have NEVER encountered employees like the one's at this specific store. Therefore I am extremely disappointed by the treatment my family received at this Salvation Army Thrift Store, my wife (who is white) and my black children were followed throughout the store by several employees. The situation escalated when they falsely accused my 8-year-old son of stealing a toy he did not have. We felt targeted and racially profiled during our entire visit. name: The Salvation Army Rockford/Winnebago County Social Services

top_reviews.text: I had to come here for help with rent because my boyfriend and I both lost our long term jobs around the same time. Very shortly after we had an unexpected and tragic death in the family. We also have three children in the home. We have never asked for help, never received help, it was a last resort. They originally said they cannot help us unless one of us gets a job. My boyfriend went back to work shortly after this conversation and I called again. I throughly explained the situation and they set up an appt for me to bring the documentation. At the appointment she told me what day they would cut a check for the landlord and how he could get it, either via mail or pick up. Three days later she calls and says her supervisor doesn’t think we are in need. After being unemployed for three months and a death in the family I questioned what more would have to happen for there to be a “need” in their eyes. She couldn’t answer my questions and told me I’d have to look elsewhere for help. I’d recommend being more upfront during the appointment, we were never told it had to be approved by her supervisor she implied we would get the help. She told me her supervisor said that “in comparison to other applicants, there are others with more need”. Two hardworking people who lost their jobs, no fault of their own, who also have three children to take care of… do not qualify for help. I still do not understand this comparison method of approval or  what else needs to happen for someone to be considered in need. Thank you for making a bad situation worse.
top_reviews.author: Jennifer Lewis

top_reviews.text: I shopped at this store before but had an uncomfortable experience with a young female manager who mistreated us, as if we had switched the price labels. The store was a mess, which we understand due to the nature of the business, but customers shouldn't be held responsible for that. A chest of drawers had four labels on it; chair and sofa labels among them... one said "dresser - $39," and another said "vintage dresser - $59." The issue isn't about the actual cost—if a customer feels something is worth it, that's valid. However, the manager began questioning us aggressively about whether we attached the labels, and she approached the cashiers, speaking loudly about the issue. This behavior was unprofessional and unpleasant; she seemed more problematic than helpful. The situation ended up making us leave the store without purchasing anything and feel like not returning to a place one goes to help but is treated unfairly.

name: The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center

top_reviews.text:
I entered The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center in Rockford, IL in 2019 and graduated in 2020. When I came into the program, I was homeless, hopeless, broken, and spiritually bankrupt. The transformation I experienced here has been nothing short of miraculous.

Today, I am proud to say that I work as a Spiritual Counselor for the Rehabilitation Center, have my own apartment, and have found a loving and supportive home within The Salvation Army. The program provided me with the tools, guidance, and spiritual support I desperately needed to rebuild my life. The compassionate staff and the structured environment helped me regain my sense of purpose and self-worth.

I am currently actively pursuing training for full-time ministry work, and I owe my new life to the incredible work done by The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center in Rockford. This place not only offers a second chance but also helps you discover the strength and faith you need to thrive. I wholeheartedly recommend this program to anyone in need of a life-changing experience.

Thank you, Salvation Army, for helping me find my path and for being a beacon of hope and love in my life.

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Prices here are higher than retail!

For example, this location charges $5+ for a basic plate or cup, which you could instead buy at Walmart for $1.54. Savers on the other hand, a FOR-PROFIT operation, charges less than half of that for the same items.

I notice in this location's review responses they attempt to justify these prices by claiming the high cost is necessary to fund their charities and pay their staff; however, if your store is so unprofitable that you need to charge used, donated goods at a price higher than retail, maybe people are better off just donating elsewhere, as this location seems to be bleeding money, despite their free inventory and minimal staffing.

On September 11, 2025, I visited your store at approximately 8:25 p.m. One of the employees — an older Black woman with a short white haircut — began loudly announcing, “The store is closing, please come to the front,” even though the store’s posted closing time is 9:00 p.m.

Earlier, I had observed this employee sitting in a corner scrolling on her phone; she even remarked, “I’m just here hiding from the cameras.” Her tone during the announcements was rude and unnecessarily brash. She repeated the message several times, which ultimately led me to put my items back and leave the store without making a purchase.

I was disappointed by this behavior, and equally by the lack of response from other staff who witnessed it. I hope this matter will be addressed so that future customers can have a better experience.

top_reviews.text:
Please DOUBLE CHECK your Receipts and please DOUBLE CHECK your Items to make sure that everything you bought is in the bag (the bag that cashiers put your things in)!

But on the receipt it said flat $44.99… 44.99 is not 50% off of 85.99!.. and also the shoes I bought had a 7.94 green tag, but receipt says 11.94!!!

top_reviews.text:
I went to go volunteer today.  The lady answered the door and she seemed all nervous.  I let her know I was there to volunteer.   She said ok, volunteer or community service, she asks.   I said, Volunteer ma'am.   We then proceed to the next door.  At the kitchen door she looks in and there is a guy there.   He sees us and turns to us and seemed caught off guard and asked what do we need.   I said I am here to volunteer.  The guy seems confused and not sure what is happening.   I said I signed up to volunteer and help today.   I said i signed up online and have my picture added so you would recognize me when I got here.   I am here to help, i am not doing community service for the courts.    They looked confused.    So I stood there for a moment.  Then said ok, thanks for your time and left.     I am so upset because I once used Salvation Army for things I needed and wanted to give back.  I even signed up on the schedule.  I dont understand why they are confused and make me feel like I am a criminal trying to slip in the back door or something.   There is a reason I signed up.  They would have the information at their fingers tips on her computer at the entry.   I just wanted to help and here I am not helping and feeling like they made me feel like I was the creepy one.    I just wanted to do some good and pay it forward, and here we are.  The lady at the door and the dude in the kitchen act like it was strange.  I felt extremely judged and unwanted.   So much for coming out to feel like I am giving back to my community to help.     Funny, cos I frequently help at the Rescue Mission and have never felt that way when I help there.   Thought I would expand my volunteering time with the Salvation Army, but I guess not.    So much for practicing good christian values and good service to the community, because I most definitely did Not feel that this morning when I came to volunteer at Salvation Army this morning.   No wonder they are always asking for help, it is hard to willingly help when they treat the volunteers strangely.
****UPDATE*****
They reached out and apologized for the mistake on their end.   They said that when you sign up, it is suppose to alert them and get an approval, however mine got through and it confused the morning.   She apologized and we got it all straightened out.    Please remember when signing up make sure to give yourself a few days so you can get approved and the system will be fully updated.    Now you wont have to feel strange if you just show up.    Thanks for the quick call back and response.

top_reviews.text:
My experience with The Salvation Army of Johnson County was extremely disappointing and added stress during an already difficult time. I was working with a caseworker named Savannah Jones while my family was experiencing housing instability.

Throughout my time in the program, there were missed appointments and lack of follow-through with Savannah. Communication was inconsistent, and despite my efforts to stay engaged and ask reasonable questions about housing assistance and next steps, I did not receive clear guidance or meaningful support.

When I began advocating more actively for my family and asking for accountability, the support did not improve. Instead, I was left without assistance or resolution.

Programs serving families in crisis need to provide consistent communication, reliability, and transparency. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here. I hope this organization reflects on how cases are managed and how families in vulnerable situations are support

top_reviews.text: I meant to post a review the day I went to receive help with utilities. I am only giving a 3 star review because of how the lady was the moment I walked in the door. She grilled me the entire time about where I was spending my money. I had already told her that I fell behind because I was in school, (also paying out of pocket) only working part time. The current job I have now,I've been there two months. She kept telling me I had a certain amount left over each month, and I'm like where???? I am a single mother and have 4 kids!! Then she kept telling me that there are other people needing help and that they need more help. She also kept telling me that priorities should come before pleasures, because I purchased a bed and furniture and am paying a least for both. It's not fair. I have compromised, and sacrificed so much and deserve to have what I want. I took off taking classes again because I am the only breadwinner. I eventually told her that if she doesn't want to help me, then I will just find somewhere else to go. The entire thing was very uncomfortable. I only gave three stars because of how I was treated. I just only ask that people who are working in this type of field to have compassion because everyone is going through it. I don't need someone telling how much I messed up. I just needed to catch up.

top_reviews.text: Not much of a yelp reviewer, but the way I was treated made me more angry than I have been in years. My boyfriend and I are going through the moving process and brought a fair amount of misc household items over for donation. I was told to walk it down the stairs, which is fine, but after I brought down 2 boxes and a couple of bigger stand alone items, the employee stood at the bottom of the steps as I was coming down, going through one of the boxes (hadn't even touched the second yet), and as rudely as she could have possibly been, told me that "everything in these boxes are broken, why did you even bring this trash in here and not just have thrown it all away?". I calmly apologized and stated I was unaware of anything being broken, stated it must have happened as we were bringing it over, and asked her what was broken and if she'd like me to take it back. She continued to go off on me that "the entire box is trash". When I said okay, I can come down and take it back out to throw it away, she told me no and to just leave and not to bring anything else down, including what I had in my hands. My boyfriend then walked down the stairs to see what all was broken, and the only thing she actually had to say was broken was a pair of old binoculars. I guess I'm a horrible person to have thought the some little kid may have thought they were cool and bought them for 2 bucks. My boyfriend again apologized and offered to carry it back out, and she told him no again and just to leave and not leave anything else. If she had just politely stated that the store wouldn't have any use for any of the items I brought in, I would have gladly taken them back out to my truck. There really just was no need to have been so rude and angry. Upsetting because I'd much rather do my thrift shopping there instead of give my money to a large corporation like goodwill, but I will not be returning after the way I was treated today.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Prices here have skyrocketed to the point where items routinely cost more than they do brand new—and that’s regardless of condition. Broken, heavily worn, or dirty doesn’t seem to matter.

Even more frustrating: if an item is missing a price tag or the sticker falls off, staff won’t tell you until after you’ve spent time shopping the entire store. At checkout, they refuse to sell it, assume you’re trying to “get away with something,” and pull the item to be held for 24 hours so it can be repriced and put back on the floor.

These stores seem to have forgotten that their inventory is donated for free and that their stated mission is to serve underserved communities. Instead, the priority is clearly profit. Seven dollars for a dirty T-shirt? Five dollars for a plain drinking glass?

The whole experience feels hostile, cynical, and completely disconnected from the purpose they claim to serve. I won’t be coming back.
top_reviews.author: Sidney

top_reviews.text: I have a long history of donating to the Salvation Army across multiple states. However, on my very first visit to this location, I had an exceptionally poor donation experience. The staff member stood their with an attitude and said I cannot help you unload and walked off. No hello, no good afternoon, no thank you. I did not require a receipt, but it would have been nice to be offered one. That is absolutely not the way to get people to return. I understand that staff may be part of the outreach mission and may need to develop employment skills. I will never give up on the Salvation Army, but it is highly likely I will drive further out in hopes of a decent experience.

top_reviews.text:
This specific store is the epitome of corporate greed! The prices are so high that I’ve audibly laughed after picking something up. Once again, people are DONATING these items for free and you’ve jacked up the prices beyond expensive antique boutique prices.

They’ve got a local “influencer” as the their manager. I say this in quotations because she just goes to other thrift stores and antique malls and either bashes the prices or says the things that they are selling aren’t good enough. Not to mention she’s scouting the esthetic and the prices for her own store, a spy. This is more than double dipping on her behalf and a horrible call on the Salvation Army’s part.

Anything in a THRIFT STORE -that isn’t furniture- should never cost more than $5. I shouldn’t pick up a small wood box that was originally from Hobby Lobby that clearly needs some TLC and see $12.99 on the tag. Are you kidding me?! You’re clearly missing the point. You’re supposed to be selling to people in need, not for your own greed.

STOP TAKING THE SLEEVES OFF OF BOOKS! Thats part of their value!!!! There are people out there that live for the artwork and you throw it away for the sake of an ugly end cap display. Also, stop throwing away books that don’t meet your evangelical ideologies, not everyone who shops there is Christian.

You’re not a store that people go to for decoration advice. You’re a store that people go to when they need an item for their house, but places Target and Walmart are too expensive for their income.

The Salvation Army is an organization built for the purpose of meeting human needs and without discrimination. However, your prices show that you are discriminating against the very people your mission is meant for.

In conclusion, knock your prices down by 75% and get rid of your manager, she’s hurting your sales.

top_reviews.text:
My husband and I love to explore thrift stores.  As recent Newton residents, we visited this store and the Goodwill store, just browsing.

Our first couple of experiences at the Salvation Army store were very positive.  There was an eclectic selection of merchandise and we found a few treasures to purchase.  The employees were friendly as were the other shoppers.

Today was a 180 from the other times.  A lady ahead of me in line wanted to purchase a framed picture that was not priced.  She asked the clerk if she could go to the back and ask (I assume) whoever was in charge of pricing to get a price for her.  She was told, no, that the merchandise would go to the back and for her to come back tomorrow when the price would be on it.  I doubt the lady returns.  If this is Salvation Army's policy, they need to remember that good customer service involves avoiding unnecessary trips.  Unless I desperately wanted something, I would not waste the time or the gas to come back because someone decided it was too much trouble to slap a price sticker on an unmarked item.

When I checked out, the clerk asked if I wanted my card run as a debit or credit.  I said "Debit" I thought clearly.  She looked at me again and said, "De-bit or Cre-dit" as if I were deaf or slow.  I repeated, "De-bit" again.  She rang up the sale, bagged up my items, shoved a slip in my direction to sign (no pen was offered, although they were right by the cash register, on the other side of the counter where I was standing).  So I walked over, got a pen, walked back, and signed.  She didn't say, "Thank you", "kiss my posterior", "get out" or anything else.  So, I said, "You're welcome", got my bags and left.  We won't be coming back.

Edit:  I notice this review disappeared a week or so after I originally left it.  There is nothing in it that contravenes Google's ToU and was an honest summary of my last experience at this establishment.  The fact that someone at Salvation Army seeks to censor it only strengthens my resolve to not return as well as ensure that my experience is posted on other websites as well......

I’m extremely disappointed with how the Salvation Army treated my uncle.
He’s homeless and struggling with addiction, and Mental issues and instead of getting compassion and real help, he was judged, looked down on, and kicked out.
Places like this are supposed to help people at their lowest, not turn their backs on them because they aren’t “perfect” or clean yet. Addiction is a disease, not a character flaw.
If you only help the people who are already doing okay, you aren’t really helping the homeless — you’re just picking and choosing who’s “worthy” of dignity.
We needed support, not judgment. We needed someone to care, not make things worse.
I hope they rethink how they treat the people they claim to serve.

Salvation Army when I went homeless after the military I didn’t know they had services for veterans like this. The KCVA helped to get into the Salvation Army. I had to stay here due to indifferences at my house. My stay was comfortable and peaceful. The other Veterans are kind. My case worker Irene was very hard on me at first lol!  After I was admitted in she was kind and loved all of us. Integration was easy. Irene will help you get more % to help in your case. She is there for you. Use her and let her know how you feel. She has been working there for 15 years (KC,Kansas). What an accomplishment. There are others that work with Irene that are just as  important to you.
You have to do chores but they aren’t large duties. Roger will be on you. It’s good to clean your surroundings makes you feel good.
Breakfast isn’t the greatest but, that will change. Yvette serves breakfast she has to have thick skin because she didn’t make the food. She has no control on what is being served. Be nice to her always and your days will go better. Lunch and Dinner are more filling. Blake is one of the cooks trying to make new desserts and new meals. There is a “suggestion box” downstairs so fill it out. They have snack later on in the night. I met Tom from Salvation Army very stand up person he is kind and cordial. They have a gym for basketball and a small workout room.
The Veterans I met are my forever brothers. I will stay in touch after I leave. Thank you Salvation Army for helping me find my way.
top_reviews.author: Maximillian Ulibarri

top_reviews.text: Would give less stars if possible.  Staff treats Vets like dirt . They'll talk bad   about vets to other vets and other staff. Bathroom floors always covered in urine . No personal food items or more than a few days worth of clothes allowed. I've already filed complaints with the VA and Salvation Army's main number. top_reviews.text:
This review is not about the assistance they offer. This is plainly about the customer service and unable to ask questions without getting talked over with. I called a couple of weeks ago explaining to a man who answered the phones, that I had black mold and had not been living in my residence. I needed help with a really late energy bill. I had to throw away everything and am debt because I had to get myself out of this situation after being denied by the landlord. So to start off, this man did not give me the details but led me to call for two consecutive weeks, to then put me on hold and say sorry, “if you don’t live at the residence, we will not help”. It was the fact that I called this man, talked to me two weeks ago, even remembered me on the phone today just to tell me information wasting my time.
He is extremely difficult on the phone. Won’t let you speak at all and when I had asked for other resources, he said none. He was rude and unwilling to even let me speak or say anything without rambling over me like a monster truck.

I had called last week again and got a wonderful female on the phone who had given me three religious resources to call. Btw I called and left multiple voicemails, no answer. He wasn’t helpful in that matter and immediately say no,no,no like he was the angriest man in the world. Disappointed and extremely disrespectful. 0 stars to the man on the phone because you don’t bulldoze people

Extremely disappointed I couldn’t speak to a manager about or someone higher about this. I mean a competent person, not someone who can’t communicate.

name: The Salvation Army-Olathe - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text:
I encountered this amazing location 2/10/2019-3/1/2021(I lived in their Transitional Living Program). We got there at closing time Mina was on her vacation on her way out the door when I walked in with my daughter. After Karlea got us checked in Karlea got my daughter new pajamas, body wash, deodorant,  let her pick out her a scarf, towels because the 1st thing she said to my baby "YOU HUNGRY & DO YOU WANT TO SHOWER" SHE ALWAYS TOOK CARE OF US DURING OUR DAILY NEEDS. I'M TELLING Y'ALL THEY KNEW EXACTLY WHAT WE NEEDED IN THAT MOMENT. I can't begin to tell y'all how Mina has impacted my life even up until this day..She was with me while I went to court (the court clerk remembered her when he was a little boy, Mina helped them as well), she was there for support with my daughter taught me coping skills while raising a teenager(my relationship with my daughter always represented love between us both but again she was a TEENAGER at the time we all know how that goes 😂), she was there when we moved into our new place, she was there to help us get beds, hair grease(yes hair grease coconut BLUE MAGIC), BLACK GIRL 👧🏿 hair products, bras, shoes,  food, you name it. She came in prayed in our new home. I came to say this yesterday I received ny certification as a Medical Assistant, she's the 1st person I called, text & sent pictures to. SHE ALWAYS EMPOWERS & UPLIFTS ME. Now this is where Salvation Army gets even more COOLER. NATHAN & CHERI WOODARD( THEY REALLY ARE A YOUNG & BEAUTIFULLY MARRIED GOD FEARING, COMMUNITY LOVING PEOPLE). My Father passed away 11-10-22.  THEY PERMITTED ME TO USE THE CHURCH TO HAVE A MEMORIAL FOR MY DADDY(Nobody showed up but Cheri, Nate & Mina was there they stayed 12-6-22) I was completely hurt & embarrassed for my Dad because nobody showed up because of my family not respecting the fact that my daughter & I respect Dad's wishes to stop doing dialysis(It was Mina who helped me do HOME HOSPICE for my Daddy, it was the most gut wrenching & beautiful time I had, I'LL DO IT AGAIN TOO because the peace I feel knowing my daughter held his hand until he couldn't hold hers back anymore)... Cherish & Nate at the time had a toddler & child at home THEY STAYED WITH US, THE MOST UNSELFISH THING THEY EVER DID WAS GIVE ME THEIR TIME, THEY WERE TRULY CONCERNED,  THE EFFORT & BEAUTY THEY PUT INTO DADDY'S MEMORIAL WAS TOP TIER. I've done interviews with Fox 4, I've spoken at luncheon about my encounters with the center. I know I've said a lot but HEAR ME OUT. PLEASE KEEP THIS PLACE AROUND FOR AS LONG AS THEY CAN, OLATHE NEEDS THIS PLACE, OLATHE NEEDS THESE EXACT PEOPLE IN PLACE TO HELP CHANGE & SAVE LIVES. THEY'LL GO ALL OUT FOR YOU ESPECIALLY IF THEY SEE YOU APPLIED YOURSELF, DON'T BE AFRAID TO ASK FOR HELP. THEY CHANGED MY THINKING PROCESS, THEY HELPED ME WORK IN MY CREDIT ETC. THIS PLACE IS ONE THE BEST PLACES OUR LORD SAVIOR JESUS CHRIST DOES HIS WORK & WE ALL KNOW GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD HE GAVE HIS ONLY BEGOTTEN SON...YOU GO TO THIS PLACE THEY'LL LET YOU KNOW OTHERS MAYBHAVE FORGOTTEN ABOUT YOU INCLUDING YOURSELF BUT GOD HAS NOT FORGOTTEN ABOUT YOU(MINA TOLD ME THAT AS WE WERE WALKING INTO OUR UNIT THAT NIGHT WE WENT TO THEM)...

THANK YOU KINDLY FOR ALL YOU DID. ALL I HAD TO DO WAS SEEK SALVATION AT THE SALVATION ARMY. WHO KNEW BUT NOW YOU DO!

the prices are extremely high, you get this donated for FREE. this is not a curated vintage clothing store, it’s a thrift store. it’s greedy and selfish. goodwill and savers are no different.

name: The Salvation Army USA - Louisville Area Command

top_reviews.text:
We were turned away twice on two separate nights by this compassionless, uncaring, and apathetic agency.
We made both reservations for the overnight shelter beds through Coordinated Shelter Access.  On each separate night, we arrived at the location at the agreed upon time and were turned away each time by the most unfeeling, uninterested, condescending, security guard named Andreas.
I swear to God, this has to be the coldest, most uncaring woman that I have ever had the displeasure of speaking to.
Her tone, her voice, her sense of entitlement, all came across over the phone. She has to be the most patronizing, condescending person I've ever spoken to in my 56 years on this planet.
She had the unmitigated gall to say to a homeless person over the telephone,
"What do you expect me to do? It's Sunday night at 11pm, everyone has gone home to their warm beds"
Did she seriously just say that to a freezing homeless person seeking shelter at the facility that she works for?
Ummm... yes she did!
She said a lot of hurtful and unkind remarks, I couldn't believe my ears.
Hopefully, no one else has to ever go through what we went through.
It wasn't a pleasant experience at all.
top_reviews.author: Jeffrey Kahler

top_reviews.text:
We were turned away twice on two separate nights by this compassionless, uncaring, and apathetic agency.
We made both reservations for the overnight shelter beds through Coordinated Shelter Access.  On each separate night, we arrived at the location at the agreed upon time and were turned away each time by the most unfeeling, uninterested, condescending, security guard named Andreas.
I swear to God, this has to be the coldest, most uncaring woman that I have ever had the displeasure of speaking to.
Her tone, her voice, her sense of entitlement, all came across over the phone. She has to be the most patronizing, condescending person I've ever spoken to in my 56 years on this planet.
She had the unmitigated gall to say to a homeless person over the telephone,
"What do you expect me to do? It's Sunday night at 11pm, everyone has gone home to their warm beds"
Did she seriously just say that to a freezing homeless person seeking shelter at the facility that she works for?
Ummm... yes she did!
She said a lot of hurtful and unkind remarks, I couldn't believe my ears.
Hopefully, no one else has to ever go through what we went through.
It wasn't a pleasant experience at all.
top_reviews.author: Jeffrey Kahler

top_reviews.text:
Many of the Goodwills in the Metairie and Kenner areas used to be good but are now terrible. Bridge House also falls into the same situation but has some areas they are better at.

Books are very cheap here along with VHS and DVD movies. That's where the positives end. Electronics, furniture, shoes and clothing are priced up to retail despite some items you'll find being heavily worn. Bridge House attempts to use a unique pricing system by saying every price tag is 50% off. You'll find in the majority of situations, it's still very overpriced despite this.

Bridge Houses most overpriced items are it's furniture which makes no sense as Goodwills and salvation army stores have very cheap used furniture prices. Bridge House will sometimes take furniture from Walmart and TEMU then price it well above what it costs to obtain brand new from either of those stores.

Buying electronics here is especially risky as they'll claim to be tested and working but priced to near retail levels and often missing major components to properly work like power cables or USB dongles for wireless electronics. The only other good thing about this place is when clothing doesn't sell for a week, it gets moved to a dollar rack. I was a resident there recently and found that the treatment and care of Men, Women and Children at the shelter in New Orleans on So. Claiborne Ave to be deplorable!!!  To say the staff was grossly incompetent is an understatement!  The millions of dollars in donations given to the Salvation Army are being mismanaged and outright stolen by staff and their families!!!  It is so blatantly obvious that the staff at this shelter is ill suited to care for the needs of animals let alone the needs of vulnerable men, women and children.  There should be an independent investigation of this agency as soon as possible!!  The lives of the people in respite care are compromised by inadequate medical and nutritional resources.  Mrs Miner and Chanel have No training or knowledge of dealing with the medical issues the residents face everyday day and simply don’t care.  The three months I was there, they did not serve a single fresh fruit or vegetable.  The residents are picked up on the daily by ambulance because of illness partially due to the lack of fresh food!!!

The help with founding suitable housing is lacking and importance is put on getting $10 a day from people who have nothing and those who are desperately seeking shelter are put out because they couldn’t obtain a voucher or $10!!! Those who do manage to get a voucher are forced to chase after them on a weekly bases one by one at various locations using their own resources to do so!!!  The staff , some who have been there for years are not even qualified enough to have their own housing, some living in the shelter with grown family members using up space that should be provided to the truly homeless!!!  The staff is putting many in danger by letting people who are clearly under the influence of something to harass other patrons and refuse to hear your complaints or Threatening to put both parties out!!  In domestic abuse and child neglect cases they make excuses for the abuser!!!  There is no accountability for the behavior of the staff, not even when the scream, curse and attack the homeless!!!  When you try to sound alarm they escalate the situation to call the police and have the complaint removed!!!  I will make it my business to let donors as well as corporate know what is going on in that shelter!!!! Even the donations of two brand new computers Still set in the dining room collecting dust, because they have not been even plugged in or setup properly for 3 months!!!  The keyboards lay on the floor underneath the table!  I guess eventually they may end up in the possession of one of the staff.  They are not good stewards of any donations or anything but their own interest!!!

I’m calling for an immediate independent investigation of this shelter and an apology from Mrs Miner and Chanel for the treatment I received!!  Also Ms Q and Mrs Denise and Ms Kim every last one of them!!!

top_reviews.text:
I am grateful for the shelter that this organization provided for me and my family during our time of need. However, there are several issues that need to be addressed. Firstly, upon arrival, it became evident that this shelter is not particularly kid-friendly, despite being intended for families. There is no designated play area for the children, and if they happen to run around due to their energy, they are yelled at. The staff does not seem to be sensitive to the needs of children with disabilities.

Additionally, our room did not have a functioning toilet, and we did not have access to hot water for proper showers. It was not until my last day here that the toilet was finally fixed. Furthermore, we were placed in a room with a microwave that appeared to have caught on fire at some point. We were also lacking basic essentials such as bed linens, bath towels, and washcloths. I was given a tablecloth to use as a makeshift towel for myself and my two children. Despite the storage closet next to my room being full of toilet paper, I was told to purchase my own.

The rule requiring residents to stay out until 4:00 pm is understandable, but having to wait in a room for an additional 2 hours until 6:00 pm with children who have short attention spans seems unreasonable.

Lastly, I experienced what I consider to be an incredibly cruel act. When I waited in line at the food bank on a Thursday, I was informed that I could not receive food for myself and my children because I was a resident at the shelter. Even after explaining that I do not receive food stamps and that we had no food or snacks for my children, I was still denied assistance. I have never witnessed a "Christian" organization refusing to provide food for a mother and her children in my entire life.

top_reviews.text:
Historic Facts for all those shopping!

The site at 100 Jefferson Highway was home to an illegal casino known as O’Dwyer’s Club , which operated from about 1949 to 1951. It was part of a network of gambling venues run by the O’Dwyer family, who were involved in illegal gaming in Louisiana from the 1910s through the 1960s. Despite its unlawful status, O’Dwyer’s attracted large crowds nightly, offering patrons a chance to eat, socialize, dress up, and gamble in a time when much commercial gambling was prohibited by state law. The club’s popularity ended when Governor Jimmie Davis’s administration cracked down on illicit gambling operations, leading to its closure in the early 1950s.

Today the original building no longer operates as a casino — a Salvation Army store occupies the address where O’Dwyer’s Club once drew crowds. The legacy of O’Dwyer’s reflects a colorful chapter in Louisiana’s gambling history, when underground gaming halls played a lively role in local entertainment long before modern legal casinos emerged.

Awesome Awesome Awesome... The mission, the people, the passion, the purpose...

Being His hands & Feet is what we're supposed to do & be. Second Harvest gets it and does it well.

Second Harvest receives donations and they also purchase food and distribute it to the masses. Various churches, ministries, schools, individuals, agencies etc are able to receive food directly from Second Harvest Food Bank.

The word NO, doesn't exist here. Never have I seen a more benevolent group of people that are ALWAYS going over & beyond to help a person/families/groups in need.

This place is a haven goodness. The volunteers POUR in and give of themselves, tirelessly!!!

The senior boxes alone total 19,000 EVERY MONTH and volunteers come in daily shifts to assist with packing those boxes. PLUS, Second Harvest also feeds hot plates to senior citizens, lunch for school aged kids, good for pantries & still manages to do food giveaways to the general public that don't fall into the aforementioned categories.

This place is a god-send!!!

top_reviews.text:
What was I expecting?

I'm in a Lesbian marriage.

We got a thanksgiving basket
..... And it was like nothing. To top it off, it was in some woman's car when my wife went to pick it up, and they couldn't find it. I'm just so annoyed that they can blatantly discriminate against a couple. I know single people who received more in their basket than our family of 2. This is not okay. Next year, we will do something else than get a basket from them.

In response to the WONDERFUL MESSAGE the salvation army left, when my wife signed up, she said she was married. The person who signed her up IMMEDIATELY asked her HUSBAND'S name.

And.... We had to call THIS MORNING, because we do not have our own transportation, and ours fell through, so we made emergency plans.

So, yeah,  Jesus may not judge, but they sure do.

top_reviews.text:
I rarely stop here because every time I have it has been an absolutely horrible experience and after today I will NEVER shop here again.
Before today they have: overcharged my credit card twice, a woman working behind the register put a long rip in a piece of clothing I bought and couldn't understand why I didn't want it anymore and so many other similar instances.
Today was the final straw, there were two ladies working stockings racks, which is great and we all love to see new merchandise! The problem was they were continuously bumping into customers and one more or less pushed me out of the way to get to a rack, if she had said excuse me or let me know she was behind me I gladly would have moved aside. Then when my husband went to go into the dressing room the door was open, the bright green sign said vacant, he puts his hand on the knob to step in and a customer looking through racks screams at him that someone's in there. Which is fine, he apologized even if we were both confused, the customer then continued to berate him and call him rude and that he shouldn't be trying to go into an occupied dressing room, mind you she is yelling for the whole place to hear. Again the door was ajar and it said vacant. From our angle there was no way of telling someone was in there and further more who uses a dressing room with the door open? This all happened with the staff standing there watching, they didn't ask the person was in the dressing room to please close the door, they didn't ask the lady to stop screaming and they simply pretend like nothing was happening.
It was uncomfortable and upsetting to both my husband and I. As we walked out a lady in the parking lot stopped us and said she saw what happened and was also very upset by there lack of action and that it was totally out of line for the lady to scream and yell.
This place is not worth it.

Now as I sit here with a work ticket arriving ten minutes early to be courteous of their time, I realize, everybody arrived 5 minutes late, further more my time was not being respected and honored as I honored their time. But as I sit here I listen to the receptionist listen to a voice-mail complaint from a customer who left their number for resolution and he deletes it and makes a crass remark with some lively words, furthering even more negative experiences. I'm appalled by the behavior here. I ended up leaving after waiting nearly half an hour to do the work they hired me to do. Captain Michael you really need to clean up your crew. It's absolutely unacceptable and we expect more from a Christian organization.

top_reviews.text:
While I am extremely grateful for the food my experience was not good.
This was my first time at a food bank ever. I arrived at the location with no instructions. I followed the signs that led to a door with a doorbell. I rang it. The man on the other side put his hand up, shook his head no, and walked away from the door. Panicked, (thinking I missed my appointment I was told that I had when calling information, thinking my son and I would be without food) I yell through the window " please sir I have a 9 am appointment" he then comes to the door and says no you don't,"  so of course I am panicking even more I say " sir,  this is my first time here, I was told by the information line for this bank that I had a 9 am appointment". He cut me off before I could finish my sentence and said " no, no one would tell you that there are no appointments" When in fact that is what I had been told. He then gives me a nasty look and shuts the door. Because of this interaction I believe he purposefully gave us undesirable food options. I watched 3 people before me leave with cakes, loafs of bread, fresh fruits and vegetables.  I got 4 packs of tortillas, 38 total. 2 lbs of hazelnuts,  half of a half rotten watermelon that leaked all over the back of my car, expired raisin bran muffins,  and canned fruits and vegetables and a box of 240 pencils. Why?
I was the 4th person in line. I dont believe it was a matter of food running out, because when loading my groceries, the man in line behind me also got fresh fruits, a loaf of bread and a cake. While I am desperately in need of food, I do not feel comfortable coming back to this location because of the way I was treated. Its a really crappy feeling to be in need looking for help, and then have someone talk down to you like that and then have control over what food you receive. It was not a good experience. And disheartening at that.
top_reviews.author: Ashley Sellers

top_reviews.text: For a small thrift store operated solely by volunteers, this is by far one of the BEST local 2nd hand stores in the area! They have a "Cash Only Policy" because their philosophy is for people to live within their means and don't want to encourage credit card debt, especially for those with limited incomes. Yes, this can be difficult at times. As one who still prefers to pay in cash whenever possible, in a society that relies on plastic more & more, I relish the idea of using my cash here. This policy also allows every cent taken in to be used to pay the bills associated with running a business and to help with their other assistance programs. No, they are not open every day and not a lot of hours during the days that they are open.  If your schedule can accommodate a visit during the days & hours they are open, they won't disappoint. Excellent quality for 2nd hand items & reasonable prices! As with any 2nd hand store, their stock changes often. No paid workers here, only volunteers, who believe in the mission of the store & enjoy giving freely of their time. I noticed someone complained about the "No Stroller Policy," and I think it's a great policy. Too often, I've seen people park their kids someplace in a store (usually in the middle of an aisle, making it difficult for other shoppers to maneuver) while they continue to browse the store's merchandise without them being encumbered by the stroller or cart with their children. I've never had a bad experience here because of their prices, selection, or quality of merchandise, nor because of the generous volunteers or the store's policies. If you don't like their policies, shop elsewhere. If  you would like additional days or hours to shop, contact them to see what they require to accommodate that want. Just perhaps if they suddenly found themselves with a lot more volunteers willing to work additional days and hours, it could happen. As it stands, they don't have a huge army of volunteers to do more. I still prefer spending my money here than commercial thrift stores (Goodwill, for one) impersonating as charity thrift stores.

top_reviews.text: Google markets them as being handicapped accessible, but judging by their rules, I’m not certain. Regardless, they didn’t allow me into the store with my stroller because they supposedly didn’t have enough space for me. Looking around the store, they had enough space, they just didn’t want a stroller there. Not sure how you can hypothetically have space for a wheelchair but not a stroller, but who knows. Width wise, my stroller was the same size as a wheelchair. Length wise, it’s a bit longer, but very maneuverable. My guess is it’s not a space issue but a worry over theft issue, since the sign right next to it says no backpacks, or large bags. Regardless, the way I was all but shoved out the door (the sign about the strollers was inside, not outside And a woman was blocking it on my way in) felt very rude and I ended up just leaving with my baby since I didn’t have a different carrier option and I felt unwanted there. The way the lady seemed to look down at me also didn’t leave me with the warm fuzzies but it’s possible I’m over sensitive b/c I’m postpartum. Coupled with their ridiculous hours, and it seems like they don’t actually want people to come here. top_reviews.text:
2/13/2026. New update. Although the prices were getting a little bit better a couple of the women in the back room still have an attachment to free inventory. Rumor has it they spend way too much time researching items before they hit the floor.
New photos from today.

I stopped in on Christmas Eve eve, and I took a quick tour around the store and noticed that the prices are getting better. The only things truly overpriced cashmere, sweaters, and a few jackets. Keep up the good work! Let’s make thrifting fun again. The more you turn your inventory the more money you will make. Overpriced items change your business model from a thrift store to a storage unit. higher priced items will sit longer & you’ll end up ragging them out. Let’s work together to keep items out of the landfill.

* update * after not shopping here for 6 months I decided to see of thrifting was fun again. Ummmm, NOPE! Prices are sky high. The woman in the back who has the emotional attachment to the free inventory is rubbing off on her coworkers. Sad but true. Take a look at the items they feel are treasure. 🙄. Supposedly Brockton will be taking over pricing the inventory. I’ll keep shopping but choose other thrift stores.  Bye BW. Good luck selling your overpriced merch. One of the regulars
Told me the Brahman bag has gone through 3 half off days. lol

Prices are very high for a thrift store. Y’all get your inventory for free. Make thrifting fun again.

My response to Salvation Army.
Are you referring to competing with are retail prices? I am in your stores when employees are ragging items that didn’t sell & I look at what’s getting ragged out and it’s generally the overpriced items. Salvation Army can still make a very good profit keeping prices lower because people will buy more and you won’t be ragging out your overpriced inventory. Take a page out of the Goodwill price structure all sweaters are 4.99 All dresses are 7.99. Employees don’t get attached to the inventory. Make thrifting fun again.

top_reviews.text: While I understand how helpful the service center is in providing families in need with food etc, I came here several years ago inquiring about health insurance as they have workers who are supposed to assist you with your Masshealth application. I was 17 at the time and practically homeless, sleeping on my sisters couch. Even though I was within the income limits, I was told I was not eligible for Masshealth because I had enrolled in college. Because most colleges offer insurance plans to students, I was expected to purchase insurance through my school (which was thousands of dollars, which I could not afford!). Several months went by and I eventually was able to purchase a health plan that I could barely afford. At that point I had accumulated thousands of dollars of medical debt, between not having insurance for several months and then the copays of my extremely expensive Aetna college health insurance plan. When I called the Health Connector myself they were able to assist me with getting health insurance. Seeing as I was 17 at the time and just figuring out stuff on my own, I trusted the word of the staff here when she told me I was ineligible for Masshealth or a Health Connector plan. I wish I knew then what I know now, but it's too late. My experience was so unpleasant and the woman who was supposed to assist me clearly had no idea what she was doing. Staff here needs better training!

top_reviews.text:
Visiting this store always feels like a little adventure. You can come across something fun or unexpected, especially if you enjoy exploring a large variety of items. The atmosphere is lively—sometimes even a bit too energetic—but that’s exactly what makes shopping here unique and never boring.

There can be some hustle and bustle in different sections, yet I still end up finding things that genuinely surprise me in a good way. Sometimes the place gets quite busy and everyone is wrapped up in what they’re doing, but I actually like that sense of constant motion—the store has its own rhythm.

The staff is always active and on the move, keeping things in order and refreshing the selection, even if they work at a fast pace. I take it as a sign that the inventory stays updated and things never feel stagnant.

If you approach shopping here with a bit of patience and an open mind, you can uncover some real gems. For me, this place is all about surprises, variety, and enjoyable finds. And that’s exactly why I give it the highest rating.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: THIS PLACE SHOULD BE ASHAMED OF THEMSELVES! I have been accompanying my aunt to this store for years. Not only has she donated there for years but because of her love for this store I myself always donated there. The last time we went there we were both disgusted to see how the prices of clothes and products have doubled. First, everything they sell has been donated to them ( given for free to help those  who don’t have extra money to blow on clothes). Secondly, this is supposed to be a Christian founded store. For the management ( we asked who set the prices) to be up charging on second hand clothes that are donated to help those who need a hand during tough times or elderly people who live on a fixed income is disgraceful. My aunt is so completely disgusted that she will not be returning nor donating to them anymore and neither will I. She will be taking her business to Savers or looking elsewhere. The greed shown here has lost a longtime customer and I would bet she is not the only one. I will be contacting corporate or whoever I can to make a formal complaint. SHAME ON YOU PEOPLE!
top_reviews.author: Rachel A.

top_reviews.text: Most items are written on in SHARPIE to indicate the price. Not a sticker, not tape, not even chalk marker. Sharpie. Permanent marker with no hope of coming off. Even their glass items had this done so you can see without even touching the item that it is written on the bottom because glass is CLEAR. Also saw a bunch of things that were clearly dirty and many completely broken like toys missing legs or purses with missing clasps so you cannot close them. They clearly do not care at all about the things they sell, I get it is for charity so its cheap but why deface the items and lower their value before they are even sold? That lack of caring only hurts the charity, especially for resellers like me who will over look dirty items (you can always clean them), and will ignore broken items, but we cannot do anything with items that are written on like that. If you are a reseller, do not come here, they ruin their items before they even hit the shelves. Such a shame as not all Salvation Army stores do this and frankly NONE of them should!!

top_reviews.text:
Bob's Bins is a fantastic discount store that offers a wide selection of top-quality products at unbeatable prices. The store is well-organized and easy to navigate, making it easy to find exactly what you're looking for. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and always happy to help with any questions or concerns.

The selection of products at Bob's Bins is truly impressive. They offer a wide range of items, from household essentials to electronics and beyond. The products are all from top-quality stores, so you can trust that you're getting high-quality items at a fraction of the cost.

One of the things that sets Bob's Bins apart is the fantastic deals they offer. They are constantly updating their inventory with new products, so there's always something new to discover. And with the discounts they offer, it's easy to stock up on all your essentials without breaking the bank.

Overall, I highly recommend Bob's Bins to anyone looking for a great deal on high-quality products. Their selection, prices, and customer service are all top-notch, making it the perfect destination for all your shopping needs.

top_reviews.text:
Savers Pricing Needs a Rethink

Savers operates on donated goods, yet prices have climbed so high that many low income shoppers can no longer afford basic items. A secondhand shirt shouldn’t cost nearly as much as a new one.

If donations are given in the spirit of helping others, pricing should reflect that generosity. Savers should reassess its mission or risk losing the trust and support of its community.

Also, the return policy need to  be evaluated because their is no fitting room, and if you need to return Savers, do not give your money back.

name: The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center

top_reviews.text:
Poorly run store. Very overpriced.  I see the same things on the shelves for months. This is supposed to be a thrift store. They’ve forgotten that these are donated items. The object of the game is to get the stuff to sell so that you can make some money!
I was there last week, and I hate to tell you how much stuff they were throwing away. They were literally shattering the glassware and throwing away completely good usable items because they didn’t sell. I said “that’s disgusting, all you have to do is price it at $.50 or a dollar and it would sell; It’s all over priced that’s why it didn’t sell.” They agreed but said the manager wont allow them to do that!!!
I will never donate anything here again.
This place desperately needs a new manager.

-FYI: They copy and paste the same response onto every review!!!! Pathetic!
top_reviews.author: Julie Daigle

top_reviews.text:
Horrible. Way overpriced. Things that sell on eBay are 10x the price here! Old rusted lunchboxes are priced $150 or more. Dirty old used shoes for $99 or even over $200! Chipped cheap plaster bric a brac for $60.  Four chairs for a whopping $1000.

These are items that are donated by people for charity.

I’ve even seen stuff marked beyond its original price. Today one of the ladies asked a manager about the price of a kind of dirty coat and she told them $70!

You would think at such exorbitant prices, the store would be impeccable or even at least organized, but their organization goes as far as grouping clothes by color. Good luck searching for something that fits!Employees are often just standing around, or chatting on their phones. It boggles the mind.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center
address: 534 Grand Army of the Republic Hwy

top_reviews.text:
I am a loyal Salvation Army family store customer, have been for years. Today I was met with horrible service that left me questioning my years of support for this “charity shop”. While shopping, I had picked out maybe 5 clothing items and a jacket. I went to check out and was accused of removing the tag from the jacket? I was told by the cashier, Ashley, that I would have to pay $75 for this if I wanted it. I expressed that  I couldn’t justify paying that price point, so she took the jacket and threw it to the side. I asked to speak to a manager who came over to reason with Ashley. She said “I make the price points and this isn’t going lower than $75, you can come back on a half off day if you can’t afford it.” I am disappointed that I couldn’t get the jacket, but I am concerned about the behavior of this cashier. I asked for a receipt and she made a comment about “if your card goes through.” Salvation Army, from what I remember, receives their merchandise through donations. My mind instantly thinks of the sweet older woman who would be appalled to see this behavior over a jacket she donated in hopes it would find a new loving owner. This prioritization of profit is gross and intolerable, and Ashley’s behavior disregards the company’s values.

It was actually my birthday. You never know what someone is going through. I choose to believe Ashley may be kind at heart, but unethical and abusive business practices like this directly reflect a company’s values, and I’m conflicted about whether I will continue to support the Salvation Army. And Ashley, I hope when your birthday rolls around, you get a big cake and a jacket you love. ❤️
top_reviews.author: Sydney Noelle Cushing

top_reviews.text:
I want to know what happened to Ashley in reference to Sydney’s experience with the jacket.  Congratulating Sydney for “ keeping it honest” doesn’t cut it in my book.

I go to a thrift shop in my neighborhood and this would never happen there.  I have been to other thrift shops where they have been indifferent and sometimes discourteous, and I completely stopped donating my clothing and household items, and trust me they had gotten some beautiful things from me.

Your store clerk Ashley was having a bad day and took it out on the customer.  I don’t go out and spend my money to have to take somebody else’s bad attitude.  I also wonder if your manager has any authority in making decisions. It sounds like Ashley calls the shots.  Sorry, but you won’t be seeing me anytime soon.
top_reviews.author: M Watts

top_reviews.text: This store always had TONS of stuff to look through. They always have 2 colors off and they always have one color that is 99 cents. I’ve found some amazing deals here over the years, but sometimes you see an item marked way up, you just know it’s going to be there once 99 cent day rolls around. The colors change over on Tuesday I believe maybe Monday. I love that they seemed to have moved to sorting by size in all sections now vs sorting by color. Makes things  but easier.
top_reviews.author: Fashion Life

top_reviews.text:
I really enjoy this place. If you ACTUALLY LOOK, there are some really good finds here, I think the people of Taunton are just not used to how bins work. At an average thrift store, it is the workers who have to go less desirable items- for you! Hence why they charge higher prices. If you are willing to take the time and get a bang for your buck, it is absolutely worth it. I also have a washer at home, but you should wash clothing from all thrift stores prior to use. I have found some questionable things mixed in, but again, I usually take the time to look through the entire bins and find something awesome!
As far as customer service, they are also in my good graces. They have never once been mean to me & I'm pretty sure me and the older lady have opposing political values, but she has never treated me like less than, even though I look very strange. :) I hope to see this place keep coming around, as there are literally no bins in Massachusetts whatsoever!

I have attached a few photos of things I've found here. There's plenty more aside from this I have found 🥰

top_reviews.author: Rebecca Campbell

top_reviews.text:
I’ll start by saying I’ve been going here years off and on. I’ve donated so many items to this store including brand new items. I’ve shopped this store and spent money on home decor items.

So I’m truly disgusted by the way we were treated today. I entered the store with a very young toddler who was sitting in their stroller. A worker ran over to say I couldn’t bring it in by pointing at the corner and saying ‘no’ ‘no’. This was news to me as we were just in there with a stroller. Oddly enough, I have to explain why you keep your kid in a stroller: you can’t carry them everywhere, toddlers aren’t easy to handle in public places, we’re actually helping you out so our kid doesn’t knock over all your crap. A stroller gives them a space safe to sit while you shop, duh!

They want you to leave all your belongings on an unwatched shelf at the front of the store including small purses and bags. There’s no organizers or security to watch them so ANYONE can walk in and take your things. I asked if they had cameras facing the area and she didn’t say anything.

Said ‘okay’ took them out to try and walk them through the store and I have another employee run up to me and say ‘NO FOOD!’ So here I am standing with the kids snack jar being told I can’t bring him in his stroller and I can’t hold his snack. So I go back and put it away. I did a quick sweep and left because my child started crying. They were super rude and unapologetic.

I’ll never set foot back and I’ll never recommend them again. Disgusting and honestly discriminatory behavior. If a child has special needs would you expect a parent to walk their kid through? You’re asking for a lawsuit. Check your policies. If you’re so worried about people stealing hire security.

Yes, I called the store to speak with a manager and no one answers the phone.
top_reviews.author: ALEXIS JAMES

top_reviews.text: I’ve been coming to this place for years and I found some really great stuff. Recently, I found an item that actually did not work and they have a policy that you must have a receipt to return it. I couldn’t find my receipt, but the manager was kind enough to make an exception. I really appreciated her warmth and understanding. I’ll definitely keep being a customer for years to come.

name: The Salvation Army Waltham Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text: I went there this past Friday with a helper, who's homeless and he told me he would rather go hungry, than eat there,(that's the second time a homeless helper had told me the exact same thing) when asked why, he told me he was tired of Maria, the cooks rotten, abrasive, abusive and condescending attitude toward not just him but others as well. It didn't take long to see first hand what exactly what he was talking about. We got our meal and ate it because it was Friday, we were offered seconds and accepted, my helper got up and walked toward the serving window, someone had just mopped the area in front of the serving window, but there was no wet sign even though the salvation army has them and uses them everywhere else. Maria came running out of the kitchen and screamed at him "WHAT THE HELLS THE MATTER WITH YOU, CAN'T YOU SEE THE FLOORS WET. Chris said "I told you dave, I'll wait outside. Now I was busy on my phone, tried to ignore it, but when I got up, to get my seconds I accidently stepped on the section of wet floor, it was mopped before lunch was done and no warning sign. Then Maria yelled at me, "WHAT THE HELL IS THE MATTER WITH YOU, DIDN'T YOU HEAR WHAT I JUST SAID TO HIM. I said where's the mop I'll fix it right away. She Yelled "NO, YOU'LL GET THE HELL OUT OF HERE" I went straight to the lieutenants office and was told he was on vacation until next week. A few months back, she came running out into the parking lot to tell me to move my truck, when I asked why, she said it was too big to fit. The Salvation has the exact same size truck. I ran right past her to see the lieutenant, but again I was told he was on vacation, I let it go and still park in the parking lot. I saw the lieutenant since then as I was parking and he said nothing to me. Any other place she would have been fired immediately for yelling at a customer/client or whatever they call people who use their services. I know for a fact she was ordered to apologize to another customer/client for rude ignorant behavior in the past, but she doesn't seem to learn. This place runs on donations from people looking to help the poor, the Salvation Army is not a jobs program for the undiagnosed, untreated mentally ill. Another reason she should be fired, asking customer/clients to sign in more than once and under different names. She's asked me to do that several times. When you solicit funds to serve meals to the poor and you missrepresent the number of people beung served thats fraud.
top_reviews.author: David Hay

top_reviews.text: Just stopped into my local Salvation Army here in Fort Gratiot, Michigan, and I wanted to buy a book. I found a copy of a game guide but after a quick glance to see the condition of the book, I noticed two price stickers that showed the book at $13. I brought the book up to the register to see if the price was a mistake on someone else’s behalf only to be told that the book was $60 online at a retailer and so they marked it $13 because “It’s the lowest we could go on the book competitively.” For a book that was literally donated for no charge to the Salvation Army, they should not be price matching or scalping prices to compete with companies that sell new merchandise for retail price. I thought thought this company cared about giving to those in need and not about their wallet size? As a former employee, I am beyond disappointed and I recommend not shopping at your local Salvation Army if you’re looking to thrift. You’ll be treated like a weirdo for being uncomfortable with donated goods that cost too much.

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
This is a horrible location. I have been going to this location for many years but won’t be returning since the last two visits left me feeling very shocked. One of the young guys at the donation dock, and the store “manager” were horrible to deal with. The last visit I was dropping off donations. At some point during or right after Covid, they put out a sign by the donation dock that says to stay in your car. I thought this was a Covid - don’t spread your germs, thing. (So when I gather up my donations around the house, I collect items for Salvation Army, and other items for a woman’s shelter. so usually I have two sets of donations. Also I may have items in my trunk cuz they live in my trunk, such as a large basket I use for produce when I go to the grocery store.) So I stepped out to make sure the employee grabbed the right box. An older gentleman told me that a young guy would be out to meet me, so I didn’t need to lift the box. Then he disappeared inside. The young guy came out and told me I have to stay in my car. I explained that I needed to make sure he grabbed the right box since I had other stuff there. Then he got snotty and asked me if I could read the sign. So I said again, that I was just making sure he got the right box cuz I didn’t want him to take the other stuff. So he said super annoyed,  “You can see the sign, right?” (What? Seriously bro?
Do they think people who are donating are going to steal from the clothing bin outside the dock?) I said, well if you’re not going to allow me to make sure you don’t take the wrong boxes then I guess I’ll have to make my donations elsewhere. And his response was “yea, do that. Don’t donate here if you can’t stay in your car.” So that is what I will do. There’s a Good Will at Ford and Telegraph which is closer to my house so I will do that from now on.

The second to last time I made a donation here, I went in to shop. I bought a dining table and 4 chairs they had for sale. I paid for the item and returned later with a friend to help me load it. An employee got us a big  flat bed type cart to load it, but it looked big to fit thru the front door so I asked if we cud got thru the back which was right there, to the dock, which was another 20 feet and out the back. She said she would ask and disappeared in the back. She came out and said yes you can go out the back. So we loaded it all on the cart and we were bringing it thru the back, just like the employee said we could. Suddenly a really tall guy starts yelling at us “What are you doing back here! You can’t be back here!” We explained that we were told we could go out the back since the table was so wide and it wouldn’t fit out the front door. He kept yelling “Who said you could! I am the manager! You cannot be back here! I am the manager! I didn’t give you permission!” I seriously wanted to reassure him that “HE IS THE MANAGER AND THE WHITE LADY WASN’T USURPING HIS AUTHORITY. ITS ONLY BECAUSE ITS A BIG ITEM AND IT CANT FIT THRU THE FRONT DOOR. ITS NOT THAT DEEP!” So we had to go back into the store and disassemble the entire table, and bring it out the front door in grocery carts.

Maybe this place gets robbed a lot or something? Ugggggg Just never mind. Not going back here again.
top_reviews.author: C'est Moi

top_reviews.text: I delayed in writing this but decided it was important to do so in case anyone else was thinking of donating to this particular Salvation Army. When I'm giving to the Salvation Army or Goodwill I give gently used thing. Including beautiful guest bedroom blankets, sheets, clothing, kitchen wares and electronics. The one particular day I pulled up an an older white guy came for the donations. I had lots of decorative pillows that were clean and showed no wear. When he got a few things out of the back seat of my car, he said you should have just thrown all this stuff away. What, I asked. These pillows and blankets you could have just thrown them all away. I felt judged and unappreciated. It was such a negative experience. I was made to feel like they were above what I had to offer. I dropped similar items off at Goodwill earlier and they were so gracious. I told them I was splitting the donations between them and Salvation Army. My suggestion to you if you're looking to make a donation is not make a donation at this place. Because you don't want to get that same ugly guy that spoke to me that way. You'll  drive away never wanting to go back. For  an organization that affiliates itself with "Christianity", you displayed zero Christian behavior.
top_reviews.author: Kim Carson

top_reviews.text: Parking is easy, but this store location has a “we don’t care” attitude. Staff was unnecessarily rude at register to two customers while I was there. When it was my turn to check out, they continued chatting and playing with their phones, ignoring my presence until they felt like doing their jobs; very unprofessional attitude. One of the items I bought was supposed to be part of a set - it was marked “2 pieces/$10,” but the other half was missing. Neither woman was interested in helping look for it, but one said I could buy the single piece, which I opted to do. Instead of charging me half price for half ($5 of the $10), she randomly chose to charge me $7. She didn’t even bother to tell me; I just happened to notice. When I asked about it, she rolled her eyes and said, “Yeah, I charged you $7. You want it or not?” SO much attitude. After responding in the affirmative, I stayed quietly polite and left. If you hate your job that much, maybe look for a different one instead of taking it out on your customers?? Side note - the guys manning donation drop off have always been lovely.

name: Salvation Army West Michigan Harbor Light

top_reviews.text:
An excellent place to go if you have an out of control addiction and need help. Or if you just fell off and need a hand getting back up.

Friendly staff, smoke breaks, ample time to socialize and work out our problems amongst ourselves... the place is amazing. And welcoming to people that return.

We can't all always get it right on the first go around. Sometimes it takes two, three, four... hell, even thirty tries. But admitting that there's a problem and working to fix it is the first step. And this place is an excellent resource if you need that kind of help.

I'm also an atheist. If you're worried about going to a church-affiliated group, don't be. They take a light touch with religion (mostly stuff in the daily readings), and try to be open to everyone. Same goes for LGBTQ+ folk: this is a safe place.

If you need help, these folks are who you need to get started

I have eaten lunch at the SA for several weeks talking to many of the people who attend regularly... Everyone I have talked with including myself always leave with the feeling of family and belonging... I have observed the Corps Officers dealing with others in a gentle and loving manner regardless of our individual walk in life... I was in the Dollar Store in Hillsdale, there was discussion going on about how valuable the Salvation Army has been to the Hillsdale and surrounding communities... America is in great need of the Godly resources that the SA provides, I have seen the hand of God is working through the Salvation Army across the world... The Hillsdale Corps is no acception, I could never express the loving care the SA has shown me over many decades...May God Bless You All For All the Good You Do in GOD'S name throughout the years...

top_reviews.text: I signed up for Christmas help back in October over the phone. They were understanding then and knew I wouldn't be able to come in because I just had major back surgery. I explained how I had another surgery scheduled for December 5th and that I might not be able to even pick up. They told me I could have someone pick up for me. I'd just need to write a note and they show photo ID. I asked if I could call back with someone who could do it. I called back and let them.know my BF would pick up for me. That was the end of that. I get a call a week later stating I needed proof of his income because I said he was in the home. I informed them that was never said. He is not in the home so his income doesn't matter. They kept insisting I told them he was. I got frustrated hung up and called back. Spoke with a major Heidi. She said she would look into it. She called me back and left a VM stating I either need to bring something notarized stating what his income is or his ID showing he is not in the home. I decided to go with him today in case we needed to pick out any clothes or anything for my kids. Get all the way there and get told that they are not helping me. That I did not complete my application. They tried to call me 3 times yesterday and my VM box was full. That they were informing me that I needed to bring something notarized stating he isn't in the home. That if I had answered my phone they could of helped me today. They never called me, my VM box is not full. Not only that but I called them numerous times yesterday trying to see what time I needed to be there. Spoke with one person who said there is no designated time to just show up at 10. Was not told anything then when I called. So not only am I out that gas for going there but now I'm left with no help for Christmas just weeks before. Seriously so cold and rude on them to turn away someone in their time of need. Not only that but someone who's had 2 major surgery in a matter of months!
