name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
I’ve visited this thrift store several times, and I’ve noticed a few consistent things.
The store is generally organized and there’s always a wide variety of items to browse, which I really appreciate.

However, many of the prices feel surprisingly high for secondhand items. I’ve seen simple glassware close to $10, damaged items still priced near full value, and purses that cost more than brand-new ones at big retail stores.
It can make shopping here feel a bit discouraging.

Another concern is the atmosphere toward closing time....
About an hour before closing, most of the lights are turned off, the dressing rooms are already locked, and the staff can come across as impatient and unwelcoming.
It becomes difficult to shop when the store is nearly dark and you feel like you’re being rushed out, even though there is still time left before closing.
Overall, there are good finds here, but the pricing and customer experience — especially in the evenings — make me hesitant to shop at this location as often as I’d like due to feeling like an inconvenience. 😅
top_reviews.author: Amber C

top_reviews.text:
I don’t usually leave reviews for thrift stores
and appreciate what they do for the community.
However, today I was very disappointed.

I asked an associate about their authentication process for higher-priced designer bags and was told that a Coach bag priced at $24.99 was authentic. I was specifically told they use an app to scan items in the back to confirm authenticity.
After checking with a knowledgeable resale group that specializes in Coach and higher-end bags, the bag was confirmed to be fake.
Despite this, it was being sold as authentic, with no paperwork and no option to return.

This feels very misleading, especially with the rising prices lately. I hope the store improves transparency and authentication practices.

name: Salvation Army - Soup Kitchen & Food Pantry
The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: If you have the chance to visit the Salvation Army in Michigan, you'll find the prices much cheaper than in Canada. I bought an exercise bike for $3, most clothing is under $5, men's shirts are $1.45, and aluminum pots and pans in very good condition are also under $5. This place is also clean and the employees are very friendly. Many thanks to those who make stores like these possible.
top_reviews.author: Magda Gtz.

top_reviews.text: Not a good experience. I came in to browse and had store credit that I was told could be used anywhere in Michigan, which turned out not to be true. When I brought this up, the man I spoke with was very rude and dismissive and wouldn’t even let me get a word out. Poor customer service and very disappointing.
top_reviews.author: makayla santangelo

top_reviews.text: Clean and well organized. Very fair prices on most items. Staff was very friendly.
top_reviews.author: Nikki Merrick

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Used to be much better.  The store is grungy and not well kept up, but I used to find lots and lots of good things.  Now, not much inventory.  Add to that the resale hawks (people who buy and resell in their own stores or online) who line up at the door for the dollar deals and race through the store throwing all of the low priced items in their baskets before anyone else can even look at them.  Yuck.  Two words for would-be shoppers - don't bother!
top_reviews.author: L Joes

top_reviews.text: One of my favorite resale shop. My friend and I do a girl's day out and spend the day visiting several SALVATION ARMY shops. We always find something to purchase. Our "shopping" day is Wednesday to take advantage of senior discount. Needless to say we are greatly disappointed that the shops have changed the senior discount rate. 20% made it worth our day out....the new senior discount of 10% not so much!
top_reviews.author: Anna Garrett

top_reviews.text: Prices are insane. The company as a whole needs to slash prices in half on all products. It was donated for free, I am tired of their corporate excuses.  You can still help people in need without price gouging donated items. This location used to be the best.
top_reviews.author: Rae Rae

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: I had a really positive experience at this store. It’s very well-organized and the prices are great. I ended up finding a solid wood coffee table I liked but I couldn’t find the price tag. I asked an employee about it and he dropped what he was doing to come and help me. It turned out the price tag was underneath one of the many TVs on top of the table (he moved them all for me)! I also met the manager, who helped with the tag issue, and she was really sweet. The people who work here are truly kind! Bonus points to the customer who helped me load my car. This visit made my week!
top_reviews.author: Hannah Breyer

top_reviews.text: Don’t bother shopping here, people will just take from your cart and management will do nothing to help you. I just left empty handed after spending 2 hours in the store shopping because someone took all of the clothes that I’d already tried on and decided to buy from my cart while I was in the dressing room. A woman who worked there tried to help me but when she called the manager over to help she told me there’s nothing she can do. I asked if she can check the cameras and was told no. What a waste of my day, thanks!
top_reviews.author: Takala Havermahl

top_reviews.text: Big shout out to the staff at this location! They were so kind and helpful, not just to customers, but to fellow staff members as well. Everyone sounded like they genuinely enjoyed each other's company and that makes any day or place better 🥰 An extra shout out to the person on register (name on my receipt was Madeleine). She was extra awesome and helpful. Thank you to all!
top_reviews.author: Rebecca

name: The Salvation Army Great Lakes Division

top_reviews.text: As a Christian based place organization you would think they would be somewhere who accepts and forgives. They are nothing but a cult. They do a 7 year background check. Now I did get introuble 14 years ago but since they I haven't really gotten into trouble with the law. I was denied a job as a bell ringer because of my 14 year old felony. This cult just appoints whomever they want to lead people. Folks, you wanna reach God you can talk to him yourself. You can praise as you would like. You don't need man who is no better than you telling you what to do. A Christian based organization who judges people. CULT!!!!!! Please use a different organization like Gleaners, who actually helps people, not judge them. This cult and other salvation cults will be audited and posted to my YouTube channel. Time cult leaders pay.
top_reviews.author: FireStarter Publications

top_reviews.text: Salvation Army 16130 Northland Drive Southfield Michigan please stop sending my dad requests for donations. He used to give donations but now he's in Hospice. His name is Gerald and his last name begins with an M but I won't put it here. He lives 5836 Applewood Apartment 1207 West Bloomfield Michigan 48322 thank you very much for taking him off of your mailing list. After you do so please remove this review if you can there was no other way to reach you other than this. Bye for now
top_reviews.author: nancy4366

top_reviews.text: Everyone who I spoke with at this location are wonderful! There was an issue with my donation and the lady took care of it quickly.
top_reviews.author: Beatrice Birdsong

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: I have worked many cash registers in my life and it's always the most difficult at close with the last few customers taking forever and not knowing when it's time to leave. So I understand that frustration. Well I was the very last customer tonight and there was one woman being cashed out before me and my goodness.... She was an interesting character. On top of being eccentric she also took AGES deciding if she was going to buy items she had in her cart or not. The girl working the register is a much better person than I am because she handled this customer like a true saint. She never once showed any frustration and she smiled and laughed with her as if it wasn't 20 minutes after close. I am so impressed with the customer service because of her and her amazing attitude. Tahsheera you are such a patient and kind employee and whatever you get paid now needs to be doubled because you'd deserve every penny. Good job Salvation Army!!!
top_reviews.author: R. K.

top_reviews.text: To the angry old black man that took my items please know your own policy before telling me I can only get one slip your policy states that I could get as many slips as needed. I told you I have five different donations from five people, and you told me you could only give me one slip per car per day. I would like for your staff to be trained on policy one and customer service. I won’t be back cause I live out of state. Also watch your tone you never know what a person’s attitude is about sign. You never know who I was secret shopper.
top_reviews.author: Butterfly Ice

top_reviews.text: Staff is always friendly and helpful however, I am very unhappy with how the pricing has significantly creeping up in the store.  I realize that the proceeds go toward very important programming but the pricing is along the lines of resale instead of thrift stores.  Often I can find cheaper new clothing on clearance at retail stores.  The discount for Seniors, Teachers, Mililtary has also changed from 25% to 10%, why?
top_reviews.author: Michele Davis

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Found a superb pan to cook and it made up for the juicer we got. Juicers are frightening. I enjoy the store have been a lot and like the items they put out in the front middle to highlight because I usually like them a lot. Fun. Oh and the books! Great selection of books and records and cds if that’s your thing. I am a cd player user for life or I guess we’ll see!
top_reviews.author: Emily Morsello

top_reviews.text: Went to donation drop off with boxes of Christmas decor. No one came to help me unload. I was told to leave it all by the door. How rude & thankless. Hopefully they didn't throw the boxes around. Probably won't be coming back here to donate.
top_reviews.author: Mary Nagy

top_reviews.text: Definitely no “public” restrooms. Go potty before you shop.
top_reviews.author: Alyce Fetterhoff

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Actual store employees are great, however the donation center employees are some of the rudest people I’ve ever encountered. Not once did they say anything nice to me. I asked if they had a cardboard box I could move my stuff to so I could keep my tote and he replied “if you didn’t want to donate your bins you should’ve brought them in boxes. We can’t touch your stuff” I then informed him I would move the stuff myself but needed to keep the totes. He almost didn’t take the stuff because of it. Then I asked for a receipt and he asked why I would need one and made me fill out the form myself of what I was donating verses him filling out the form.
The workers in the donation room are extremely rude and I will not be donating any more items here again. Recommend you find somewhere else to donate your stuff.
top_reviews.author: Molly Cottrell

top_reviews.text: Prices have increased. No Teacher, Student, EMS discounts anymore. Senior and Veterans reduced to just 10% off. Manager just shrugged me off when mentioned. I understand this is a corporate decision but you’re already getting my donations for free and now you want to rob me of my discount too? Don't bite the hand that feeds you Salvo! Grace Centers of Hope will be getting all my future donations, they still reward their customers with 50% off every Wed and Sat. On a positive note: Cashiers are great and very friendly at this store.
top_reviews.author: Jethro

top_reviews.text: I find it weird how this location is the only one that turns off all the sales and outdoor lights 30 minutes before closing and doesn’t allow people to come in, I could see 5 to 10 mins before but a half hour before closing is unacceptable towards people’s safety, especially in a snowy icy parking lot. Update the hours so people don’t waste their time coming to your store
top_reviews.author: Florence

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: It's my understanding this is a new location. The store was clean and nicely organized. I thought the prices were fair. My only problem was there wasno one at checkout. When I first came in, I noticed another customer waiting at the front, then afee minutes later when I had something I wanted to buy, again no one was there. My husband had to go find someone because we stood there several minutes without anyone noticing. Maybe a bell, or a clear line of sight from the backroom to the front of the store is needed....just suggestions.
top_reviews.author: Linda M

top_reviews.text: This Salvation Army has lost it’s mind. I’ve been thrifting for over 20 years and have stopped at pretty much every thrift store in the lower half of Michigan and this store has the most laughable pricing I have ever seen. I don’t mind paying fair prices for quality things but this store has worthless tchotchkes priced at $29.99. The old location had more merchandise that was more interesting and prices that made sense. I don’t think I’ll be back.
top_reviews.author: Audrey Zofchak

top_reviews.text: Super disappointed I came to return some Timberland boots I purchased for my 4-year-old, they are brand new! I came to return them because they don't fit and the manager Heather tells me that they don't return shoes. There's nothing posted in the store at all and I've been shopping here since 2005 and never heard such a thing. How about you guys posted in the store! Put it on your website or something. Literally perfect condition
top_reviews.author: Marsha Beaudoin

name: Salvation Army Food And Meal Site - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text: I found this food pantry to not be helpful at all, I went during the hours listed for Monday and Thursday - the woman working at the front desk flatly turned me away while yelling not for any specific reason but she had decided to close the pantry that day and not help people. She was belligerent, angry, and rude - do not go to these people for help. It's obviously some weird front group and also she was bizarrely dispensing whole turkeys to people on some list and I doubted any of them were actually needy based on her behavior. Totally weird. Update: I went back in the Spring, just once and it was better....
top_reviews.author: Deborah Corey

top_reviews.text: Nice variety of food and some hard goods like sunglasses and stuff. It's out side and waiting is longer then expected
top_reviews.author: Isaac Popa

top_reviews.text: Incredible people here doing God's work please pray for and support them
top_reviews.author: Del Kollhoff

top_reviews.text: Receptionist Kate Dafoe was incredibly rude. I called the Restore and was told I need to come here and ask for Patty to receive a voucher. She yelled rudely as soon as I walked in because I was looking for the restroom. Her tone acted like she was disgusted to see a human being. She said she would help me, then hassled me for a voucher because I don't have a local address. I am disabled and homeless, if I had one I wouldn't be here. Why hassle people for vouchers to a store that receives free items? The voucher was for $50, and with the ridiculously high Restore prices that might get me 4 clothing items. Her behavior is on par with all the religious organizations I've had to deal with. Shame on you.
top_reviews.author: D R

top_reviews.text: The Salvation Army co-sponsored the Sara Lee Cares event honoring our hometown heroes and helped provide transportation to the event for attendees.  Their volunteers were some of the nicest, easiest going, and funniest(!) people you could ask to meet.  Grand Traverse would not be the same without them.
top_reviews.author: Mikhail Flip

top_reviews.text: Thank you so much for helping people in their times of need
top_reviews.author: Jeramy Walker

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
We were looking for a couch and making the rounds of all the resale shops in TC.  While we were in Salvation Army they were bringing out a new couch and I asked the manager if they had any more in the back :)
He then took us to their "storage facility" and let us look at more options!  What a great guy!  Definitely went above and beyond.  We got a great 'new to us' couch thanks to his great customer service!
top_reviews.author: Heidi Wilker

top_reviews.text: The staff was so friendly! They kindly held some shirts i really wanted for a few hours until I came back just off my good word. The selection is pretty decent 👌
top_reviews.author: Bradford's Best

top_reviews.text: Not a huge store and not super great stock overall but there are some excellent vintage finds if you have the time to look.
top_reviews.author: Jen Djuracic

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Clean store and well stocked with quality products.  Store is so nice!  I scored a real nice pair of nearly new Eddie Bauer shoes and a North Face top.  At first I thought the prices were high for a thrift store, but after really diving in I realized that the products were top quality and the prices were good.
top_reviews.author: Tammy Wodarczak

top_reviews.text: My favorite thrift store!  You never smell an odor like in other places. Everything is clean, organized, and displayed nicely. There is always a great selection of items. The staff is so nice.
top_reviews.author: Lynn G

top_reviews.text: Nice clean store with some very good buys. I bought 5 articles of clothing for under $20. Little bit of everything your looking for. This store does not have that typical must smell.
top_reviews.author: Michelle & Shannon luv 2 eat

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Third strike, final straw. This location apparently doesn't realize there are 3 other SA stores within a couple miles. Friday Jan 2, spent 45 minutes choosing items. Love thrifting cuz it's good for the environment n helps reduce costs in retirement. 8:45 PM there is a line of customers waiting to check out. Mgr on duty closes one register so we can wait longer and goes about doing nothing useful that we can see. Finally at register and cashier refuses to ring up a birdbath marked $1.99 and calls mgr over to back up her decision.  Geeze, they had scratched platters with peeling paint tagged $14.99 - get a grip! I should have left my entire lot and walked off. Instead will visit the other local stores hoping for better experience with employees. The people serving matter. Do better.
top_reviews.author: Sandy A

top_reviews.text: I had a great experience visiting this thrift store! They offer amazing deals and a wonderful collection of items—from clothes to home decor and more. Everything is well-organized, and the prices are a little bit high compared to new items but honestly It’s the perfect place to find hidden treasures without breaking the bank. Highly recommended for anyone who loves great finds and good value!
top_reviews.author: Rana Ayoub

top_reviews.text:
The lady at the cash register was very helpful and friendly. The whole place is well-kept and clean. Loved the selection of clothes. Not as crowded as other popular Salvation Army locations nearby.

Got a lot of maternity bottoms compared to other locations. I got L and XL long tops since they didn't have a lot of those for maternity. Great prices.
top_reviews.author: Katia Barretto

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Mom and I love shopping at thrift stores with Salvation Army being our favorite thrift to shop at. We are from Sterling Heights so it took us about 50 minutes to visit this particular thrift store. It's fun to see all the different Salvation Army locations.

This store was huge and clean. My guess is it is so huge because it used to be a Kroger's grocery store. I'm so happy it was converted to a Salvation Army vs, say a Halloween Store, lol!

There was a huge selection of wares from art to clothes to appliances with wide isles to navigate. I push mom in her transporter chair so we appreciate the wide isles.

The location is ideal, close to the 59 freeway with plenty of parking outside.

I purchased a like new black cardigan sweater and a nice dressy tank top for when the warm weather returns. I also found a cool flower emblem that I added to one of my purses. Mom struck out and went home empty-handed. Everything was had for a mere $16.00 - how fun is that!
top_reviews.author: Kelly Smith

top_reviews.text: I get that Christmas was a few days ago and I didn’t mind waiting 20 minutes in the donation line but when I finally got up there, the worker told me that none of my items were in good enough condition to be donated. I had a fully functional CLEAN Keurig, K cup holder, crockpot, and kitchen storage (items that a family i need could definitely use) and they “passed” on it. This location has been going down hill for years, if you go in the store, the shelves are bare and this is why.
top_reviews.author: Ashley Pierson

top_reviews.text:
Prices are good, store is organized, and location is great. However, the cleanliness of the carpets are terrible by the entrance and cash registers  Please consider replacing these. They are really bad.
I love donating and supporting such a great organization. 🍁
top_reviews.author: Do La

name: The Salvation Army Warren Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
I was there at the M.A.T.T.S. Program. They was respectful, helpful, and very patient with rude people.
The people there with children should really keep an on their children, not let them run around.
They help you if you want to help yourself and your family.
They have good meals. The salvation army helps out a lot. They have a social service there that helps you out.
You call and then go up there before 8:30 to see if there is a open bed.
Thank you Salvation Army 🙏 you have been so helpful.
top_reviews.author: Roberta Waellus

top_reviews.text: New owners finally raised the prices and changed the deals. Including getting rid of the 25% for veterans everyday and only making it Mondays - 10%. Will no longer be donating or spending money here. They put out fake designer and raise the prices on those as well. Every piece of clothing is about 2-5$ more then is used to be last year.
top_reviews.author: Vee

top_reviews.text: went here after calling sat on the parking lot but after reading some of the reviews I left doing the Indy 500 off the parking lot. this place only helps certain people the rest they rudely discharge.
top_reviews.author: Yvonne Harris

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Won't be shopping here again, unfortunately, so I wanted to leave a review as to why. Place is really small, no fitting rooms would fit unless they converted a bathroom into a changing room. I understand no color sales until October, but I was here Sept 30th, a Tuesday, and still no specials. They should've started it on Monday. They have lots of clothes, shoes, outerwear, kids items, home decor, decent furniture selection, but I really needed bed sheets and pillows and found nothing. The rack is maybe a few feet long worth of all the bedding/ towels/ pillow cases they have. Other thrifts have several aisles worth. The pricing is inconsistent. I found a great pair of like new pants at $2.99, then the next similar style and brand, $14.99. Many basic shirts $2-$4, great, then suddenly $12.99. Snow shoes I was interested in, $39.99, I couldn't believe it. I picked up so many items to put them right back. What is the point of a thrift store? 4 coasters they wanted $3 a piece for and I found them all scattered in different aisles, lucky to complete the set, I took them but it wasn't a fair deal, they should have been $6 for the set maybe $8 in a bag together. Just a let down over all, employees are very welcoming and friendly, but I will not be back since there are better locations who put a little more thought in pricing fairly, keeping sets together, etc.
top_reviews.author: Laura Sosa

top_reviews.text: I'm not impressed with the new location. First of all they have no changing rooms. So if your clothes don't fit, you have 3 days to return for a store credit. Also for the first several months, no color tag discounts at all. So for a 3T pair of USED sweatpants for my toddler grandson it was $3.99. Better off shopping on marketplace!
top_reviews.author: Lori Bryant

top_reviews.text: Prices here are a complete joke now. The store is TINY and the men’s section is basically nonexistent. Charging $28 for used free people shorts is crazy. I will not be back to the new location.
top_reviews.author: Maddy Miller

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Nice store but their register stopped working before taking payment and the manager didn't say a word about it just made us stand in silence for 15 mins while they tired to fix it. Stuff happens but you could at least do your best to make up for it and not hold my day up. Ended up leaving eventually.
top_reviews.author: New Angle Makeup

top_reviews.text:
Line was way too long for them not to have had more than just one cashier. Staff was hanging clothes and no one cared that the line was so long.
So I left without buying anything.
About $40 worth.
top_reviews.author: jenn furd

top_reviews.text: Very nice and clean store. Needed help and the Manager Diane that help me was very polite and helpful will send my friend and family to that store.
top_reviews.author: Matthew Laptosh

name: The Salvation Army Wayne Westland Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
Love this church! They have done so much for my family, and the Sunday service is awesome. We start at 9 AM for those who may be interested..

I also love all the youth activities they have throughout the week to help keep kids off the streets and out of trouble, as well as their summer programs.

They also have a women's ministry group that meets on Tuesdays at 5pm that is very fun group of ladies!
top_reviews.author: Kialee Rodwell

top_reviews.text: If the donors cars are lining up on weekends, there should have been more volunteers working at the donation gate. Donors cannot afford donating goods while wasting time lining up for half an hour.
top_reviews.author: Dr. Q

top_reviews.text: Wonderful kind organization help me in my time in need as well as my family definitely suggest
top_reviews.author: nick helton

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Normally I love this store and the workers…We really never had a bad experience here until the women with white hair working asked my partially deaf friend “Am I not speaking English” when telling him move. So rude and never had anyone ask him that. I was speechless when I saw the way she was speaking to him. She was very very rude and shouldn’t be working with customers EVER.
top_reviews.author: Jennifer Whitehead

top_reviews.text: First time visit and found a couple good deals and saved more for Senior or Military. Lots of parking. Books only 99 cents. Clothes could be more organized and I had a hard time finding jeans in any meaningful order. Saw size 34 in an XL rack. Also, they don't supply bags so keep that in mind.
top_reviews.author: Brian Csikos

top_reviews.text: So the employee Luke makes the experience! I would specifically choose to go to this salvation army specifically because he works there. I only met him today and me and my Girlfriend had a blast shopping and his personality is charismatic and he is super helpful! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ To Luke!
top_reviews.author: S. B.

name: The Salvation Army Downriver Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army Downriver Corps Community Center is absolutely fantastic! From the staff to the services they provide, you truly feel that agape love. I highly recommend their food pantry, they go above and beyond to make sure your family has a good amount of food based on your household size, and you can really tell they care.
To the staff, thank you for always being kind and caring!
top_reviews.author: Ariel Wade- Welch

top_reviews.text: I used to go there as one of the kids and they do like babysitting service, most of the employees/Staff are super mean and they barely serve us any food. The only real good one is Ms Anna. Also, they are very mean to the kids but very nice when their parents show up
top_reviews.author: Kenneth Stone

top_reviews.text: If you need food or clothes this the place and they are very helpful and very kind
top_reviews.author: Miss Michelle Hamel

top_reviews.text: We went on one of the nastiest weather days this year. The staff was warm,  welcoming and helpful. We found Christmas gifts for our granddaughters and a few clothing items for us. Any question we asked was answered cheerfully. They even did an internet search, for a brewery I asked about on one of the coasters by the register. We left with a large shopping bag and spent less than $25.00! Highly recommend. We'll be back.
top_reviews.author: Brian Otto

top_reviews.text: We stopped in for the first time yesterday and were absolutely charmed by this clean, well-organized, and welcoming thrift store! As avid thrift shoppers, we were thrilled to discover such a delightful gem. The owner herself rang us up, and her warm, friendly service made our visit even better. The selection was fantastic—we can’t wait to come back and treasure hunt again soon!
top_reviews.author: Sherrie Brindley

top_reviews.text: Tons of things from throw backs to recent clothes. Prices are reasonable. Clean and organized. DVDs , VHS board games ,
top_reviews.author: C Green

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: The people are usually very kind and most items are clean, overall the store is well maintained and not cluttered like some other thrift stores these days. Prices are usually mid range and the discounts are usually very good.
top_reviews.author: Caden

top_reviews.text:
Good thrift shop,

Note, if you have a backpack, they will ask you to leave it at the front of the store.
top_reviews.author: Brandon Johnson

top_reviews.text: Great prices and clean. Well stocked with many must have items at low cost  good staff.
top_reviews.author: Donald H

name: Salvation Army Albert Lea - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text:
A tad confusing but SA set me up nicely with a hulking box of food MY ONLY CRITICISM IS the lack of drink.

Only a mere can of flavored water but OVERALL O(1)CE A MONTH and it's GOOD!
top_reviews.author: DANG! X

top_reviews.text: Friendly
top_reviews.author: Sandy Stone

name: The Salvation Army Church and Food Shelf

top_reviews.text:
I see a lot of reviews are for the store and this location is the church/food shelf...

The church is filled with many people who just want to help make others lives a little easier. From as simple as a church service to putting clothes on the back of children. Its a great place to go to find help and peace of mind.
top_reviews.author: Tabitha Hayek

top_reviews.text:
Amber always goes above and beyond to try to help anyone,  even though at times I can tell she might be inwardly frustrated with "the system " and the funding available to use . and I think she wishes she could " do more" .
she is always cheerful, positive and has kind words .
top_reviews.author: Jennifer

top_reviews.text: They are always super friendly and super helpful!! I always get a lot of food and it's really good!!  It's not like some of the food shelves I've been to where the food spoils within a couple days of you getting it home! This food is always good!!!
top_reviews.author: A Hummel

name: Salvation Army Austin - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text: Picked up some food from the food shelf . Much appreciated . Thanks to workers and volunteers .
top_reviews.author: Samuel E. Thorpe

top_reviews.text: Nice polite Christian people very helpful
top_reviews.author: N.A.P.D. Outreach

top_reviews.text: God bless you 🙏 ❤️
top_reviews.author: Filomina Hawle

top_reviews.text: Poor not much help given to those who need it. They don't keep up on there food there have been sometimes I gotten food that was months old and some of the food will go bad faster then you can eat it. I wouldn't support them on anything.
top_reviews.author: Wickedjoejoe 86

top_reviews.text: Preaching the TRUTH from the BIBLE... Not a singlet or interpretation ... Bible chapters and verses are visible on large screen so you can follow along with the Sermon
top_reviews.author: N.A.P.D. Outreach

top_reviews.text: Facility is somewhat outdated but the staff are utilizing the space as best as they can. Programs and services offered are well needed in the community.
top_reviews.author: John Gray

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Update (2026): I recently visited the The Salvation Army Family Store and noticed changes to their discounts. Veterans now receive 10% off every Monday, and Seniors receive 10% off on Wednesdays, replacing the former 50% off clothing discounts. Weekly deals like Toddler Tuesday and Student Thursday have also been discontinued.
They still offer 50% off during certain holidays and selected color-tag sales, but I didn’t find many discounted items I needed. Customer service, cleanliness, and inventory were not an issue. The staff was helpful and the store was well kept. My disappointment is strictly with the pricing and sale changes, especially since items are donated. Because of this, I likely won’t visit as often.

I really enjoy shopping at the Salvation Army Thrift Store! They have some great vintage finds if you take the time to look. I also love their weekly discounts—children's clothing is half off on Tuesdays, and students get 25% off on Thursdays. Plus, they have a good selection of household items at reasonable prices. Always worth a visit if you're hunting for unique treasures or shopping on a budget.

top_reviews.text:
I genuinely hate to leave a negative review about The Salvation Army, because I strongly support the mission and the good they do in communities. However, this The Salvation Army Family Store location was a very disappointing experience.

We stopped in to purchase several jackets to donate to a children’s drive, so we came in with good intentions and positive spirits. Unfortunately, the atmosphere inside the store felt tense and uncomfortable from the start. The staff appeared unhappy and irritated, and it showed in their tone and body language. My own kids even asked me why the workers seemed so grumpy and mean, which really stood out to me.

While we were checking out, one employee spent a few minutes correcting a new hire about how important it was to staple the receipt a specific way because “her boss likes it that way!” The conversation went on while we were standing there waiting, and it felt awkward and unnecessary to have that discussion in front of customers. It added to the negative tone of the visit.

I truly feel for anyone working in an environment that feels that stressful, and I can’t imagine it being enjoyable day to day. I still believe in the organization’s mission, which makes writing this even more disappointing, but this location could really benefit from improved leadership, better morale, and a more welcoming customer experience. Hire some smiles..

top_reviews.text:
Google needs to have a NEGATIVE
“— ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️” NEGATIVE 5-STAR ranking option for dumpster fires like this place! I’ve tried giving this Salvation Army location multiple chances — easily 20–30 visits — and every single time the experience has been awful. The staff openly cherry-pick donations before anything ever reaches the floor, which explains why this store never has a single decent vintage item. The employees yell back and forth about what they’re keeping, argue in front of customers, and seem irritated by anyone who tries to actually shop.

Tonight was the final straw. Despite posted hours saying they close at 9pm, the staff began yelling at customers at 8:00pm to “check out now because the registers are closing.” When I politely asked what time they actually closed, the employee confirmed 9pmgyz….  yet still insisted we stop shopping and check out an hour early because they “didn’t want to stay late.”

After deciding not to spend hundreds of dollars due to the terrible treatment, we put all of our unwanted items back exactly where they belonged. At checkout, the cashier still accused us of leaving behind a random cart of items that wasn’t ours. Even after telling him multiple times, he continued to argue and blame us in front of others.

I’ve worked in customer service for over a decade and have never seen anything like this. The disrespect, the early shut-downs, the yelling at customers, and the unprofessional hoarding of donations have turned this store into a nightmare. Management desperately needs to intervene — or shut this location down entirely.

name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope - Gulfport

top_reviews.text:
Very professional and helpful staff. The food pantry here is awesome and it provides you a basket full of healthy meals and snacks. You may apply by bringing a utility bill in your name with the address of where you live or a signed lease most current  lease and it must state if your utilities are included in your rent. Also a list of all household members and all income. The food pantry helps those individuals or families whose  incomes are limited. Those who are eligible may visit the pantry one time every three months .

There are social workers who will assist you with your individual case. Some services are available while some are not. If your case required a service that is not available , then the worker will provide you  referral . It will be up to you to go .

In my opinion there are always those people who never get enough and always complain. Well you can't please them all. If you make the decision to request the help of others , then beggars should not be choosy. If help you receive is not good enough for you because you expect gold platter service , then it's very simple to look elsewhere.

Some services they help to provide or offer s referral to another program may include  learning programs for those who want to learn how to read or obtain  a GED, food pantry , referrals to local programs that offer rental assistance , snack bags , information on how to obtain an identification card,  info on how to receive your mail if you do not have an Address , showers for the homeless, washing and drying clothes assistance for the homeless, emergency shelter , information on it referrals to transportation assistance for medical or personal ,  breakfast donuts and coffee. Please be patient while the facility is being remodeled to make it a comfortable place for those who visit and work here.

If you are a new visitor then you may be asked to fill out a few sheets of information explaining your immediate needs, emergency needs and short term needs .

If you.have the correct proof of income and.address and meet the requirements then you will not be turned away. Please be patient while waiting to receive help because you are not the only one in need and there is only limited staff and some may even be volunteers .

This  charitable organization has quite a long history in serving citizens who need help or live at or below poverty level . This program is an income based program designed to help make ends meet.

They strive to provide the best service and make a difference in the lives of those who request their help .
top_reviews.author: Shannon Lynn Farlouis

top_reviews.text: This place is run like a cult or satellite prison. They make you leave the building every morning at 7:30 accept on Saturdays and Sundays, and you must be in by curfew, 9:00 every-night . You pay $75 a week to stay there , even though they received donations receive tax breaks as a homeless shelter. They make you breathe in a breathalyzer before you can enter the building; if you are found over alcohol level they put you out. They give random drug test that you must take or they put you out. This is advantageous act because most homeless people has either a drug or alcohol problem. And what do you get for your $75 a week , a twin sized bed, a cabinet and dresser, a shared room with 3 other strangers, and a shared bathroom with  7 stranger! They force you to go to their church services Thursday and Sunday, and if you complain about anything they put you out! If you are asked to leave for any reason you must gather your things and leave immediately, without a pro-rated refund for the week! Most people who are homeless have no transportation, no place to store their property, and no where to go. But if you refuse to leave they call the police and have you escorted off the property! Wow, great charity right! The only reason they get two stars from me is because; (1) out of all of shelters and transitional housing in Jackson this is as good as it gets; and (2) this is the best looking Salvation Army that I seen throughout the Nation!

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Would give zero stars if possible.
I went in just to look around, but the condition of the store was shocking. I noticed dead cockroaches in glass bowls, and many of the baby toys looked like literal trash. I tried to overlook it and continue browsing, but I was too uncomfortable to even look at the clothing, worried there might be bugs on them.

When I moved toward the bookshelves in the back, everything was so overpacked that I couldn’t safely navigate the aisle with my toddler and infant in a stroller. My daughter did find a toy for $2.99, which I was willing to purchase.

At checkout, I was oddly asked if my last name started with a “P,” which made it seem like family members of the staff receive an even bigger discount. On top of that, I was charged a $5 fee for using my debit card — on a $2.99 purchase. I understand fees, but $5 is excessive, especially for an item that will clearly need to be thoroughly cleaned before use.

The entire experience felt less like shopping secondhand and more like digging through a dumpster. Just because items are donated doesn’t mean the store should look or feel like a trash heap. A little care and pride in the store’s presentation would go a long way — especially if the proceeds are meant to support charity.

If I had known it was going to be this bad, I would have never walked in. Absolutely do not recommend.
top_reviews.author: S M

My advice to mgt: At least half of your customers are resellers, and all of your customers are looking for a deal or they wouldn't be there. I've seen the same items sitting for months, this tells me you are over priced for your customer base. To price vintage, antique and rare items correctly, I suggest researching SOLD eBay items, not listed items. Then pricing at 30% of the average sold item price.
I will admit that things have improved since the management change recently. But, still a ways to go.

top_reviews.text:
I briefly volunteered here and have patronized their kitchen. There is no shame or judgment from diners nor servers: in fact, you may be surprised to see some of your neighbors or fellow church members there. Food insecurity is more prevalent today than ever and affects many. Maybe you're just on a tight budget. Either way, it is a great option for those living from paycheck to paycheck or worse. Many times, it was catered to buy an outside group like a hotel (tax break), and the food was great. I was a vegetarian and allowed second helpings of meatless options the first time through the line. I did enjoy volunteering, although I felt my time was better spent elsewhere as they weren't in need of assistance.
I would only advise that some of the patrons are homeless and may have mental issues. They are no more likely to be dangerous than a neurotypical,  but engaging them in conversation may result in odd comments. I have had unwanted advances by some of the patrons and had to make a concerted effort to always dress conservatively (unfortunately).
Health code disallows leaving without any uneaten food or drink to prevent foodborne illness. Please respect the rules, they can be shut down of you don't.

name: The Salvation Army Midland Division Headquarters

top_reviews.text:
I do not recommend donating to The Salvation Army based on a recent and deeply disappointing experience I had with their furniture pickup service.

I scheduled a donation pickup for the day before my move out date and proactively called to confirm details. I spoke with a representative named Chris and specifically asked whether the pickup team would be able to collect furniture from an upper level apartment unit. He informed me that they do not go upstairs and that all items must be placed on the ground floor. I explained that, as a woman, I would need to find assistance to move heavy furniture such as a dining table, and he acknowledged that. Chris also stated that the pickup window would be between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. This conversation took place around 9:57 AM.

To my surprise, I received a voicemail from him at 11:59 AM saying the driver would arrive between 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM, significantly narrowing the original time window. I immediately began preparing to move items downstairs. However, by 12:10 PM, the driver had already arrived and refused to wait, stating I would need to reschedule the pickup because he couldn't sit and wait for the furniture to be brought down.

I was truly trying to do something kind by donating nearly new, high quality furniture to those in need. Items such as a dining table I paid over $1,000 for and used for only a year, a brand new queen size bed frame still in the box, nightstands, a TV stand, a desk and chair, a full size bed frame, and two dressers, all in excellent condition. I was motivated by generosity and faith, believing that giving back would bless others and, in time, bring blessings my way.

This experience left me disheartened, not just by the lack of professionalism, but by how difficult it was to give away items that could truly help others.

top_reviews.text:
I do not recommend donating to The Salvation Army based on a recent and deeply disappointing experience I had with their furniture pickup service.

I scheduled a donation pickup for the day before my move out date and proactively called to confirm details. I spoke with a representative named Chris and specifically asked whether the pickup team would be able to collect furniture from an upper level apartment unit. He informed me that they do not go upstairs and that all items must be placed on the ground floor. I explained that, as a woman, I would need to find assistance to move heavy furniture such as a dining table, and he acknowledged that. Chris also stated that the pickup window would be between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. This conversation took place around 9:57 AM.

To my surprise, I received a voicemail from him at 11:59 AM saying the driver would arrive between 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM, significantly narrowing the original time window. I immediately began preparing to move items downstairs. However, by 12:10 PM, the driver had already arrived and refused to wait, stating I would need to reschedule the pickup because he couldn't sit and wait for the furniture to be brought down.

I was truly trying to do something kind by donating nearly new, high quality furniture to those in need. Items such as a dining table I paid over $1,000 for and used for only a year, a brand new queen size bed frame still in the box, nightstands, a TV stand, a desk and chair, a full size bed frame, and two dressers, all in excellent condition. I was motivated by generosity and faith, believing that giving back would bless others and, in time, bring blessings my way.

This experience left me disheartened, not just by the lack of professionalism, but by how difficult it was to give away items that could truly help others.

top_reviews.text:
My partner has been there for two months. The only thing he does for addiction and recovery is the required 2 meetings a week which you must walk to. Required to work. 40 hours a week in exchange for food & bed. He gets $5 at end of week. If you need hygiene products, they must be bought from them.  No cell phone is allowed which is OK but the community payphone is inoperable and you have no way to make doctors appointments , etc unless you fill out a request form to use the office phone. Also if you need a jacket in the cold weather you need to do the same form.  It’s been almost 3 weeks and he has not yet got either. The second week he was there another resident overdosed late at night. No phone to call for help and no more than 1 or 2 “employees” there after 5 or overnight, per 50 or so residents. He has not received any counseling, any help working on recovery, or any rehabilitation. They are strictly a faith based program. If you believe that God can fix your addiction and give you a life of sobriety, then that’s great. But if you believe you need to be taught new behaviors, learn coping skills to prevent relapse, tools to live a life in recovery, then this will not be the right place for you. This program also does not help you when you are finished and go back into regular life as far as getting a car, job which isn’t allowed when you reside there. For $5 a week pay, what can you do with that after you complete the program? You won’t have any income to get housing. Keep in mind this is a 6month program.
One day at a time.

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army, an international movement, is an evangelical part of the universal Christian Church. Its message is based on the Bible. Its ministry is motivated by the love of God. Its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and to meet human needs in His name without discrimination.

Come an join us Sunday Mornings at 10:45 am. Youth night is Monday at 6pm till 8pm. The youth learn about Christ, life skills and eat dinner. Women's bible study is on Wednesdays is from 6pm to 7pm and following is Ministry 7pm. and 8pm.

Doing The Most Good!

Rent and Utility Assistance
No one should have to choose between heating their home during the frigid winter months and putting food on the table, and yet, those living in poverty are often forced to make such a choice. That's why we are grateful to work with local renters and utility companies to help people pay their bills when they are struggling to make ends meet. For example, our partnership with Black Hills Energy offers utility assistance via HeatShare funds to those in need. Learn more about HeatShare.

Personal Care Pantry  |  Tuesday & Thursday, 9 a.m. - 12 p.m.
We offer everything from household items like laundry detergent and dish soap to personal hygiene products like soap, shampoo, deodorant and body wash to anyone who is unable to get these items, those experiencing homelessness or individuals or families who are struggling to make ends meet.

Back-to-School Assistance
Supplying kids with new backpacks, notebooks, pens and pencils can put an extra strain on a family's already-tight budget. That's why each August we partner with other agencies in the community to ensure that every kid in Fremont is prepared for the start of school with a new backpack filled with school supplies.

Pathway of Hope
The goal of Pathway of Hope is to guide families with children 18 years and younger through crisis to a place of stability in order to ultimately break the intergenerational cycle of poverty. We offer strengths-based casework, providing services such as:

financial counseling and planning
goal setting with manageable action steps
job training, referrals and employment assistance
assistance with securing housing and child care
emotional and spiritual support
Pathway of Hope works with people where they are, offering practical guidance to help families overcome obstacles and achieve their big-picture goals, one step at a time.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army is one of my go-to places for affordable clothing and it consistently delivers amazing value. If you’re willing to spend a little time browsing, you can find some truly great deals that are hard to beat anywhere else. From everyday basics to surprisingly nice name-brand items, the selection is often much better than people expect.

What really stands out is how inexpensive the clothing is compared to retail prices. Shirts, pants, jackets, and kids’ clothes are often just a few dollars, making it an excellent option for families, students, or anyone trying to stretch their budget. I’ve found gently used jeans, work clothes, and even brand-new items with tags still on them at a fraction of the original cost.

The store is generally well organized, with clothes sorted by size and type, which makes shopping much easier. You don’t feel overwhelmed digging through piles, and it’s simple to scan racks quickly. The staff are friendly and helpful, and the overall atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming.

Another big plus is knowing that your purchases support a good cause. Shopping here doesn’t just save money — it helps fund programs that assist people in need, which makes every purchase feel a little more meaningful.

If you’re looking for affordable clothes, unique finds, or just enjoy thrifting, the Salvation Army is absolutely worth checking out. Great prices, solid selection, and a positive mission make it a place I’m happy to shop at again and again.

top_reviews.text: I really loved this thrift store for years, but the past several times I’ve gone I’ve been super disappointed in pricing. I thought it might have been a fluke the first few times I saw sky rocketed prices, however I’ve come to see that it’s the new normal for them. They wanted $8 for a dirty, hair matted, naked Barbie doll that costs $8.97 brand new. They had doll cars priced at $15 covered in stickers and drawn all over by the previous owner. These things cost $20 max brand new. It’s really disappointing to see them price gouge simple things like beat up kids toys, especially when they’re supplied by donations only. We even tried negotiating a fair price with them for such things and they refused to budge even a little bit. My 5 year old and I’s favorite activity is a day of thrifting and seeing what little treasures we can find, but sadly we won’t be returning here again after several years of being frequent loyal customers. Thrift stores used to be for low income people to be able to buy home goods and little trinkets but management running their stores like this is killing it, and it’s really sad to see.

top_reviews.text:
Overpriced junk! I don't understand how the store stays in business. Everything is ridiculously overpriced and is all junk- nothing good.
You can tell they look up items on eBay and price their items according to eBay prices. This place iseven more overpriced than Goodwill. People go to thrift stores to find a good deal, if they want to pay eBay prices, they'll go on eBay, where sellers have to pay fees, shipping and you're paying for their time to source items. The Salvation Army literally gets everything donated to them, and most of their employees are actually volunteers. They were asking $50 for a silver plated Item, and $45 for a basic silver necklace that would probably cost $10 elsewhere, $50 for a brass buckle,. People always think their items are worth more than it really is.
It's such a shame because the place has a lot of potential to be incredible. The staff and people who work there were very kind. But the prices were so out of touch with reality. And the people who go into the store, let's just say it takes all types of make the world go around.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: Wow!  Not in a good way.   We arrived at 2:45 pm with items for donation.   I read the signs which said all donations must fit in the metal donation boxes.  I walked over to put the first bag in and was yelled at by an older gentleman wearing a Salvation Army coat.  At first glance, I thought he was a homeless man as he was leaning over back of our truck looking inside Asking “what do you got?”   We said we had household items some art work Some brand, new shoes and boxes And a new never used sleeping cot.    His reply was “you’ve got to be kidding me”.   We said why do you mean that? And he said we don’t want any of This stuff    I thought he was joking.   So I laughed   And he said I have the right to refuse anything    And he started picking through the items in the truck tossing breakable things aside.    I turned to my husband and said “let’s go we’ll donate elsewhere”.  The employee said “suit yourself”.    We drove a half mile to Second Hand Thrift store who gushed with thanks having seen our items.   I’ll donate items and cash elsewhere but never Salvation Army again.   Really Salvation Army - do better!

top_reviews.text:
We went today to donate a bag of baseball style caps. My husband said the outside guy the takes the stuff is not very personable.
So I made a distinct effort to be nice - said " Hello - How are you doing?" No Reply..  So I ended by saying " Try to have a nice day!"
I see a number of complaints about this person here - obviously if management deems this is the person that represents them to the public - well then it doesn't say much for Salvation Army as a whole.
I recommend finding another place to donate to - Goodwill is just in Dover - the next town over.

top_reviews.text:
I've been shopping here off and on since 2011. The store has always been pretty dirty/disorganized and prices were on the higher side. I hadn't been in here for a few years but I really couldn't believe how bad it has gotten. The prices are absolutely insane. $14.99 minimum for any shirt and many $20-$25 if it's somewhat of a decent brand. Saw many items for $50 and above too. We are talking USED stuff.

They just refuse to let anyone get a decent deal on anything. The whole reason people go to thrift stores is to find a decent deal, otherwise we would all just shop at retail stores. I seriously doubt this place lasts much longer and will likely close like the Nashua location did.

The people in Saugus just don't know how to run a business. I remember when I was told by a former manager years ago how the "Major" (the guy in charge there) promoted his daughter to a top position in the company. She then opened up her  own 2nd hand store, I wonder where the stuff she sold came from?

Anyways yea avoid this place. Goodwill down the street is about half the price and they aren't even cheap over there. Many other stores thrift stores are 1/4 the price of this place. Just a total shame to see such a decline since they would actually make much more money giving people decent deals then price at $30 and have stuff sit for months and months before it gets ragged out and shipped to Africa.
top_reviews.author: Braden

top_reviews.text: I've always enjoyed visiting this thrift store and seeing what's available. But I must say, leaving a donation can be painful, and this is why I give it only three stars. It should not be difficult to donate good quality items to a worthy cause. But the person running the donation area is not working in the best interest of the store. In my opinion. Last week I arrived at 3:01 p.m. and was told they were closed for donations. Of course there's nothing posted on when they are open for donations, so I asked when they accept donations. The woman that appears to be in charge told me 11:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Tuesday through Friday. So the following week I arrived at 12:30 p.m. on Tuesday. Once again the "Closed for donations" sign was out again. The same woman came out and said we're closed for donations, and I said well last week you told me you're open Tuesday through Friday. She quickly responded that they are closed the day after a holiday. So I said " That means I need to make a third trip?". And I guess the worst part of it atl, is the appearance that she had such joy in turning people away. At the same time. Another person pulled up, but of course had to leave as well. It's amazing to me that on the first day I arrived one minute after 3 pm, and she couldn't take the donation. But I understand keeping a schedule. So, the nice items that I wanted to donate ended up in a dumpster. It should never be this difficult to leave a donation to a worthy cause.

It is so disappointing to hear you accuse me of stealing your most generous and wealthy clientele, when ALL I asked today of Brenda, your fellow client donating boots today, was if she would be willing to pass on some gently used clothes with ZERO resale value and toiletries for the women's shelters I was donating to this Christmas.

It truly breaks my heart that after all the tips I’ve given you towards improving your business for free, that you think so lowly of me and assumed I was bribing with your client, Brenda, outside the store today. I can talk for ages about the line of work that I do and that it is never in my intention to steal your clientele and the beautiful things you sell in this store.

You told me to never come back so I won’t. You also said you’d be calling the police if you ever see me again in the near future. Hopefully, time tells all, because everything I’ve written here this afternoon is the truth. I’ll provide pictures of the hats I was giving to NYC all of Sunday night to prove my work is based on non-profit and providing for the community in NYC that so direly needs it. top_reviews.text:
Hoboken Shelter is truly an invaluable nonprofit organization serving the community of Hoboken. I have been donating and volunteering here since my mother took me when I was in middle school, I am now in my 40’s. Their commitment to providing essential services, including three meals a day, speaks volumes about their dedication to ensuring the well-being of those in need. The availability of hot showers and laundry services highlights their commitment to promoting good hygiene, which is vital for the dignity of every individual.
The shelter offers a safe and welcoming place for both men and women to sleep, along with the presence of compassionate social workers on-site who provide support and assistance. Furthermore, their initiative to accept clothing and food donations shows a collaborative effort to empower the community. The shelter also has a remarkable program aimed at helping individuals find permanent housing, which includes assistance with securing necessary deposits.
It's important to acknowledge the staff and volunteers at Hoboken Shelter; they are truly the heart of this organization. Their tireless efforts and unwavering compassion create a supportive environment that makes a real difference in the lives of those they serve. Hoboken Shelter is not just a place to receive help; it is a home for hope and healing within our community.

top_reviews.text: Honestly this is the worst Salvation Army in the county. Since receiving their “help” I’ve been slandered and treated unfairly.  Some case workers do not do their job and penalize you for absolutely nothing. They speak down to you most of the time when you need to speak with staff. I’ve been disrespected and harassed at their location sexually and verbally threatened. My car was attacked by a man much larger than myself. This man kicked and threw things at my car because I did not want to give him a hug in the parking lot. Staff made me out to be the bad person for defending myself against a man and his unwanted gestures. Furthermore, I had to face further humiliation because the woman here do not realize that their male clients are aggressive towards females. Lastly, I had an incident with an ex that had nothing to do with Salvation Army and the lady who works here is asking me questions because she personally knows my ex(he is an older man) she has no business asking and prying. I can assume she lied to the police about the incident but I won’t go into that here. I would not recommend anyone to go here unless they my want to feel little and stupid. I won’t lie there is a tension that feels mildly racist/prejudice. I want to make as many people aware of this before deciding to go, I will not be going back and will inform members of my community to be aware, because this place will make you feel like equality and fairness are not virtues.
top_reviews.author: Erica Price

top_reviews.text:
I applied for rental assistance through the Salvation Army in Montclair, NJ, and unfortunately, my experience was very disappointing. After waiting two months for a response, I finally received a call from a case manager who told me she didn’t “think” I would qualify. When I offered to bring in my paperwork and explain my situation, she dismissed it, suggesting I find another program instead, without even reviewing my documents or understanding my circumstances.

I believe everyone deserves a fair chance to have their application and situation fully reviewed before being turned down. It felt like the decision was made without any genuine consideration, which made the process seem arbitrary. The organization should treat all applicants equally, rather than picking and choosing who they feel like helping. If you're looking for assistance, be aware that this may not be the most reliable or compassionate option.
top_reviews.author: Rosaly

top_reviews.text: Not my favorite Salvation store, but it is the closest to me. I do find nice items here, and the employees are so kind and friendly. However, they need some work on the pricing end. Almost every time I come, they refuse to sell me an item because it does not have a price. Even if it has a tag attached, but no written number, they will not sell it to you. I always assume the item is .99 when there is no written number next to the printed .99 on the tag. In other locations I’ve been to this is usually the case and they will sell you the item for .99¢. This location will refuse the sale. I feel if they are going to be that particular about price tags they need to work harder to ensure that all items are priced before they go out on the floor. Also, some of the stuff is grossly overpriced. The shoe prices are ridiculous. Some items are in very poor condition (stains, severe pilling, etc) which leads me to believe they need better quality control measures especially if they’re going to charge top dollar for some items. The employees are super nice, the store has potential, but the pricing end is a big stumbling block.

And advanced to the line. when we got up to the front of the line another lady asked if we were together or separate appointments in which we said we were together this lady looked me up and down with what I thought to be a dirty look (I have tattoos on my face) and then just flat out said "um no sir you need to wait outside" I was confused by this and questioned what she meant at which point she said only she (my girlfriend) can select the gifts for the child at which point I politely said to her "you mean we can't pick together for our child?" At which point the lady just looked away and said "I said you need to wait outside." I felt completely disrespected but I wasn't going to make a scene so I just turned around and told my girl I'll be at the car and went outside. I was pretty upset by this being that I felt as if I was being stereotypically and prejudically judged by my appearance for having free will to have tattoos forever I want them as if I was going to steal donated gifts that a non-profit organization was kindly supplying to us anyway. I'm 33 years old now and probably a few years ago I would not have just turned around and not spoke my mind back. It's more I thought about it it was completely uncalled for and at least for whatever reason this lady had she could have been a little bit more personable about it especially being it is a holiday season. So I took to posting this review. And I just had to reminded myself I have to accept that everybody is entitled to their own opinion but weather I let myself validate it or not is up to me. If I could change one thing about it I think I would have guess I'll turn the eye and smiled until they're Merry Christmas and went on to wait at the car instead of letting another Grinch rent space in my head. People will be rude and say offensive things but if we give a reaction or not is what matters.

NOT ONLY is this averaging 2x to even 6x what they used to charge just a few weeks ago, but there seems to be no reason… i asked the workers (which all the workers i talk to are always the best) but they don’t seem to know who is making these decisions… $7 for a used plain white t shirt UR OUT OF UR MIND 😂

This was the first time I’ve left the store without getting something, I love supporting The Salvation Army but I refuse to be disrespected by these new prices. I truly do hope that next time i come in it’s back to their old pricing BECAUSE THIS IS A THRIFT STORE TO HELP THE COMMUNITY NOT A PLACE TO BE GREEDY. AMEN. 🙏

response to salvation army:
i’m sorry but that is a ridiculous response. i’m aware of prices at other stores, for instance the goodwill down the street charges no more than $4 for any t shirt yet you’re over here asking $7 for a stained grimey plain white t and $12 for raggedy under armour shirts. NO other salvation army charges as much as you are for shirts - i’m excited to see how this works out for you guys but just be aware that it’s ridiculous and disrespectful to 3x ur prices overnight for no reason.

name: The Salvation Army Family Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
I stumbled upon this store while trying to get somewhere else. I didn't even know it was there.

The first thing I saw when I got inside was the rack of greeting cards.  I asked the worker how much they cost and was happy when she said 10 cents each  (including envelope). I picked out eight cards.

From there, I looked around the rest of the store. Things were neat and organized,  but some of the prices were HIGH.  I saw a cloth basket (the kind you'd  buy at Walmart or Target to organize closet shelves) priced $19.99. Whoa! Clothes were pricey for a thrift store too.

However,  there was a white board where they had written the sales. Dresses and lady's shoes were 50% off. All yellow tag items were 75% off, and slacks were $1. There was also a shopping cart full of scarves for $1, and some creepy old fashioned dolls were 50% off. (I did not linger near those dolls!!!) So there were bargains to be found.

I ended up finding a pair of slacks to wear to work for only a dollar! (The pants were originally priced at $7.99.) I also found a pair of Lee jeans in great condition with a yellow tag on them. I got them for $1.75 instead of $6.99.

The dressing room was available to  shoppers, so I got to try on the pants before I purchased them. The dressing room is small, but functional.  You do need to consult a worker before you use it.

The workers answered my questions. They weren't rude, but they seemed tired. I don't blame them. A steady flow of customers kept them busy.

The store is big, and there is a lot of inventory. The store was clean, and well organized.  All merchandise was put away in its appropriate place. The store did seem a little dark though.

I would definitely return to this store and shop here again.  I'd  especially pay attention to sale items.

top_reviews.text: This used to be my favorite thrift store , not sure what’s going on or what happened the last few months but I stopped going and periodically will check back. The prices have gotten outrageous and the sale tags are far and few between. There are never any good brands on the racks anymore , at this point every good brand is on the $50+ yellow tag rack. This is the only thrift store that separates so many brands into “luxury” but I guess it’s to make their useless membership seem like something. I’ve been coming long enough to watch these brands go from regular racks to yellow. You might get lucky to find a stained up Veronica beard sweater with a gaping hole for $30 ,or a Johnny was top that has one sleeve 75% torn off for $60, madewell tops for $24. Vintage sweaters from the 80s with yellowing and holes are 19.99?  The housewares are priced like an antique shop. A cusineart enameled pot for $50 when the pot is $30 new at Marshall’s .My recent favorite was a pair of very fake doc marten sandals for $59.99. At this point they’ve priced out the thrifters and resellers. The only thing that has remained consistent here is the horrible attitudes of the employees and the dust.

This place is huge, with a ton of clothing options!

I will say however the line at checkout moves super slow. So if it's crowded then prepare to wait awhile. And depending on your size it might be hard to find clothes you like because the sizes are random. Other than that though, if you're looking to buy more clothes for cheap then this should be your goto place!

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
This was my first and definitely my last time visiting this store. The moment I walked in, there was a girl sitting at a table by the door and a guy standing nearby watching customers as if everyone was there to steal. It made the environment very uncomfortable.

The prices were ridiculously high for a thrift store. A Zara jacket was priced at $49, kids’ Alexander McQueen shoes were $149, and Zara shoes were $39 — and they weren’t even in good condition. At that point, I stopped browsing because nothing felt reasonably priced. Why sell donated items close to their original retail price?

I understand that stores have to sort and organize donations — I donate to Goodwill all the time, and they do the same. The difference is their prices are affordable. I once bought a brand-new bread maker at Goodwill that originally cost $169 and only paid $25.

This store was cluttered, smelled unpleasant, and the staff made me feel uncomfortable. I stayed less than three minutes and walked out. I will definitely stick with Goodwill moving forward.
top_reviews.author: Holder Afiya

top_reviews.text: I visited the Salvation Army thrift shop today expecting a typical shopping experience. Upon entering, I was not greeted by the two staff members at the front door, a man and a woman, who barely acknowledged us and gave off an unwelcoming vibe. The moment I stepped inside, a strong and unpleasant odor hit me, which immediately raised my red flag, indicating the cleanliness and comfort level might be lacking. The shop itself was cluttered, with clothes and items strewn about haphazardly, making browsing difficult. Overall, the staff's attitude and the store’s condition made the experience disappointing. As employees working in customer service, I believe you all need to improve your approach to ensure customers feel welcomed and comfortable instead of unwelcome and uneasy. I won't be back, do! 🤢
top_reviews.author: Kaykay (kay)

top_reviews.text: Items are not discounted. They're being sold at prices higher than the original price. A planter with the original price tag on it that the store didn't bother to mark down or put a tag on. Shein for $20. A junky tshirt likely given to the former owner for free sold here for $6. All shoes essentially start at $20. Saw a small Gucci children's shoe for $80. A single worn towel is $6. Used bath mat for $7. Loose playing cards for $5 each—split into separate bags as if they were collectors' pieces (a quick google search revealed they are not).
top_reviews.author: Audrey McBride

top_reviews.text:
When I found out there was a Salvation Army store in Bensonhurst, I was excited because I had a lot of clothes and items to donate as my boyfriend did too. I've only been here  one Friday and 2-3 times on a Saturday. This Salvation Army has also turned into a place of worship as well. The woman that has signed off on our tax deductible forms before took her sweet time filling it out for us and she's also not the nicest and showed little to no appreciation for our donations.

This Salvation Army doesn't share their hours unless you call them and ask for it. Last time I called this location, the woman on the other line was a little rude and talked to me like it's my first time donating and also this Salvation Army location isn't flexible at all! The woman said they aren't open every Saturday, on  Friday only opened from 9AM-4PM (how are people suppose to bring their items after work?) and they are only open on Sunday from 10AM-2PM. She also told me that they are only taking clothes and small house appliances. I told her okay and that I would need the tax deductible form and said it wasn't itemized,  of course I know that.

Overall, I feel that this Salvation Army is very inflexible in terms of hours of operations because everyone works day in and day out and the only time they really have to bring their donations are the weekend. I just wished the hours of operations here were a little longer and service would improve just a bit.
top_reviews.author: Jessica Deng

name: Housing Works Thrift Shops - Park Slope

top_reviews.text:
I’ve been donating to Housing Works on 5th Ave in Park Slope for many years, and I’ve always believed in supporting a store that’s meant to serve the community. Unfortunately, the experience has changed drastically.
In the past, donating was simple, and shopping felt like a true thrift-store experience with fair and reasonable pricing. Lately, however, the store has shifted toward boutique-level prices—especially in the home and décor sections. Items that are donated for free, including chipped glassware, worn Pyrex, or plates with visible flaws, are now marked at prices comparable to high-end retail.
It’s frustrating to see a community-based donation store lose touch with the people who support it. Many of us donate and shop here with the expectation that secondhand items remain accessible, not treated as luxury goods. This recent pricing approach feels out of step with the neighborhood and with the mission of a donation-based organization.
I hope Housing Works takes this feedback to heart and reconsiders its pricing strategy so it can once again feel like the welcoming, community-focused thrift store it used to be.
