Items are disorganized, either on the floor or tangled and falling off the hangers. I've always complained about the tags being stapled on the size of the clothing or on the clothing itself leaving holes.The fitting rooms are always crammed full of clothing and hangers left by other customers. By the way if that's how you keep your store, customers have no respect and won't clean up after themselves. There are huge dust balls in the fitting room so you're afaid to let the clothing touch the floor however that's impossible since there's not enough hooks and they're constantly falling. DEFINITELY DO NOT take off your shoes. The selection of children's clothes has always been poor and the furniture selection always scrungy. And all of these things including smells and dirty clothes are not found in other thrift stores. I used to buy everything that would fit and come out with bags of clothes. My last visit I bought one dress and one t-shirt. The cost of the other clothes were not worth spending that much money on. Was angry with myself for buying anything at all because of my complaints above. I had a routine of stopping at Salvation Army first because they close early then heading to Savers right down the road. Now I just head straight for Savers. I was told the profits go straight to the men's housing next door but I'd rather make cash donations then shop there again. The only reason I'll go back there is to take more pics of evidence so you see I'm not exaggerating. Just because this is a thrift store doesn't mean you should feel like you're digging through a garbage can. I've said a lot here so I won't go into the comparison to Savers or other thrift stores.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Totally disappointing now. If you’ve visited here years ago, you’ll remember the musty furniture room, and the fans blowing tobacco fumes around the building. Those were the good days of this place.

Now, their prices do not match anything “competitive”, WHO ARE THEY COMPETING WITH. They’re the only thrift store in the area now! Remember: they get their inventory for FREE, delivered TO THEM. The building itself is in horrible shape, wires on the wall behind the register, literal trash on the shelves and racks…all for the price of $4.99 and up. Don’t even get me started on the red (permanent price) section with brand new items from Walmart frown the road, with their SA price at $1 under the tag price. Yes, there are costs to have employees sort and price the items. There absolutely should be a cost associated by that. But unless you’re paying your employees an abundant salary, these tag prices do NOT line up. If you are paying an abundant salary way above minimum wage though, please brag about that! That is something to support and I will update my review.

Want some examples of their pricing being crazy? 16.99 for a used vintage dress. $16.99 for a used, pilling jogging set. $29.99 for a used no-name duffle bag which was locked in a glass case (???).

Their clothing prices now are actively on par with the TJ Maxx down the road. Is that their competitor? It sure shouldn’t be.

The amount of stained, torn, and ripped clothing and shoes was astounding. I visited to waste time, and I sure did just that. The shoe section was particularly disgusting as well. People donate things they shouldn’t, but this store is also still putting those things on the shelves (looking at you, mud and odor encased soccer cleats and Uggs shredded by something).

They get one star for still having their tag/color sales, which are nice if you can find any of those tags. They do get a point for keeping that around.

That being said, honestly do not shop here if you do not have to. They have priced themselves even above the Goodwill in Warren, PA. If you are in need of cheap goods, go to Saint Luke’s, Paws and Shop, or literally any thrift store that claims to help others. This particular location is not worth the steep costs they claim are necessary.
top_reviews.author: mel shopping

top_reviews.text: Employees were decent upon entrance.  As it grew closer to closing time, some of them became very pushy,rude, and just downright disrespectful towards the customers. It began about 25min prior to closing time & just got worse as minutes passed. At one point, an employee demanded a customer go to the checkout.  It was as though customers were being corraled or wrangled like animals. Witnessing and experiencing this was very disheartening. Had this been the first time experiencing this at this particular location, I would have just brushed it off, but this instance had actually been the third time within a fairly short time frame. I am beyond disgusted with this place from experiencing this treatment. I recommend not being there close to closing time if at all possible.

I typically like thrift shops that support a cause and seeing how this shop is run by members of the The Women's Civic Club of Katonah, I liked the idea of a non-profit that serves women who seek assistance and find support that helps empower them.  After selecting a few items at this basement locale totaling over $65+, I was most happy about an antique-looking tile that seemed to fit my Middle-Eastern home decor theme.  The cashiers were pleasant as always and we even had a few laughs during the checkout process.  After stepping out with my purchases, I decided to snap a photo of the tile in my car while still parked in their parking lot to send to my mom to show her my find.  After looking down at the piece I just paid $40 for, I saw a break that went from the front to the back that I hadn't seen while in the windowless basement of the shop.  I quickly ran back inside and told the cashiers the item they sold me was broken and explained how I hadn't noticed it in the store due to their poor lighting.  The cashiers couldn't find the crack either due to the same reason until I pointed it out to them.  Quickly, they agreed to the unfairness of having purchased a BROKEN item and referred me to their manager.  After speaking to a woman who worked in the back with grey braided hair and glasses and having her unapologetically tell me “NO RETURNS”, I asked to speak with the manager.  The manager with dyed dark brown hair above her shoulders walked out telling me story of a woman attempting to return a dress she had worn after purchase and that there were no returns.  Her tone was very accusatory as if I was attempting to pull a scam!!!!  I bit my tongue to respect her as an elder and told her I did not want my money back but merely the opportunity to select something else.  I also told her how it was unfair of them to expect me to be happy shelling out $40 for a broken item they sold I couldn't see was broken in their lighting.  She flat out said, "THE LIGHTING HERE IS JUST FINE!" in a mocking tone to dismiss a what she thought was a fake claim.  At this point, she escalated the frustration I had with her condescending comment and it became evident to others I was not standing down.  They quickly stated they would discuss after they realized I was still standing there and not motioning defeat.  I waited up front with the cashiers where they stated it was unfair that they were attempting to stick to their "no returns" policy given that the item was broken.  One volunteer even stated she couldn't believe what management was attempting to do.  The woman with grey, braided hair came to the front where I was standing and stated that they were doing ME a "ONE TIME FAVOR" by "ALLOWING" me to EXCHANGE!!!  For an organization that promotes women's empowerment, this very act was EXTREMELY DEGRADING and EMBARRASSING to me!  This played out in front of other customers in their small shop!  I felt it was unfair that I trusted them to selling items that were still usable.  In this case, the tile was flat out broken and if not for the fabric glued to the back, it wouldn't have been accepted at their shop for selling purposes!  HORRIBLE experience for a return customer that has been referring friends and family to their shop.

If I could rate a -5, I would!

He's what we'd call "Good People." Thanks again Jackson!

It's important to support our local businesses and services. I'm actually on a mission to scout out and report on what I find here in Kingston and will be publishing it in my magazine PLOTS JAMERICAN MAGAZINE "The Jamaican-American Diaspora (available on Amazon). To highlight what Kingston has to offer, from services, healthcare, food, you name it, that is included in daily life here. I'll share the good, bad, and the ugly, lol! Why? top_reviews.text:
The manager david took my personal belongings and dumped them into the store bins!

I had a troubling experience at this Goodwill location involving the handling of personal belongings. Our cart, which included my coat, items in the coat pockets, two scarves, and other belongings, was dumped into store bins by the manager, David. Other items included store merchandise, which we had spent hours finding. This incident took place December 31, 2025 on new years eve at around 2 pm.

David claimed that our cart had been placed in an employee-only area. There were no signs or indications of such a boundary, ZERO, and the cart was not within the area he later described. The cart remained untouched in the same location for two hours which at any point he could have came up to us or announced that the our cart was not where it was supposed to be. When we realized our items were missing, we reported them as stolen. One employee took the complaint seriously, but when we spoke with David, he avoided taking responsibility getting really aggressive with us. When asked directly if he had dumped the cart, he avoided answering, and became confrontational when we mentioned calling the police, even threatening to have us escorted out of the store, without doing anything to help us get our stuff back. I had to yell out and ask the store if anybody had our stuff and fortunately someone did and gave it back. If I hadn’t done that my items would have very much have been stolen and goodwill will be profiting off of my stolen goods. What if I had important documents inside of my coat, like my wallet? Goodwill policy states that items containing personal and sensitive documentation cannot be sold, this very well would have been the case.

This was a very stressful experience, mainly caused by the lack of accountability from management. I hope higher management can review its policies and ensure staff members handle customer belongings responsibly, and that something can be done to improve the current management at this location.
top_reviews.author: Daniel Lin

top_reviews.text:
It's the only nearby bins in the city, it's not glamorous and not for the faint of heart. The rules and system change occasionally so it's up in the air what you'll walk into. It gets really packed and can be up to 10+ people sorting through one bin. Sometimes they'll change the bins one at a time, sometimes everyone has to stand to the side and they'll rotate a few. Most of the time it's a bunch of carts lined up with people's finds and they're walking around sorting through bins. The environment and "regulars" can definitely be competitive and sometimes aggressive. No real rules are enforced so a lot of behaviors are ignored and continue. It's definitely one of the more intense bins but you never know what you can find! Found some of the cutest most random favorite items in my closet.

I get it, they're understaffed and have a lot to sort through. I wouldn't say it's anyone's individual fault but this is my honest experience and it really can be all fun and games until it's not, just be prepared for the unexpected.

Pricing:
0-49 lbs $2.29/lb
over 50 lbs $1.99/lb

top_reviews.text:
Housing Works Thrift Shop in Chelsea is a charming little spot that’s worth a visit, especially if you’re on the hunt for unique furniture pieces. Despite being a relatively small store, the selection of vintage and secondhand furniture is impressive—well-made chairs, tables, and other statement pieces that often come with character and history.

Beyond furniture, you’ll find clothing, books, and home goods, though the inventory can feel a bit limited compared to larger thrift stores. That said, everything is thoughtfully curated, and the prices are fair for the quality.

What makes Housing Works special is its mission. Proceeds support programs to fight homelessness and HIV/AIDS, so every purchase feels like it’s going toward a meaningful cause. It’s a great place to shop sustainably, find hidden gems, and contribute to the community.
top_reviews.author: Arthur Trusov

top_reviews.text:
Housing Works Thrift Shops is hands down my go-to thrift shop in NYC. I absolutely love this place — the prices are great, the selection is always interesting, and the staff is consistently friendly and helpful.

One of the things that makes it even better is the mission behind it. Knowing that your purchases support an important charity and the amazing work Housing Works does for the community makes shopping here feel even more meaningful.

I’m often coming in last-minute when I need something for an event or a special occasion, and somehow I *always* end up finding exactly what I’m looking for. Whether it’s clothing, accessories, or unique pieces you don’t see everywhere else, this store never disappoints.

Overall, it’s an awesome thrift shop with a great vibe, great finds, and an even greater purpose. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.text:
Salvation Army Henrietta

Salvation Army is my favorite thrift store compared to the few others we have in Rochester NY. My go to place for older cotton bed sheets. You know the ones that are cool and crisp and smell amazing when you hang them outside to dry! Yup!!! Those are available for just a few dollars! But!!! I was really shocked at some of the other prices! I'm not sure who is coming up with the prices but they are completely outrageous. I understand they're a not for profit but you're not selling this stuff for the amount you're asking so nobody wins. Not the store and definitely not the people you're supposed to be helping. Salvation Army needs to rethink the pricing of their items. I get they have rent to pay and employees need to get payed but again,if you're not selling stuff, you're not moving the stuff. On a good note the employees are very nice and the store is clean 🫧

UPDATED REVIEW 😊

Response to owner,
I agree with you in regards to Salvation Army doing a much needed community service for people struggling to overcome addiction, homelessness and other situations that arise in ones life. I also understand overhead costs. While I find Salvation Army a better thrift store, In my opinion, pricing is a bit high. Personally I think something marked $2.99 from the dollar store is not something I think is ok. I also think there are bargains to be found! I've found many.  I am also happy to hear Salvation Army has a program to help folks that need clothing and furniture, I know a couple of families that are currently in need of things they can't afford and will have them call to apply. I will update this post with that information.
top_reviews.author: Amirs Sittu

top_reviews.text:
I don’t usually leave reviews but I’ve shopped at this and other thrift stores for years. Over the past year or so this store looks better and better every time I come in. It is by far the most organized thrift store I have ever been to.
It is clean, organized and not overcrowded with junk like some others I go to. You can definitely tell the people that work here care about the store. Every one there is friendly, helpful and hardworking.
However, I’m not a fan of the new pricing they’re doing. They took the price tags off everything and only have small hard to read signs here and there to let you know the price of certain items. It is very confusing and hard to remember what each item costs. I don’t want to hunt down the price of each item so I passed on a lot of items I would have otherwise bought.
Don’t be like Goodwill. Put prices back on your clothes!

top_reviews.text:
This thrift store is fine but the organization of the clothing is by color and not sizing which makes it more difficult to browse and harder to find things. The home decor section is always pretty empty and pricing is strange. Most items make sense but sometimes items are way overpriced for no reason - my last visit I picked up a plastic stained glass coaster type item that was marked $12.99 but was just a small piece of plastic, it was comically overpriced. My biggest gripe with this thrift store is they don't use traditional tagging guns for the pricetags - they STAPLE THE TICKET RIGHT INTO THE CLOTHES!!! There have been so many pieces I've had to carefully remove the staples from just to tear a hole into the fabric and it's just because they don't want to buy a couple taggers? I'm not sure.

I'm not trying to totally hate on this thrift store, they do run good sales on the different colored tickets throughout the week and the cashiers are kind (although the folks at the donation center have been quite grumpy with me).

I'd say it's an okay thrift store worth checking out because you never know what they'll have, but maybe check it out on a day you're looking to hit up multiple thrift stores.

The Salvation Army USA im sure nothing will come of this. But to say that I’m a bit enraged about what just took place inside this location would be a bit of an understatement.

I’ve been coming to this particular location weekly for a little over two years now and I almost always make a purchase and have seen just about every employee that works there multiple times. Today I was looking to do the same thing, albeit at a different time than usual ( I usually take my trips in the afternoon but this was a morning affair ) I entered the store empty handed/without a bag to carry anything in as usual because I make purchases that are often small and can be carried directly to my vehicle where I either have bags already or can just be carried into my house.  I picked up two items and bought them to the register. Behind the register was the cashier and a fellow worker who I would assume was a manager? I paid for my items and received a receipt. As I turned around, an item closeby caught my eye and I had wanted to take a Quick Look at it. Thinking nothing of it, and as people normally do when something similar happens, I turn to go look at said item only to hear someone start screaming like a banshee. I turned around out of curiosity wondering why the screaming wasn’t stopping. And was told that I had to leave the items that I had just purchased in front of her and received a receipt for at the counter while I “looked around” When asked why I was told because I might add stuff in that I didn’t pay for. In all the times that I have been in this store and been in this same exact scenario, I have never been made aware of this so called “policy” nor is there any kind of video evidence of me shoplifting at any given point. And to make matters worse, employee/manager stated that she had never seen me in this store before when I for one would never be able to forget just how unnecessarily loud she can be even when she is standing directly next to someone.

name: The Salvation Army Westbury Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
Call me Bernie. I am a Westbury resident now, but as a teenager 50 years ago, I traveled back and forth across the Country TWICE in successive Summers, and at the suggestion of someone I met the 2nd day on the road, I stayed in a Salvation Army "shelter" (in Snyder Texas, it was a room in the Snyder Hotel), and they fed me dinner, gave me a clean bed for the night, and breakfast the next day, with "Farewell and Godspeed". Ever since then, when anyone asks me for a donation, I politely inform them that the Salvation Army is my ONLY charity, and for the kindness they showed me long ago, I have willingly repaid them for it dozens of times over. When I was living in Floral Park, there was a thrift shop a mile away, and anything of value that I no longer needed, appliances, furniture, clothing, etc., I gave to them. I also bought many things there, increasing their cash flow as a result.
As charitable organizations go, their use of donations has a higher percentage than any other charity I know. My Father told me when I was 10 years old, "There are 3 types of Palm. The Coconut Palm. The Date Palm. And, oh yes...
The OUTSTRETCHED Palm.
Many so-called charitable organizations collect millions, and keep most of it for themselves. I could name several, but they know who they are. The Salvation Army's ONLY mission is to help those in need, and they do it better than anyone else on Earth. As an American citizen, I am exercising my right to this opinion, and whether or not you share it is entirely up to you. Either way, if there was an approval rating of MORE than 5 Stars, they deserve it, period!

name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope

top_reviews.text:
As a man who is not only HOMELESS, NOW, but has been HOMELESS BEFORE, I can tell you it is NOT a blessing to have to run into a homeless place to avoid spending hot or cold nights on the mean streets.

And by the way, I heard from somebody which The Salvation Army used to be known as the Starvation Army. However, my adoptive Auntie, whom I very recently met up here told me the guy who brought up the term "Starvation Army" was just pulling my leg when he told me this.
...One has to wonder if it's really true or not.

The reasons I dislike them so much are two-fold...
I: When I first came unto them for help, they did not allow all my extra baggage into their facility. As a result of this pathetic policy, most of those precious belongings of mine had been stolen out from their "vestibule"/entryway.
II: During the single night I stayed in here, I met a SUPER-handsome, clean-shaven young man by the name of Josh. During the very next day, shortly before noon, I caught up with him and we ate brunch together at a crowded, open dining place/joint. He told me he had LITERALLY NOTHING!! And I mean this! He had no house, no job, no car or truck, no money, no friends, no family...
Not even a phone or a girlfriend!! o_o
So, as I was preparing to repossess what few items of mine which HADN'T been stolen, Josh walks into the "Center of Hope" in the hopes of reclaiming his place to stay. But, because they claimed which they were "full to capacity", they were about to turn Mister Josh away!! I was right in their entryway when their security told him this, I WILLINGLY gave my spot up, insisting on handing it over to Josh. Needless to say, he was BEYOND ECSTATIC!! Even asked me 3 times "Are you sure, man?" I told him: "Yeah, man. I'm positive. I'll be fine, so hurry up and get in there!"
He and I hugged each other twice and I headed off to a different shelter, which wasn't much better.

...Whew! Long review, but you have my truths, yeah?
top_reviews.author: Feral cat rescue

**My review is based on receiving assistance from the food pantry.

This location does offer services such as rent, utilities assistance as well as a nurse on Wednesdays who may help with minor issues. If you can't get through to them on the phone to sign up, make sure you go early in person to sign your name and bring your ID and disconnection/past due bill with you.

For food: Mondays, Wednesday, and Fridays from 1-3PM is when they pass it out. Make sure you call them or show up early with your ID so they can have your name down so they can reserve a shopping cart of food for you. Now if you don't show up, I can't guarantee you will have food because they will give it to another person in need who is there.
I am very appreciative that they were able to help me in such short notice. I came early around 10AM and though the food pantry was not open, they did offer me much needed toiletry such as an assortment of feminine products and told to me return at 1PM which I did. The wait time was not long, so they are fast when it comes to the service. They gave out several boxes of food ranging from canned goods to dessert on a cart. They also had fresh fruits and vegetables, and animal supplies (cat litter) for us to pick that was in front of the building. It was a pleasant experience and I am grateful for their help.

I highly recommend taking advantage of their quarterly "Quarter Sales". I went to the last one-- it was very, very busy, but it was so well worth it. The staff were very helpful and even tried getting the line taken care of faster by letting people with exact change pay right there in line. They had tons of stuff. Clothes for all ages, uniforms, kids toys, kitchen gadgets, home decor, DVDs, books, strollers, furniture.. a little bit of everything! I stocked up on board books for my son. They had a kids book section and it was organized pretty well. I found some that were basically brand new, and the rest were only gently used showing some wear on the spine. I paid $3.50 for 14 books, which is less than what I would have paid for just ONE of those books brand new! If you enjoy saving money this is the place to check out. Plus all the money here goes toward a scholarship which is very cool. Don't forget if you have stuff to donate, bring it along with you when you head there to go shopping!

only putting 5 stars so it’s higher in the reviews. they lie about not having beds. this place is full to the brim with mold. bed bugs spread like wild fire and all they do is spray the mattresses (rarely will actually throw them away like you’re supposed to) . you either get your water from a school water fountain, bathroom, or from the nasty jugs they use and do NOT clean. the cleaning staff does a half assed job. kids dip their hands in it as well so yeah, so not sanitary. if you have kids who get sick easily, please please please make sure that this is your absolute ONLY option for safety. you get 3 meals. only time you get hot breakfast is if the cooks are in a good mood, you get the cooks that actually enjoy helping people, or when the churches or volunteers come out. THEY RARELY HELP WITH HOUSING SO GET YOU A JOBBBBB AND GET TO WORKKKK! save save save is your best option. sign up for SNAP benefits and medicaid bc they will help you, especially if you have kids.

make sure if you’re eating the shelter food that you’re paying attention to how your body reacts to it. people stay sick at this place. and i don’t mean colds, i mean covid, the flu, food poisoning, kids with low immune systems will suffer here im telling you.

they let random strangers and men on the property and will do next to nothing about it, just tell you to call the cops. and the cops don’t do anything bc they’re there every day for minimal issues, fights, or child abuse cases. the charlotte hospitals will drop people there who don’t know a lick of english and leave them there to suffer. they will kick you out in an instant for things out of your control. it’s like a jail house.

this is no safe haven. this is temporary shelter. if you’re a strong minded person, alone, then yeah sure come here. but lord god if you have kids, make sure this is your ABSOLUTE LAST RESORT!

top_reviews.text:
I go to this Salvation Army about once a week, and I’ve always appreciated that they weren’t greedy with their pricing. Unfortunately, over the past few weeks, I’ve started noticing a change.

First, there was a green vintage Caterpillar item marked at around $100. Then I saw a vintage horse saddle priced extremely high. Yesterday really surprised me, though. I found a wooden spoon and fork set I’ve been looking for and was excited to finally see one. I picked it up and saw $40 which was already $10 more than the antique store had them priced. I thought, “Okay, I’ll still get them and support the store.” Then I realized it was $40 each.

The Caterpillar item is still sitting there, as is the saddle. I understand that when you Google certain items, you may see them listed for much higher prices. But listed prices don’t mean they actually sold for that, and a Salvation Army shouldn’t be pricing items like an antique store.

I’ve also overheard employees talking about marking certain items up higher, which was disappointing to hear. It feels like the focus has shifted from serving the community to trying to get top dollar for donated goods.

I’ve always supported this location, but the recent pricing feels excessive. I probably won’t be back for a while and will stop donating. I really hate seeing greed I might as well donate to goodwill now again

top_reviews.text: I visited the thrift store today. I've found good deals on some vintage & antique items in the past (if you can get there before the local antique dealers!). I've noticed that their supply of curtains & linens has been significantly diminished over the past several months.  Possibly due to all the natural disasters across the country? There have also been fewer employees available for assistance & theft prevention. But they definitely serve a vital mission, & I believe in supporting them whenever I can, however meager it may be. They also have free grocery items on a table near the door, but you have to go early in the day if you hope to have access to any of it as the items go quickly. They're often willing to work with you on larger, more expensive items, like furniture, especially if their display floor is full & they need to make room for more merchandise (they have limited storage). When I'm searching for/in need of something specific, I always check here first.
top_reviews.author: s hoogie

top_reviews.text:
I can always find something great here! The prices are reasonable,  the staff is friendly and it's neat.
The only thing I don't like is everything being colour coded and not separated by size or type.
I don't like going through shirts of every size just because they're all a certain colour! I want size XL, not S,M,L,XXL, etc. It's annoying sifting through shirts that I don't like while trying to find one in my size that I DO like!
Same thing with kitchen or household items. Glasses should be together, not spread across 4 rows of stuff because they're not the same colour!!
It makes it hard to shop.
I have no idea why places have adopted this change, but it isn't fun shopping this way. I lose interest very quickly because I can't immediately eliminate what I don't want, like a size 4 anything!

top_reviews.text: I was there today at Thrift Store on Robinson St.  For the last three times I’ve been there, I spent most of my time finding items that I liked but couldn’t buy because prices were not on items and they can’t sell it to you without prices. I’ve seen other customers go through this same mess so it’s not just me with a problem as I’m sure that’s what they will tell higher management.  The little manager that was on duty today waited until she got to the back and started talking trash saying that I didn’t have to shop there if I didn’t like the prices.   I never said that I didn’t like the prices.  How can I like or dislike the prices when I don’t see any? She was so busy trying to argue about something totally different than what my concern was about.  Why are they putting unmarked items out only to say that they can’t sell it  to you until someone put a price on it on Monday?  Something more has to be going on behind the scenes at this particular store because I refuse to believe that a business is operating with no posted  price guide for customers to go by.  I would like to know who hired the little mouthy manager that was there today without training her.  The first thing you need is a set of rules to guide customers into having a hassle free shopping experience.  Y’all need a price list on the wall and y’all know this.  Do y’all just not want to make sales?  This particular thrift store use to be my favorite store but after today, I decided not to waste my time and energy asking how much is this and that all day long only to hear, “we can’t sell it because It isn’t priced.”  And if you suspect customers are taking prices off, do something different like maybe stapling the price tag to the garment label.  That might help to keep prices on clothing items a little longer.  Maybe they all got together and planned not to sell anything because they are tired and don’t feel like working. Or maybe they want to keep unmarked items for themselves. All I know is that shopping becomes stressfully a boring when you have to ask how much everything costs.  I know y’all can do better. Please do.  Thank you!
top_reviews.author: Tawanda Cato

top_reviews.text: I loaded up a pickup with nearly new items and was refused donation because they "decided to close donations" during business hours.  Stuff ended up in landfill.  If anybody knows a reliable place I can donate in Fayetteville please let me know.   I won't go back here.  Update:  Gave them another shot.   Nope!!!!!  Doors locked at 4:25 PM.  Great job guys. top_reviews.text: I’ve been a loyal customer, but the two women working the register — including who I believe is the manager — treat customers with shocking disrespect. They act like you’re bothering them just for asking a simple question, as if you’re interrupting their personal time. It creates a really unprofessional and uncomfortable environment. top_reviews.author: Chrissy Chris

top_reviews.text: I am absolutely livid and would give this place less than zero stars if I could. I used to shop here for four years, but every year they've been going downhill - and today was the final straw! I experienced something utterly unacceptable and unprecedented in my life. I saw a racing jacket in the cashier's hands, asked to take a closer look, we discussed the price, and I put the jacket in my baggy and continued digging. That was a rare and expensive jacket, and I was so thrilled to find it! But when I was ready to pay for my items, the store manager showed up and asked me to return the jacket 'because she had promised it to another family'! Can you believe that?! They forced me to give back the jacket, saying 'sorry'! Sorry? Really?! That's all you've got?! Imagine putting food in your cart and the cashier taking it out because 'it was promised to another buyer'! How would you feel about that?! I felt utterly disrespected and humiliated; they just ruined my day. That was completely inappropriate, disrespectful, and unacceptable behavior. I didn't deserve such treatment, and neither does anyone else. How could this even happen?! I'd like to ask the manager, do you think it's normal to treat people this way?! Your store is non-profit and exists solely because of people's donations. Your goal is to serve people, but it seems you don't give a damn about respecting buyers who aren't your friends. I don't need your pathetic 'sorry'; you should apologize to that family because the jacket was already in my cart, not theirs. But it seems like you decide who can buy the items people donate to you and who can't! This is not only disrespectful but also illegal. As I said, I will never come back to your store, and I don't recommend shopping here to anyone!
top_reviews.author: Natalia Zaikina

top_reviews.text: I  want to start by saying there are a select few really great folks there at the store in forest city. That being said, I went in to buy a large organ That they clearly didn’t have room for anyways. I turned it on to see if it worked and was immediately kick off it. Second, I went back to purchase the item and go ahead and take the risk and there was a worker stacking panting all over the palace near the organ. Apparently I was in her way and it didn’t matter that I’d come to buy an organ, it mattered that I got out of her way. To preface, I have a disabled son with me crying, so it was going to be a difficult task without the attitude of one of the workers anyways. I assume shes there for community service, that the attitude o was getting from her, but maybe they should train the workers to be patient with customers. Or care AT ALL….  I would have bout that organ, instead, since my disabled son and I were push out of the way, ignored, and given attitude with rolling eyes, we left. I would have loved that organ, but I’m not going to be profiled and endure predjuce because I have a disabled son and and look poor and am being rushed out the store. top_reviews.text:
This is a little boutique style Salvation Army thrift store. They have nice clothes, some are a little overpriced, others are a deal. The clothes are organized by type and gender, yet the sizes are all mixed up, making it a challenge to find the sizes I am searching for. They also have fashion jewelry in and on top of display case near the registers.
The back room has some food products and small housewares and knick knacks.
A small children's section has toys and clothes.
The bedding on the top shelf is minimal. I made the mistake of purchasing a twin size blanket without inspecting it properly. When I got it home, I washed it and found that it had several dark stains on it. I'll just use it for my little dog. He won't mind a few stains.
I'm not sure why this is called a "select" store. My first thought was that they would have higher end items, stain free, undamaged items, etc.  But that really isn't the case.
All in all this is a decent thrift shop. I would only advise to be selective and inspect everything before committing to buy.
The staff here isn't very welcoming nor interested in answering questions. They all seem to be stressed out or overworked so I don't hold it against them.
top_reviews.author: Sharon Lane

top_reviews.text:

Great parking lot and easy to access.

top_reviews.text:
I am posting this review because I believe in giving people their flowers while they are living. I frequent this establishment because it has a purpose. They help the less fortunate. I would like to commend the manager, Ivy, and her assistant, Angie. These two are a dynamic duo and their team works together as if they are a family.
Each and every time I walk through that door they greet me by calling my name as if they know me personally, and I am a part of their family. They make me feel as if I am at home. There are a mixture of people from all genders, nationalities, and I have never seen them treat anyone of us any different from the other. This establishment is a Christian base business and believe me you can tell. The gospel music that is played over the intercom, soothes me as I shop and think about the goodness of God. I think to myself how grateful I am, that I am able to be a blessing to someone else. We never know the plans that God has for us, so it is so important that we treat each other as if they are our very own brothers and sisters.
The word of God says, " Am I my brothers keeper?" If your answer is yes, then you know you are doing something right and God will be pleased.  I want to thank Ivy and Angie for the AWESOME  customer service that they and their staff render to me each and every time I walk through those doors on Gate City Blvd. in Greensboro N.C. May God continue to BLESS you and keep you as you continue to be servants of the most High God. 💐 💐 💐 💐 💐 Let these 5 Flowers be a symbol of the 5 star 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 service that you give, not only to me but to the many others. I appreciate you all, thank you very much.
top_reviews.author: Pamela Gill

top_reviews.text:
One of my weekly rituals is to go thrift shopping and I don’t let it ride to go by without going to check in the Salvation Army on gate city Boulevard.

Everywhere I go I can ask about the outfits that I wear and nine times out of 10 on the days that they asked me the most. I got it all shirt, pants, shoes, and purse from the Salvation Army in mint condition— often times brand new with tags on it and the price is B from free to cheap that anyone can afford on any budget.
Mts Ivy and her staff don’t play.
The layout of the floor and the visuals are beautifully done by Miss Brenda  and I always get an idea of what to wear my what she puts up on mannikins   It’s one of my favorite places and they help me with my wardrobe while I’m helping them help families in need.  A perfect service work cycle all in the yoke of giving us commanded by our father.
I don’t know about any other Salvation Army in here is a gym and I love that it’s only two blocks away from my house

The preacher and his wife are great people who really care about their parishioners. When my grandmother was sick he visited her in the hospital and at home. They brought food for the family and were there for all of us. When she passed away a few months ago they prepared a meal for the family before the funeral. You couldn't ask for a better congregation to belong too. The Salvation Army does so much for the community. They help anyone and everyone. If you're looking for a church to belong to that will treat you like family then you should check out the Salvation Army.

top_reviews.text:
It's a decent program. You can bring children if needed and small emotional support dogs with special request. Curfew is 10pm 7 days a week and you get one month free then they charge up to 30% of your income for another 60 days. Case management and day programs are easily accessible and readily available.  Dinner and breakfast are the two meals served 7days a week. You are required to pass a drug test and a daily breathalyzer test between 3:30-10pm.

Doors open at 3:30, dinner is served at 4:30, and we have to be out every morning by 9am.

I have 5 other girls in my room but we have a personal bathroom in each room.

There's a day room and free laundry once per week.

top_reviews.text:
This used to be the best thrift store in Cabarrus County. Yes, used to be. It has gone downhill ever since they reopened after C*vid. That's part of the problem too - all new staff due to firing the old staff during C*vid times...ones who had been there for years & were so sweet.
The new manager is a guy who frequently complains openly about people shopping in the store, has literally complained about having to check my cart of stuff because I "got too much" and it'd take a while to scan it all in (I had maybe 6 books, a couple of shoes and some small nicknacks - it wasn't a lot). He's also changed sale hours - day of - closing early because he felt like it. He does not make people feel welcome to shop there - it's like we're bothering him to be in the store.
Also, the pricing has gotten really bad - it's frequently at or above retail now, which is so sad since this stuff is always clearly used and *given/donated* to the store, but they grossly overprice it. Case in point: A used coffee grinder for $24.99 when it's new for $18.95 on Amazon or $19.98 at Walmart. The clothes have been really stained, hole-filled, torn and ripped lately. I really hate how bad the store is these days... I went in recently and they were selling a side table that was missing two legs, but still had it priced at $39.99. Look at the pictures I posted.
It just makes me so sad since this used to be my favorite thrift store in the area, and it's awful now.
top_reviews.author: Shelley D.

top_reviews.text:
Talk about losing the plot. Prices have gone sky high to the point where they dont even make sense. $20+ for random glassware that doesnt even cost that much NEW. Entire dress rack is $13. Even for Shein dresses that cost that much NEW. Hate to say it, but the Goodwills up the street seem to have much fairer pricing. Its unfortunate. This used to be one of my fav stops. Not anymore.

In Response: You and all other non-profit thrift stores essentially have the same goal. You can copy and paste that "approved" response S much as you like. The fact still remains that your customers are complaining about pricing. You're surrounded by thrift stores who have the same costs as you, but manage to maintain reasonable pricing. Theres no reason why USED Shein dress is $13, while Shein sells those same NEW Shein dresses sell for $10-$15. Theres also no reason to sell dollar tree items for $3+ USED while they are $1.50 or less at the dollar tree. You can ignore the reviews about your pricing and lose customers, or you can fix it. The decision is up to you.

top_reviews.text:
_5-Star Review: A Thrift Shop Gem!_

I'm thrilled to have discovered this exceptional thrift shop, and I'm eager to share my outstanding experience with others. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the store's cleanliness and organization. The aisles were well-arranged, making it easy to navigate and find what I was looking for. The shop's atmosphere was welcoming and tidy, with a clear attention to detail that sets it apart from other thrift stores.

The employees and management were friendly, helpful, and courteous. They were happy to assist me with any questions I had and made sure I had a pleasant shopping experience. Their customer service skills were top-notch, and it's clear that they take pride in their work.

What really impressed me, however, was the vast and diverse selection of merchandise. The store is extremely organized, with items neatly categorized and displayed. I found a wide range of high-quality items, including clothing, accessories, household goods, and more. The prices were very reasonable, making it easy to find great deals on gently used items.

Overall, I'm thoroughly impressed with this thrift shop and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great shopping experience. The combination of cleanliness, organization, friendly staff, and excellent selection makes it a standout in its category. Whether you're a seasoned thrifter or just looking for a unique shopping experience, this store is definitely worth checking out. Five stars isn't enough - I'd give it ten stars if I could!

I also asked if the paperwork could be emailed to me or picked up by someone else, since I cannot keep leaving work early without losing money. She did not handle this professionally at all.

I took everything elsewhere immediately after, and they were THRILLED to receive it — as any donation center should be.

The Salvation Army is a Protestant Christian church, believing in the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), Jesus' divinity and atonement, and the Bible as God's inspired word, emphasizing salvation through repentance and faith. Their mission, rooted in the love of God, is to preach the Gospel and meet human needs without discrimination, famously translating faith into action through service, but they don't practice traditional sacraments like baptism or communion as essential for salvation, focusing instead on spiritual regeneration and practical charity.

top_reviews.text:
employees are indolent, uncouth, negligent and possess a total lack of initiative. we moved out of our house recently and had 15+ garbage bags full of quality clothing/blankets/etc... I usually try to donate to this organization because it seems more people in need tend to shop here/take advantage of their services. however, upon trying to drop off the donations (at 2pm on a wednesday) I was told they didn't have anyone working in the back by the donation area. I proceed to ask if someone could come with a large bin or something similar to collect the items I wanted to donate, and they told me I could bring them inside in a shopping cart, *if I really wanted to do that* - reiterating the fact I had a LOT of items and a shopping cart would take me 20+ trips inside.... UPDATE: I called again and a Hispanic lady was helpful and kind and even gave a hello and greeting. The previous woman should get customer service training from her.

This review is regarding an interaction I recently had while attempting to assist a friend with contacting the Salvation Army Myles Park location in Cleveland.

When calling the facility, the operator answered the phone huffing and puffing, then passed me on. I then spoke with the individual responsible for billing. During multiple attempts to communicate, she was extremely dismissive and unprofessional. She repeatedly stated she was “busy” and “with a client,” and when asked if there was an alternative way to reach her or a better time to call back, she provided no guidance or assistance. Her tone was abrupt, dismissive, and lacked any sense of compassion or willingness to help.

I understand that staff may be occupied; however, the manner in which this interaction was handled was discourteous and did not reflect the values or mission that the Salvation Army represents. As a Christian organization dedicated to service, compassion, and support for those in need, it is deeply concerning to encounter behavior that feels the opposite of those principles—especially when individuals are reaching out for help during vulnerable situations.
Individuals seeking assistance should feel respected, supported, and treated with empathy.

I hope this feedback can help ensure a more compassionate and professional experience for those reaching out in need.

top_reviews.text:
I'm unsure as to who answered the phone but whoever she was was incredibly unprofessional and unhelpful. My fiance and I are both chronically Ill and just lost our residence due to a fire set by one of our next door neighbors, and when I called looking for assistance the woman there answered the phone but didn't say anything and continued her background conversation. When I waited for her to get finished, she said in a frustrated tone "Hello?!". I said hello and she finally said "Salvation Army"
I explained that we lost our place due to a fire and I was looking for any type of assistance and she just asked me what assistance I was looking for. After pausing for a moment, caught off guard because I expected her to explain to me what kind of assistance they could offer, I just confusingly said "any type of rental or housing assistance.." She then told me that they don't provide rental assistance nor hotel vouchers and told me to call CMHA.
I said "Oh, okay... Thank you" then the woman just hung up on me before I could say or ask anything else.
(I had looked on the Salvation Army website that said that they provided emergency housing assistance but I didn't know that only certain Salvation Army sites offer housing assistance and this wasn't explained to me)
After this phone call I felt not only more frustrated than the original situation left me feeling, but also confused and like I was being a bother to someone who was supposed to provide assistance during a trying time.
I'd say if you can avoid calling this location at all to do so, but if you unfortunately do have to call this location, try to get a caseworker to deal with them instead. A much better place for assistance is the Red Cross if you need any kind of emergency assistance.

I messaged them on Facebook, explained, and sent photos of my receipt. I also explained that I live out of town so I only stop in when driving through. I was told to bring my receipt in next time and they would give me a store credit.
I just now made it there more than a month later, brought my receipt in, and was told by the assistant manager that I needed to talk to the manager who was not there. The assistant manager, who also happens to be the same one who assured me she didn’t overcharge me in the first place, said their policy is 3 days, so apparently, AGAIN, she did not listen to me, because I explained and showed her my message saying I could bring my receipt in next time I came in. THE 3 DAY POLICY DOES NOT APPLY WHEN *YOU* OVERCHARGE SOMEONE! *YOUR MISTAKE* NOT MINE. I’m not returning or exchanging, I am getting money back that you overcharged. (So if I did come back within 3 days but the manager wasn’t there, then what?)
So I send a message while I’m there, hoping to reach the manager, who I assume is the one who replied to my previous message. They read it, didn’t reply. Sent another message later, they read, didn’t reply.
So, I guess I’m just out of the money.

top_reviews.text: So, this is a Days Inn, not the Four Seasons or Grand Hotel.  I stayed 3 days/nights and all 3 days/nights cost me less than one night in some of those hoity-toity places.  Is it pretty?  Nope.  Is it sterile in every millimeter of the place?  Not even close.  Were the beds Sealy Tempur-Pedic or Sleep-by-Number?  Not even remotely close...my bed was more akin to taking 2 baskets of laundry and throwing them into a big pile on the floor.  It was HARD, LUMPY, I felt like I'd been hit by a Peterbilt semi when I tried to get out of bed.  I was (and am still) in EXCRUCIATING pain from easily THE WORST mattress I've ever almost slept on.  The place needed a total remodel 65 years ago, and it's obvious the minute you go in.  All that being said, it was EXACTLY what I paid for...a cheap room for a short get-away from life.  It wasn't spotless but it wasn't filthy.  With the exception of ONE old bat of a woman who came in my room while I was sleeping and started SHOUTING at me (NOT KIDDING) that I needed to pay.  I had no idea that I was required to pay for additional nights by a certain time as long as I did so.  So, after being RUDELY awakened and yelled at by a 300 year old woman I went down and added two more daus/nights, and made it known to the elderly man at the front desk how I was treated.  Aside from that one lady everyone was very kind and helpful.  I needed a shower stool as I'm disabled and one was brought to me in under 5 minutes.    My only real complaints are that old bat that shouted at me, the ABSOLUTELY HORRENDOUS mattress, and the shower that kept going ICE COLD to the temperature of the SUN'S CORONA!!  I needed a cheap, relatively clean place to stay with no vermin and that's exactly what I got.  Also, I plan on doing this more in the future as I have no set hours for work.  I drive Amish and I've made my availability 7 days a week, 24 hours a day.  So, once in a while one needs to regroup and just get away.  I will be back here again for my next recharge, although I'll more than likely request a room with a bed that is less like broken concrete and more like a real bed!  Oh, and a MAJOR PLUS is that there are SMOKING ROOMS here.  I have included several photos for your enjoyment and if you enlarge them you'll be able to see areas where cleanliness could use a little more attention and the outdated appointments in the room.  One other nice thing is that there are balconies on the 2nd floor that can be accessed if desired from each room.

top_reviews.text:
I came in to get some fabric for an art project and found a pair of curtains that fit my needs. I had a $5 budget. I checked the posted prices and saw that curtains were marked at $2.99.

The curtains I grabbed had two panels. Each was on a separate hanger, but the second was hooked into the first, so they were connected. There was one blue tag on the top curtain that said "1 pair of curtains." When I got to the checkout, the lady at the register asked if I knew it was $2.99 per panel. I was not aware of that, but I said it was fine, as I only needed one panel. She then said, "But they are a pair; they go together!" I replied, "If you are selling them separately, I will take one, please." I asked if she understood why I was confused, as they were both together with one tag. I said it's like me telling you I am selling a pair of shoes for $50, and when you go to pay, I say, "It's actually $50 per shoe." 🤔 She told me she was just following their policy. I honestly didn't mind just buying one; she was the one bothered. As the situation progressed, I became irritated because it made no sense. Had they been marked $6, I would've passed them up.
We both were respectful, and it ended on a pleasant note. This is just a heads up, apparently the sets, even when they put them together, are sold separately.
Edited to address the reply:
The woman at the register told me SHE put the curtains together as a pair and tagged the item that day (yesterday 1/18/26) she hung the 2nd curtain off the other and made ONE tag that said "ONE PAIR OF CURTAINS". Then told me I had to pay for each one separately. I am not sure what people swapping tags has to do with this at all? If you are insinuating I was trying to get the 2nd curtain free, you're dead wrong. I didnt even need both. Im cutting it up for a project.
Anyone else I talk to about this can understand the issue. Sorry, you cant. If you have cameras, I encourage you to go through and watch my entire 5 min in store. This isn't that serious. I used your store for materials because I make art. I can get cheap fabric elsewhere.

top_reviews.text:
EDIT: Over the last few months the Salvation Army has went down hill dramatically.  The prices are almost brand new.  You can easily get anything they sell online from ebay or sometimes amazon for less money and the item will have at least a 30 day warranty.  They have stopped taking donations that are even questionable.  I had a nice coffee table and 2 end tables that did have just a few (less than 3 scratches).  The guy taking donations said they wont take any of them.  He also said that they are changing what they are taking for donations and hopefully getting better quality stuff for sale, but are going to be charging even more.

This makes no sense to me, we want almost brand new items for free, then sell them for more than brand new prices and don't give any warranty for anything.  This is not sustainable, nor does it help anyone that works there (everyone will be out jobs very soon) and it hurts everyone that can not afford a brand new item.  Some furniture is better than no furniture.  There are some people in Cincinnati that don't even have a couch or a chair or tables in their house and the salvation army used to be a wonderful alternative for very cheap.  Now it is not any alternative for anyone, you can purchase most items new for cheaper.

I love the salvation army for what they do, but they are starting to not help the needy and that makes me very sad.  I truly hope they help out our less fortunate neighbors. Until then I can not change my rating.

OLD REVIEW: I love shopping at the salvation army.  They have all sorts of treasures.  I have bought REAL Coach purses for the wife, and PS4 for me.  Most everything works, but you should always try it out before you buy it.  PS they hire people that can't get a job anywhere, and that want to work.  The addition part of the building is a really great program that helps out a lot of people.  So when you are looking for a shirt for $1.99 think of the great deal you are getting and all the people that you are helping along the way.

PS tell Robin (the manager) that Jordan sent you and he will give you a big Hi Five!!

PPS he really likes robin, batman and robin.

Needless to say I was dumbfounded, especially considering I just recently moved here upon buying a house and have only been in this store one time for 5 minutes. I tried to ask her for a reason and that I believed she was confusing me with perhaps someone else(?) but she was extremely rude, condescending AND adamant. I do not appreciate how I was treated(like a criminal) nor being verbally threatened. I have never in my life been treated this way. I buy most of my furniture from thrift shops and spend a good deal at these places (because i prefer vintage items and it recycles and helps community)Honestly I was half tempted to tell her to go ahead and call the police for I have zero clue but I don't like confrontation. I will be trying to contact management for I prefer to have this cleared up. Regardless this employee did not have to behave the way she did & from other reviews it seems this behavior may be common. The whole thing lefte shaken and confused leaving a very bad impression if the store and doubting if I would even shop there. I did want to add that later that day I did realize it was a Saturday which is a day that they are indeed "closed" and I hadnt realized what day it was. I'm guessing THAT must be the reason this employee behaved the way she did but it still does NOT excuse ger behavior. All she had to do was answer my first question in regards to being closed...I then would've turned and left asap! I work 60 hour weeks graveyard shift and lose track of days often. Secondly the doors were unlocked and I had previously watched another lady enter and exit prior to me which led to believing they was in fact open. Guessing that lady before me was donating? Regardless, the situation was escalated immediately to threats and defensive behaviors. I did also just notice an employee(?) has now responded so I will contact them in response. top_reviews.text:
I would give zero stars if I could.  I was in the men's section and personally saw this guy push an ENTIRE CART of clothes that he picked from first - from the employee section where clothes are tagged.

When I told the staff including the manager that it wasn't right for him to do this they responded "he comes in here every week and spends $400".  Another staff said to me "I'm not going to deal with this on Christmas Eve".  RIGHT.  On Christmas Eve, the day we celebrate the birth of God - who came into this world and abundantly but you are defending this man for being greedy and denying other people an equal opportunity to purchase donated items.

You claim to be a non profit and a ministry but you show favoritism?  Other customers can't go in the back and fill a cart with clothes before they go on the floor.

Ironically, if you let everyone have a fair chance more people would come in more often, and your sales would be higher.  But you would rather not do things God's way.  The Bible says "each one did what was right in his own eyes" by showing partiality you are doing just that.  "God does not show favoritism" (Romans 2:11) or try on another translation for size "For there is no respect of persons with God (Romans 2:11).

___

Update: Last week I spoke with the warehouse manager and store manager and they said I could also go into the employee section and have first choice. name: Salvation Army Social Services - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text: I wasn’t going to do a review because they helped me when I needed it but these things should be said. Salvation Army has lost a significant, regular donor to the organization based on the way myself and others were treated. I wasn’t aware that my cats foster parents are donors to Salvation Army. She would ask how things were there and I would tell her how no, they don’t have clothes or shoes for us here or everyone is forced outside all day from 7:15-3 because they don’t want to deal with us and how I was accosted by Johns, witnessed a fight in the alley across the street and was regularly harassed, because I had to be out wandering the streets all day. I told her how a lady passed out from heat exhaustion (I had to catch her to keep her head from hitting the concrete) and because it was still about five minutes until 3pm and she didn’t want an ambulance, they just left her there on the ground to wait until after 3pm outside and wouldn’t even let her in the vestibule to cool off. I told her about being written up continually and not allowed an extension for oversleeping even though I have a neurological condition that makes me have excessive daytime sleepiness. I told her how we were constantly yelled at and how it felt like jail. Finally one day she got so mad and said she was removing them from her list of donors and won’t be sending any more checks. That was the first I knew of them being donors. The employees could be nice at times and not so nice at times. One employee asked how I was going to make it in the world, knowing I have this brain condition that makes it impossible for me to make it and is why I’m unhoused now, but it wasn’t always the case. I say this to say, you never know who people know so just treat everyone with kindness, compassion and empathy. I am at a different facility now and it’s night and day. This facility is now being placed on my cats foster families donor list to replace Salvation Army.
top_reviews.author: Ardis Glover

top_reviews.text: My family had been trying to get utility assistance from this place for almost 5 months now. Calling every single Monday at 8:30 am as instructed and it's the same thing every time. I've got a funny feeling that they cherry pick people to help with utilities. Probably someone that works there hooking up family members with assistance every month and real people not getting any help at all. I cant understand why I am never ever ever ever able to get any assistance with utilities here. Seems fishy. top_reviews.text: I’m extremely disappointed and can not believe the way I was treated by the “store manager” in Shawnee. I called on Tuesday to ask if they were taking donations again after COVID. I was told yes so I stated I would bring my donations by on Thursday at 10:00 am. I arrived at 10:30 on Thursday to find the gate locked so I went inside the store and asked the only person working there what I should do with my donations. She said leave them outside the gate (there was already several boxes & bags there). As I started to unload my donations a man yells at me telling me I can’t do that. He states he is the store manager. I explained I asked and was told to leave the items. He said can’t you read the sign, nothing is to be dropped off if the gates not open.  I said I called, I also asked the store employee and I pointed out their hours to accept donations was 10:00 am to 4:00 pm and it was now 10:45.  I asked him what should I do with my donations and he said it looked like junk and he would probably have to throw it away. I said it’s not junk, the boxes were just dirty. He said it looks like it’s been sitting in a garage. I said it has but the items in the boxes were good. He said he didn’t care he was not going to accept it, which totally shock me. I’ve been bring donations to Salvation Army for several years and never been treated like this. The donations were in the garage because of COVID and no one was accepting donations when I boxed the items. He said again he wouldn’t accept the donations which he called junk so I went to the main office to complain. A very nice lady told me she would meet me down at the store. I went back to the donation site and he still refused my donations. I opened the box to show her what was inside (wrapped drinking glasses, plates, and other kitchen items). She said it look nice but the man still refused. He was being so arrogant and condescending to both of us.  She turned to me and said we could take it to a nearby dumpster or I could take it to Goodwill. I told her I couldn’t believe I was treated this way and I would never donate to them again. How disheartening it has been to be treated this way when I only wanted to help Salvation Army.

top_reviews.text:
I’ve supported Salvation Army for years because of its mission, but what happened at the S. Harvard Tulsa location was one of the clearest displays of racial discrimination I’ve experienced in a long time.

I arrived 10 minutes before closing to quickly purchase an item I had already chosen earlier in the day. I had assistance lined up and was ready to pay immediately. The staff flat-out refused to let me enter.

Moments later, they allowed a white customer inside after I was denied — a customer who openly said they had no intention of buying anything.

So let’s call this what it is:
A Black customer ready to spend money was turned away, and a white customer with zero intent to purchase was welcomed in.

There’s no “policy” explanation that makes that acceptable but this was enforced by manager on duty "Clinton Boyles" (if that was even his real name).

As a business owner myself, I know the difference between enforcing closing procedures and selectively deciding who is “worth” bending them for. This was not about time. This was not about rules. This was bias.

If this is how Salvation Army treats loyal customers — especially African American ones — it needs to be known. I will be escalating this, publicly and privately, until corporate addresses it.

Your mission says one thing. Your staff’s behavior says something entirely different.
top_reviews.author: Anthony Pegues-Johnson

top_reviews.text: I use to love Salvation Army but the fact that the store on Harvard  has an enormous amount of people buying  to sell for higher prices online. They are constantly on their phones taking photos of items they believe are worth more. It's a disservice to communities and to shoppers who shop online. SA should regulate this by doing what these people do  research  and mark up these items so SA gets the profit for the needy. Or they should ask them to stop. It creates an environment that I personally don't want to shop in while all these people are digging researching & pricing. There are other places they can buy merchandise for their online business. top_reviews.text:
The Salvation army is an absolute scam and joke. The poor guys who are there work their tails off for $7 a week. Not $7 per hour, but per week! I was a "client" there in 2022 and we would work 48 hours per week in that incredibly hot and dirty warehouse for that pitiful pay and they get away with it by calling what we get paid GRATUITY. When you first arrive they sign you up for Food Stamps and keep YOUR stamps. They are scamming the system and need to  be exposed and shut down.

I remember one day a donor came for a walk-through with the Captain. They had SPECIFICALLY told us to NEVER speak with the donors, but she came straight to me. She asked me about my job. I told her I ran the electronics department and sent all my products to the stores and the weekly auctions. Then she asked me if i got paid well enough for "working in the hot warehouse?" To which I laughed and told her "No ma'am. I get $7 per week which is as about  .$15 an hour." The Captain tried to cut me off but I had already said it. He was deeply offended and whipped up a quick story and said "That was their old pay, we're still working out the new pay rate." I can still picture the look on that woman's face. She was mortified she had donated and supported S.A.

SA is able to get away with it by calling it WORK THERAPY. All they really care about is how much money they can make at their stores and their auctions. I'm sure when the SA was founded and began they really were interested and focused on helping people. But the man has become a monster. Clients are no longer people, just numbers who they get  free labor out of and makes them money. Shut these corrupt crooks and thieves down! DO NOT donate or support the Salvation Army!!!

top_reviews.text:
I’ve had very disappointing experiences with the Salvation Army since the new management took over. The organization has become extremely unorganized and difficult to work with.

Any time I’ve asked for assistance, the answer has always been “no.” I witnessed a heartbreaking situation where a woman was trying to get a food box for a disabled person through J Bar J, but the staff refused to help because the person couldn’t pick it up themselves. There was no compassion or effort to accommodate his situation.

I also had issues when trying to get Christmas assistance. The process was chaotic and poorly managed. The staff barely spoke English, seemed disorganized, and acted suspicious—constantly peeking out of the blinds before opening. When I went to sign up for Christmas help, I had to beg to use the bathroom, and they told me to use a porta-potty in an alley while I was holding my 2-year-old son. wouldn't let my son play with toys near by said I had to hold him while trying to get through the application.. I've been there years before even volunteering a couple Christmas and have never been treated so poorly.

Last year and this year, the Christmas assistance program has been a nightmare. Despite providing a list of needs, the only items I received were a few outfits for my boys—no toys for my girls. I was initially told to come on December 19, but on that day, they called to reschedule for December 23 at 2 PM. Even then, my items weren’t ready until after 3 PM, and they almost didn’t give me my ID back. They also allowed others, seemingly their friends, to cut in line while the rest of us were made to wait.

This place feels disorganized and untrustworthy,  they never answer the phone always have a full message machine.
and I can’t shake the feeling that something shady is going on behind closed doors.
I hope someone looks into this, as their treatment of people in need has been unacceptable.

top_reviews.text: I am a Christian woman, was considering the food bank for the 1st time and since Salvation Army was right by my home, my daughter (6) and I stopped by to get some food help. I tried calling 3X before going there to make sure there was availability but nobody ever picked up the phone. My daughter and I drove there arrived at 1130. The bank closes at 12 and we had an appt across the street an hour before. We were nervous and clueless about what to expect so I reached to open the door and immediately, the door was ripped from my hand from a Senior woman in a walker (assuming she runs the program or front desk area). She yanks the door closed, locks both sides and preceded to yell at me from inside "We are CLOSED, CAN'T YOU SEE THE SIGN?" And she walks away. My daughter looks at me scared and I am just shocked so I gently tapped on the door and then knocked only to ask when we can come back and if I need to sign up or anything before hand. She preceded to yell through the door that I needed to come back tomorrow and said she isn't allowing anyone else in... my daughter started to cry and we left... I was shocked, this is supposed to be a place of unity, peace, a place of worship. That is not the behavior you would've expected. To be honest I felt like I was being talked down to and to behave in such a rude, unwelcoming , aggressive and hurtful way in front of a child was just astonishing. It ruined my first attempt at getting help from my "community" charity..I am sad that my daughter had to see this entire thing.

top_reviews.text: Now my review is based on my experience in 2016-2017… during the intake process, which is uncomfortable to begin with if you have never been homeless before, the woman had no smile on her face and actually told my daughter (3yo at the time) to sit quietly bc she was walking around looking at things in the office as baby’s do… at that point I felt more hopeless and realized I could lose my only chance to keep my baby warm if I tell this woman not to talk to not only my child like that but any 3 year old like that. I forget her name, she had an accent.. I felt hopeless. We had just left my child’s father and this was our only option bc he was also financially abusive and would even hide my food stamp card. Anyways we get “settled” in I suppose and I don’t remember any of the staff being friendly at all. My daughter had thrown up in the cafeteria on the floor and i proceeded to clean up my child before I took care of the floor. An elderly woman with white hair and glasses was mean and nasty and actually had the nerve to tell me I should be ashamed of myself and that she can tell I clearly have no experience being a mom. My jaw dropped. As if I already didn’t feel ashamed for being there in the first place I had an old woman standing there watching me clean my child and making yet another difficult situation even more difficult. Things like this happened often. Just staff being rude and authoritative instead of kind and hospitable. All I needed was a smile and some kindness, nothing more. I was there 4 days and this is what I experienced. I know I couldn’t get myself together in this facility. I was trying to heal from a toxic relationship, and was being mistreated. I couldn’t chance someone mistreating my child. I got into the sixth street shelter and there is where I realized staff at shelters are not supposed to act the way they did at the Salvation Army. My father stored most of our belongings and I was able to bring all of our stuff with us to 6th street. They were truly kind. I wish I could remember my counselors name… after I left the 6th street shelter I went back to see if he could possibly get one of my moms pots I forgot in a cabinet, although he said no, he sat with me. Talked to me, cared about what I had to say and offered guidance. I walked out of there content and grateful and he even gave me two Easter baskets for my 2 daughters. Again, this was between 2016-2017. I pray 6th street shelter only moved up and continue to love on those who need it and that the Salvation Army on 7th street got rid of there staff from back then and learned some compassion and empathy bc I will never recommend this place to anyone struggling. I’ll give up my couch first before I allow any woman or child to go there.

Sometimes they may not be able to accomplish certain needs, but if there is a way, there is definitely a will on their part to help every single person who asks.

Assuming they are a community driven store, they would have no issues with the community using their parking lot for the parade, also the store was closed. When we tried to exit the parking lot after the parade, we were greeted by a sarcastic, im assuming employee, we were berated and threatened to have our vehicle towed.
Good bye Salvation Army
top_reviews.author: patrick lare

top_reviews.text: The store went through a renovation recently and the layout is way more convenient! There is also a new staff running it that seems much more knowledgeable about what should be in the store (less junk). Pricing is comparable to a ther thrift stores in the area and the selection seems like it’s updated daily. It’s a great place to shop!
top_reviews.author: Kevin Riley

top_reviews.text: Wow! I stopped in the thrift store on Tuesday and it looks amazing! Long gone are the out dated clothes, cast off books, and useless CD’s. Now the store is more like a boutique that offers Michael Kors bags for $15 and London Fog trench coats for $6! Great job to the new manager & staff, you guys have done a fantastic job!
top_reviews.author: Ashley Coffman

top_reviews.text: I went to go in for something quick five minutes before they closed and when I walked in the door, shorter older woman Snap at me saying “you have two minutes” With the rudest tone and expression. She Did not say hi nor did not have any customer service at all. I immediately left and will not be back.
top_reviews.author: Lisa Boltz

top_reviews.text: they're nice and they give hygiene bags did you not give food but on there soup kitchens breakfast kitchens they give you a list of all the places that you can get help with and that's it they push. U to 211 or the church lol the church would tell u the salvation army but there's still helpful

top_reviews.text: They have really raised their prices!
