top_reviews.text: People are full of drama here when you try not to pay them any mind; They still find a way to bring you down. If you don't NEED to come here , DON'T. Some people forced to live here are great BUT the staff needs better Supervision from the upper Mgmt. Volunteers take supplies home instead of using it for the needy. Lou Morse needs to keep a better eye on Sharon and Matthew. They do not take homelessness seriously.
top_reviews.author: Al Sander

top_reviews.text: I was there for like 8 months 2 years ago and it was one of the worse experiences ever. They made people sit outside all day on Saturdays rain or shine cold or hot. They don’t really care about the people in there like they claim. The staff is disrespectful except a few. They don’t make you feel heard at all.
top_reviews.author: Ciani

top_reviews.text: I was forced there because of professional abuse I was beaten by 7 police officers at my apartment complex. These people told me I had to stop being a chronic homeless person with mental issues!?  Where do you see that at when I was unconscious for 7 days in the hospital and was discharged after a month?
top_reviews.author: Francene Faustino

name: The Salvation Army- Chester - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text: Always helping and supporting anybody n everybody in need in so many different ways.....The after school program was always amazing n my son always looked so excitedly n happily forward every week to the van pulling in to pick him up to take him to a place where he could just be who he was n be fully accepted n loved n surrounded by happiness, joy, support and all around positivity.....The people there were always such great role models for the kids n my son was lucky enough to have one of the younger male volunteers really take him under his wing n share a beautiful bond even outside of the program to have the type of male figure in his life that he so desperately needed.
top_reviews.author: Virginia J Rose

top_reviews.text: Come and greet the newly appointed officers to the Clearfield corps, Major Stan and Norma Newton! If you're looking for a welcoming church family please stop in and say hi. Bible study is Sunday 10-11 A.M. and worship service is from 11 A.M. to noon. Hope to see you there 😁
top_reviews.author: Rob Carr

top_reviews.text: the food pantry was very generous it was what I needed to get me through till payday
top_reviews.author: John Fiscus

top_reviews.text: So I didn’t have the most pleasant experience at first either. However, after waiting and sitting in my car, someone came out to help a person with food. I approached the guy running the place, Captain Davi, and found out that this location since Covid, is largely understaffed. It’s also not the main West Chester site, which I had made a mistake on. They do as much as they can, but they need help!! Anyone looking for a job, they need a front desk person. After finding out what’s going on behind the doors, it eased the anxiety and helped me be more empathetic. Have some patience and try to talk to Captain Davi. They do all they can.
top_reviews.author: Bethany Swank

top_reviews.text: Leave your number and they'll call you to let know if they can help.....nope! Left my number with a hispanic woman and she was suppose to give my info to whoever and never gotten a phone call back with the help I need! No wonder here and there I only go there to get food!
top_reviews.author: Rachel C

top_reviews.text: I donate clothing here. Nice people.
top_reviews.author: Robert Richie

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: When I first started shopping at this location, maybe a year or two ago I loved it. Prices were reasonable and the clothes and shoes were looking good in my opinion. Fast forward to this week, the prices are ridiculously high for items that The Salvation Army gets for free. Coats are $99, some dresses (that again were donated) are $69.99 and up and I saw a pair of boots in there for $60.00. Now I know that people have to get paid, there are bills that need to be paid and other things that should be taken care of. However, the prices that are set in this store you might as well just go to Ross or Marshalls. I enjoy thrifting but the prices make me walk out and go to any type of retail store. Half off days are good but the prices are outrageous!
top_reviews.author: Danielle Barron

top_reviews.text: Today I got rid of a lot of things, I came in to ask if I could bring my mattress and a old guy said yes, I even showed him pictures. I came back with my mattress and an old lady said they couldn't take it because it had some yellow stains that weren't pretty much visible and she said to bring it back outside with an attitude. Honestly I would give this place a 0.
top_reviews.author: Brigith Duvon

top_reviews.text: Um...so...is this a joke? Because what kind of pricing strategy is this? 🤣 It was half off day and the store was DESERTED. That's unheard of at a thrift store. I took an Uber home with the money I had planned to spend because why on earth would I buy used goods at retail prices?
top_reviews.author: Aziza Walker

top_reviews.text:
I don't know that I've ever donated goods to a less helpful or less friendly center.

I came around the drop off window in the back, where two staff ignored me.

I came in the front, where I was informed "we need to grab someone to see if anything you brought is worth having in the store." I have never, ever heard something like that about donations.

When the staff member came out front to check whether my donations were "worth it", he seemed impatient. Not so impatient that he actually helped unload any of it from my car, though.

I asked him before he wheeled his dolly back inside if they were interested in any other goods I had planned to donate. He said they'd consider it with what is best described as a sneer.

I donated a wooden table, some wall art, and some clothes. But I'm afraid this will be the only time I do. I've heard they do good in this community, but I don't plan to donate in the future. I would not recommend anyone else do so either.
top_reviews.author: Brendan McWilliams

top_reviews.text: Zero stars!!! Here I am again in search of utility help!! Courtney is extremely rude she told me they won't help me because of my zip code but I told her I am in Fayette county!!! Some people's kids man!! SMH 🙄 in the process of speaking to her supervisor....
top_reviews.author: meagan shaffer

top_reviews.text: Nicest people ever and always do their best to help any and everyone they can
top_reviews.author: Simone Cooley

top_reviews.text: People there are great and helpful. Stop in and explain your situation, they will help you.
top_reviews.author: Chris Mcdannel

top_reviews.text: They are always willing to help if they can. Very friendly Captain and family.
top_reviews.author: Kelli Price

top_reviews.text: Not open though it states it was online. No one answered phone.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
OMG!!! I love to shop and this store has great things, but when you come to register you need to watch closely!!! The very first item was charged wrong in stead of $4.99 it was $5.99. She is not cancelling the wrong charge, but adding a new one on top!!! Then, by mistake the lady charges 0.99 cents for the item that cost $9.99 it ok , again she is not cancelling , but charge a full price, So I purchased 28 items, but was charged for 31.
I don't care how much cost what ever I choose, but when someone is lying to your face, that is UGLY! I would rather DONATE this $$$ to the people that are in need!!!!!
top_reviews.author: Orders Absolute

top_reviews.text: This store doesn't compare to the store in Bloomsburg!  The windows look awful, the only things plentiful are the clothes and shoes and they aren't hung by size so it takes forever to find your own. Hanging by color accomplishes nothing if it takes you half an hour to go through every item to find your size!
top_reviews.author: Jacqueline Nash

top_reviews.text: This store has gone down hill.  It is messy and the shelves a not full,  prices are high.  They have so much in stock but never put it on shelves.  What’s going on?
top_reviews.author: Linda Fowler

top_reviews.text: I was blown away with how friendly the staff was at 11:43 AM. Everybody was upbeat checked in on me to make sure I was finding things OK the store was very clean and neat and in order I frequent thrift stores on the regular the only negative I took from this experience was that I felt a lot of the items were priced a little high, but one of the best staffs for any thrift store I ever walked through.
top_reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

top_reviews.text: I took a friend here a couple weeks ago for help. The lady who helped her was so kind. She was one of those people who radiate happiness and I couldn't help but smile while with her. They were serving lunch and insisted my friend take some soup. She's still telling people how good it was. It makes me happy to know that our poor and or homeless are being fed with such care.

top_reviews.text: The prices at this salvation are so screwed up. Junk is over priced and nice jackets I found were $30 $50 and $90?! For old winter jackets . Dumb

top_reviews.text: Had what I wanted @a good deal!

top_reviews.text: Salvation Army is the Pillar of our Community, they help the Children up to 18 year of age By passing out Over 100 Food Trays in all the Neighborhoods in the Summertime! They have Food Pantry one a month. There is Bible Study, Summer Camp for the Children, Church Services on Sunday and other worthwhile programs! I love to volunteer!

top_reviews.text: I didn't know about the Angel tree at all tell they told me about it cuz started in late August and I didn't see anything on Facebook about the sign up cuz there was nothing posted so how people supposed know about anything on Facebook for that now I can't get hardly anything for my son

top_reviews.text:
If it wasn't for the kindness of these people I might have gone hungry at times. Although they don't give gormet food they try to help and that's all that matters.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart

top_reviews.text: I always have liked to donate anything I no longer use to Salvation Army, why? Because they always give so much back to others
top_reviews.author: Gayle Punchios

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Before I would have rated this store 5 stars. However in the last few weeks the prices have went through the roof. Things that were normally a great deal are now on par with retail prices. It's disappointing, especially when you take into account that the inventory is donated. Do yourself a favor and if you go to this store research the prices before you purchase.

*This is an edit to a review posted a year ago. It seems as if they have not gotten better with their pricing but have gotten significantly worse. It is almost comical how much money they want for things. The only thing that is worth purchasing in here is when they have $0.99 tags. Otherwise more often than not you can get them new cheaper. For instance I will add two pictures that I took today. One is a stormtrooper they want $15 for. I understand that some of these action figures can be worth a large sum of money this one is not and it has dirt on its face. They also have a grab bag of old beat up letter blocks it is not even the full set It is eight of them for $6. I understand there is overhead to running a store and doing the work that they do And at times that may be difficult. But it becomes impossible to do that when you price your items so comically high that customers do not come there anymore. I know I will get a generic response about how it cost money to run a store and they will certainly get with the management but there has been plenty reviews on this store about prices being absolutely out of control and nothing has been done so I won't hold my breath.*
top_reviews.author: Alexander Evans

top_reviews.text: Prices are OK. Books are $0.99 for paperbacks and $1.99 for hardbacks. DVDs/CDs are $1.99 for each disc. So if you find a box set that contains 8 discs they want $16  for it. Other than that pricing is a little high but somewhat reasonable.

top_reviews.text: Everything is color coded. It's great. The cashier was also very pleasant. We got many name brand items.

top_reviews.text: The gal there was friendly when we dropped off food, we couldn't take it with us heading back home on the plane from our vacation. Glad to not have to throw out good food.

top_reviews.text: God is good there anytime things are low there always there to help that are a blessing
top_reviews.author: Trudy Truss

top_reviews.text: I live in Easton Pa; it would be nice to have someone answer phone calls at the front desk.  I called about 10× today no answer. you are very nice people and I enjoy going to the food pantry.  I do understand completely that you are busy with other things.  It would be nice to hear another person on the other end of the phone saying Hello and Thank you for calling the Salvation Army.  I had forgot my appointment today at 10 a.m. and no one has answered the telephones please work on having someone at the front desk to answer calls when they come in.  I know and understnad to leave a message when no answers but in reality it can be a waste of time.  Its Okay though everything happens for a reason I am upset about no answering the phone.  I will continue working with the Salvation Army.  I will be up shortly for my appointment for the food pantry and lunch.

top_reviews.text:
There is no thrift store here, even though it comes up as one on Google when you search for thrift stores in the area. It is just a community center.
I wish there was one here, it'd do very very well if there was....
top_reviews.author: Russell Sienkiewicz

top_reviews.text: This is a very small but great spirit filled church. The sermon is in English and Spanish. I love the pastors. Most of the regular members and others are also active volunteers. They have many community services.
top_reviews.author: Carol Williams

top_reviews.text:
Stopped in on Friday, February 27th, 2026 at 4:30 p.m., and while I was shopping, an employee with thinning long hair decided it was the perfect time to talk politics with a separate customer.

He made the charming observation that if “so many people” from a particular group engage in a behavior, then it’s not a stereotype. He followed it up by declaring that anyone who opposes ICE should be tried for treason, while openly supporting the idea of the current administration staying in power for a third term.

Fortunately, like most extremists who feel comfortable spouting off in safe spaces, when someone actually challenges them face-to-face, theynget real quiet.

Customers deserve to shop without being subjected to political rants and half-baked authoritarian fantasies from someone on the clock.
top_reviews.author: Samuel Steinmiller

top_reviews.text: I donated clothes. It was a very awkward transaction. I think I'll just throw them away in the future.

top_reviews.text: Nothing but junk!!! Workers are taking the good stuff an reselling it.

top_reviews.text: Christmas food and toys sign up going on .every Wednesday 10am till 2 pm bring I'd and proof of income.

top_reviews.author: Jeanie Crunkelton

top_reviews.text: Good people. They help out community
top_reviews.author: tammy harvey

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: I love Salvation Army ! It's like an adventure treasure hunt. You never know what you're going to find. So many customers are like family. Missy is a fantastic boss, tries to place us where our gifts lie. She understands we're all human.  I asked myself where would I like to work if I could do anything, and it came back to Salvation Army. I get to see friends that I haven't seen in decades. Everybody that I know from some place or another comes in and it just makes the day so pleasant. It's great to get items for $0.99. I wish they sold gasoline and groceries. I'd never go anywhere else! LOL God bless Salvation Army!!
top_reviews.author: Ruth Giaimo

top_reviews.text: Love this place! Very organized. Great prices! My only issue was a worker passing gas as he walked down the aisle I was about to go down. Needless to say I did not go down that aisle
top_reviews.author: MelSee

top_reviews.text: Fair priced thrifting and always lots of good finds. I love how they price the books and have sale days. Always a fun treasure hunt.
top_reviews.author: Amanda Campbell

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Evidently I can't afford to shop at salvation army anymore... I'll just have to go with the cheaper option of buying new....
I was at this location today and the prices on things are ridiculous $7 to 10 for a used hat(baseball cap, football team), $20 for a used dress hat. $16 for a pair of used pants, $12.99 for used fleece???  Come on, people come here to SAVE, not spend RETAIL or OVER RETAIL You can literally buy 60% of the stuff here brand new shift gear door cheaper. I don't know what's going on but it's kind of crazy.
top_reviews.author: CPS computes

top_reviews.text: Long that every day the have a different color tag half off. Nice selection but make sure you have time to browse. They also have a dressing room which is very convient!
top_reviews.author: Kelli Jordan

top_reviews.text: The women that work here are extremely rude and prices are insane. Smells bad too
top_reviews.author: Lehnix

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text: I used to go to this place all the time spent tons of money and donated plenty of stuff. Lately the staff has just been irritable and nasty to their customers today their machines went down. Everything went down so they could not ring up my almost $100 order on my credit card so I offered to go to find an ATM and get them the money for my purchase when I came back I TRIED To show them that I had gotten out 60, which was apparently the ATM’s limit and immediately after it went out of service, which I had a picture of, I explained that I just needed to remove some things out of my purchase in order for it to be the right amount since I was short about seven dollars or so. I was cut off twice while telling the cashier she told me she needed to ring this up first and she deal with that later. Once she had it rung up, I explained again what I said in the beginning and she got irritated and said well why didn’t you pull out what you didn’t want originally. The fact that I went out of my way to get currency when their systems were not down and the attitude was well you didn’t do it right, Is absolutely absurd. You are an organization that tries to raise money and when somebody tries to spend money there, they get angry with them and make it nearly impossible to do so. After her, raising her voice To me and telling me how I could’ve done it before and I messed it up. I finally started to try to pull the things out in order to make it the right amount that I had which was about $85 compared to the 95 I had rung up. I started to do that. She kept going on about how irritated she was that I didn’t do this in the first place I finally put the clothes down and said forget the entire order and walked out without any items and all my money in my pocket. I will never ever ever ever return to that place again. I’ve had multiple bad experiences and now it’s just not a place. I’m going to give my money.. There are plenty of other organizations and homeless shelters. They can receive my donations and plenty of other thrift stores that can get my purchases.
top_reviews.author: The Crow's Nest With Rochelle Davis

top_reviews.text:
While donating a brand new motorized wheelchair that cost  15k 6 months ago. I was given attitude by the person taking in donations. First I wasn't parked in the exact spot to donate items and was made to move my truck twice away from the donation area. Because 6 inches apparently matters when there is an empty parking lot. Then when I mentioned that I wanted a receipt for tax purposes because the chair cost me $15,000.00 the person asked if I wanted "to donate the thing, or tell him how much it cost"!
After that I was done with the attitude.
Later after reading the fine print I noticed I was given the wrong kind of receipt.
top_reviews.author: James Kinser

top_reviews.text: I went to this store for the first time in a year, and noticed this bookcase. Anyone who is even slightly knowledgeable about the value of media should know that VHS tapes are NOT worth $4, especially at a thrift store. They are hard enough to give away, and can be found for $1 or less at every other place that has them.
top_reviews.author: William O'Neal

top_reviews.text: I like this specific goodwill a lot but man we really gotta bring these prices down at goodwill in general. 6-8 dollars for a used blank shirt? You can quite literally buy them brand new from Walmart or Michaels for the same price if not cheaper. Why would I buy someone elses used clothes at that price? They used to actually be fair prices 2-3 dollars. What happened? Please tell me the employees are at least being paid more these days. This place is supposed to be for people who cant afford to go buy a bunch of clothes brand new from Walmart now they’re undercutting your prices why even go anymore if I could get everything else I needed under the same roof. I know my review won’t change anything but its really frustrating as someone who doesn’t have a lot of money to spend and for some reason every t shirt is like $8 a piece that adds up to a lot of money quickly. As for the guy that made his review about finding and selling stuff on ebay get an actual job because people like you are why we cant get good priced stuff anymore.
top_reviews.author: COS MIC

top_reviews.text: I was impressed with how clean and well organized the Fogelsville Goodwill is.  The employees are friendly, courteous, and know their merchandise.  Thank you Dee!

top_reviews.text: Very large selection of clothes good prices even on electronics just not a lot of items worth re-selling on eBay today but will check back another day.

top_reviews.text: This place was chosen by a group of folks that are new and long time residents to the Greensburg Area as a charity to donate to because the Salvation Army’s dedication to providing such a large percentage of what they fundraise and the services that they do and have done for almost two centuries.

top_reviews.text: Lieutenant Donna was very helpful and kind. She answered all of my questions. She is the one to talk to.

top_reviews.text: They are really laid back. And they feed you lunch after service! It's my new home church, and I'm not forced to wear dresses just to participate in the church!

top_reviews.text: This is the cleanest and nice thrift store around. The staff are always very professional, friendly and helpful . Everytime we are visiting from NC we have to stop here. Much much more  unisex bathroom. Handicap parking and access.

top_reviews.text: I was there today shopping and an employee  was yelling at a customer so loud you could here it outside. They should be ashamed with the way they handled the situation. The salvation army should do better and train there employees to handle situations appropriately.
top_reviews.author: Bobbi Brommer

top_reviews.text: Very kind and helpful staff. Anytime a manager is asked for, always very helpful and attentive. I understand it is a business and has to make money as well, so fair on their pricing. Definitely recommend this store for unique finds.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Dear Salvation Army Clientele and District Managers: HORRENDOUS experiences lately! The store is dusty and stinks of MOLD and MILDEW! What happened here under new management the last few years?

There is a huge display sign in the front window saying they’re in desperate need of donations and to bring them to the bin in the back. You go to the back and there is no bin, but a small sign that says bring donations to the front of store. No consistency. I didn’t bother donating my things that day because when I returned to the front, THREE female staff members were smoking cigarettes in the actual doorway entrance to the business! Why represent a business like this? You couldn’t walk a few feet away from the building? People, children are walking into clouds of smoke just to enter the store. I don’t like clothing that smells of smoke, yet my hair smelled like it from this store. GROSS!

The manager and the assistant manager were rude, dazed over, and not personable at all. Good thing I came alone because I would have been embarrassed if I recommended this place in its current state. It’s a shame because this very Salvation Army family store used to be spectacular, now it’s an eyesore inside and out!

My entire family shopped here for many years - the longtime manager DONNA was a doll. MARIE was fantastic! The lady with the apron, bigger hair and cool makeup was fun! I’ve had many great vintage finds. The store was clean, organized, prices just as fair as Kidder street in Wilkes-Barre, Stroudsburg in the Poconos, etc. Sales and donations seem to be down here because there’s such LOW QUALITY product put out on the floor by the current team. Clothing is CUT with scissors, HOLES, STAINS, RIPS, ODORS, etc. I’ve never seen $8.99 or $10.99 or $17.99 price tags in any Salvation Army. I assume they’re not following the standard prices of the company in hopes of compensating for lack of items and sales - a direct attempt to lowball us customers, for sure. The family won’t come here and rack up anymore. SAD!

top_reviews.text: Entering the shop, the layout and displays can feel a bit overwhelming at first, but they truly offer a fantastic selection for both men and women. top_reviews.text:
I participated in the Angel Tree program for my Girls this year and had a very disappointing experience with communication and professionalism. The receptionist and her supervisor (her Mom) communicated poorly and without empathy with me because
I misplaced the pickup slip that listed the pickup date and missed the scheduled day. When I was called the following morning, (this morning 9:30am ) I immediately apologized, explained that I work full time and am also in school with finals week, and asked respectfully if there was any flexibility or an alternative pickup option.
Unfortunately, the staff member spoke to me in a rigid, dismissive, and condescending manner, repeatedly cutting me off and speaking at me rather than listening. When I tried to clarify logistics (including whether someone else could pick up on my behalf), the instructions given were contradictory and confusing. The initial receptionist hung up on me and her supervisor (Mom) called back, called me “Honey” then proceeded to say she called back as a “courtesy”.The tone of the conversation escalated unnecessarily, and I felt shamed rather than supported , I forfeited my kids gifts because this left me feeling judged.
This program is meant to serve families during an already stressful time. A little patience, empathy, and clear communication would go a long way. Policies can be enforced without speaking to people in a way that feels disrespectful or dehumanizing.
I’m grateful for the mission of the Angel Tree, but this interaction left me discouraged and hurt. I hope leadership considers additional training in compassionate communication, especially when working with families under stress.

I recently had a disappointing experience with the Kittanning area post.
I stopped in to ask for an application for rental assistance. After the form was completed by my landlord, I returned it to the woman in the office. She proceeded to tell me that they would not help me because I already received help from them last year!! Needles to say, I was devastated to hear such a rediculace statement from a front desk clerk! What does it matter if a person needs assistance this month, last month, or last year!! I am driving a car that is 19 years old, and it was in need of a few repairs, therefore, I didn't have what I needed for the entire cost of rent and was desperate for a little help!!
As I think of all the donations my family and friends have given to this organization over the years, It now makes me wish we had never given them anything at all!! Maybe I should have asked if they were able to help me with the car repair costs. I just don't get how 1 person (that I never met) had any right to deny anyone in a time of need!! It took a lot for me to get enough nerve to ask for assistance in the first place, and to be turned down was a real disappointment and embarrassment!! I truly hope the next person who goes to them as their last resort, doesn't get embarrassed and disappointed as I was!

top_reviews.text:
Donors need to know the truth!!!!

I visit these stores all the time, and the prices are skyrocketing — sometimes changing within hours. And on top of that, they still have the nerve to ask if you want to “round up,” as if any of us are getting raises every hour to keep up with their greed.

Today I went to Salvation Army for their “50% off,” then checked the other stores too — all the same story. Free donated items priced like brand-new retail. It’s disgusting. These places are supposed to help people, yet they’re gouging the very families who come in because they’re struggling.

Everything on their shelves was donated at no cost — zero — but they turn around and slap ridiculous price tags on it. That’s not charity. That’s exploitation.

Whoever is setting these prices should be ashamed. Major chains, ministries, so-called “nonprofits” — they’re all copying each other and pushing the same outrageous markups.

When I told the staff the prices were extremely high, all I got was: “Sorry, we don’t set the prices.”
Exactly — because the people who do set them clearly don’t care about the community at all.

People donate out of kindness, hoping to help someone in need — not so their items can be resold at prices struggling families can’t afford. Don’t donate to places that profit off generosity. Give to families, friends or places that actually help.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
Unfortunately corporate greed strikes again

I’ve loved this store for years, and most of the employees are lovely to interact with.   Unfortunately since COVID, prices have become unrealistic and “competitive pricing” is no excuse. To whom are you competing with in Apollo ? Remember all, Salvation Army is a corporate non profit, therefore all markups and “profits” don’t go back to the community, the not even to the employees who are marking such items up. Corporations increase their operating expenses in order to reduce profits, not to donate to those in need. So “going to a good cause” is also not a reason. If it is the case, lower the prices so the people in need in this area can afford to clothe themselves.

$20-30 for USED items, or even buyouts from big brands like Zara is outrageous to the common person in this area. Zara clearance isn’t even that much - for those who don’t shop there often.  4-5 hours of minimum wage work for one item at a charity shop is sickening.  A single shirt in this store is the same price as minimum wage, so you would have to work an entire hour for someone else’s used shirt (not including income taxes, ofcourse).

I understand having to mark things up a bit after Covid to make up for losses, but it is 5 years later and the prices are only continuing to increase. pure greed.

Also the woman with the white mullet must think the hard line items are her own personal antiquity shop. I’ve seen prices of $50 for complete junk, sell on eBay instead.  God forbid someone in need needs some half decent cookware and doesn’t have $20 to splurge on a used pan.

Donation process: let’s not begin to mention why prices have probably increased.  Trying to donate here is a lost cause, and employees are often nasty about it. Particularly the same white mullet woman. Those of us who are employed would have to take time off work to donate here. Only accepting donations 9-1? Really? So it’s unlikely anyone with a job donates here, this would explain why there are so many buyouts and price increases. Donate at the church shop 2 miles up the road instead, atleast it benefits the community.

This store is located in a rural town of western Pennsylvania. Your competition is a church charity shop and a Bealls, whose prices are equivalent for brand new clothes.

Remember what a charity shops purpose is-  to serve underserved communities and those in need. Shame on you. Those doing pricing- do you get a bonus beyond the minimum wage that you are paid? If not, I suggest you revolt.

top_reviews.text:
Alert!!!!
Stop donating to places like this….

This is a thrift store, yet the prices are outrageous. Everything here is donated — completely free — but you’re charging like it’s a full-price retail store. It’s honestly wrong. People come here because they’re struggling and hoping to find something they can actually afford, but instead they’re met with prices that push them right back out the door. A thrift store is supposed to help the community, not take advantage of it. These prices don’t support people in need — they hurt them.

People who are in charge of setting these prices should be ashamed. Turning free donations into overpriced merchandise completely goes against what a thrift store is supposed to stand for.

And donors deserve to know this. When people donate, they believe their items will go to help others — not be marked up to the point where the very people who need them the most can’t buy them. If a thrift store refuses to support the community, then the community should think twice before donating here. Choose places where your donations actually reach the people who truly need them.

And to make it worse, they still dare to ask if you want to “round up” — as if any of us are magically getting raises every hour or every day to match their nonstop price increases.
top_reviews.author: ****TKM ****

top_reviews.text:
I usually have pretty decent luck at this Goodwill, and today was no exception in terms of finding things. The home goods section was pretty sparse this time around, but I still managed to fill a cart with clothing to try on, so it wasn't a total bust.

That said... today was rough.

The store was absolutely freezing. The loading/processing doors were open for a long stretch while items were being brought in, and the constant blast of cold air made it really uncomfortable to shop. On top of that, it gets very noisy when they're processing donations back there, which makes browsing feel chaotic instead of relaxed.

Pricing is also becoming harder to justify though that's honestly a Goodwill-wide issue at this point. It feels like the minimum price for most items now starts around $8, with sweatshirts hitting $10.99. That's not exactly the thrill-of-the-hunt pricing people come to thrift stores for.

Overall, I'll still come back because I usually find something worthwhile here, but the temperature, noise level, and rising prices definitely took away from the experience today. A little more comfort (and a little less sticker shock) would go a long way.

This store brings in anywhere from $3,000 - $9,000 a day. The store is open 6 days a week. Only about 4-6 employees work there a day.  Everything sold at the store, furniture, appliances, name brand clothing, is donated. Making the turnover 100% profit.

Their workers, who even worked throughout the COVID-19 Pandemic as Essential Workers, get paid only $7.25 an hour. This is one of, if not the lowest paying Employers in the area, and is the lowest paying employer in the Plaza it is a part of.

Actually, please allow me to correct myself.

In February the workers were given a congratulatory $0.25 cent raise, the "biggest raise they've given in years."

A 3% raise to combat the 7% inflation.

What is even worse is the fact that is only $0.25 cents more than the Federal Minimum Wage which has not been raised in Thirteen Years.

Sad Fact: This is the longest the Federal Minimum Wage has gone without being raised since  FDR signed the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938.

Furthermore, the store is not managed properly. Cashiers are not given change or small bills. They have to exchange them with customers, ive seen customers go next door to the Tractor Supply to try and get small bills.

Almost daily workers are still in the store finishing up anywhere from 10 to sometime 40 minutes after clocking out. Because "Corporate will be mad."

The way this store is operated is ridiculous.

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army in Washington has become a beacon of hope for countless individuals and families facing difficult times. Their commitment to helping those in need extends beyond just providing basic necessities. From offering financial assistance with bills to organizing Christmas drives for children, they consistently demonstrate the power of compassion and generosity.
The Salvation Army also plays a crucial role in bringing joy and laughter to families during the holiday season. Their Christmas assistance program allows parents to provide their children with meaningful gifts, creating lasting memories and fostering a sense of hope during a time that can be particularly challenging.
Whether you are seeking assistance or simply want to contribute to a worthy cause, the Salvation Army in Washington is a deserving recipient of your support. Their unwavering commitment to helping others makes them a valuable asset to the community and a beacon of hope for those in need.
top_reviews.author: Samantha Schneider

top_reviews.text:
I recently had an incredibly frustrating experience at the Salvation Army store in West Mifflin. Not only did they chase me out of the store with a false battery-operated wall clock, but when I confronted them about it, the response was shockingly aggressive.

Instead of acknowledging their error, they defensively compared their clock to those in banks, which was entirely irrelevant. Last time I checked, banks don't arbitrarily set their clocks differently from the rest of the world just to inconvenience customers.

Their clock being off by 7 minutes resulted in them closing early, effectively robbing customers of their shopping time. And who knows, maybe they open early too, using some mystical clock only they know about.

To top it off, the staff had the audacity to talk negatively about me when they thought I couldn't hear them because of my headphones.

This level of unprofessionalism and aggression towards customers is completely unacceptable. Corporate needs to step in and address the behavior of their employees before they drive away any more customers. Needless to say, I won't be setting foot in that store again.

top_reviews.text: I've always liked coming here. I've shopped at this store occasionally for like 18 years. It's one of the few thrift stores that has reasonably priced items. So on any given day, two color tags will be 50% off and one color tag will be 99 cents. I was actually there today and found many NICE things for only 99 cents. This is definitely a fun place to go look around. The most important thing to remember about this location though is that they do not give plastic bags for your items. top_reviews.text: This place is the very reason there's homeless problems in Anderson. They turn these people out early in the morning and they do not let them stay in the facility. top_reviews.text: This place… where do I begin. First off let me say this, I am a HUGE advocate of non profit  organizations… but only when those organizations allocate their resources in the best and proper way to help the people who need help.  I feel like this, the people who donate to places like Salvation Army and Goodwill, as opposed to selling or trashing their unwanted items, are doing so bc they want to give others who are perhaps on a different financial level the opportunity to afford and enjoy these items at an affordable price.  I thought that nothing pissed me off more than the way these ‘non-profits’ over price these things that they have received for FREE!! But I was wrong! Let me tell you what is happening to these donations!!! A very large portion of the donations go straight into the trash. I’ve visited many many thrift stores and none of them are more wasteful than the Salvation Army! They throw away perfectly good items by the loads on a daily basis. I visited the Salvation Army in Beaufort to see if they were exercising the same practices as the one in Georgetown and yes! They do! Did you know that ANY baby item such as high chairs, strollers, swings, playpens etc go DIRECTLY into the trash? For safety reasons they are not allowed to sell baby items but they don’t tell you that, instead they continue to let the public donate expensive swings, cradles, high chairs and walkers, etc. etc. etc. and then they throw them directly in the trash! The number of TVs that I have seen in these dumpsters is ridiculous. The number of kitchen appliances… is ridiculous. I could go on and on about that but let’s move on to the  gentleman that works inside Beaufort, South Carolina Salvation Army. I have not met another sales clerk as snotty as this man ….he had me so aggravated. I had to leave the store and my husband had a”to pay for our  purchases because I was afraid I was going to go off on this man.  He is rude and he made my shopping experience very unpleasant.. if I could give this ZERO  stars, I would! So could those of you kindhearted people who take your time to donate your items to Salvation Army, please consider donating to a privately owned thrift store ? or better yet. Curb alert for free to the public. Do not donate to these places with the illusion that your items are being resold to the public at a reasonable price, they are not! A few pictures of the items that were outside of the trash at this thrift store.

top_reviews.text:
The products and pricing at this store are great, and I’ve had many positive experiences with the staff in the past. However, my most recent visit was extremely disappointing due to the way closing time was handled.

I was in the store at 4:30 PM when staff began announcing that the store would be closing in 15 minutes—even though posted hours state closing time is 5:00 PM, not 4:45. By 4:40 PM, the lights were turned off—20 minutes before closing. As someone who works in retail, I completely understand wanting customers to wrap up their shopping by closing time. Announcements are reasonable (though they should be accurate), but turning off the lights well before the posted closing time is unprofessional and unnecessary.

What was especially concerning is that this appeared to be directed by a manager (I overheard staff referencing her). I believe management should model strong customer service, and this did not reflect that standard. Customers were being rushed and even turned away despite there still being 15–20 minutes left before closing.

I know this doesn’t reflect the entire team, as I’ve had great interactions with many employees before. However, this experience felt rude and dismissive, and I hope it’s addressed so future customers aren’t treated the same way.

My family and I drove 40 minutes to visit this Salvation Army store today and the door was locked at 3:15 pm. I said that the website and the sign on the door said they are open until 4:00 pm. She was extremely rude to me and told me that they closed at 3:30 today (even though it wasn't even 3:30 yet.)

Lastly, I understand the mission of the Salvation Army, but putting prices higher than eBay is just driving my business away....not everything is of priceless value and by doing this type of pricing, it makes me believe that these folks have forgotten the mission of the Salvation Army.
top_reviews.author: TJ Leesch

top_reviews.text: They used a coffee table for display, but refused to sell it. Hear me out....why not...go grab 1 of like 50 other tables to use for the display? Why not sell the stuff you are actually getting for free? Isn't that the point of the store? Its not like the table had 100 + precious moments on it or something, IT LITERALLY HAD A PAIR OF SHOES AND A SCARF! I need to calm down.... But think about that Salvation Army
top_reviews.author: Trista Skyberg

top_reviews.text: You name it, they've got it! Always a huge selection of items. The prices are a little high on some things but I always enjoy shopping here because the staff are always so smiley and genuinely friendly, which we all know is what the world needs more of, and I appreciate it so much! I love thrifting and have found a lot of treasures here! I definitely recommend checking them out!
top_reviews.author: Dana Sherman

top_reviews.text: After spending well over $50, getting checked out by a person, and putting my cart away- another employee approached me and acted like I was stealing and kept asking me questions. I pulled out my receipt to show proof. Then I kept getting asked more questions and being told my items have two different stickers on top of eachother, being asked if I know the person who checked me out and wanting me to point out who it was, being asked if I knew the items where doubled stickered(I don’t even think they had two stickers on them). I just don’t want to be berated after showing my receipt and clearly only having the few items in my cart on my recept. One of my items also got discreetly taken apart to see if there was something inside. Just absolutely ridiculous. I get you can’t directly accuse someone of stealing for legal reasons, but how is this any better? I don’t have any desire to come back here again
top_reviews.author: tyler

top_reviews.text: This used to be a great secondhand store. But now its cluttered and their pricing is so expensive. Your almost better off buying new. I think twice before visiting this place anymore

top_reviews.text: The gentleman you see in the photos attached will harass you in line and make a big deal if you don't follow his exact instructions and then gaslight you and proceed to make it seem like you're making a big deal when in fact he's the big baby who is making a big deal about everything. Everyone is there for free food and he needs to back off of everyone. Proceeded to harass me in line and he knew that someone cut in front of me along with kicking my bag multiple times in line. I'm sure all of it is on camera in your corridors before you get to the actual giveaway. Proceeded to then chase me out of the giveaway walking right behind me like he's going to do something to me when we all know he's not going to do anything to anyone. I get outside as I already was proceeding to leave and he follows me out of the door with one of his other co-workers and proceeds to watch me sit in my car for over 5 minutes. Clearly he has nothing better to do than harass people who are coming to get free food. Most of the staff here are on high edge and are not nice. No I will not shut my mouth I can talk loud and obnoxiously just like all of your other guests do when they're waiting to get food. I followed his instructions and that wasn't good enough. We will be taking this up the food chain as far as it goes. You guys skimp people everyday and you leave people with literally skimpy old moldy food. Standing at the beginning of the line acting like a security guard cop. I'm sure you guys are really proud of having this guy run your establishment. And absolute joke putting his finger in my face multiple times and stepping to me like he's going to do something when I was clearly not threatening anyone whatsoever.
top_reviews.author: Wittifer

top_reviews.text:
$50 boots $40 shoes, $1 dirty stained smelly clothes, no hard rock music and no horror movies like it's filtered out or should I say censored. Tapes, records, cds, vhs, dvd, books, knick knacks, jewelry, clothing, toys, crafts, clothing. Some great prices, some awful prices.

A staff member (she) yelled at me across the store with a very angry face and said I couldn't be in that area which I didn't know because there were no signs saying I couldn't, but there were plenty of items with prices on them there. I watched another staff member (guy) treat a customer unpleasantly. Before I got to the thrift store I found a wrong door (north west) in the same building, a lady came around the corner at the top of a set of steps and said with a condescending voice and crabby face "can I help youuuuuu".

Look at how many signs they have telling you to do this or that! This usually means someone in charge is not a happy person or dislikes talking to customers.

Overall a bad experience for me, actually the worst thrift store I have ever been to now that I think of it. I was having a great morning until I went here.

What would Jesus do?
top_reviews.author: Joe Cool

top_reviews.text: I try to go here every time I'm in SF. They r friendly and prices r very reasonable I always find something there for me and my kids
top_reviews.author: Bonnie E

top_reviews.text: At St Vincent DePaul , you can find much better bargains and bigger discounts than Goodwill.  Parking here is limited so you may have to park on the street, or in the back parking lot, and walk around. They have feature colored tags every week that are either 50 or 75% off which offer a huge savings off already low prices.
top_reviews.author: Amber Hunnel

top_reviews.text: Cheyenne is a super kind and friendly person! Yesterday she checked us out as a cashier and complimented my shrek beanie which made my day!
top_reviews.author: Phoebe

top_reviews.text: A great thrift store well organized and reasonably priced clothing and household goods
top_reviews.author: M. R.

name: Good Samaritan Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
DO NOT GIVE THESE PEOPLE YOUR MONEY!!! I just visited this store for the first time with my fiancé, who had been in there before, and although it is very very small, there is a LOT to look at. So being my first time there, I walked around a few times (the place is literally arranged so you walk a circle), just browsing, when the scuzzy looking attendant came over to us and announced they were about to close…my fiancé was looking at a sound bar and told him he wanted to buy it. Again the worker said they were about to close….my fiancé asked if he could purchase the sound bar and another item. Maybe it was because my fiancé is black… Or maybe we just walked around the store one too many times looking at one too many things because they turned away our money and said again that they were about to close, that we had been there for over an hour, and that if we didn’t leave he would call the police. (Btw we were there for about 20 minutes) My fiancé just did not understand why he couldn’t purchase the items he was interested in… So I explained it to him loud enough for the employee and the store owner to hear:  they think we’re casing the joint babe they think we’re about to steal from them… And walked out the door disgusted… And now thanks to them I have a new mission… To tell everyone I know never to go to that store and never to spend their money there…

Good Samaritan Thrift store, 227 S Prairie Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57104, and according to google, they don’t close til 8:30….3 1/2 hours from now!

I really regret having to give them one star. If I had a choice, I would’ve left them -5 stars!!

I’m all about supporting local businesses, but these guys aren’t local…they just do business out of a local building

*visit was on March 15, 2024 and review was mistakenly left for Sisters LLC, which I just caught and will correct**
top_reviews.author: Joy Ratzlaff

top_reviews.text: This place was my favorite thrift store… changing my review from 5 stars to 1. Went in this week, whole place smelled like a cigarette, the man working didn’t even look at me when I walked in and said hi. Looked around and they had sweatshirts $10.50, blow up air mattress for $30. Was also not acknowledged leaving the store.
top_reviews.author: Keile Wood

top_reviews.text: Seemed a little sketchy. Made a purchase. Item was slightly damaged and asked for a discount. Then was told I had to pay cash. No where does it say cash only. Also I could see the credit card machine. While checking out the cashier talked on the phone the entire time. I won't return.
top_reviews.author: Kari Bullion

top_reviews.text:
I was in need of at least a size 3X in Women's shirts & pants but there was nothing beyond 2X. The only way to find the occasional 3X here or there was going through them one at a time. I've not the patience nor time. The whole store is laid out poorly, but especially the clothing with the sizing a confusing mess.

I went ahead & browsed the rest of the store. There was a loveseat that caught my eye but the man sitting on it playing with his phone made it difficult to see the price & he wasn't very cooperative. The woman sitting on a desk chair positioned in front of the other side of it was at least able to guess at the price for me.

I haven't been a fan of Goodwill for years, but decided to give this newer location a try. However, after such a disappointing experience I don't need to return to any.
top_reviews.author: Kelly H.

When I mentioned it was not only my kids the goodwill employee stared at me for a few minutes and went right to the back. top_reviews.author: Star DuMarce

Ariat jeans in my size for $7? Yes please! The staff was friendly and quick checkout. There are dressing rooms so you check the fit of the clothing as well.

top_reviews.author: Ryan Juno

top_reviews.text: I frequently find good deals at this goodwill! Although, just like everywhere else, the prices are starting to go up, up, up! But still a good deal on many things. top_reviews.author: Amber Hunnel

top_reviews.text: Probably the best Goodwill in Sioux Falls but still has things marked up to high for getting in for free.
top_reviews.author: Keile Wood

top_reviews.text: This office has the most professional Soldiers I’ve ever met in my life. My fiancé and I felt welcome, IMMEDIATELY when we walked in the door. After we were introduced, the Recruiter sat down with us and just talked to us - he wasn’t pushing for my fiancé to join, but actually took the time to get to know us and learn how the Army could fit into our lives. We always knew about the benefits of joining the Military, but he broke it down in a way that it made sense of why to join and how it could better our lives. The information was phenomenal - and it wasn’t just from one Recruiter, but it was everyone that seemed to chime in whenever we were looking for a different perspective. You can tell it’s a family environment, and that convinced us that we weren’t going anywhere else - we can’t thank the Army Recruiters enough for all the help!!!
top_reviews.author: Emily Caskel

top_reviews.text:
Those guys are awesome! I thought , they might get me into the lousy contract, just for another sign up,  but then, all my concerns obliterated themselves, believe me or not  , the stuff  does  it's job with the heart!
Thanks a lot to my recruiter, Carl Holm, who worked above and beyond  with all my Legal resident paperwork , supporting and guiding me through, also Camillya Belle  , who were so helpful and super attentive to all the details, and  Christopher Beddow, who had  to call  the top, concerning me , multiple times  , and made all my last minute doubts vanish.
5 stars! the best! Thank you for everything you do!
top_reviews.author: Dmitry

top_reviews.text: No pressure, very informative and honest help about the opportunities the Army has to offer tailored to my goals and aspirations. Experienced soldiers give share their stories about how the Army helped them and how it could help me.
top_reviews.author: Jake

top_reviews.text:

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sioux Falls

top_reviews.text: Habitat ReStore provides exceptional service and reliability, making them a top choice for local professionals like AAA Mobile Welding in Sioux Falls. As a specialized welding service provider, we appreciate their polite and helpful staff who consistently go above and beyond to support our operational needs. This collaborative partnership allows us to source unique materials and hardware for our custom projects while supporting a great cause, proving that Habitat ReStore is a premier destination for sustainable building supplies and community-focused business support in the region. We highly recommend their team for anyone seeking expert advice and a seamless business-to-business experience.
top_reviews.author: Paul Donahue

top_reviews.text: While I didn’t find exactly what I was looking for, I was impressed by how well-organized, clean, and orderly the store was. The items that did catch my eye were fairly priced and accessible for most budgets. The staff were friendly and in great spirits, which made the experience even better. If you’re renovating or just need to repair a single room or item in your home, definitely check them out before heading to the big box stores—you might be pleasantly surprised!
top_reviews.author: Asisa Rolle

top_reviews.text: Habitat for Humanity is a great place to find materials for many types of projects! I've gotten a variety of things from them over the years. Sometimes it's new stuff and sometimes it's used, but it's never the same stuff. I truly appreciate that they use their funds to help people get into homes!!
top_reviews.author: Sheldon Hovaldt

top_reviews.text:
A Different kind of "HEARING AID".
* If you have a problem & need help, the Best place to call is the "211 Helpline".
* They take the Time & Patience to LISTEN & do their very best to help you with your Problems.
* They do a Wonderful job for All.  And it's FREE!
* Even the City suggests that you Call them!  We had a big Storm a couple of weeks ago &  the City said to Call 211 for help with the Clean up.  The next day,  a young Knight in Shining Armour showed up "Alone" & Cleaned up All the Downed Branches in my yard.
* They're the next best thing to Ghost Busters!  Thx so much 211!!!

* IBB
top_reviews.author: Jennie Constant

top_reviews.author: Maley Moejoe

top_reviews.text:
Asking for millions in donations, but I the old disabled homeless recipient  cannot get to use the toilet: college students pour coffee for extra credit, I went to college homeless and cannot get coffee?

Even though I have had what amounts to nil homeless services in Chattanooga, it is fair to say that the Churches involved are not ''in for a penny, in for a pound'' themselves but are rather wishy-washy about their help and when dealing with pantheon of types of homeless people it is not always the homeless service providers fault yet the service providers are at fault and rarely if ever adjudicate fairly in arising disputes or allegations.

Like today, as happened many times I traversed the city at my expense, and walked in the Salvation Army and they said they were closed. I needed to use the toilet and first they said it was okay and that  I had 5 minutes then another one forbid me to use the toilet, after already coming into the building and basic need to use the toilet. I did not know they were closed when I came inside, as a number of other people were inside, more than the usual number of helpers on duty on a given day. Okay then, I guess all their friends was OK or they arranged to sleep and eat inside while I am out freezing, I gather. It doesn't seem a reason to make debacle issue about unless you need to use the toilet .

But the case of the matter is, that the people that serve in these homeless providers are skilled or tend to make an issue over a non-issue in which patron addresses in adjudicates sometimes that they are correct and the volunteers or staff are incorrect and the issue accelerates into defense and denial of civil rights of the issue at hand. (In other words, sometimes they want to kick the patron out when nothing is going on worth arguing over, except their envy of my disability income consumed  in gasoline and food, like I am the rich man). Can I use the toilet at the Salvation Army?? If not, then staying inside or getting any help from vast spectrum of resources of assistance from the Salvation Army is barred and out of limits for me also, due to past and ongoing blocking access to the services by the provider themselves by their conceptions or misconceptions of me and my status.

Because over the years, I had traversed the city to try to get a meal or mail at the Salvation Army or Community Kitchen or try to get a tent from Methodist Church  and get stiffed from the service they themselves proffer to the public such as meal or shelter at  the Community Kitchen which has shared population of helpers with Salvation Army, under the reason to deny is the patron is asking for the fair use of the item or service offered or even after acceptance takes place and some dialogue or incident places the patron in no-win  position of self-adjudication of civil rights or fact of being wronged like a kicked dog that has no choices but to do without the items and services the homeless providers  themselves are seeking donations to make a go at helping the homeless and joint-relationship of homeless donors-providers-recipients. Although I am disabled person, I have been left without help and even though disabled seemed to qualify for some of the help or attainment of shelter and volunteer myself, which fundamental opportunities is in a damaged context now due to the arguing going on when I appear, on after a month or months  without any help, then without any real cause am centered in arguments over nothing but standing there trying to get acceptance of the  item or service in the donor-provider-recipient relationship, whereas the other parties want discord and failure to provide the goal of the donor-provider-recipient relationship. Like dogs to be kicked out into the cold but all day their friends walk in and out using the toilet.

At other times if the homeless, [ if I am in for provisions, it is said I, who as a disabled veteran with nil  help ],  am stealing... so if stealing is what they say occurs for me to accept the acceptance in the donor-provider-recipient relationship, then what is in Trust?

They make sure they have clean clothes to wear - the volunteers wash their laundry. I'm not sure where the food and water came from for dinner, but they had HUGE metal baking trays filled with it, smelled really good and they did offer a plate to me, but being diabetic I watch everything I eat and it looked like mashed potatoes on the bottom and chicken and gravy spread on top of that.

While I was there (JOSIE & JOE(?) I MADE IT, BLESSINGS CAME DOWN THE ROAD). They were trying to help a disabled Veteran find housing, the whole team was working like crazy.

They allow some dogs in the shelter, which surprised me as it is a BIG "NO!!!" even if it is your service dog. The couple of volunteers I met came right in to do some work helping  lean up  wash, dry, and fold laundry.

I really felt for all of them, the workers, the volunteers, whoever provided the food for dinner, and the residents down on their luck and looking for a hand up.

top_reviews.text:
The Salvation Army treatment center is anointed ground! I have personally witnessed God move through this program in powerful ways. Lives are being transformed, families are being reunited, and people are discovering their identity and purpose again.
This isn’t just a place for sobriety—it’s a place where hope is restored and chains are broken. I’ve watched individuals come in lost, broken, and full of shame, and walk out sober, renewed, and reconciled with their families. God is in this program, and His hand is evident in the restoration happening here.
If you or a loved one is battling addiction, I cannot recommend this program enough. It gives people more than recovery—it gives them redemption.

top_reviews.text:
This place is great if you're able to get into the program, it's a very limited and stricter program than other shelters. They will allow you to stay in their emergency beds for up to three weeks and three months. The first night of staying here I got wrote up for not turning in my phone. They allow you to get two write ups and after two write ups they are supposed to put you out regardless of your situation. Luckily I've been at this shelter for seven months and I was able to find a job during this time. Today is now February 14, 2025 and I am now currently looking for another place to stay. The program director Iris Wade told me that she was disappointed in me because she feels that I have been in non compliance with the rules of this program and that I always have excuses and that she has done all that she could do, otherwise she would have let me stay a little longer because of my circumstances. I can admit that I received more than one write up and all of the write ups were small situations like (not turning in your phone eating a snack having outside food and drinks having wrinkles in your bed and not getting out of the bed in time after the wake up time at 6 am) Lights go out at ten and you are required to get up and out of the bed by 6:05 no matter what you've done that previous day or what kind of medicine you take (you will get wrote up) (& Let's not mention the arguments between all of the ladies and smart ellect responses and pettiness)
All in all I did not receive help to find housing like I thought that I would. (Which was one of the main reasons of wanting to be in this program) I am very disappointed on how my stay is ending. I had high hopes that I would be okay prior to entering the single women's program. My valentine's day and weekend is not so happy but thanks Salvation Army for your help thus far with a place to temporarily stay.
top_reviews.author: Brianna Taylor

top_reviews.text: I want to emphasize that The Salvation Army does not provide housing assistance. Unfortunately, the disrespectful and condescending manner in which they communicate with individuals seeking help is disheartening. They treat The Salvation Army like a detention center. The staff talks in a degrading manner, making individuals feel less than human. They also expect individuals to pay rent, which contradicts the purpose of providing salvation and helping people in need. The staff up here is not proactive, and I cannot recommend this place to anyone. Action needs to be taken to either improve the staff's attitude or to bring in new, helpful people. Ms. Dorothy Ford should be let go because she always sides with her staff, even when they are wrong. It feels like our opinions are not considered here. They unjustly write us up for trivial reasons simply because they can. Even after dinner at 5, women and children are left feeling hungry. The infestation of roaches and spiders is being ignored. The walls in the rooms are in a deplorable condition with mold and dirt coming out of the vents. Despite the presence of COVID-19 in the building, they failed to inform us about it, neglecting our health and the well-being of the kids. This is unacceptable is unfair that they only help those they want to help. This is not right at all.

top_reviews.text: Manger disabled Facebook reviews and blocked me. The prices are insane. Twice what goodwill gets and we all know goodwill is at the high end  in pricing  an old used coffee pot is $25. A pair of 90s bar stools that I sold at my yard-sale for $10 for the pair she priced at $35 each! A $5 (retail)hand soap dispenser is $4 at any other thrift store in town this is 50 cents. Look at my pics. What I do know is that a lot of stuff is priced retail. A lot of it is junk I’d throw away after Ive had a yard-sale. Junkie old half burnt 90s candle $4? 🤣 other Salvation Army stores are not like this at all. She needs a business class. The only sunshine I’ve found is that the selection is dense. No surprise with all things considered. I started counting reviews that say prices are too high for a thrift store and wow. What more does the manager need to wake up? For what it’s worth, I consider myself a bit of a thrift store expert. I’ve been thrifting for 30+ years. Everywhere I travel I map the thrift stores on the route including vacations. I’d venture to guess I’ve been in 300+ stores and I’ve never seen such high prices. It feels like you’re in a prank video as you walk around. When you lower prices (for example) say 50% your sales quadruple. It’s simple math.

top_reviews.text: Today was my last time to go to this thrift store! The manager has got to be stopped! It's 20/80 on whether she will be cordial, or downright rude. If she's cordial to me, then she is rude to others in line and it's very uncomfortable. It also depends on how much I have in my basket. On one occasion, she argued with the person in front of me because she was quoting a higher price for an unmarked item than what the signs indicated. When that customer was walking away, she (manager) loudly exclaimed to me (but everyone in line, including customer that hadn't exited store yet) could clearly hear her, said, "maybe if they had a basket full like you, they could have it cheaper." I was shocked! People behind me left, but she was already ringing my stuff up and I didn't know what to do. I personally have also experienced taking unmarked items up and she will claim it to be "special", then charge at least twice the price (sometimes more). If you decide not to purchase said item, her attitude changes drastically. That was my last experience and I didn't go back, until today, for 3 months. Not only are the prices crazy (even on half price day), but she treated the three customers in front of me so bad that I abandoned my cart and walked out. Example of crazy prices: faux fur coats that are marked as "fur" are $200! You can go to Route 66 antique stores and get faux fur coats for less than half of that. She tells people that they should look up what items are selling for online. Well, she's apparently only looking at what some sites are asking (and not getting), but NOT "what they sold for" prices. It's a real problem! Only authentic designer brands sell for that price on ebay. I realize a lot of people that go thrifting are re-sellers, but the majority are people looking for a cheaper way to live and can't afford those ridiculous prices. I know this is a long review, but it's been a long time coming. If corporate continues to ignore the issue with the manager, they will continue to lose business. I really can't believe someone hasn't sued them yet!
top_reviews.author: Tmb PhilAma

top_reviews.text:
Don't waste your time at this store, Annette the manager is extremely rude to everyone who comes in. I have been coming in for about a year 2-3 times a week and have spent thousands of dollars in this store, I always try to make a point to be extra friendly to the manager because she is always so rude and condescending. to no avail she constantly demeans people, talks bad about them after they leave and is down right rude. one time I was looking at a pair of shoes in a cart by the counter and she walked up and ripped them out of my hands saying I haven't priced these yet! customers in line took notice and commented how unbelievably rude that was of her. If an item is unmarked she will definitley jack the price up to an insane amount when you bring it to the counter, and probably tell you to look it up if you decide the price is too high ( i look up nearly every item i purchase and she is severley misinformed on the pricing) Most other reviews mention the same about her this review hit the nail on the head

"The comments about the manager are right — she’s rude, combative, and obviously doesn’t like her job. I feel like I have to walk on eggshells around her, as if my shopping there is a burden to her. Not fun at all.

Another frustration: the pricing isn’t clear on most items, so she arbitrarily upcharges items randomly at the register and gets upset if you decide not to pay the unexpectedly higher price.

I would be happy to pay up for good items that have been screened for stains/tears/holes, etc. and are clearly priced, like how every other thrift store operates. That’s not the case for this place though.

Overall it’s just an unpleasant experience all around, and their pricing is high for low-quality inventory.

I’m removing this location from my route and will take my business elsewhere moving forward."

I won't be coming back to this location until this problem is addressed.
top_reviews.author: Jake Hoeffner

top_reviews.text: AWFUL first experience and will NOT be going back. If I could give zero stars I would. This will be about the same rude old lady at the register that everyone has been talking about. My girlfriend and I had never been to the Salvation Army before to shop and we were super excited because we had been waiting for a few days for them to open back up after the holidays. After finding some things to purchase around the store we walk up to the front a ring the bell to check out, and this lady yells at us from the back saying she would be right up with us, we don’t respond but we wait patiently for her to come up and help us because we understand they probably have other job task to do. After my girlfriend makes her purchase, I go up and hand her my items, unaware that they have a policy where you’re unable to use your card if the purchase is less than $10, because like I said we had never been there before. After saying “Oh! I’m sorry I don’t have any cash” She said “Okay” and keeps the items. Annoyed we go and pick out other items that we had passed on for the price, but in order to make $10 for the items that we really wanted we go back. This takes us about 2 minutes to do and we go back up to the front to ring the bell AGAIN and wait for her to come back to front to check us out, about a minute passes and she comes up and says “I was knocking at the window to get your attention and I almost broke my knuckle, but I was gonna tell you I’m going to be a minute” she then walk BACK into the back where we proceed to wait 5 more minutes for her to come and check us out. AWFUL first experience and will NOT be going back.

top_reviews.text:
Low stars because it's really busy, and the checkout line is ridiculously long. I don't know why the people in line want to get 50 or 60 items, it just seems excessive.

Basically I looked around for a while, found a pair of pants I liked, tried them on.  Note: I did have to wait on a dressing room because they don't have enough (3) for the amount of people in there in.  They fit, and then I realized that there was a line that was about 12 people long, two or three of people in line had a cart that was stuffed full of clothes. As I was observing checkout counters, which they were four cashiers present, three of the cashiers were checking out people with ridiculously large carts, Don't take forever. I probably waited in that line for 20 minutes. More than the amount of time it took me to find the pants.

They really need to be limits on the amount of clothes someone can buy, or more cashiers, terribly inefficient and unless you just have time to waste you should not go here.

In general the selection is okay, but there is so much there that you have to sort through a thousand things to find the thing you like.

Good luck thrifting, I would go check out Buffalo exchange just down the street, it's way better.

top_reviews.text: Buyer beware! I went in this shop for the first time yesterday. I noticed it was not a typical "thrift" store. Prices were not typical of our local thrift stores. I had on new contacts, and asked the owner to read the number on the deadwax. I typed it in my phone to show her fair value. It was priced 84.50. Long story short, she offered it to me for 30.00. I got it along with four other albums. I got home, pulled out the record to test it and it was Tom Jones!  Im attaching a photo of the deadwax number she told me I typed in my phone. And when I called her today to see if the correct album could be found. She said no, she didnt see it, and basically too bad. All sales are final. I would NEVER treat a customer the way she did. To add to this shops issues...apparently they cant make enough money to cover their Mastercard fees. So, in lieu of using it as a business expense, they charge customers the MERCHANT fee so they do not incure any cost. I contacted my credit card company and have disputed the 30.00 charge and the charge of their merchant fees they clearly cant afford. I will never go to this place. In my opinion this is unethical business practices, and will not support sellers who believe they have zero accountability.  Prediction, wait for their closing sell. They will reap what they sow.

top_reviews.text:
Im disabled and was previously homeless for 7 years before finding out that I have COPD, something they called Fungal pneumonia and acute HIV.
Through God I was set up for a meeting with a young lady by the name of Ms. Amber Rosales who heads up a program called the Permanent Supportive Housing Program which is funded through HUD.
As a client of this program i couldn't have asked for ANYTHING better. The program placed me in my own apartment which was saught out and secured by Ms. Rosales. For the first 4 months she payed 100% of my rent ( all bills included ) and once i started receiving my disability check the program continues to pay 70% of my monthly rent as well as a food pantry box each month, and whenever i am in need of hygiene items the Salvation Army always gives me what i need.
To say that they are doing the most good is a vast understatement. They also have emergency housing for men on a 3 month basis where they can get 3 hot meals a day, shelter and a safe place to sleep which allowes the men to have a place to stay while either working or looking for work.
They have the same kind of programs for women and families. They also have a similar program for veterans. I cant speak about tjat program because i really dont know much about it.
These people at the Salvation Army of The Costal Bend have hearts as big as the building that they are working in. Which by the way they will have a brand new facility around November of 2020. They also go in a food truck out i believe once a month to hand out sack lunches to the homeless. Im absolutely positive that if they had the time they would send that food truck out much more than that.
Honestly if it were nit for God directing me to the Salvation Army i dont think i would have made it through the past winter alive.
"Doing The Most Good" doesnt even come close to what they are doing for this community.
If you are looking for a worthy cause to donate to i very highly recommend donating to the Salvation Army of The Costal Bend.
