top_reviews.text: I went online to donate a bed to salvation army. I had to wait two weeks for pick up. I described the bed in detail in my notes. The guys came to pick up the bed and said they could not take bed because it was not disassembled. The pickup guys, the dispatcher, and the Dallas supervisor were all well aware that this information was not on website but said guys would be fired if they took 5 min to disassemble bed. My boyfriend disassembled the bed that night and I called to get pick up. They could not come back for two weeks. The Dallas office is aware that website does not have correct information on what can be picked up. They have no access to a supervisor who can help. Also they cannot pick up voice messages so you you have to keep calling back until you get a person. The guys I spoke with in the Dalls office were great and willing to help, but they have no national support and no way to correct the website or inability to pick up messages. I ended up having to pay a junk removal service $400 to pick up the bed. This is money that could have been donated to the salvation army if they had a better system. At a national level Salvation Army does not care about the people donating to them. I will never donate to Salvation Army again.

top_reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️ 2/5 Stars – Salvation Army or Surprise Probation? 🤡🍽️🚔

Fresh out of jail thanks to my ex-wife’s perjury-fueled legal magic trick (she convinced the court my son didn’t live with me when he absolutely did—bravo, Michelle! 👏🎭), I found myself stranded in Galveston.

Now, jailhouse reviews aren’t exactly the New York Times Travel Guide, but when every single inmate tells you: “Bro, get off this island before you get arrested for existing” 🚔👀—you start to believe it. But with no money, no ride, and no desire to test local law enforcement’s enthusiasm for unnecessary arrests, I needed food and maybe a place to crash for the night.

Enter: The Salvation Army.

🍛 Meal Time – A+ Experience, No Questions Asked!

Let’s start with the good: Dinner is served at 5 PM sharp, and it was solid. ✅ The volunteers were nice, the food was hot, and if you hang around until 5:30, you can get seconds if they have any left. No judgment, no weird rules, just food. 🍛✨

Most importantly, you can walk in absolutely hammered, and no one will care. 🍻💃 Fantastic! (Hold that thought for later.)

For a moment, I thought Maybe this place is a safe haven! Oh, how naive I was.

🚨 The Intake Experience – Welcome to the Breathalyzer Gauntlet 🎤💨

Feeling slightly optimistic after a good meal, I figured, Alright, let’s see about a place to sleep. BIG mistake.

I approached the intake door at 6 PM, expecting some basic instructions or maybe a “Hey, how can we help you?” NOPE. Instead, I got a breathalyzer jammed into my face like I was on parole. 🤯🚔

No hello. No explanation. Just BLOW.

Now, I’m no stranger to bizarre legal procedures (thanks again, Vanessa! 👋), but this was next-level weird. Thankfully, I watched the poor guy ahead of me do it, so I knew the drill. Monkey see, monkey do. 🐵💨

But imagine if I hadn’t? Would they have tackled me for failing the Mystery Breathalyzer Challenge? Was I about to get arrested for looking confused? The world may never know.

📄 30 Days or GTFO – The No-Options Housing Plan

Once I successfully proved I wasn’t drunk (which, again, wouldn’t have even mattered at dinner 🍷🤦‍♂️), they handed me some paperwork. No explanation. No instructions. Just “Sign here.”

Turns out, I was signing up for a 30-DAY PROGRAM.

Now, look. Structure is great, programs are great—but I was just trying to survive the night, not accidentally enlist in a month-long Salvation Army internship. 🏕️😵‍💫

So I asked a reasonable question:
“Is there an option for just a night or two?”

BIG mistake.

The staff member IMMEDIATELY got an attitude, as if I had just demanded room service and a spa treatment. “This isn’t a hotel. If you don’t like it, leave!” 😤🏨🚪

Bro, I just asked a question.

Was I supposed to instinctively absorb the rules through osmosis? Or maybe they expected me to have already taken the Salvation Army Entrance Exam™ before showing up?

Either way, I wasn’t about to sign up for a 30-day commitment on an island full of cops who arrest people for sport.

🏃‍♂️ FINAL VERDICT – Great Food, Terrible Hospitality

✅ Food? Great. Show up at 5 PM, eat well, grab seconds at 5:30. 🍛✨
❌ Intake? Terrible. If you need a place to stay, expect a surprise breathalyzer, zero explanation, and a 30-day program you didn’t sign up for.

If you’re just hungry, this place is fantastic. If you need shelter? Prepare for a weird power trip and an unexpected game of “Sign Here or Get Out.”

Moral of the story: Come for the food, flee before they make you enroll in an unadvertised month-long stay… or worse, before Galveston’s cops find an excuse to lock you up again. 🚔🏃‍♂️💨

top_reviews.text: Food is always good. Donuts and cereal every breakfast. Dinner always includes enough carbs. Case management offers services to help you. But, its on you to reach them. They are pretty understaffed i feel for the needs of everybody. But not everybody reaches out. And, if you arent making positive steps to better your situation by becoming responsible, you are limited to 30 days here. If you have issues preveNting you from bettering your situation im sure they will help you. But you have to be the one that tries to get help from them. This is a night shelter. While i was here typical schedule was 1700 dinner 1800 check in no later than 2200 breakfast 0630 out of the door by 0730 or so. Then they usually have a bus take you to a day place that will also help you out called the Christus the daily bread. With both services you should be able to get back on your feet again.

Horrible experience. Every year, Salvation Army has the Christmas Angel tree program where you can pick a list from the tree and shop for the particular person. I stopped doing it a few years back and wanted to started doing it again. I went to Galleria mall to pick out my list from the tree. There was no one there behind the desk. Since I went during the late afternoon, I figured there was no one working at the time. So I picked out my list. Now, having done this before, I remember that usually they take your name and contact information and in turn, you'll receive a big red plastic bag with detailed instructions on how to wrap and put your gifts in it, etc. I didn't get a red bag. There was none provided, so I have no idea how to bring the presents. There was also no phone numbers on the sign, or any contact information other than the website. I went on the website and called the 2 phone numbers mentioned on there. Both of those phone numbers were automated systems with no information provided on business hours like any normal business would. I had no idea which department to reach about my questions. So I tried reaching the operator. The first time I called, the operator was laughing for some reason before hanging up on me before I can even talk. The second time I called, I reached him again and explained my issue. He gave me a 3rd phone number to call, which also lead to another automated service and a dead end. Not to mention he was extremely rude to me about it. Your operator was extremely rude and unprofessional. I work at a call center. You don't behave like that when you're on a call with a customer.

I'd like to contribute to the Christmas Angel tree program but I can't when y'all are acting this way. I can always call back during business hours but the way your operator was acting was extremely unprofessional. I will be giving my Christmas Angel list back without any contribution. Not because I don't want to contribute but because of how disorganized and how rude your employees are.. It's a shame because I don't want to underprivileged to suffer due to me having this issue. But because I'm having this issue, I don't have enough information on how to contribute...

The food is good, the facilities are nice. Most staff and residents are kind most of the time. We're humans. That said...
The resources and programs here are primarily pamphlets. Due diligence is necessary to be successful, but even that won't save you from the caseworkers if you are not Black.

I am grateful that we only had to sleep outside for a short period of time before we were sufficiently pathetic enough to be accepted into the program. The staff was able to look past my whiteness, grow past their utter disgust with my children and I being sexual assault survivors, and wait until the day my disabled child's SSI cleared before they tried to shove us out the door and put us directly back into the situation that had us helpless and sleeping in the park. Now let them reply about the apartment they offered to pay a deposit on with no access to furniture, no placement for my children into public schools, no approval of government assistance, no access to transportation, and no possibility of employment while we have no childcare whatsoever. I understand this is an emergency shelter. But, how dare you offer access to programs encouraging our growth towards independence, but before any of the resources become available you send us back into the darkness with nothing but our money spent for us. You saved us for 2 weeks just to prop us up for an even worse fall from grace. Houston is solving homelessness, indeed.

Edit: Nevermind, they do Black people like this, too.

Had a good experience at the Salvation Army auto auction this weekend.

There were 12 cars for sale of various makes and models which were promoted ahead of time on Facebook. They opened from 8:30-9:30am to public viewing of the cars, and there were a couple dozen people there when we got there.

There is a fee to receive a bidder’s placard, I think it was $25.

The auction started on time, and bidding was very clear and relaxed.  Each auction took only a few minutes.  Some of the cars (maybe all) had reserves on them, though the reserve was met for al of them.

It seemed like the cars went for good prices.

Overall, great thing to check out especially if you really are interested in a good way to buy a used car.

During the event, a stressful situation with my parents and the police occurred because they accidentally crashed, and the leadership didn’t help at all or they just didn't care. I received no acknowledgment for my volunteer work, bad gift for me, and no apology or thank-you after the kettle season ended. For example, when I first started there, they had bingo 04 days a week. (Senior program Monday-Friday.) At some point they cut it to 02 days a week which upset some of the Seniors and they quit coming entirely. That's all I posted about that, but the Major was displeased I posted that even though it was true.
At some point, I asked him if he called me into his office just to complain about my review. He said he wasn't complaining, but if he wasn't, why did he dissect everything in the review as if I intentionally cast a poor light on SA?
They did cut bingo from 04 days to 02. What was wrong about reporting that when it was true and also true some of the Seniors quit coming because of that?
I quit going there December 2017.
PS After I went back to the dining room at S.A. that day, someone told me I should have posted anonymously and not posted I was in the program then he would not have known it was me. He gave me an extension to stay there week to week ( which I was grateful for) and he would encourage me to keep putting applications for work and show him proof of it. Seems fair enough. I received a call from my aunt's husband to go work with him at his ranch in Miles, TX just for one day. I needed the cash so I took it. I notified the shelter in advance that I was going to take this job but I had to leave the evening before and stay the night at the ranch so we could start early in the morning. I told them I could provide any kind of proof that they wanted including talking with the gentleman and the counselor said I would be suspended from the shelter if I stayed anywhere else once I had an extension. top_reviews.text:
This is normally an outstanding store to visit on Wednesdays. During the week, prices are generally overpriced for a thrift store, but on half-off Wednesdays the prices finally feel more in line with what a thrift store should be. Because of that, I’ve been a happy, loyal customer here for many years.
Today, however, was a very different experience.
I found a shirt that did not have a price tag on it. In the past, this has never been an issue — staff would simply assign a reasonable price. Today, the store refused to sell it to me at all. I even made what I believe was an extremely fair and logical offer. The highest-priced shirt on the floor was $12.99. I explained that if the tag hadn’t fallen off — whether due to a customer or an employee not stapling it properly — the shirt would almost certainly have been priced at $12.99. I wasn’t trying to lowball anyone.
I asked the manager not to let a missing piece of paper prevent the store from receiving the same amount of money it would have received if the tag had still been attached. I was offering $12.99, which is already a lot for a used shirt, and at half off, still a fair price. My intention was to support the store’s mission and cause.
While the manager was polite, she refused the sale.
This is an extraordinarily poor rule for a business that receives its merchandise at little to no cost. I was actively trying to support your mission, and instead you chose a rigid rule over common sense and revenue. Managers should be trusted with discretion — that’s why you hire them and pay them for their judgment and integrity.
The fact that the store didn’t want to take my money was incredibly disappointing. This shirt absolutely should have been sold for $12.99 (half off). I truly believe that if the founder, Ms. Booth, had been there, she would have said, “Take the man’s money — we have bills to pay and a mission to support.”

name: The Salvation Army of Wichita Falls

top_reviews.text:
This review reflects my family’s direct experience over approximately three months at this Salvation Army facility.
From the very beginning, my family felt targeted. Rules were changed after we arrived, and despite following instructions given directly by a Major, staff later verbally reprimanded and blamed us for doing exactly what we were told. Communication between leadership and employees was extremely poor, and my children and I were repeatedly spoken to disrespectfully and aggressively as a result.
There were multiple serious safety concerns involving minors. An elderly resident named Joe was scrolling through his phone in a common area, and explicit sexual images appeared on the screen where my 17-year-old daughter could see them. This was extremely disturbing and inappropriate, especially in a family shelter environment.
Additionally, I personally witnessed an employee put their hands on one of my 10-year-old children. Due to staff behavior and lack of awareness, my 10 year old nearly fell down the stair. He yelled so loud and my 10 year old was so disturbed he was bawling...over MISCOMMUNICATION.
My daughter has documented trauma related to church settings, yet this was dismissed, mocked, or treated as untrue by leadership, which was deeply harmful and humiliating for her. We were made to feel unsafe, unheard, and emotionally distressed.
Over time, it became clear to me that my family was being singled out and treated differently. The ongoing targeting, verbal abuse, lack of staff coordination, and failure to protect minors created an environment that felt unsafe and hostile rather than supportive.
I am sharing this so other families especially those with children...are aware and can make informed decisions. No family seeking help should experience what we did. My best advice is to never take children to a salvation army.
top_reviews.author: Rachelle Ross

during anytime of visit.

I believe someone  must have gotten  the prices on both chairs backwards.   But to my advantage!

They are closed now, but I hope they do reopen.
Maybe by being forced to start completely over from scratch,
They will allow themselves  to take time to really clean up the place, and get an organized stocking plan, and Train staff to be friendly with good PR skills. name: The Salvation Army USA National Headquarters

top_reviews.text:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to urgently bring to your attention a deeply troubling situation involving a supervisor: “ana ,” at one of your programs, which I believe warrants immediate investigation. The ongoing misconduct, neglect, and apparent lack of oversight are not only unacceptable but also undermine the integrity of your organization and the well-being of the vulnerable residents you serve.

Recently, I examined the food menu on the board and was shocked to see it dated 2024. Despite this, I believe the supervisor continues to follow an outdated menu, which compromises the quality and safety of the meals provided. For instance, during a recent meal, residents were served a hamburger patty with uncooked rice—an unsafe and unnutritious combination that clearly indicates a disregard for proper food preparation standards.

Additionally, during a recent inspection conducted by the Bureau of Prisons (BOP), the food prepared was drastically different from what is regularly served. The diet consistently lacks vegetables, offering only canned green beans vegetables and iceberg lettuce—an inadequate and unhealthy meal plan that raises serious concerns about nutritional neglect.

Most disturbingly, I have learned that this supervisor has been taking food items from the kitchen to take home for her family, including supplies meant for the less fortunate, homeless individuals, and residents living in the halfway house reentry program. This theft of resources is both unethical and deeply upsetting, especially given the vulnerable population relying on these services.

When I inquired about the menu and spoke with other staff members, I was told that the supervisor “ANA,” dismisses concerns and states she will feed residents whatever she prefers,and she doesn’t CARE. using only the food ordered to her personal taste at her own home. This behavior indicates a lack of professionalism and a failure to adhere to organizational policies.

What is even more alarming is that the Director of this program, Darla, has a copy of the official menu and should be well aware of the standards and procedures that need to be enforced. I do not understand why she is not ensuring that the supervisor follows the menu and maintains proper oversight. It appears that Darla may be sitting in her office and being disconnected from the day-to-day operations, effectively being in her own little world instead of actively managing and enforcing the rules that are meant to protect both staff and residents.

This lack of oversight and accountability is unacceptable. The program’s success depends on strict adherence to policies, proper enforcement of the menu, and vigilant supervision. I strongly urge you to conduct a discreet, thorough investigation into these matters to uphold the integrity of your organization and ensure residents receive the care and respect they deserve.

This situation is urgent and requires your immediate attention. Thank you for your prompt action to address these serious concerns.

Sincerely,

Evan Graves

The address for this property: 2400 Edison Ave., Fort Myers, FL 33901
top_reviews.author: evan graves

top_reviews.text: Very dissatisfied with the donation/pickup process.  On June 23 I made an online reservation for a pickup on July 17. On July 17, I put my items out and verified via the website the pickup was still scheduled for that day.  At 2 pm my items were not picked up and I contacted the Salvation Army Call Center and was informed that at 1100 am my pickup was postponed by the Jersey City NJ Salvation Army dispatcher until August 16.  At no time did I receive a call or email regarding the postponement.  Canceling a pickup on the scheduled day and not being notified is a poor business practice.  I tried to contact the Jersey City dispatcher 3 times and was told they were on break and then too busy to talk to me.  Not taking time to talk with a customer is another poor practice and sadly the Salvation Army has lost my business and support.  I will now pursue donating to other charities.

Please keep in mind we aren’t from this area and we were NOT aware of the “no walk-in” policy they have going on in this office. The lady who spoke to my relative had a negative and disgusting attitude because my relative asked if we could be seen for help. She responded saying we don’t do walk ins but her tone of voice was nasty. Then we came into the office area and they said to leave and just keep calling the phone line to get and verify an appointment and by the time someone FINALLY answered my call. They had placed me on hold after asking if I resided on the city or county side and then they said they’ve filled up all the appointment spaces for that area and the call ended. So, nobody warned me but I must warn others. IF you’re in dire need of financial assistance or any type of assistance. CALL after 9 am on the 1st of the month and get an APPOINTMENT!! If you want to be mistreated and disrespected…. This is the place for you. Otherwise, look for other resources to help you. The attitudes from certain members of this team was unacceptable, disrespectful and down right unprofessional. I wouldn’t recommend them to help anyone !

top_reviews.text:
This is one of the most upscale and most expensive thrift stores I ever went to on a military base  & in general. The staff is one of the most professional and knowledgeable in customer etiquette and in organizational & pricing skills. They are very thorough in curating & displaying high quality items, researching the items displayed, and placing a fair price on items sold. Some of the items are priced at what may seem outrageously expensive yet it is not. Mint condition or well known high quality items are priced at 50% (most of the time) of their selling price online used or new ( at this thrift store’s highest amount price). I found an elegant Mikasa bowl for $8 there that seemed over priced, yet it is selling for $60 online used and a discontinued style.

If you want dirt cheap and super low prices, you are better off going to a yard sale, typical thrift store, gimme a five, or general dollar store for a bargain or steal if you want items at a low price. If you are looking to resell items for profit, I would NOT recommend this place as well. According to my experience, the most superb deals and low priced items sold here are usually low key high quality luxury brands and not desired or well known by the general public.

Once in a blue moon, you will find rare and spectacular items at a stellar price; even though, you might not realize it until you research or know the item’s worth. I have purchased a vintage Rolex brand leather - brand new wallet with fine detailed & metal engraved hardware for only $4 there. I just bought it because it was red, real leather, and well made. I also found a low key yet high quality British luxury brand - new leather - wallet for $3.75 there too. Retro style curvy wood bar chairs for $35 each - was one of my most desirable finds here. I couldn’t find the exact chair online because it might be vintage or no longer manufactured. The closest duplicate to it was priced at $244 a chair and had an unattractive cut out design on the chair back.

Their book selection is always amazing and always have a buy two books & get one free deal. I always find the best giant coffee table photography books there and fascinating books. Another rare yet wonderful find here is vintage vinyl records in mint condition for $1 each.

It took me a long time to write a review for this store, because I didn’t think it was like your usual thrift store. It seemed that most of the items I was drawn to were consignment boutique or antique store prices - not at my price range except for the books and certain items. I realized this thrift store excels in customer service and had a lot of hidden gems & high quality items in the end that people usually disregard.

name: The Salvation Army Family Services & Emergency Shelter

top_reviews.text:
To stay all you need to do is pass a drug test by peeing in a cup. And go to police station to get a sheet of paper basically letting them know you're not in any type of legal trouble or hide or anything. On the rules paper ideally they want you in and out in 6 months) I've been there for about 9 months.
Breakfast is from 6am to 7pm but usually a bowl of cereal, coffee or breakfast cereal bars
Shelter closes everyday at 8am so must be out by 8a.m doesn't open back up until 4pm. So if you have kids or no car to get around in wouldn't recommend staying here. You'd just be sitting outside in yard all day.
Single adults are roomed with other single adults (separated by male and female) you share bathroom with everyone in your room. 3/4 adults to a room (unless you're a family and husband/bf rooms with wife and kids or single with kids you get your own room. ) each side has free washer and dryer.
Dinner is at 5pm to 6pm roughly
sometimes a church will come and serve a hot meal if not the monitors will find something quick to put together (maybe leftovers from some event they had something or quick and simple like a slice of pizza and corn.) resident are not allowed to use kitchen. On female side you can store drink only in fridge. If with kids can store snacks in room for kids
Snack time is at 8pm
Lights out is at 9pm ( just need to be in shelter)
After a week of staying you get added to chore list that everyone suppose to do.
You have to be in by 9pm
Smokers can be out until 11 pm to smoke
If you need basic toiletries they usually have some to give ( toilet tissue, soap laundry detergent etc)
If you want to stay out overnight you have to fill out a form two weeks in advance for permission)
Once a month meeting with shelter manager usually don't last more than about 5/10 minutes..at least that's been my case. It's a place to sleep.

If you have kids I'd recommend Mercy House. I've heard you stay in day with own kitchen  and bath. I didn't know that before hand. The only two places in the area I believe. Oh, open doors I believe is also a shelter. Don't know anything about it.

We went to court bc she tried to just give us 2 weeks to leave, and she owes us money just wanted her property back. Anywho, we called the salvation army and Pam put us on the waiting list. Lisa Anderson was extremely helpful and friendly and immediately got us on the referral list for housing and got us working with Miriam's House. They helped us with our application fees, first month and security deposit and a percentage of our rent until we are stable. They offer breakfast and dinner, sometimes goodie bags. The family unit room was clean and furnished and comfy, we even had a bath tub. You leave at 8, and come back at 4:30 in the afternoon, except weekends it's early and come back at 12. Curfew of 8:30 at night. The security guards are understanding and welcoming. Extremely friendly staff that want nothing but to see you succeed and prosper and they give you the toolset to do so.  We are very thankful for the salvation armys help.

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
12/20/24 Is this some kind of upscale boutique and they just never sent out a Memo? I made the mistake of stopping by this store again. I was hopeful that maybe things changed, but, oh no, they're worse.  They should call this place a museum because most people are just going to browse at things they'll never be able to afford. $700 sofas. $50-$100 leather jackets.  $80 purses.  $50 dutch ovens. $30 pyrex. The prices are higher than you can get items shipped purchased on the internet. So, don't bother going here. It's highway robbery.  Don't donate or shop here.

Organized and clean.  Anything with a name brand,  no matter the condition,  is violently over priced.  $80 handbags.  $10 plates.  Good grief. It's embarrassing.

Edit 8/24/24 I returned to the store on a Wednesday, 25% off day.  All Starbucks products were pulled off the shelves. Product they over price for $9.99-$16.99 each anyway. Starbucks cups are priced around $.99-$6.99 in almost every other thrift store in the area. Better bags are pulled from the floor as well (the bags they're pricing for$80), they only leave bags between $30-$45 in beat up condition on the floor. Which is already a laughable price when other salvation army in the area are pricing bags $2.99-$24.99. Found a vintage Stanley thermos, beat up and rusted inside for $39.99!!! Other locations are selling the vintage thermos for maybe $7.99. You could get one online for $20, on the high end. They have one but no more than 2 people working the registers on Wednesday. The line to check out was easily 25 people long and wrapped around the store. This location should be ashamed of itself. The other Salvation Army locations in the area are fairly priced and aren't pulling items off the floor during their promotion day.  This place should actually be audited. Whoever runs this place is price gouging and trying to match internet pricing without any consideration for your clientele. They can't be moving much at these prices. I wanted a polo shirt and it was priced at $14.99!!! I could get brand new items at these prices. I could go on the internet and get these same items in like new condition for cheaper with shipping included. Terrible horrible business practices at this location. Go ahead and  hide behind your charitable causes nonsense. Other salvation armys aren't treating their loyal customers this way. And the amount of waste this location must create because of the things they're not moving.  Avoid this location. I won't be back until I hear things have changed.
top_reviews.author: J A

top_reviews.text:
Prices were a little high on the furniture and some clothes. Sorry I didn’t get photos of the clothes prices. But, there was one lightweight jacket that was $24.99 and it wasn’t a name brand. You can get similar new items at Walmart or Target in that range. I realize they have to pay rent and there are operating costs, but $24.99 isn’t a thrift store price.

Currently, every Wednesday is 25% off the furniture, so maybe that’s why the prices are higher so they can then offer the discount once a week. Honestly, I don’t have time to go shopping on a Wednesday. As seen in my photos, there were a couple pieces of furniture that were $179.99 and $199.99 respectively. Those also aren’t “thrift store” prices.

I’d like to see the data if they changed their marketing strategy. Reduce prices by 25% across the board or they could keep current prices and market it as “Everyday is 25% off”. Would sales increase, would they have less inventory that they have to put in the trash when it doesn’t sell?

I’ve been to other Salvation Army stores and other thrift stores that have more reasonable prices on furniture.

They did have several couches, sorry again for not getting prices on those.

The store was very neat and organized, so management is doing a good job in that department.

They had a lot of clothes and kitchen dinnerware, glasses and china.

The close up photos are to show some of the prices.

The four stars are for the store being very organized and having a large variety of items. There was also ample parking out front.
top_reviews.author: Northern Virginia

top_reviews.text: This is my favorite thrift store in the area, I love the selection and for the most part the prices are fair. The store is clean and organized. Some things are a bit over priced like the furniture, “luxury items” behind case, and new with tag items. I’ve seen new with tag items with yellow clearance tag from Walmart priced at $3 and the SA priced item at $9.99 and if it’s a new with tag dress it’s $14.99. I can live with all the negative mentioned and still consider this my favorite thrift store in the area but what has really been ruining the experience lately is the employees. What a terrible attitude, they don't ask if you’re a rewards member and if you happen to mention you are and want to give your phone number to acquire points you get the whole eye roll huffing and puffing attitude. I have stopped using the rewards program to save myself the negative experience. I have overheard employees criticizing and ridiculing customers in the store. If the customer service wasn’t such a downer this store would be pretty close to a perfect thrift store.

name: Salvation Army - Martinsville - Food Distribution Center

top_reviews.text: I am compelled to inform you that this organization is unwilling to provide assistance to individuals with disabilities. As a homeless and handicapped individual, I have been denied aid, specifically food, on multiple occasions. The reason cited was my need for sustenance, which I find unacceptable. This establishment's policy of rejecting vulnerable populations, including the elderly and those with disabilities, warrants scrutiny. Furthermore, the director's dishonesty regarding the services they provide is alarming. I have never encountered a food bank that operates in such a manner. As a result, I am forced to endure hunger due to their inaction. It has been approximately a year since I last received food from this organization, and the uncertainty surrounding the arrival of food stamps only exacerbates my situation. It is unconscionable that individuals with disabilities are being turned away, and I strongly believe that this organization's practices require immediate attention.

name: The Salvation Army Hampton Roads Area Command

top_reviews.text:
In 2022, when I was struggling financially and was unable to save up enough money for Christmas (I usually save up as much as possible & it was even harder with gas being $6/gallon in the summer time...)... So I applied for the Salvation Army Angel Tree & I was honestly in tears! 😭 Absolutely ecstatic with all of the gifts of clothes, toys & gift cards my two children received! It was honestly overwhelming lol So much so, that I even donated some of the things we received to another family in need that unfortunately missed the deadline for the angel tree!

The only thing I will say is, it IS a bit difficult to wait in line for your donation pick up (especially if you have your kids with you, I had my 8 year old son & 4 year old daughter with me bc i didn't have anyone to watch them that day😭), If you have somewhere to be like work at a certain time or if you have a disability that limits you from standing for a long period of time. We were there for about 1hr and 45 minutes... But, it was TOTALLY worth it! Also, everything was like triple bagged in dark red opaque bags, so my kids wouldn't have been able to see anything in the bags fortunately!

top_reviews.text: This place is a biblical prison. You’re forced to attend church and bible study which completely goes against freedom of religion. The head guy Brandon is a drill sergeant. In the beginning you have to work at their store or loading dock making $7 a week. You work 9 hours. They add a dollar each week maxing up to $25. Which isn’t anything at all when you’re working in 110 degree weather. They take $420 from people with social security and disability and make them work full time anyway. When I was there, there was an elderly man with stage 4 cancer working on the loading dock. They take 40% of food stamps and serve you out-of-date food. I was kicked out of the program after complaining to the counselor about working a full 2 weeks with no day off. Which she said would be confidential. I was woken from a deep sleep by Brandon after taking my sleep meds. He put all my belongings on a cart and brought it outside the building. And was told to leave. It was 10:00 at night. I now see why there are 5 lawsuits against them. This place is not religious. It’s a cult. DO NOT COME HERE!!

name: The Salvation Army Thrift Store & Donation Center

top_reviews.text:
I have a complaint about your manager at the store on Gordon Boulevard, in Woodbridge.
Note that I am going public in this because the public is being grossly mislead about the Salvation Army’s stores and what actually happens to their donations.
On August 28, I went to the Gordon Boulevard store, during the 25% off sale and saw an item that I wanted to buy. It was on the floor along other similar items. When I picked it up, I noticed that it did not have a price tag. As many times before when this has happened, I asked for assistance to get a price. Regretfully, the person I asked was extremely rude to me, and snatched the item from my hands, yelling at me that she could not sell it to me. I was puzzled. She also made some derogatory remarks about me being gay. When I asked to see the manager because of the inappropriateness of her behavior - she said that she was the store manager and because it was her store she could do as she pleased. She even asked me to get out of the store!!! I asked her for the name of her supervisor but she said she had none, and needless to say, she refused to give me any information. She proceeded to hide the item behind the storage room doors -which so thought it was truly ridiculous. I asked her to let me take a picture of the item, but she refused and shut the doors behind her. The item I wanted to buy was an small artificial plant do I could not understand what was going on and why she was being so rude or mysterious about it. I walked out of the store and returned 2 hours later, and noticed that the storage room doors was open. I looked from the outside to see if I could see the artificial plant, but it was nowhere to be seen. One of the employees approached me and told me that she probably wanted it for herself or a relative and could not understand why this “manager” had treated me like she did.
From this interaction I can deduct that this woman is using her position as store manager for personal gain and taking, if not stealing the donations that patrons like myself give to that store all the time. The whole interaction caused a lot of distress that caused me to seek medical healthcare after the incident later during the day.
One of the employees shared her name with me because she would not offer that information for me either - I believe her name is Meceré though I don’t know if that is the correct spelling.
Today I went to the store again, but the item that I wanted to buy is nowhere to be found, so she definitely kept it for her own use or a relative’s. Needless to say, I called this store to ask for someone to help me but no one answers the phone and the voicemail is full.
Because of this, I am going public on this event so people know that your store on Gordon Boulevard in Woodbridge is running a SCAM and using the donations of the patrons for the personal gain of the store manager and possibly the employees who are part of her clique.

You need to conduct an investigation and ask this  woman why she snatched an item from the hands of a regular customer and most importantly what she did with it!!!!

I walked away  with nothing. Food Pantry. They play games with the food as to who they give what. I waited in line for over a half hour hoping to get some food. Food that I can eat. I am diabetic. But today at the pantry I was told that I could only get bread and produce and that I couldn't have any of the meat even though they had some. Who are they saving it for? This isn't fair. top_reviews.text:
we brought about $1000 worth of used tools to the Federal Way Donation Center.  they happily accepted a full box of nail guns, routers, electric staplers, drywall cutter, circular saw etc.  All name brands; Porter Cable, Grizzly.com, Craftsman, De Walt. When they got to the 2nd box that contained a hand sander, planer, 100’ tape measure, sawzall, tape measures, goggles, they started asking questions and the Asst Manager, Steve Nolan, came and said the tools were a little dirty and they’d have to clean them before they could be sold. I  of laughed and he asked if I thought it was funny.  I said “Yes, they are tools”. He said that costs them money. I asked if they were still a non - profit and did job training. He said yes but they need to make money to pay the employees. I said “Nevermind, I’ll take them back. ”.   They stood around and watched us reload the truck.

What a joke!  They could have easily sold the tools for hundreds of dollars. Their loss will be someone else’s gain. I would never donate there again or shop.

top_reviews.text:
I had the worst experience here!
I'm an older senior citizen and I've never been here before.
Apparently there's a protocol for parking here.
I was made fun of and bullied because everybody assumes there's only one rule for parking.  Here's the other rule: WAC 174-116-261(1): "No vehicle may stop, stand or park so as to obstruct traffic along or upon any street or sidewalk or in any parking lot." Blocking your sidewalk for pedestrians won't get me towed, but blocking vehicles access behind me will!  Guess who's going to win.
If you're assuming that no vehicles ever park over the bumper and end up with part of it in the sidewalk, then you're ridiculously wrong, nor will I get towed for that so long as there is access enough for a wheelchair.
I suggested if there's a protocol for parking in front of your building, that you put up a sign and ask people to park in a specific manner.
I was literally bullied and made fun of in front of other people by your volunteer!
Most unpleasant experience ever!
Would not recommend anybody come here.

name: The Salvation Army Puyallup Corps Community Center

top_reviews.text:
Since the first time I entered their recreation center after seeing the sign out front for Bingo, I went to check it out. Their rec center is open to all ages and during the weekdays, a free meal is offered from 12pm - 1pm. Be careful that if you are a minute or two late, you’ll miss out on getting a free meal. Activities usually begin at 1pm. It was nice to know this is available because I didn’t hear about this anywhere or seen this until I saw the sign outside. Many places have age and family restrictions where adults without children cannot receive resources immediately or at all because the others are prioritized.

So this was a pleasant surprise at first, however, there are many people that I’ve met there who are discriminatory and have caused problems mistreating me in several ways. Only a few members were staff, but the others have been from toxic community members. When keeping to myself or only a few people, then my times there have been pleasant. I still visit and keep things cordial to get what I need, but the hours have been changing quite a bit with more closures. This year, the rec center has been closed for a day to a week at a time so there has been a struggle trying to acquire resources.

While trying to seek shelter, I had left messages on their voicemail in which I did not receive an answer. However, when I needed a job, I was referred to their job openings on their website while visiting their rec center and was able to get a job in a short amount of time during last year’s holiday season as a bell ringer, which I am very grateful for. It was fun and efficient in the process of getting needed supplies for the job to get done. My Manager Ryan Miller was very professional and did make sure that I received my paychecks in a timely manner while working around my schedule to ensure my financial needs were met.

He is also part of the church service on Sundays and invited me to their program and other events. During the Christmas Season, they do a beautiful Silent Night Prayer and offer gifts to their attendees.

Their Food Bank has helped me during desperate times, but their hours have been changing a lot throughout the year that it can be difficult to keep up with, especially without transportation. Delivery is not available. There are food bank cards offered now that you get from their office as they updated their policy and procedures. It may take awhile as I had to wait four weeks for my card so I am unsure how long it would take a new food seeker to get one now.

I’ve been denied food here a few times this year, but they have been able to offer food to me most of the time that I have gone here for a few years on and off. Their new schedule is now three days open schedule from 10am - 1pm on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. On Wednesdays, they now only give food and clothing for appointments only, which I am unsure why. After a few tries of visiting the food bank last week, I was able to get some food to help stock my pantry. The staff is friendly and they are willing to help pack your vehicle as well if needed.

There are boxes of food available for people to pick through, but a concern I’ve witnessed is that the food does look spoiled in mass quantities. As shown in one of the photos I’ve added, there are many bananas and zucchinis that look rotten.

There’s also clothing offered when there is any. I’ve donated here a few times over the years as well bringing in large trash bags full of gently used and new clothing. There’s usually some for children as well, not all sizes are guaranteed, but it is helpful when needing something when you have nothing as an option. They helped clothe me after I had all of my belongings stolen. I was able to still manage with a broken zipper jacket, but was also able to get new shoes and bras too.

One of the best people I met there was Amanda. She is an amazing person—kind, hardworking, and always ready to lend a hand. Her positivity and dedication to helping others were inspiring, and she made every shift enjoyable. She truly embodies the spirit of The Salvation Army.

top_reviews.text:
I first attended the Salvation Army of Camas/Washougal in 2017.  After moving back to town. And having my Sister and Aunt beg me for about a year to come visit their church.
I finally decided to check it out. Feeling defeated in life and struggling with great depression. Due to permanent neuropathic pain down my whole right leg into foot that I live with every day from a previous back injury. The first year I always sat in the very back row. So I could get in and out as quickly as possible. But I kept coming back every week. The way Pastor Samantha taught the Bible was just what I needed to hear. With Love and compassion.
After the pandemic occurred in late 2019. This church never stopped masks and all. When they were forced to shut their doors. They moved online with their weekly worship and sermons. As well as Wed on Zoom. Where I eventually felt comfortable enough to talk a little about myself and share my testimony with a screen full of people I had grown very fond of.
This church has only a handful of "employees".  Which include Paster Samantha Wheeler and her family. They never quit serving and loving others during covid. In fact when they were forced to shut their doors. They made sure to personally visit the doorsteps of every church member leaving boxes of foods and goods. They put warming heaters outside their doors and still never turned anyone down that showed up with a need.  It's been amazing to watch this church grow and be a part of it. Seeing the amount of volunteers we have weekly makes my heart rejoice. The love and support this church brings to our community is absolutely bountiful. The way they gladly work with other churches in our area is pretty awesome as well. Because in fact it does take an ARMY an Army of the most high GOD to serve and LOVE one another. Today I sit in the front row and have even joined the worship team singing. "Which I only used to do in the shower".😆 I've also joined their Ukulele group that is yes open to anyone interested. I encourage anyone reading this review who may feel lost, broken, hurt, struggling with addiction. To come, come as you are! And to know that you were created perfectly in the image of the most high GOD. With the seed of Love planted in your heart. Hope to see you Sunday. 🙏✌️❤️😊
top_reviews.author: Tina King

top_reviews.text:
Disappointing Experience at Goodwill Woodinville

I recently visited the Goodwill store in Woodinville to donate some furniture, and I must say, I was extremely disappointed with the experience. The staff exhibited a lack of professionalism and seemed untrained in handling donations. When I arrived, I was informed that they only accept new furniture, yet no one even took the time to look at the items I had brought along.

It felt as though my donation was disregarded without any consideration. Goodwill has a reputation for helping those in need, and I expected a more respectful interaction. Instead, I left feeling frustrated and undervalued as a donor. I hope they can improve their customer service and training for future interactions. I won't be returning anytime soon.
top_reviews.author: Dan and Ruby Kamcas

top_reviews.text: Typical experience: Stopped at 11:50am. There were three cars in line. Two of them were exasperatedly waiting outside their car trying to get someone's attention. Employees clearly saw us but just slowly shuffled around doing who knows what with no explanation. top_reviews.text: I used to go there fairly often before they changed everything and brought in new prices and new staff. The prices are so   high now that people who are truly poor or on a fixed income have had to look elsewhere to shop. Books went to 2.49 for hard backs and 1.49 for paperbacks and a person who reads a lot cannot afford them anymore. The misc. items, whatnots , etc.,  have more than doubled in price. Furniture is  ridiculously over priced. Saw a little bedside table for thirty dollars! Really! Used potty chairs for twenty dollars! You have to clean and disinfect , repair, paint, or whatever all this stuff and you are also risking that it may have a chip, tear, crack, flaw that you aren't even aware  of and they want so  much for it. No thanks, I'll just buy new or shop elsewhere. These thrift stores need to get a grip or they will be out of business soon.

top_reviews.text:
I used to not like them here. Especially at the food bank. But over the years I kept politely persisting they be mindful of my food aversions and they are now. If you have food allergies or aversions this is the first food bank that really will work with me that I know of. Especially with the new front desk worker. She's very nice and accepting of people with differences. I hope she stays that way or they don't replace her, as the are some working there that are hateful.

The hateful workers, I don't take it personal, they must just be miserable people and must be suffering really badly in their own lives to treat others so vulnerable and living in poverty like we aren't even humans that deserve their compassion. It takes someone with a toxically fragile ego to need to feel like they are better than people that are marginalized and suffering, to look down on others like they do. I know they don't target me, they do this to everyone. So if I just smile, keep my own kindness and compassion, and get the resources I need to help me survive as a disabled person, it doesn't bother me like I used to.

The thrift store is about the only good thrift store on the west side. They actually have the clothing intellectually organized (with an actual plus size section) along with their other items. Since the store is small they have limited items, but are better than the Goodwill! I'd say this store and Mountain Mission are about equal, though I haven't been to MM in a good while. Some employees in the thrift store are grumpy too, but most are nice and polite.

top_reviews.text: Previously, when my family and I had needed cheap housewares, furniture, we have come to this thrift store. Recently, we had family move here, looking for cheap furniture as well, and we’re completely shocked to find how they are pricing items in their store. Donated, Visibly used couches, tables and chairs, recliners, desks, etc. are being charged upwards of $200. This is supposed to be a Christian organization, and you are reselling donated goods. Think of the people who are coming here to purchase items and how they are trying to stretch their money as far as they can. You ought to be ashamed that your pricing, as high as it is. If anyone in a managerial capacity sees this review, I encourage you to go take a look around your furniture warehouse. Look at the condition these items are in, and see if the pricing makes sense.

top_reviews.text: We are a family of 5, including a newborn baby. I called December 22nd to see if we could get help with our Energy bill, they said yes and to come down the following Monday. We got there the following Monday and they were closed. Called the next day on the Tuesday and they said to come back the following Monday. We paid the $100 they asked us to pay on it in the meantime as that’s the only way they would help and we came back the following Monday. That was our last $100 by the way. That Monday, we go in there and the English woman who is incredibly RUDE told us they were unwilling to help us because the termination said $167, even though it also clearly stated at the top that an additional $570 was owing. She told us the amount was too low to help & that because Kroger had taken the bottom of the bill for the $100 payment that they would not help us. I said the bottom of the bill just as the same information as the top half of the bill and she argued with me and said she couldn’t take a ripped piece of paper with missing information. I pointed out to her that when the Salvation Army calls in the pledge, they’ll speak to an account representative who can tell them the full amount of the bill and any questions they have and that the only reason the bottom of the bill is missing is because SHE told us to go pay $100 on the bill first. All she wanted to do was stand there and argue, while I had a baby in my arms pleading for help. My termination notice was for December 26th and I just had a baby so I’m not working right now. It’s now January 6th and the power is about to be cut off on three kids. I hope this woman sleeps well knowing she just hurt my family and left kids to freeze in the middle of winter.
top_reviews.author: Chellie Anne

top_reviews.text: The word salvation should be removed from this organization in Princeton.They treat someone truly in need like a thorn in their side. After hours of going through the process of being approved for assistance you are given a small bag of canned food and told it should last 3 months. All that's donated free to them is put in the thrift store and priced higher than you can buy it at any other store, meanwhile the workers are carrying loads of food, clothing and other items of preference out to load up and take home. I have only recently had to ask for help and I truly regret donating to them for 20+ years. Now I see that the word salvation stands only for their own selfishness and greed. My family and I will starve before being subjected to that kind of treatment and for gods sake if the employees are loading up all the food, clothing and anything else they like, please don't discuss and do it while someone is there and getting only your leftovers!

top_reviews.text:
I just wanted to say a huge thank you to the entire staff and everyone involved in organizing this incredible camp in Wisconsin. I was truly impressed by how well everything was managed — the cleanliness, the order, and the care from the team were outstanding.

The natural beauty of Wisconsin was breathtaking, and the activities organized throughout the camp were both fun and meaningful. I especially enjoyed the fishing — such a relaxing and memorable experience. The atmosphere was amazing, filled with positive energy and good vibes.

Thank you to everyone who took part in making this camp such a special place. You created something truly unforgettable.

Even after four days, I’m still under the spell of those wonderful moments. I’ll definitely be coming back with my family — we’ll be missing this camp and its unique vibe all year long.

Absolutely amazing.

top_reviews.text:
The VFW isn’t just a bar — it’s a home away from home. Every time I walk through the doors, I’m greeted with genuine smiles and great conversation.

The bartenders know how to pour a solid drink, the food hits the spot, and the prices are exactly what they should be — fair, honest, and perfect for a day or night out. Wacko, meat raffles, karaoke, and trivia… there’s always something happening, and it brings people together in the best way.

But what really makes this VFW special is the heart behind it. The veterans, the families, the regulars, the volunteers — everyone shows up for each other. It feels like being part of something bigger than yourself.

Not a very welcoming place. The people that eat there for the daily lunch are only good to you if you've been going there for a long time. You have to get there quite early just to get a spot because if you come a bit late and are trying to get a spot, people will stop you by putting their foot on chairs as you approach a table or just downright look at you funny before telling you that the spot is taken. The people that work there are the same way as the patrons. They will put up a front and only be nice when they have to be. But that's the culture of this town.

You're also not allowed to use your phones while at this place because you're expected to deal with who's present.

The only saving grace with this place is the annual Thanksgiving meal when volunteers that don't normally come there to help with the big meal. This is the only time of year where you can be an outsider and be treated half decently.

Anyone can post a bulletin of how something is open to everyone, but that bulletin is nothing but false advertisement when it only applies to those that have been going for years.

My advice, steer clear of this place if you're new to town or new to the lunches.

My rating: 0/5 stars.

name: The Salvation Army of Dane County

top_reviews.text:
Hello, I would like to take the time to thank the Salvation Army of Dane County for providing housing and nutritious meals. I arrived at the Salvation Army mid October, 2022. I had only been in Madison since August 2022. I lived in Chicago all my life so this was definitely a scary experience never leaving my hometown before. Although, I was met with homelessness I knew God would have to be by my side to make it though the biggest obstacle in life HOMELESSNESS. There was so many times I just wanted to give up but I just didn't know how to give up. So, the only option left was to fight. I was mentally, emotionally and physically exhausted. The homelessness for me started in mid June in Chicago now it's October and still no place to call home. On October18, 2022 the doors open for me at the Salvation Army I was scared, nervous and hopeful. I know I had plenty work ahead of me. I wasn't sure what to expect but I was ready for whatever challenge there was for me to face.  Essential needs were provided for me food, clothing when available and a warm bed every night. I received meals that was prepared with a lot of love. Melissa McClain worked as an exceptional Case Manager. Melissa provided necessary apartment leads, information about accessible apartment, referral information for therapy, bus cards  for use to make necessary business appointments. Melissa returned my calls in a timely manager, she always communicated any updates with me. I felt what Melissa provided is exactly what I needed which was hope. I finally feel like the is a road opening I just need to find that road. I must say for the first time I am feeling very hopeful. So, I decided I must help myself also. I applied for a senior apartment and I was offered a one bedroom apartment. However, I developed Covid and spent the next 10 days at The Microtel. I applied for the apartment on November 18, 2022 and I moved in on December 5, 2022. This year will mark 2 years in my new apartment. Chloe is another Case Manager that worked with me she was always so excited to help and she always smiled which made me happy. Positive energy is the key. Chloe went above and beyond with the help she assisted me with once I moved in my apartment.

I feel because I was afforded the opportunity to be housed and provided with the essentials I needed during that time. I was able to use that time to plan my future and figure out "where do I go from here" I didn't know the answer at first. So, I decided to transition from disability to employment. During the time I was displaced I had been disabled since 2005. So, my goal is to transition to employment I haven't worked since 2002. However, with the support from the Salvation Army I didn't have to think about bills, food, transportation or where I would sleep from day to day. I used that opportunity to plan my future. So, in January 2023 I reached out to the DVR to discuss my transition from disability to employment. I enrolled in Madison College HSED 5.09 program to acquire my high school credential. I started Madison College GED program in June, 2023. I am happy to report that I completed the program in January 2024. I will be graduating in May, 2024 with my diploma. I started school at Madison College in the Accounting Assistant Program January 2024. I will complete my first semester as a college student in two weeks. I plan to attend school this summer also. I'll take 2 classes this summer Personal Finance and Business Spreadsheets. I can't wait to continue my journey.
If it wasn't for the Salvation Army of Dane County I'm not sure where I would be. However, because of the Salvation Army of Dane County my life is filled with hope not hopelessness. Whatever happens in life never give up. I didn't give up now the sky will be the limit for me. The sky can be the limit for you.
I'm sharing this post in hopes that it reach current and future donors who support the Salvation Army because your support is needed and greatly appreciated. I am the result of what your donation can do.

thanks
Regina

top_reviews.text: We like to hunt out the SVdP's all over Wisconsin because we love their mission and how much they help their communities. On our Madison-area adventure this weekend, we put "St Vincent de Paul Madison" into Google Maps and were pleased to see how many popped up -- including this fun "Dig and Save" option. We went here first and arrived right as it opened... to a line of about 20 people waiting to get in! We brought our work gloves as other reviewers had suggested; the clothing and linens bin in the front of the store were free of sharp objects, but you could hear people  hunting through the bins in the back where kitchen and household objects are located, and glass was definitely breaking as people moved stuff around. The staff do their best, though, to keep things safe. They've put the glass items into smaller cardboard boxes so that if something gets broken, it's not mixed into the bottom of a huge bin; the box with the broken item can be removed while the rest stays safe. The prices were so good! $1.50/lb for cloth items, and 60¢/lb for anything else. You can't beat that! I walked out with 3 coats, 5 sweaters, a blanket, a curtain and a glass pot lid for $12!

name: The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center

top_reviews.text: SURRENDER YOUR ADDICTION AND BEGIN AGAIN! For anyone struggling with addiction, or that knows a loved one struggling, this place can be a saving grace. I spent my teens and 20's a slave to drugs, state rehab, jail, none of it worked. 12 years clean now and The Salvation Army ARC in Milwaukee welcomed me with open arms, no questions asked. Did I have to work to stay there? Yes. All beneficiaries have to volunteer their time. Did I have 3 quality meals a day (including a salad bar at lunch and dinner?) Yes! Did I have to go to church? Yes! ( and thank GOD I did). They clothed me, fed me, gave me a safe warm place to sleep and a relationship with God. What did I have to give them? 40 hours a week as a volunteer in a number of roles at the facility. How many of us work more than that for less reward spiritually and physically? This place saved my life and not only did it save mine, after I graduated from the program (with a real job and my own apartment near the lake) my sister went to the womens facility in Romulus Michigan and she is now clean, with a husband, house and 2 children. Thanks be to God and the Salvation Army. Any previous "clients" of this facility with complaints are clearly entitled and dont understand that getting clean and sober requires a commitment from the USER and the facilitator. The Salvation Army couldnt provide these things without your work while you attend the program. Thankfully, Gods grace is free and part of the program. Stop being selfish, surrender yourself, your selfishness, ego and time to finally make a change in your life. I "sacrificed" 6 months of my life for an eternity and long term prosperity. Thank you again ARC, I will remember you this Christmas when our family is making charitable donations.

top_reviews.text: I had heard great things about this place and was able to get in in February to may. My first case manager told me she would vouch for me once my 90 days were up to stay longer.   I knew someone who lived there for two years before finally getting his own place.   Well after she left everything went downhill and I got traded like an object for another person at a different shelter.   What I liked about salvation army was they had a nurse during the week,  and a doctor once a week.  I liked that it was handicap accessible.   I liked the front staff, and the older cafeteria lady.  The young girls down there were rude.  I liked my first case manager but like I  said her replacement was about useless.  The shelter they transferred me to almost killed me with my mental health.   They decided I needed a higher level of care and kicked me out onto the street.   I tried getting back into the salvation army but thr director said no. top_reviews.text:
I bought a love seat on June 18th, 2025. My son and I picked up the love seat a couple of days later. When I sat on the love seat, it seemed comfortable and my son needed something that was sturdy. The manager Rogelio rolled the love seat out to the U Haul and loaded it into the back of it. We drove back to my sons apartment. When we took the love seat out of the U Haul, we heard stuff rolling around inside of the love seat. We did not know this when we purchased it because when you purchase something, you usually do not tip a love seat up and roll it around the store. When we got it into the apartment, we started to clean the love seat. We vacuumed the top of the couch. Then my son tipped the couch up so I could vacuum the couch on the bottom. There was a ton of stuff inside the love seat and there was dog urine on the bottom of the couch. I put the hose into the bottom of the couch and we filled up the whole entire vacuum 3 times with dried dog food. There was also a dead mouse that was vacuumed up.
We could not get all of the dog food out of the couch because the hose was not long enough to get it all out. We would have had to rip the bottom of the couch apart to get it all out. It was disgusting. My son dragged the couch to his porch because of the smell on the bottom of the couch and all the dog food we could not get out of the love seat. He was afraid that mice would come into his apartment to get at the dog food. A day later, he dragged the love seat to the garbage dumpster and put it in there to be disposed of.
I then went to the Salvation Army in Racine on Washington Avenue with the huge bag of dog food. I also had pictures and videos of us rolling the couch with all the dog food in it.
The lady behind the counter seemed concerned with what we found. She went to get the manager Rogelio. When he came out, I explained to him what happened and asked if I could get my money back. He stated that we should have checked that out before we left the store and he said I could not get the money back. He also tried to take the bag of dog food that we got out of the couch. I said, I will take that and left. I was not happy.
I then left messages with the Racine store and actually talked to someone on the phone. They said that I was going to get a call back from another store about this, but no one bothered to call me back.
I did not know when you buy a love seat from a second hand store that the customer should stand the love seat up and roll it back and forth to see if there is dried dog food, dog pee and a mouse in the couch. I believe that the manager of the store should have to check those things out before an item is donated to the store.
There is no way that the manager did not hear all that stuff rolling around inside of the couch before he placed it on the floor to be sold.
It is disgusting that such an item was even taken into the store to be sold.
Please remember if you buy a furniture item from this store that the manager said it is your responsibility to check out the item before it leaves the store. This means you better bring someone with you so you can tip the furniture up and make sure it is not loaded up with dog food, a mouse and urine.
